title: Very strong scent at first, but it disappears very quickly.
text:
I really loved the idea of this Boiess Baby Cologne "Les Enfants" in White Blossom. Not because I think it is a good idea for a baby, because boy, is it not. I actually thought it would be perfect for myself since I don't like loud fragrances. The description of the scent profile really enticed me, as I love all of the notes. I was able to try both the Lavanda and the White Blossom scents.
Both of the "Cologne" sprays smell identical to me. I can't say that I can tell them apart at all. They both have a very strong earthy, herbal, slightly floral scent that is heavily ladened with alcohol upon spraying. It stays very strong for several minutes, but then starts to dry down.
Sadly, once it dries down, the scent pretty much dissipates. If I don't spray it heavily at first, which is too much for my asthma to handle, much less any baby, the scent just goes away completely. I must spray it on me again. If I spray it on a few times over an hour or so, I can smell the ever so slightest hint of it on my clothing later, if I put my nose right on it. That is a lot of spraying for very little payoff.
I know this is meant for kids mostly, but I would think the scent would and should last longer. Sure, my grandsons will like using it, maybe or not, as it is quite strong at first. But, I think it would just be more for the fun of it and very short lived. This is also very expensive "Cologne" to not be able to smell it after 30 minutes, and right at $28 is too expensive for me to buy just for the fun of it.  
For others this "Baby Cologne" may be something wonderful or maybe they can smell it more than I can. As I said, I really love the idea of a light fragrance, but not for babies. I do wish the scent stuck around more for me.

There's neither anything special nor anything disappointing about this set.
What sets this set apart from others is the lighted mirror. Otherwise, you can actually get larger sets for a lower price, with wider assortments of picks, scrapers and that even include tweezers.
However, since I needed these tools for crafting/tinkering purposes and not for teeth cleaning, a smaller set with a lighted mirror was suitable for my needs. The tools and mirror help me reach into and look into spaces, helping me to scrape or remove flashing, pry things, pick out broken parts, position parts when epoxying, etc.
The tools are strong and durable. The mirror has a sharp image and the light is very helpful as I'm using this to peek inside small cases and enclosures. I don't doubt these are more than adequate for tartar removal, they're a strong and precision crafted stainless steel.
Overall I give the set 4-stars, it suits my needs at a fair enough price.

3. They have lasted very well for me and I work with my hands a lot as well as play guitar often with no pick. This will chip your nails quickly, but this hasn't happened yet.

What I disliked:
1. This kit does not come with a base or top coat.
2. I already have a few base and top coats hanging around the house and the first attempt I made using this polish I used a base and top coat that was not comparable. It would not dry even when under the UV light for quite some time. The second attempt I switched my base and top coat to another brand and it worked. They should really just include the base and top coats if this is a potential for customers. Just keep this in mind if you find the polish isn't drying the first attempt.

Given the pros and cons as long as you can find a compatible base and top coat you'll really like this product, if you want to avoid the frustration I'd suggest finding a kit that includes the base and top coats already.

title: Works for Eye Puffiness & Amazing Off-Label Headache Relief!!
text:
This eye cream was far different than I was expecting -- but in a GREAT way. I'm 29-years-old, so the lines around my eyes aren't terribly deep, although they are probably deeper than many other females my age due to my sun-worshiping in earlier years. I do suffer, however, from severe seasonal allergies and am constantly plagued with dark circles ("allergic shiners" as they call them) and extreme puffiness of both my upper eyelids and just under my eyes (the infamous "bags").

To be honest, my impression of this cream at first glance wasn't too great. For starters, the jar of cream was much smaller than I had imagined, but I guess that's my fault for not noticing the (very) small-printed "0.5 fl oz" on the label in the picture. (I do think that this was a little deceitful though, because the size/amount of this cream is not listed anywhere on the product description.) In addition, while trying to read the teeny tiny print on the jar, I also almost immediately noticed a spelling typo on the front of the label that reads "Nautral & Healthy" rather than "Natural & Healthy." I know this seems like a rather minuscule and knit-picky detail to point out, but it did make me at least wonder about this company's quality control standards.

Despite my initial impression, I gave the company/cream the benefit of the doubt and have been using it for the last few days. With my first application under my eyes, the cream felt more on the "thin" side (similar to a lotion rather than thick cream), but while rubbing the cream into my skin in a circular motion, the moisture that the cream delivered was far better than I anticipated. It takes at least 3-4 minutes before your skin feels like the cream is completely absorbed, which gave me ample time to slowly massage the area during absorption (and felt very soothing and relaxing). I had absolutely no issues with any side effects or skin reactions such as burning, tingling, redness, or irritation. I noticed a small "immediate" reduction in the pores and fine lines of the areas I applied the cream, though not as impressive as some of the Retinol and Vitamin C serums that I've used in the past. There was no obvious difference in the dark circles or puffiness right after application, however, within about 30-45min, the puffiness started to visibly decrease and the area all around my eyes felt less tender/achy in general.

With each subsequent application, I noticed the same resulting decrease in puffiness as was observed initially. My puffiness did return each morning, but I expected because I'm still constantly being exposed to my allergens. (After all, the cream is meant to relieve a symptom of my allergies, not be a miracle cure for my chronic systemic condition.) I've noticed that if I apply the cream immediately before bed and spend more time rubbing it into my skin in the circular motions, I do have a noticeable decrease in the morning when I wake up compared to before I started using the cream. As far as the under-eye dark circles, I can't tell a difference so far - but in all fairness, I've only been using the cream for 4 days (twice daily) so there's still hope.

Now for the best part (in my opinion, at least). On the second night of using this cream, I had yet another one of my throbbing headaches (allergies are the worst!!) About 15-20min after my evening cream application, I noticed that my headache felt a little better -- I'm not saying that there was some miraculous change here, but it did feel less severe. This was very unusual for me, as I hadn't taken any ibuprofen or Zyrtec at that point (my usual go-to medications when my headaches are severe). The only thing I could think that I had done differently this time than any other time was that I applied the cream -- it was a strange connection, but stranger things have certainly happened to me. I went back to look at the ingredients listed on the jar and saw that it had rooibos in it. I had absolutely no idea what this was (and probably didn't notice it the first time I looked because I don't have a magnifying glass), but I looked it up online and read that it's an herb from South Africa with a laundry-list of health benefits -- including antioxidant properties and... headache relief?!?! Although still relatively skeptical that this was just a coincidence and that I had gotten "lucky" on my google search, I was still optimistic and proceeded to rub the eye cream on my temples and at the base of my skull to see what would happen. After a good 30-45min, my headache was almost completely gone. I know this headache thing sounds ridiculous and obscure, but I encourage anyone to research this mysterious Rooibos for themselves. I haven't had a headache as severe as that one since, but I have had a few headaches start to come on, and with each headache, I applied the cream to my temples, under my eyes, and to the base of my skull and the feeling has gone away each time within about an hour.

With all of this said, I couldn't rate this "eye" cream turned headache remedy anything less than 5 stars despite my initial less-than-thrilled first impression. Because the cream is light and only requires a very small amount with each application, I think the small jar will actually last me a reasonably long time, too. Between the headache relief and the disappearing eye bags, I would be confident in recommending this product to others. I was also fortunate to receive my first jar of this cream at a discounted price or free in exchange for my honest and unbiased review.

title: I tested this controversy
text:
SEE BOTTOM FOR MY UPDATE: Is the 51s foil and cutter really terrible? Is the 30B foil and cutter really better for your Braun Series 8000 shaver? Is there an Original Equipment foil and cutter still available for the Braun 8985 shaver? Answers: no, no, and no. I have the Braun 8985 shaver and bought BOTH of the foils and cutters mentioned in these reviews: the 51s, which Braun sells as its only replacement now for the 8000 series, and the 30b, which is supposed to be for the Braun 7000/4000 series shavers, but some buyers are saying it works better for the 8000 series shavers than the so-called "terrible" 51s replacement. Both foils and cutters fit my 8985 shavers, and I've shaved serveral times with both. The 51s does NOT pull, cut or irritate my face and gives a very close shave, particularly if I have a 2-day beard. The 30b also gives a good shave, but perhaps not quite as close. Some reviewers say the 51s wears out quickly, is prone to dents and starts irritating your face. If that happens, I will update this review, but so far, so good.

I ordered the 51s by mistake because the seller's web listing did not mention that its "Braun 8000 360 Complete Foil and Cutter Block for Models 8995, 8985 and 8975" is really the controversial 51s replacement. When it arrived with the dreaded 51s name on the package, I immediately ordered the 30b foil and cutter and planned to return the 51s, but I waited until the 30b arrived so I could be sure it worked. It does, but it buzzes differently and didn't shave much closer than my 3-year-old original foil and cutter. The 30b DOES give a more comfortable shave -- it glides over your face like nothing is happening. The shave is fine, what you'd expect from any electric. But Braun is better than "any electric." The 51s is giving me that exceptionally close shave I expect from Braun. You DO feel the 51s a bit more than the 30b, but it's not irritating. I am keeping the 30b in case my 51s goes haywire on me, but for now, the 51s seems better.

UPDATE May 6, 2012: I'm glad I kept the 30b because the 51s did indeed start inflicting red marks on my face, and it stopped shaving as closely. Very disappointing. So now I'm using the 30b, the red marks on my face are gone, and the shave is close. So if I had it to do all over again, I would recommend getting tthe 30b foil and cutter instead of the 51s.

2. Make up enhancer -- If you want that dewy look and don't want to spend a fortune at sephora, ulta or department store make-up counters...add this to your arsenal. I add a few drops to foundation I got at target and my concealer (it cosmetics...it's the only one I've been able to find that has a light enough shade for my porcelain-like complexion). OMG...I'm in LOVE!!! I have tried a couple of oils (besides vitamin c - lol)...almond and rosehip. It came with a charger (I noticed some other reviews said theirs did not), I could usually get a few hours on max illumination from one charge, and I was happy with the purchase.

Now, two years later, the mirror has completely stopped holding a charge, and the second I unplug it the light begins to dim and then almost immediately shuts off. Some might say two years is more than enough life to get out of a mirror on the cheaper side, and they wouldn’t be wrong. Personally, I’ve spent way less than $30 on lighted mirrors in the past and gotten way more life out of them. Honestly, if I were you, I would pass on this one. Bought the pump for my elderly mother-in-law who has difficulty lifting the larger size mouthwash bottles and opening the caps. Works fine for our needs.

Pros:
Fits Listerine Zero 1.5L bottles. Can't comment on whether it fits other brands or sizes but based on previous reviews, sounds like it doesn't fit other brands.
Makes it easier to dispense product vs. lifting and pouring out product.
Inexpensive solution - I paid $6.50 with free Prime shipping.

Cons:
Pump dispenses additional product as it releases/comes back up so be prepared for this and keep your cup beneath the spout the entire time until it has reset to the starting position.
Spout tip is angled outwards so place your cup directly underneath the tip to keep product in cup.
Pump flow is strong so definitely use a taller larger cup or you'll get splash back. I'd recommend the standard 3 oz Dixie type cups. I bought the tiny 3/4 oz paper medicine type cups thinking that would work but they're a tad too difficult to use with the pump.

title: A great falling sand picture
text:
In short, excellent product with well thought out characteristics. I am purchasing more.

I thoroughly enjoy the Golden Sun sand picture by Paradise Vision. It appealed to me so much I purchased it as a gift to myself. Now I am purchasing more for gifts for others. I provide below more details that may not be apparent in the product description or that are notable for me and might be important for others.

Mounting Features - The "picture" comes with design and parts for both table top placement and wall mounting. Frame is angled so that it will not stand on just the frame. Even if it could stand on the frame it is much too susceptible to falling over (and breaking glass) and the provided tapered frame prevents its support is important. It appears Paradise Vision also concluded this and, according, effected this taper. For table top support, a slightly flexible plastic "leg" is provided that supports the picture from behind. The leg attaches to the picture by press fit compression of the leg's two-prong fork feature to be around a sort of rubber grommet. If securely attached I find the leg does not come off when picking up the picture and placing it again on the table top in the same orientation. The leg must be removed and replaced 180 degrees on circular grommet/mount on back of picture if the picture is turned over for the falling sand effect. Bottom line, pick up picture, remove leg, turn over as many times as you want, when satisfied, reattach leg and set picture on table top.

Glass Face - Face is glass, not plastic. Perfect. Plastic is more susceptiple to scratching in my experience and opinion.

Great Scene - Picture has a perfect photograph for complementing the sand (OK this might be apparent in the Amazon photos). What appeals to me is that there is the photograph where other sand pictures that have no photo leaves the viewer seeing what is behind the sand when the sand settles. I find seeing whatever happenes to be behind the picutre less appealing. Also, in this (Golden Sun) version, the sand includes yellow and orange sand (small amounts of both) that complement the photograph and make the sand scene appear like the tops of hills/mountains still receive sunlight.

Great Frame - Solid frame with small grain/fatigue surface features, also painted a shiny gold coler (thing shiny dark gold gift bow). It might have a clear coat of some kind, but I am not sure. Tight, quality joints and surfaces at corners with no mis-alignment, mismatched thickness problems. I am nearly certain it is wood, but I cannot be absolutely certain.

Good Dimensions - Dimensions are big enough to accomodate more than one "hill/mountain". My experience with smaller sand pictures tend to create only one or none or more very small ones.

Air/Water Adjustment - Parts includes a blunt syringe and instructions for adding air or removing air contained in the picture. This is done by inserting the syringe through a normally blocked, one-way gasketed hole feature (about 1/8 in. diamteter) in the side of the frame. I have never seen this feature for users in water-filled sand pictures by other manufacturers. I will confess to not having tried adding/removing air because I don't want to alter the amount that seems to be working just fine as received from the manufacturer. Instructions for doing so are provided and I found sufficiently clear.

Tilt Angle Potentially Problem - The only thing I would have changed if I could was to shorten the slightly flexible plastic leg so the picture doesn't tip back , it appears, by only 10 degrees or so from vertical where it is easily tipped forward if bumped. If it falls forward, it could break, particularly if the glass strikes an object when falling. I would have suggested, perhaps, 20 degrees tip for a little more stability.

Slightly Flexible Leg Feature Good - I suspect the leg is slightly flexible, rather than rigid, so that, if the picture is bumped from the front or set down on the table top surface a little more "vigorously" that the leg will flex a little rather than, otherwise, possibly resulting cracking or breakage of the leg or picture. Great idea Rainbow Vision.

I know I have written a lot. I hope it helps.
Steven

title: MIxed feelings
text:
After reading on many shaving blogs about how much closer a straight-edge razor will shave, I decided to try it out. I got tired of using disposables and having difficulty cleaning them and dealing with the cost. Having never tried straight edge shaving before, I debated whether to buy a high end blade, a cheap one, or something in the middle. I decided to go for the higher end of the lower cost models and bought one of these.

My first impression on removing it from the box was that the gold embossing on the handle really detracted from the looks of an otherwise attractive blade. But it doesn't really matter what it looks like if it works well. Out of the box, it is not shave ready. I did everything I'd read about to prep properly (except hone the blade) and it just didn't produce a close shave and pulled quite a bit. By way of comparison, I went back over and got a much improved result from a three week old disposable afterwards.

I have no doubt that this will take an edge and function just fine, and I suspect there is some truth to the "snob" argument that a better blade will hold an edge longer, as is true of knives, but almost any blade can be honed to sharpness. In fact, I subsequently purchased a different brand of carbon steel blade that was pre-honed from the seller and it performed quite nicely. To be fair, I don't know that a more expensive blade won't have the same issues if not honed by the seller prior to shipment.

As stated by another reviewer, any blade will require maintenance and the skills to sharpen it if you plan to use it regularly. I will give a try at sharpening this one eventually since I will need to learn this skill. Just be aware that you may need to develop the skill or find someone to do it for you before you will get a good result.

title: Great Razor
text:
Solid CNC machining for super durability, perfect blade alignment, and hold. The standard blade base was very easy to use. It would be great for beginners, people with thin hair, or someone who shaves their head. The standard base also felt safe. As safe as any track or disposable razors I have ever used. However for me, I felt that I had to add more pressure, and make more passes to get the close shave I desired. I did not take away any stars for this, because this was a result of my thick hair, and not the fault of the razor.
The next day I switched to the aggressive base, the one marked with an "A". This base is for more experienced shavers, and I was very pleased with results. The "A" base opens up the razors head, giving you more access to the blade. This also gives you a larger margin for error, but it lets this nice heavy razor do it's job' and do it well. The razor glided through my thick stubble under it's own weight, with hardly any extra pressure. A quick pass under running water, and well placed rinse holes on the bottom of the head, jets water across the blade. This pushes out all the hairs (even my thick stubble), and leaves the blade clean and ready for the next pass. This razor shaves great.
In the end. I gave the RazoRock MJ-90 five stars, for it's durability, quality materials, and the adjustable head that gives a great shave, no matter what your skill level. I could not fault this razor for anything, and it is my new daily driver.

title: Hint: Pour step 1 into a spray bottle
text:
This stuff is amazing. I have a tendency to get bored with my hair color, and every once in a while I will go against my better judgment for the sake of fashion and instead of waiting for my current color to fade, just strip it instead. You'd think I'd know by now that I stand gratification often comes with consequences and sacrifice. Well, after this last color swap, which I brilliantly felt compelled to do at about 3:15 in the morning two weeks ago, I immediately knew upon rinsing that I had just pushed my poor hair over the edge. I could see the damage when I fluffed my hands through and watched tiny little, broken pieces of hair fly off my head and sink to the floor like little blonde, fluffy tears.

I used the treatment last night. The first step is runny, like water. I poured a bit into my hand, and most of it went down the drain. Wasted product is wasted money, I want gonna play that game. I almost grabbed a color bowl and brush, but decided to try something else first, because I don’t have time for that. And by time I mean the patiennce. I carefully put the packet down and grabbed a funnel, an empty spray bottle and poured it in. I sprayed the product into my hair and combed it through. Much easier than wrestling a packet, a liquid product, and my hair all at once. In addition to just being easier, I felt this was the safer route to go considering the small bit of product I did get on my hands stung my cuticles and really stung a small scratch from my rude cat. Not sure which ingredient caused it, but I was surprised the packaging didn’t recommend wearing gloves.

I let my hair air dry last night and styled it with my flat iron this morning. The first difference I noticed was how much smoother and easier the plates glided over my hair. I can often feel the roughness of my most damaged areas because any amount of buildup product on my flat iron will "catch" the roughed up cuticle. No catching this morning. I am currently floofing my hair....No breakage. Like, zero. No sad blonde tears. I am not surrounded by a hair-nado. I am not adding to the graveyard of sad, sacrificed strands that I should probably sweep off my bathroom floor. HOW IS THAT EVEN POSSIBLE?!

I didn't expect the stuff to suck but I didn't expect it to be blessed by some ancient Goddess of damaged hair either.

Ordering the full size as soon as I submit this review.

I very much would recommend them for the price, the quality, shipping, and matching online description. While they all work, if I was ever repurchasing, I would only purchase the straight ones as the plastic part of the bow shaped clips will start further down toward opening. I found I was more likely to catch hairs in the bow shaped vs regular. All clips arrived well packaged and in great condition. Completely satisfied with my purchase.

title: Sublimate Very Nice! Decent Enough Quality To Sell To My Clients
text:
I wasn't sure if these would sublimate as no other reviews had mentioned anything other then HTV and the exact type of material is not listed. I decided to give it a try and they turned out very nice!

My method: Please note I am not an expert of any type-this is just what worked for me and my equipment-your heat press may be different-plan to have a few extras to allow you to develop a method for your own equipment. It took me 2 (using both sides) to get a design and method I was happy with.

Prepress for 10 seconds at 375 degrees. Be sure to ALWAYS have blow out paper under and over PLUS a sheet between the sides of the ribbon. If you do not put the sheet between the ribbon it will meld together at the edges. Do not reuse blow out paper as you will end up with ghosting on your next sash-LOL I know from experience!

I found it easiest to lay the sash out flat and tape it to the workspace after prepressing. I made sure to tape in the middle of each end so I'd have a guide to center my words. After taping design with heat tape-tape well DO NOT skimp as you may have to press 2 times due to the length of the sash and your design so tape good so it can move without ghosting images.

Then I pressed each section for 35 seconds at medium pressure and 375 degrees. I allowed to cool flat and then rolled the sashes to prevent creases from returning.

I am very pleased with them for the price. The material is a true white. the sewn end has one edge sewn to allow it to open and lay flat on the hip. While not the thickest material it is adequate for a sash. Packaging was exceptional! Each sash was packaged in it's own clear plastic sealed pouch THEN all those were packaged in a vacuumed sealed heavy pouch. There was no odors. Length was normal however as a plus size person (size 24) I could get it on but it rode up oddly on me and did not lay flattering. A suggestion for manufacturers is to make some longer plus size sashes as I'd surely buy them to offer my clients a range of inclusive sizes. I will order again without hesitation.

title: Worked well for curly hair.
text:
I own several straightening products but never owned a ceramic straightener comb brush. Some of the previous straightening products I have used have included a blow dryer and straightening iron. The blow dryer takes the most amount of time and the straightener reacquired me to constantly brush my hair before trying to straighten (I have really curly/wavy hair). I found that this Hairika Ceramic Straightener brush cut down my straightening time. I used it on dry hair with a bit of product. First I brushed my hair out and then took small sections and brushed the straightener comb through my hair. It was pretty simple and worked well. I found that it took away the frizzy look and still left a little volume (I don't normally aim for stick straight hair). I was pleased with the results. Also it was simple to turn on (just hold the on button for 3 seconds). The + and - are used to increase and decrease the temperature. The one downside I found was while using the brush I would accidentally press the + and - and change the temperature. The screen was easy to use to see what the temperature was. It would be beneficial to be able to have a hold button to lock a temperature. Overall I am pleased with this purchase and will be using it to cut my straightening time when I choose to straighten my hair. I also appreciated the nice packaging (see pictures). The brush came in a nice box with lid, some pins to help hold the hair that is not being straightened, a bag for storage and clear instructions. I will caution that using any straightening products too often can damage hair. I straighten hair only once a week and make sure to use appropriate hair products to reduce the heat damage. This brush would make a great gift.

* I received this brush at a discounted rate in exchange for my honest and unbiased feedback.

title: Effective if applied properly
text:
I tried this product about 6 years ago. I was impressed with the results, but I had to get the hang of applying it properly.

The rule is "less is more". Applied with a light touch to the problem lines, and allowed to dry completely, you have a chance to remove any flakiness where too much got on. Use a slightly dampened QTip. Once you have "tidied up", you can then apply your foundation.

Another tip is to do the various line areas at different times. This takes bit longer, but it allows you to keep you face still while each section dries. Particularly where those pesky around the lip lines are - you need to maintain that area as still as you can with a normal expression, until the serum has dried.

I found that whenever I used it, I got a lot of compliments. I found it would last 4 to 5 hours. I think it's a super product if you have a photo shoot, or a special date, or some occasion where you really want to look great.

title: Eyebrows looking good
text:
Just used it today (3 hours ago) on my eyebrows and before use I scrubbed my brows a good amount. Then afterwards I cleaned my brows with alcohol and let it dry before I applied a thick layer of dye. I left the dye on till it dried up. Reason leaving it on so long is so it would stain my surrounding eyebrows. I wasn’t sure how to clean it up so I just used a cotton swipe and water and let dry before the next application. The color for me was dark brown like I wanted. After the first application I retouched it up till all of the dye was gone. It didn’t really burn, but my pain tolerance for beauty is higher than most people’s from what I’ve learned over the years. I can’t tell you the longevity, but from what I’ve read it lasts a good 6 weeks give or take. I’m definitely going to use sun screen moisturizer and use gentle soap to make it last longer. I am also planning on not washing them for three or four days. I plan to wash my face with a rag and just go as much around them as I can. If I remember I’ll come back and update the longevity, but no promises.

Update from the first week after dying my eyebrows. The stain lasted on my skin for a good 6/7 day before I redid the dye on my skin. I didn’t washing my brows (only the surrounding area on my face) for 3 days before washing them so the stain would last longer. Overall I’m happy not to have to throw on my brows every morning. This is a temporary fix until I can get them microbladed. Saves me 10/15 mins every morning and I don’t feel as rushed. The second application took less time because I still had stain on them and could see where to put the dye. Overall I still like the product and how easy it is to use

title: Wow, super-heavy and solid!  This extra "arm" really works!
text:
I admit that I felt silly buying this...but I HATE to blow-dry my hair because I have very thick, wavy, and frizz-prone hair. So usually when I blow-dry it, I can't use the brush properly like a hairdresser would to really work the frizz out and dry it properly and it ends up look dry and poofy until the next day when it settles down. I typically let my hair just wet-dry and then style with some cream and a curling iron to smooth my ends. But when I saw this, I just had to try it despite having a small bathroom and thinking "do you really want that thing hanging on you wall?" The answer is..."Not really, but I really want a free hand to dry my hair."

So I bought it. Although I was still really unsure about the safety of sectioning this thing to my wall. I imagined it crashing down and smashing my toiletries, injuring the cat, or crashing onto someone's head. I wondered why I decided to buy it. But then I received it in the mail, opened it, and was really surprised at how incredibly heavy and solid this thing is. Everytime I buy a product that is supposed to "suction" and be strong....it isn't. Well, this one is REALLY strong.

I first tested it by suctioning it to the wall (not the mirror as shown in the ad) and left it there for about 2 days just to see if there was any sliding, slipping, or loosening. I pulled HARD on it various ways to try to get it to fall down. This thing is 100% solid and the suction is super-strong. If it stuck to my painted wall, this would never come off a mirror! Then after I inspected it a good bit, bent the arm around, tried out the bungee, and figured out which way the holder that the blow-dryer goes in is supposed to go....I placed my hair dryer in it. I had a hard time, at first getting my dryer to fit because I still had the holder upside down. If the large bolt is pressing against the back of your dryer, it's upside down and it won't seat properly and the bungee will be super-hard to clip (or not at all). So I was like "great this thing doesn't fit my dryer". But you have to twist and move it around to figure out which way yours fits and then it's all pretty much smooth sailing from there.

The "arm" that bends is also really hard to bend and very solid and thick. Merely bumping it (which I did several times), walking into it, or yanking your dryer around doesn't make this flop around. It requires two hands to bend and stays firmly in whatever position you place it for drying. Keep in mind this means that other than minor adjustments, if you need to totally change the dryer position while drying...you will need to take a second to move the arm and reposition it a bit, which is not a one-handed job. I really like that about this. When I finally tried using it after my shower (after days of leaving it hang up to ensure it doesn't fall, playing around with it, and letting my family get used to it being in their way because of our small bathroom) I was delighted that when I moved the dryer lower to blow straight at me....it stayed firmly in place, even after accidentally slapping it with my hairbrush and hands several times. I moved it into a "downward" blowing position about halfway through to get the back and was able to not only use a brush and my hands like a normal person, but I noted that I was able to get my hair dry in half the normal time (I assume because of extra brushes and hands). My hair even looked less frizzy and more like what it should look like after I go to the salon! My significant other came home and laughed when he saw me awkwardly using it and trying to position it right....but he thinks it's cool, too.

It made my life much easier and really DOES function like a permanent fixture if you want it to. I plan to leave mine up all of the time for ease of use rather than redoing the suction and placement each time. It's easy to just take the arm and push it up really high when you're done, take the dryer out of it, and it's out of the way of anyone walking through, opening cabinets, etc until next time you want to use it.

This is a pretty innovative product and I don't feel like I wasted money on it because it has made a loathsome part of my beauty routine easier...even if it did make my bathroom just slightly uglier :-)

In all seriousness, if you have space or really hate trying to use a brush and properly dry your hair, this is worth it. If I had more storage nearby, I'd probably take it down in between uses because it really is easy to suction and adjust once you understand what goes where and how it works. I had fun trying this out and using it on my hair and plan to keep on using it in the future. It's an odd device, for sure...but doesn't hesitate if you're worried it will be "cheap" or flimsy. This thing could be a deadly weapon, it's so heavy and clearly intended to stay in place. If that's what you need in a dryer holder, absolutely buy this. I don't regret my purchase and I doubt you will, either. I hope you found my review to contain useful information and I am happy to answer any questions you may have. Thanks for reading and happy styling!!

*It was really hard to take clear photos once hung because it's large and I choose to really snake it around, but hopefully you can get an idea of size and set up from them*

title: Pretty nice quality hair for the price.
text:
I've been using extensions since 2006, due to health issues causing extreme hair thinning. I used to get the fused extensions at the salon, 1500 dollars back in the day. They broke off from the weight of the extensions because my hair was so fine and thin. The fused glob of hair was just too much and so many fell out. I started buying the clip in hair, taking the clips off and using them as weft hair. I use salon pro white glue, much like eyelash glue but used for weft hair. It is a wonderful solution and I still alternate between tape in hair and the clip in wefts. I also buy closures and custom color, to make my own toppers. What a job! But, I'm happy with the results. I have more control over the color and style, and I feel 'normal'.

This hair is a medium to coarse texture, thick, and has a really nice body wave. The is soft and smooth and doesn't feel damaged. It will blend with fine hair. You can use a straightening iron, just be sure that you can control the temperature. Once you burn this hair, it will stink and it will be ruined. However, if you control the temperature and use care, the hair looks great straight and shiny. You can also curl the hair. I have used felted hot rollers, and those work really well. They are safer, and not as damaging, and the curls last so long.

These 16" extensions are very nice. Although the ad isn't quite accurate. The color is a darker caramel blond, and a reddish brown. This is not piano keys, but close. The wefts are not in the ombre style, they are bold and varied high lights. If you look at the ad images, the photos showing the people aren't shown with this product in their hair. The wefts laying on a surface showing the color differences between the offered colors is the most accurate. I've offered some images that show the color more accurately. You can custom color most of the wefted hair, but adding color is easier. Typically the hair has so much red in it that it is impossible to cover or remove, and the dye can be hard to remove. You can add a longer root to eliminate the chunky roots. My hair is so fine, the sewn edge can be obvious, so have a good match to my natural blonde ash tone roots helps. Any coloring will add to the damage and potentially shorten the life of the hair, but for me it makes me happier to have an exact match to what I want, and I am hard to match for color.

The weight of the hair is shown in a photo in ounces. In grams, we get a little over 104 grams, far less than the advertised 120grams, and I would complain about this and have, just not for this brand. That being said, the fullness and the weight is still good, and the wefts seem to feel average when compared to what I usually order. If you order the longer options, the hair will be thinner, as most hair is sold by weight. 120 would be better, of course. This weight is significantly lower than 120grams.

Shedding. Over the last 7 years or so, shedding has become a real problem. It never used to be this bad. There is a weft glue that is meant to slow or prevent shedding and I always use it. It makes the weft more stiff, but if you use the weft the way I use them, you need to do something to protect your weft hair. You can find it online. If you are using this hair for special occasions and clipping to thick strong hair and are simply making your hair more full, wild and glamorous, then you may not need to worry about shedding. I did finger comb this hair once out of the packaging, and there was significant shedding. Again, I say, this is a common issue now, and unique to this particular brand. I have no idea what changed but the wefts should not shed this much, but they all do this with most brands. I have to say that if the wefts didn't shed so much, they would last for a couple of years or longer. Also, keep in mind I use the wefts differently, so clipping, as intended, may offer longer life and far less shedding.

The length is 16" and the hair hangs nicely, with a gentle, natural taper. There is a very nice body wave. It's not a blunt edge finish, which is nice.

The clips are the same type that I see on most clip in kits. They are small, and hold nicely even on fine hair.

Over all, I think this is a great value and will require the extra effort to keep them looking great over a year or more. To keep human hair looking good and tangle free, I use the sleep and shine shampoo and conditioner. It keeps the hair fresher and mat free longer. There are a lot of youtube videos that can help you with application and care, and give you tips and tricks.

4 stars.

title: An addition to my top of the line fragrances. A MUST BUY.
text:
This perfume screams Sophistication, Youth and Trendy. I am so in love with the fragrance that I cannot possibly appreciate enough. The notes are as below:
Starting with carambola, with a bubbly and nonconformist personality, which immediately makes a contrast with the tradition of white lemon and with the nobility of rose wood. Then the distinctive character of cedar leaves rises up, to highlight the vibrant notes of tarragon and the manliness of clary sage. Precious understandings finally leave their stamp on an irresistible trail: sycamore wood, comforting amber and sparkling musk offering mysterious and skin-deep sensations.

That was what the Versace website explains about notes. Here's what I felt.
Top Note: Woody (possibly rose wood)
Mid Note: Tarragon (It's a spice, green and looks like grass)
Base Note: This is my fave part. Once the top and mid note subsides, you will not stop smelling yourself. Amber, musk and berries - So attracting still not over-powering.

I have to agree it does not last too long. For me, it did 4 hours in fall. It could be less in summer. But it totally depends on the kind of skin you have. I am Asian and have brown skin. Caucasian will hold this for longer (somehow this seems to be the case). But also depends on what kind of environment you work on. But, that's not a deal breaker.

I would highly recommend this to college students, young people who work in office environments, perfect for a date or a dinner with someone special. Goodluck.

The fastening clasp is ultra-cheap and I found this to be the most unlikable aspect of this product. The clasps take considerable time to fiddle around with and fasten. It would have been a much better idea to offer velcro or button straps.

title: Read before you buy...
text:
-I’ve used lots of their products…and I always got compliments, but the final straw was their deplorable customer service. I figure if this is how I’m treated, then they most-assuredly treat all the other paying customers in the same exact manner. They wanted my opinion (not kidding – they really asked) so not only did I respond honestly, but I asked a question. Asked repeatedly. Rather than professionally answer my question, effectively teaching one customer at a time - waiting and waiting and waiting and waiting, continuing to ask. Ha, they tried to give me free products, and I refused them. I Just. Wanted. An. Answer - and not to be ‘bought off’, thinking that they were hiding behind emails, with no individual names, but ‘Team’ this and Team that. This may be a plausible solution for some, but not me. What an unequivocally repulsive way to treat a faithful and paying customer.

-I’m not sure what changed, but Lisa Crary (CEO and owner) used to care. Used to have great staff. Used to respond to questions. But certainly not now. The products are acceptable enough, but expensive, purchasing from retailers (I grew sick of the ridiculous price mark-up) as well as directly from Sanitas. Even directly from the manufacturer, still pricy, but shipping was too inconsistent.

-I’ve used FIVE cleansers (Glycolic Citrus, Enzyme Foaming, Milk & Honey, Lemon Crème Scrub, Lemon Crème Cleanser) seven types of treatment products (Brightening Peel Pads, Glyco Solution, PeptiDerm Eye, Essential Eye Essence, Hyaluronic Concentrate and the Serum, AHA kit, Retinol Peeling Crème, RejuvenA) three moisturizers (Topical C, Antioxident moisturizer, Vitamin C moisturizer) and three types of masks (Cranberry Lactic, Papaya Pineapple, Pumpkin Enzyme). Also, a few of the body products (Redensifying Lip Complex, Hydrating Sugar scrub, Brightening Hand cream, Foot Repair) and serums (Vita Rich, Vita C) just to try. The body stuff I positively hated, but I tried them none-the-less, since I *was a loyal customer. That’s just from memory, and there’s likely more. Oh, and their sunscreen. No one could tell me when it would be available again. The Moisture Mist too.

-Pppfffttt, the money I have spent with that line of skin care. The super weird expiration code nearly drove me nuts, but I finally deciphered it with lots of research and phone calls over time. Some of the numbers don’t mean anything, but the letters are the most crucial – indicating the year produced.
-To refrain from giving Sanitas any more of my money, I purchased online from that *huge retailer that starts with an a, that always ships so quickly – and got a few expired products. Good thing the return policy is incredibly stellar, however my time was still wasted. Well, I admit that’s on me.

-The packaging is nothing short of a nightmare, trying to get all the product out of the container being impossible, equaling a waste of money. Some of these products are in a pump style, in which case not all of the pumps even function. Of course, I called… they just didn’t care. I wish I’d save pictures, but anger forced me to toss it.

-Get this! Some of the spas, dermatologists, and estheticians that carry the Sanitas line will *sell to customers the free products given to them by the manufacturer to further promote their line. The audacity of such is so incredibly offensive, and Sanitas should have removed their products from those retailers – but they didn’t do anything of the kind, because they didn’t care. I can easily say I’m over them, and others should be very cautious.

-*Maybe what I have read on ‘job sites’ (where employees give their personal opinions about their employers, working conditions, work to life balance, management, wages, etc.) is unquestionably true, but it definitely can’t be good for the quality of products. *Maybe that’s the reason for the change. Whatever is the reason, I’ll never *ever use that skincare line again…

…and instead switched to a skin care line from the Far East. Don’t waste your time and money. Know this - there’s better products out there.

text:
I was excited to see this product because it seemed like a really cool idea. An all-in-one mechanical device that could be used a body scrubber for various uses. All the different attachment and the explanations of different power levels looked promising.

However, in reality this was not a great realization of that promise.

First the product itself isn't of the greatest quality. It has a 'cheap' feel about it.

Second, while it looks fine ergonomically and with tidy packaging, none of the attachments have labels for what they are used for right on the attachment. All the labelling is on the accompanying foldout. That would require you to always keep the paper fold-out with the appliance. That just isn;t realistic over time.

Third, I have to agree with a lot of the other reviews that the typeface on the instructions is too small.

Fourth, they promise different power levels, but honestly there does not seem to be appreciable difference in the settings. The setting is adequate for the face scrubber (not powerful enough to flay off skin) but nothing near to what you'd need for feet or nails.

In the end this is just not a really go execution of what should have been a good product,.

title: Great starter lamp for people getting into gel polish.
text:
Why all the hate and bad reviews? This lamp is the price of a Chipotle burrito (for context). This is basically the same lamp that comes with the Madam Glam Gel Kit (which costs $35 if you buy it separately on Madam Glam, this one just doesn't have the cute designs on it).

I wanted to make sure I liked the gel polish system but I didn't want to spend a ton of money on a lamp until I knew I liked the gel system. This is nothing fancy: turn it on, it lights up for 60 seconds then turns off (30 seconds will be nice but that's what your phone timer is for). USB powered so the short cord is a non-issue for me (always close to a computer and you can use your portable cell phone battery charger to power this). It's small, but I have small hands so no big deal. You can't get your whole hand in there, but it do both my thumbs last. The polish cures in 30-60 seconds (depends on what your polish says), works as advertised.

The short cord and the small sized are its weak points, but the price makes up for all that and I can live with the flaws. Since this is so portable, this is great for mani/pedi parties with your girl/guy friends, or use as a back-up lamp.

title: Afordable and easy way to stay tan all year long
text:
I have been using this product for about two months and honestly like it more than the other self tanner I was using prior that was double the price.

First off the smell is devine. Especially compared to previous self tanners I've used. Does not have a strong fake tan smell, and I also don't notice the smell lingering on my skin for extended periods of time.

The color of this product is great and never looks orange or gives me that too dark/red fake tan look I've experienced with other products. The color probably lasts me 4 days, depending on how often I wash my body, workout, and shave. As with all self-tanning products I don't find the "extreme" color to be very dark. I typically apply two coats to get my desired color, which is roughly 2-3 shades darker.

VERYY easy to apply. I use this with the [[ Premium Tanning Applicator Mitt Double-Sided Soft Microfiber Glove for Streak-Free Application]] and don't typically have any problems with streaking. I have noticed I can get streaky on my legs if I apply the product too quickly and don't pay close enough attention, but I don't know any self tanner that wouldn't be an issue with.

My only issue with this product is that I've noticed is coming off on my clothes the day I use it. Even if I use it in the morning and don't wear tight-fitting or light colored clothes until over 8 hours later it will still come off on them. I've noticed it the most on my light wash jean shorts. Fortunately, the color comes off in the wash, but be prepared to plan a head if you want to use this prior to wearing light colored shorts.

Other than that AMAZING product. Definitely worth the price in my opinion.

title: Sensitive Girl Approved. Not perfect but overall okay!
text:
Excellent set of brushes with pretty good quality.
#1 rule when buying Bella and bear products: get on their email list for discount codes! I paid a little more than half of the current price for this set. Even at full price it's a good value (price per brush) but due to a few quirks I recommend not paying full price.
I'm a makeup junkie and own many brushes ranging from handmade very expensive Japanese brushes to easily accessible drug-store brand sets. I prefer synthetic brushes due to allergies and skin sensitives and I believe most of these are synthetic or blends.
The set arrived from Amazon in a very nice giftable thick sturdy box. I'm actually using the box and lid as liners in one of my makeup drawers.
I have broken down this review into two sections brushes and the case.
Brushes:
Handles are semi-matte black and the ferules are silver metal and appear to be crimped on which is very nice. The handles/ferules remind me of IT Cosmetics brushes. They are very well made, heavier constructed, and feature the company and brush name stamped on them.
Brush quality is good over all. Except for one of the brushes, they are all very soft and the density is appropriate for the applications.
Foundation, stippling, large shadow, and smudge shadow brushes are not evenly cut. There is noticeable uneven brush hairs with all 4 of these. The application with these particular brushes is okay but it's not as smooth as it would be with perfectly cut brushes.
The flat yellow brush is made of a taklon or nylon type material. It's large, thick, flat, and useless. It doesn't work with any kind of makeup in any kind of application because as soon as it touches skin, it splays, or splits. It's not flexible or functional. I have put it aside for craft applications, as it might work to pat on glue or something like that.
MY favorite brushes are the white shadow blending blushes, they work very well for blending shadow lines.
Runners up are the larger powder brushes for setting powder and bronzer/blush applications.
Even with the damage to the portfolio, some brushes are not cut properly, and one is useless, this is still an excellent value.
3-3.5 stars because the handle quality is really 4 star quality and most of the brushes are 4-5 star quality but there are some misses here too.
No issues with irritations or sensitivity which is very important to me.

Portfolio:
My large heavy portfolio arrived in fair condition. The zipper, doesn't work properly, and after opening I can't easily zip it again it. This is not a big deal for me because I will not be regularly using my brushes in this case. There was a pamphlet in the bottom of the box with brush descriptions and it made a permanent indentation in the case, which would be unfortunate if I was going to use the case for storage.
The larger brushes all came with mesh brush guards, the smaller brushes were wrapped in plastic.

title: INSTANT MERMAID HAIR- YOU WON’T REGRET THIS PURCHASE
text:
Y’all- I am OBSESSED. My hair is thin and simply doesn’t grow and in my 32 years of existence- I have never had hair extensions. Like WHAT have I been doing with my life?! This purchase was a game changer. In minutes, I had the hair I have always wanted but never been able to have. I used one pack of 16 inch and one pack of 18 inch in the Ash Blonde color. I even have some left over for touch ups if needed. My friend who is a hair stylist put them in for me- but I am hell bent on learning how to put them in myself. The extensions look and feel perfect. I get compliments all the time and I love every opportunity to tell people how great this product is. Unless someone knew me before- they didn’t even know it was not my real hair. And even then a few of my co-workers said- “your hair grew!” And I immediately spilled the beans.
It does take some getting used to when sleeping in them. It kind of feels itchy when I sleep- I never have gotten used to it. BUT it’s so worth it! I braid it to sleep and bought satin pillow cases to ease the friction. Going from barely any hair to what I call “mermaid hair” was an adjustment when it came to washing, drying, and styling. But again- it is absolutely worth it. I instantly felt like a better version of my self. Glamorous. Confident.
As I’m writing this- my extensions are right at the three week mark and have started to slip and fall out. I immediately knew I had to buy more. So I thought I would stop and write this review because I know, if you are like me, you are obsessively reading reviews on a product like this before you take the leap. DO IT! Trust me, you won’t regret this purchase.

title: You get what you pay for
text:
Buyer beware!
Pros:
Packaging was great. Nothing spilled out or burst open. Colors are gorgeous.

Shipping was ok. I got a message basically saying shipping was delayed due to my error of not providing the right address, yet I ordered 4 items the same day and provided the same shipping address. They supposedly corrected the error and got it shipped to me in less than a week.

Now, let's talk about the cons:
I can't say this product is a true polygel. When using the slip solution or isopropyl alcohol, the solution dissipated and the brush dried out within seconds. Once I was able to start smoothing the product out, I got one good pat before the product became extremely sticky and unmanageable due to the brush drying out. It definitely took some finesse to get it to work. Also, do not use the dual forms as the product is not thick enough to hold it's own without moving under the light. If you have paper forms or nail tips, you will have much better luck with this product. I will say it definitely took me way too long to do one set but filing the product was great and so easy.

After trial and error, if you want to take the time to make it thicker, put some on a smooth flat surface and add clear acrylic. Make sure to use a metal spatula to mix the 2 products if you so choose to. Also, THIS PRODUCT IS VERY STICKY. If you are not careful, you will get this product everywhere.

I would give more stars if the polygel was a thicker constancy and the brush didn't dry out seconds after dipping into the slip solution or isopropyl alcohol.

I will give this kit a try again when it's time for me to change my set, but I'm not sure I will purchase this kit again.

title: Works great, added free bonuses but they don't sell the file refills
text:
Before you buy this...
Make sure you can buy replacement files for it. I cannot find that this company sells them. I see that Amope does sell them and although I do not know if they would fit this file, I have a strong feeling they would fit. Many times beauty gadget dupes are almost exact replicas in my experience so other brands of replacement items do normally fit (i.e. clarisonic off brand brushes, amope off brand file rollers, etc). I checked the Amope refills & at the time of writing this, they sell for about $10 for all 3. I normally won't comment on price but I find that to be ridiculously high considering it is just a piece of plastic with basically a sticker on it with a rough or smooth edge. Regular emery boards are so cheap so I am surprised the refills would go for that much. Now that is for the name brand of Amope. If dupe companies make them, they should be cheaper.

Pros...
* Includes AA battery, 3 heads (file, buff, shine), soft top separators, nail clippers & bag to keep it all in.
* Works good.

Cons...
* I think this company not selling the file refills is a HUGE NEGATIVE. At the time of writing this, I searched the internet and cannot find anywhere that they sell them.

I read some reviews about how some people didn't feel it was powerful enough. I felt the same thing when I used it but really it is powerful enough for just filing your nails. You wouldn't want anything too rough for that.

This vs Amope...
I do not own the original Amope so I cannot compare the two directly. I looked closely at the photos and they look identical to me. This brand you do get the added extras of the clippers, toe separators and bag. With the Amope brand, you are able to purchase the nail file refills. With this brand, you are not able to purchase the nail file refills at the time of writing this. It is likely the amope refills would fit this. My advice is if you are wanting an electronic nail file like this, go with the Amope version because you know you can buy refills & they will fit. I normally will not comment on price but I will say that I am taken aback that this Amope dupe is priced as high as it is. Even though this brand is at a lower cost and you get the added bonuses, I am still a little surprised that there is not more of a price drop to remain competitive since they do not have the name brand recognition.

I like to write product reviews & because I rely heavily on what other people write when I am buying items, I try to write reviews that highlight the good and the bad. I rate things from as low as 1 star up to 5 stars. I base my judgment on my experience with a product and not on the price, since the price value of an item is ultimately up to the buyer (what is a good deal for one person might seem expensive to another). That being said, I did receive this item at a discount in exchange for my honest, unbiased opinion.

text:
I got an electric Epilator awhile ago that I like a lot. It keeps you hair free for long periods of time and I've noticed the hair comes back thinner each time. I've used my electric Epilator everywhere but my eyebrows, for fear I might not have anyone I'm done. I saw this product and thought I'd give it a try to get the stray hairs and to do my eyebrows (hate wasting a Saturday morning to wax)

The directions on the back of the box are a bit vague. I was able to figure out how to maneuver the stainless steel coil and here's what I found.

I want to note at first glance I thought The free eyebrow raiser enclosed was an eyebrow brush to separate the hair. Thank God I have somewhat bushy eyebrows or they be gone 'd be gone! Now that I know how to use this razor I do really like it, I didn't want to knock off the star for my stupidity, it clearly states when I bought it it comes with an eyebrow razor. Just in case there is another woman tired coming home from work tired that wants to shape their eyebrows while cooking dinner, doing laundry and taking care of the kids .....there is a heads up '

I found by trial and error if you want to get the hairs between your eyebrows above your nose hold this horizontally and go side to side.

If you want to shape your eyebrow you can actually curve this below or above and gently move the coil around to get rid of strays.

If you have a single strand let's say on your chin you want to get I found that moving this down will grab that hair.

I was surprised at how much hair I took off with this thing

This does not hurt as much as the electric epilator does, I don't think the electric hurts that much either. When it gets to hear it hurts a little more than a wax and a lot less than a tattoo.

Once you get used to maneuvering this around it works great. It took me a couple days using this to be able to pinpoint to hear and I can now get it in about 20 seconds. It also does remove like here but it would take a long time to do.

This definitely works your wrist some, if you like the results I would say get an electric epilator and use this for your eyebrows and touchups. I have a little bit of carpal Tunnel, after about 15 minutes of twisting in moving this around it does get to my wrist a little bit, that being said I don't think this is meant for large area hair removal.

Hopefully my tips will save you some of the time I've spent experimenting with this. It's a neat little tool that I will definitely use. This may sound gross but I was actually able to even get a nose hair (if someone else is nervous to try it, I did, survived and like the results) lol

I did receive this product at a discount for my honest review. I thoroughly use any product before giving a review whether I get it for free at a discount or pay full price

title: Steep learning curve
text:
I tried these with several other bridesmaids to see if they might make our hair easier on the morning of the wedding. I'm glad we did it ahead of time, because they would have been a wedding morning disaster.
First of all, the pictures show these straightened to make waves and the package of ones I received cannot be convinced to hold that shape. This wouldn't be a big deal, except they are difficult to put on as spirals. You have to thread the hook through first, but the tube is much longer than the hook. If I'd been capable of sprouting a third hand, putting these on would have been the moment it happened. And that's only the first hurdle.
It takes some extra work to get a good curl out of these. Make sure your hair is damp when they go on or it won't hold the curl (after a lot of success in my life using regular foam curlers on dry hair, this was the most disappointing thing). Keep a spray bottle handy, because they take long enough to put on that your hair will dry before you get done, at least the first couple of times. Make sure the hair isn't tangled or twisted or it won't curl properly. Don't snag your hair section with the hook or you'll find out.
A good curl cream is a must because these don't make a curl that holds as well as-- pick a standard type of curler. Make sure you have a God hair spray to set them with, too. If you don't have a quality product or three in your hair to force the curl to hold, they will fall within a few hours and then you've got whatever your hair texture is with too much brushing and a few weird bends.
Also, these pull your hair at the root pretty hard if you try to sleep on them loose, so make sure you have a good cap/bonnet/kerchief/babushka (whatever hair covering you use) to keep them arranged into something fairly comfortable.

title: NOT YOUR "OLD DUTCH" NORELCO
text:
I've used Norelcos for over 30 years. This latest version comes from China, with questionable implications as to quality and conditions of manufacture.
Extremely light and quiet, it feels more like a woman's shaver. Therefore, it may not be suitable for men with heavy beards who are not accustomed to electric razors.
Older Norelcos were solid, well made and came with solid cases; this model has no case at all, making careful handling essential. Considering this shaver's apparent fragility, if you ever drop it you'll need a new one. Norelco switches have always been erratic, so leave the switch turned on and unplug the shaver to turn it off.
For the moment it does a good enough job, even without a closeness control. Its best feature is a full-sized trimmer, which works well.
If today's lower quality standards for small appliances don't bother you, you may find this shaver perfectly acceptable but it is not built to last as long as its predecessors.
UPDATE (11/07) - Well, this fragile shaver is still going strong - of course, I've managed not to drop it! No complaints, and the price has gone down a third since I bought it. Definitely the best shaver one can get at this price.
UPDATE (1/13) - Unfortunately I left the original shaver behind at an hotel and sorely missed it until I found a new, unused one on the internet. Norelco has apparently discontinued this model along with all their corded-only shavers, so if you can find one as I did, you're lucky!

text:
[[VIDEOID:d1630bd31368ccda2fe184c165d14852]] I have somewhat fair-toned skin and need to really protect it due to the use of retinols and various skin care acids that make it more susceptible to burning and photoaging. Unfortunately, my skin is also very breakout-prone, especially with masks, such that products that didn't break me out before do now.

This product is a wonderful. It's a small size like most Asian sunscreens, however all you need to do is draw one line of it down your index finger and that's enough to cover your whole face and the tops of your ears. You shake it up, and it's very liquidy, but it's very spreadable.

If you're familiar with MAC Strobe Cream, this leaves a bit of a radiance, which might be a parent on very dark skin tones, but it adds a nice illuminance and counteracts sallow tones found in lighter skins. It doesn't add high shine, just a bit which is totally manageable whether or not you add makeup on top. In fact, my skin can look quite matte after I'm done with my makeup, just a bit dewy if I leave it untouched.

I'm so happy to report there are no breakout issues with this. I have even falling asleep in this without washing my face first, and woke up without breakout issues. Love love love it. If you have drier skin, try the formula in the tube. I didn't find this drying, but the tube version is definitely heavier in texture and a bit more moisturizing.

title: Great alternative to brow gels, pencils, and powders.
text: I've been using the dark brown tint in this brand for years and have never had a problem.  My hair color is lighter than 'dark brown' but darker brows look nicer on most people because it gives more definition to the face.  The only thing you want to be careful with is making sure you give yourself enough time after application to get it off the skin.  Some people use a cream or Vasoline around the brow, so it doesn't tint the skin.  I apply it at night, remove it with eye makeup remover (oily liquid on a cotton round), and then the next morning wash my face. It comes off the skin without issue for me and the skin around my brow isn't raw from scrubbing.  Whatever you do, if it's your first time using a brow tint,  don't apply it right before an event, date, or work.  Give yourself time to learn how to use the product, i.e. not end up with brows too dark or with tinted skin you are panic scrubbing to get off.  Sometimes, when I want a more dramatic look or the color is fading, I will still manually define my brows, but for my everyday look, the brow tint is enough.

title: Right now it is tied as my favorite retinol product. It beat ROC products for me.
text:
I received a complimentary bottle of this serum to review on my blog. I really love it. I had finished my old retinol serum, which I liked and was ready to purchase another bottle until I was asked to review this serum on my blog. I like that this product is light. It has the same lightness as OZ Natural's hyaluronic serum. A little goes a long way. Two pumps of the serum is the most you will need. The serum absorbs quickly into the skin. Allow a full minute to go by before you apply another product over it. That initial absorption you see is just ti drying faster on the top layer of skin. It takes about a minute for serums to absorb deeper into the skin. Allowing this time prevent the pilling when you a moisturizer too soon.

Give this product about four weeks to see any real results. Retinol products take months of use to see any impact on deeper issue like lines and wrinkles. Initially you will feel a surface difference where skin my feel smoother or even softer. A couple of weeks later you may see some lighter scars fading. If you are battle crow feet apply a little of this serum at the corners of your eyes (don't get the product in eyes though) before you apply your eye cream. The two working together will give you better results.

You do NOT want this brand of dye if you make drastic changes to your color frequently [if you want to go from pink to green, for example] because it is extremely difficult to strip and you will damage your hair trying to remove it. This brand is also difficult to dye over, when I tried red for a month it had a VERY pink undertone even after fading and bleaching, other people - specifically Atomic Pink users report difficulty getting even black to go over their color without it having a purple undertone.

That being said, if you actually WANT vibrantly colored hair and don't want to recolor every two weeks this is the brand for you. I have run with atomic pink for 3+ years and just recently decided to fade in preparation for another color, and now, nearly six months after my last re-dye it's just barely starting to get patchy in places and fade at the tips. text:
Love these. I used the glue. After a few trial and error rounds of doing glue-on nails, I learned to choose the nail that is the size smaller than the size you think is right (it spreads flat after it’s glued and then this also saves your cuticles). Also use a very small amount of glue. Even if you think it’s too little, it’s probably too much. It’s much easier to glue a nail back on than to deal with dried glue all over your cuticles and between your nail and finger skin. Also rubbing alcohol takes the excess glue off if you do have issues.

Also! Big tip - start with your pinky nails first. Do both pinkies, both rings, both middles, etc. Your thumbs are very useful in the application process so it’s best to do them last.

title: Not sure what all the fuss is about...
text:
I will be the first to admit I hate taking baths; it bores me out of my skull. But because I have chronic pain, I've occasionally taken Epsom salt baths or bubble baths with a fantastic product called Muscle Soak. I found the salts were no longer really helping, so I thought I'd try these magnesium flakes. I take magnesium daily but a boost through the muscles that ache sounds great.

I was floored at how quickly and completely they dissolved. The tub wasn't done filling and they were fully absorbed into the water. With salts, I have to get in and stir repeatedly to get the crystals to dissolve, often in water that's hotter than comfortable. So that was promising.

I got in the tub and lay back, focused on the flower print on the wall....and was ready to get out in 15 minutes, but I wanted to give it the full 30. I wasn't magically relaxed or calmed by the bath as other reviewers are claiming. (You literally can't tell the flakes are there, as the water isn't salty like it is with Epsom salts.) I wasn't whisked away to a lush garden in my mind. I was just lying in a bathtub with pleasantly hot/warm water. While I was in the water and for up to an hour after I got out and showered, I felt a limited, temporary reduction in the tightness in my upper back. I put on a compression shirt to help things along but had 9/10 pain. When I can next score some Muscle Soak, I'll be going back to that. The bubbles are at least something to play with! And it is more effective on achy muscles.

This is not a magic cure for stress or pain. I'll use it to soak my feet when they ache, but don't expect miracles. If Epsom salts don't make a big difference, these flakes probably won't either.

title: Who has good-looking brows?.. I do :)
text:
I will never go back to the salon to color my eyebrows again. This is exactly the same stuff the professionals use. The first time I did it I wasn't able to remove the product completely from my brows. I tried to make a home concoction to remove the dye. Boy, was that the worst thing to do. I only irritated my skin more by doing that. It looked funny for about 3 days and then I was beautiful again lol

The second time I did it I had the best experience. I used Dy-Zoff Hair Color Stain Remover Pads also from Amazon. I swear by these things. Two wipes and all the excess dye was removed.

Now as far as the dye goes which is what I want to focus on...you don't need to use a whole capsule. I poured about half of one and then closed it off for next time. That was enough for both my brows. The longer you leave the dye on the darker they get.

I'm blonde and I have really light brows. you can see about half of the brow without any added color. I like a darker brow look because I have darker roots and I think it really makes my blue eyes pop. I'll leave it on for about 4 minutes and then I'll do touchups after if I see areas should be a little darker. I recommend starting with one eyebrow at a time because it takes a while to apply the color. Don't be shy. Apply it heavy over the brow. you need to make sure all the hair is colored. My biggest mistake is I didn't bring the dye all the way to the ends so I had stray hairs that were left blonde. Not the biggest deal, but it bothered me a bit.

When you do this always start with less time then they say, just to be safe. It's always better to go lighter. You can always add color, but not take away. Have some dye remover (like the one I recommended) on hand, and do one brow at a time. The only reason why this gets 4 stars instead of 5 is because I experiences slight irritation after.

Good luck!

P.s. If I remember next time I do my brows I'll take a pic so you can see exactly what I mean.

title: Took off black nail polish in one wipe!
text:
This is a huge bottle of Mountain Falls nail polish remover (16oz). At $5.99, I don’t find that unreasonable as this bottle will likely last me years. Though I only polish my toenails and not my fingernails so I don’t use as much as those who regularly polish their fingernails along with their toenails.

The scent isn’t overwhelming and that’s a plus. None of them are going to smell good—wouldn’t that be nice, to have a nail polish remover that smelled spiced or like your favorite body lotion or body spray!

What surprised me the most is how effectively it removed some black nail polish I had on my toes that I’d done for Halloween. I’d done my fingers too and the generic polish I had took a few more swipes and wipes than this Mountain Falls. The MFalls took it off in one wipe! So, it’ll be replacing the other generic I had - bye-bye!

What would also be really cool along with nail polish that smelled good is if the top of the applicators were smaller so you could squeeze out or pour out a little less—I often drench my tissue or cotton ball.

All in all, this is a good generic/Amazon brand product. I’d recommend it if you use a lot of polish remover. A big 16 ounces will last a good while. For me, this bottle is a little too large, but it’ll sure last me a long long time.

title: Great product with a lot of features
text:
The hair shaving kit comes in a nicely packaged box, with 8 pieces: the shaver itself, 3 different shaving guides that offer 3 mm, 6 mm, 9 mm and 12 mm hair length, a small brush to clean the blades, a power cord, a plastic hood to put around the child and to keep hair out and lastly a powder pad to dust off hair from the face. The plastic hood and the powder pad are nice touches and they come in very handy in keeping the hair off my kid’s body. I am sure little hair bits don’t feel too good directly in contact with the skin. However, my favorite parts of the products are the shaving guides: they can be snapped on to the shaver and protect the scalp from getting ever pinched by the blades. And based on the relatively length of the guide teeth, you can adjust the hair length you want to cut to. I find that very convenient to keep the hair length consistent throughout the head (which is really not easy if your kid happens to squirm around and try to get away from the hair cut). The blades are quite easy to clean with the help of the brush and the cover of the blades can even be snapped off by a light push so you can clean the inside of the blade chamber. My only issue with the product is the manual: it seems to me that the manual I get is for a different product, since many accessories discussed in the manual are not included in this particular package. However, it did not affect my use so I am not bothered by it.
Overall I think this is a great product for some simple hair cut at home for my kid. I would recommend it to anyone who’s looking for something simple to use without breaking a bank. I received this product at a discounted price for my honest and unbiased review.
