title: Ingredients don't match up
text:
As someone who suffers from chronic insomnia (and the lovely, inescapable dark raccoon circle eyes that come with it), I was pretty excited to try this. I’ve only used it for one day, and the gel is pleasant enough to use, but what I want to bring up is the disparity between the ingredients that are advertised for Nuju Revitalizing Eye Gel, and the actual ingredients. I’ll break this down the best I can.

Right off the bat I noticed that this product claims to be paraben free, but has a number of contradicting Ingredients: Ethylparaben, Butylparaben, Propylparaben, Isobutylparaben. This could be a major problem for anyone with allergies or sensitivities. This product also claims to have time released retinol, which is notably missing from the ingredient list. I’ve listed almost every ingredient in this eye cream, and its function, below. Personally I think this will be useful for moisturizing, and perhaps a temporary rejuvenated look, but it doesn’t seem to pack enough punch to tackle my under eye circles. Because of the disparity between advertised ingredients and the actual, I’m giving this two stars. Keep in mind I don’t claim to be a scientist. Just going off of easily available information.

Herbal Ingredients:
Cucumis Sativus (Cucumber) Extract (Skin Conditioner); Chamomilla Recutita (Matricaria) extract (thought to increase blood flow and aid in “congestion” under the skin); Camellia Sinesis Leaf Extract (Green Tea extract. Generally only high concentrations have substantial effects on skin, but thought to help reduce swelling and inflammation among other things)

Of Interest:
Ceramide 3 (part of naturally occurring skin structure, it helps retain moisture, regulates cellular barrier repair); Sphingolipids (naturally occurring in the body, it functions as protection for cells against environmental factors); Hesperidin Methyl Chalcone (naturally occurring bioflavinoid, often used for under eye circle treatments, helps combat free radical damage and inflammation); Dipeptide-2 (effective skin conditioner, believed to help improve lymphatic circulation and so often found in under eye cream to reduce dark circles); Palymitoyl Tetrapeptide-7 (helps reduce inflammation. Increases collagen production when paired with Palmitoyl-Oligopeptide, which is not listed as an ingredient for this product); Camellia Sinesis Leaf Extract (Green Tea extract. Generally only high concentrations have substantial effects on skin, but thought to help reduce swelling and inflammation among other things)

Everything else:
Cetearyl Ethylhexanoate (emollient and skin conditioner); Propylene Glycol (aids with shelf stability); Carbomer (thickener/controls gel consistency); Polysorbate 20 (emulsifier/solubilizer); Triethanolamine ( ph adjuster *a “moderate concern” level ingredient for potential toxicity*); Hydroxypropyl Methycellulose (used for sustained release of ingredients); Ethylhexyl (lubricant/makes skin look soft and smooth); Cocoate (derived from coconut oil, skin conditioner); Steareth-20 (surfactant and emulsifier, often found in eye cream); Butylene Glycol (solvent and used to make creams more easily spreadable); Phenoxyethanol (Chemical preservative); Titanium Dioxide CI 77891 (white pigment and sunscreen); Cyclomethicone, Dimethiconol, Phenyl Trimethicone (liquid silicone, creates a temporary skin plumpness)

I normally wear color street. I wanted to find something similar with a different variety to chose from so I tried these out. This is a comparison of the two.
This nail sticker pack has 8 sheets in it for 8 uses and color street has 2 sheets meant for one use, but my nails are short so I can get two. The price point is the same but the stickers have 6 more sets for me.
Color street is pretty easy to put on but these seemed to be slightly easier.

a) I boil water, then place the picks in them for 10+ minutes.
b) Then, I lay them on a clean plate to cool.
c) Once the picks have cooled enough for me to handle, I choose a pick to take care of my teeth/gums.

I use the dental pick with the sharp hook at the end to remove stubborn food debris stuck between my teeth that my toothpick cannot remove.
I use the dental pick with an end that reminds me of a chisel to pick away at the plaque/tartar.

The dental mirror gives me a good view of the inside of my mouth, so I know what parts need to be worked on.
I breathed on the mirror, and it did not fog up. The light is bright.
note: the product description page makes no mention of what to do if the light doesn't work. There was no user guide included with this kit when I opened the package containing these picks and mirror.

Overall, I find this oral care kit to be useful in helping me take care of my gums and teeth at home in between the times I see my dentist.

title: The best.
text:
After having used this product for a month, I find myself hooked. As YMMV when taking someone's word on shave gear, I thought I might provide some background about me: I have gentle to oily skin and stiff, tough neck hairs. I used to think I had sensitive skin until I married someone with actual sensitive skin. But the combination of the tough hairs and the gentleness of my skin leads to irritation on the neck when I am not careful. I learned to shave with a gillette adjustable years ago(which I still use), but out of "convenience" (really, a lack of good shaving products and knowhow) I stopped using it for cartridge systems in my early twenties. Since I started shaving right, some time ago, I got an EJ-89 which I use when I'm feeling raw, and an old type open comb gillette (which, for the moment at least, I favor for its closeness- I use personna lab blue blades or sharper in it). I've tried a number of different soaps and a few creams, most of which are good. Mitchell's is excellent. It has a simple, clean smell like fresh linen and is the most thoroughly hydrating shaving product I have ever used. It lathers up easily- I've used my beat up old drugstore boar brush which is now probly 15 years old and a silvertip badger brush.. In either case, the lather whips up in a minute or less with no complications. I'm not one of these people that soaks the puck either, I just heat it up in its dish, in a basin of hot water as I soak my brush and it is good to go. I've heard that water hardness and temp can make a difference with this stuff, but as I have decidedly soft water here in the city, I can't really comment on that. But once you get the lather right, with enough water, it is eaaasy on the face. Amazing even.. I dreamt wetshaving was like this as a teenager..
One might be put off by the price which may seem hefty for a newcomer to the wetshaving game, eager to start saving money (previously lost on walking the cartridge treadmill) and reticent to buy apparently expensive luxury shaving soaps, but aside from being a quality product, It lasts for a quite a while. I was really going to wait until I had exhausted mine to write this review but it's been a month, and the puck looks basically the same size! Growing up on Williams soap and favoring Van der Hagen as a drugstore standby these days, I notice one soap generally lasts me a month (some less than that), but aside from the simply larger size of Mitchells (4.4 oz to 2.5 oz for standard mug size soaps), you just get more bang for your buck. I'm guessing this one will last me three months or more.. So at that rate, the price basically factors out altogether.
To sum up, if you have gentle or easily irritated skin and aren't looking for a heavily scented product, this is the grail of soaps for you. title: I had to try it for myself.
text:
After reading all of the bad reviews on this new Norelco shaver, I swore I was not going to buy this unit.

Well, a few months ago I realized my local stores didn't stock my HQ5 Norelco replacement blades anymore and I about had a heart attack. Oh, darn, I am now being forced to upgrade and I was quite happy with my current shaver.

I have had a Norelco 5885XL for the past 13 years. I love this unit and it suits me well. This only noteworthy things about this old unit is that I have had to have the batteries replaced only two times, but this is normal since they wear out every 6 years or so.

Here is my 1050x review.. it was painful to write, but here goes..

--This is a noisy shaver folks.. I graduated to a 5885XL a long time ago and was surprised of the whisper quiet shave it delivered. The 1050x is about 2-3 time noisier than my 15 year old Norelco, WTH? This is not good. I simply cannot accept a noisy shaver. This thing is inches away from my ears at 5am and that is very annoying. I need peace and quiet at those early hours, and this would not work long term.

--What a bad shave. Starting with a 2-day shadow growth, I shaved half of my face with my trusty 5885XL [using 1.5 year old blades] and the other half with my shiny new 1050x unit. I actually had my wife feel both shaves afterwords to confirm I wasn't being overly critical of my new toy.

As I suspected, she confirmed my 5885xl produced a better shave, in about the same amount of time.

As I shaved with the 1050x, I realized that I was going over the same growth areas without making things smoother, especially around the neck. I was getting tired, frustrated, and irritated. The pivoting head technology is clearly inferior to Norelcos older units.

--Here come the skin irritations: Ahhh!!!
Just a few minutes after my shave test had ended, my 1050x side was now irritated and not feeling comfortable [like my 5885xl side was]. Having used Norelcos all of my shaving life, about 25 years, this irritation I feel is not normal, and I do not find this acceptable; even if there is a break-in period; not for me there isn't. no thanks..

--Bad charging system! What the heck is it with this terrible charging system. I should be able to plug the unit in directly and not have to lug around more junk to lose or break while on travel. The AC adapter cable does not even fit into the travel case, how stupid is that!?! I can see this cable being the 1st thing I lose on a business trip because it does not have a place to be stored.

Gosh, I wanted to love using this shaver. I was excited and wanted to prove all these other bad reviews wrong. Sadly, they are correct in every way.

My guess is many of the good reviews are being written by persons who have not had the pleasure of trying one of Norelco's older shavers to notice the amazing quality they can provide. Folks, do yourself a favor and get an older model, preferably something from the late 90's IMHO.

Norelco, come'on buddy.. Your losing me big time here.

It's back to my 5885xl, and I have found my HQ5's here on Amazon, clicking buy; and it's byebye to my 1050x.

:(

F.

title: Large toiletry bag with some nice features
text:
The first thing you notice about this toiletry bag is its size. This thing is huge. It is much larger than it appears in the pictures. The size isn’t a bad thin though, if you have the space for it in your bag. It has plenty of space to put any items you want into it. It comes with a main see-through compartment and two removable smaller see-through compartments. The small compartments have Velcro on the back that holds them into place. They can be removed easily, in situations such as going through TSA security. On the top of the bag, there is a metal hook, which can be used to hang the bag. This is extremely helpful for travelers who commonly stay in places, which don’t have much counter space, such as hostels. At first, I imagined hanging the bag might cause the bottom bags to fall off, if the contained heavy objects weight. However, this does not seem to be an issue. My favorite aspect about this bag is the silicone travel bottles that come with it. They are awesome. These things won’t spill under any normal conditions. The tops of them stay sealed tight in the bag and I have yet to see one of them leak. They also have a cool feature on the cap that can be twisted to display what is in them. The labels that can be displayed on the caps are “Shamp.”, “Cond.”, “Lotion”, “Soap” and “Sun”. In addition, there are several blank spaces that can be filled in with your own labels, if you want.

Overall I think this is a good bag, large enough to hold anything you might need, and has some nice features (bottles, hanger, removable pouches). The only reason I did not give this five stars is the price. I do not think $39.99 is a good price point for the product. I believe it should retail in the $20-$30 dollar range.

As a disclaimer, I did receive this product for free for a fair review.

title: Nice, But Time Consuming
text:
These are nice curlers and they are just as described, but I would say they are more suitable for teens and adults who tend to be more patient.
       My 10 year old daughter wanted to try them because she wanted curls without having to use a curling iron. She has somewhat thick hair so I got her two different sets with multiple size curlers so that we would definitely have enough and have the right size. Neither set included any instructions, but it's common sense to know that the hair needed to be wet prior and it was easy enough to figure out how to apply the curlers. However, neither of us realized how time consuming the whole process would be. Half way through applying the curlers, my daughter started to get antsy and didn't want to sit there anymore. She also said that it hurt a little when pulling the hair through some of the curlers. We managed to finish getting the curlers in her hair, but by the time we were finally done she was just over it all. She was no longer willing to even wait for her hair to dry. So within about 10 minute she had starting pulling all of the curlers back out. Which that was another process. You have to be careful pulling each one out because if you start doing it too fast the hair will get tangled and stuck in the curler.
     I still think these curlers are nice though and I do think they would have looked great if she would have waited long enough, but they just weren't for her. I would recommend them for someone who doesn't mind being patient for the end result. For my daughter though we learned that it's just better to use a more quicker / instant method to curl her hair.

title: This is the real deal!
text:
Everything stated in the description is true. Though it's not a cure, it sure does help. I have been using Clobetasol cream via RX to help clear up the outbreaks of Psoriasis (it's a cream that is rubbed on the effected area and helps heal psoriasis lesions that pop up on the skin); but the problem is you have to keep the affected area covered all the time; in my case it's mainly my hands; YOU TRY WEARING PLASTIC GLOVES 24/7! So I give myself a break with this lotion.
This lotion definitely keeps my hands moist and I have less outbreaks. I still use gloves to help hold in the moisture a bit more, but not all the time. Moisture is what psoriasis needs to help heal this condition. This lotion helps with that. Will most certainly will reorder again.
My hat's off to Fay Farms. Remember, skin conditions like Psoriasis, Eczema, etc. are auto-immune diseases. They are incurable. Think twice before taking prescription medications; they do NOT cure, are loaded with many unpleasant side effects, some even lethal; their outrageously priced, etc. Unfortunately, just because you're healing doesn't mean you're cured. Breakouts come and go. You never know when, but I notice I get them more often when I'm ultra-stressed. I have had this condition for many, many years. Took me until now to find the right product.

title: You get what you pay for
text:
My 2nd Sonicare toothbrush died, so I picked up this Oral-B. For what I paid, I guess I can't complain.

There are things I prefer about my Sonicare, like the fact that it had a charging indicator, it was much quieter, and seemed more powerful.

For what I paid for this Oral-B, I guess I can't complain. It does the job, although it is much louder than my Sonicare. I have noticed that the toothbrush seems to "bog down" if you use anything but light pressure. I mean it get's a bit bogged down when it's rubbing up against my cheek when brushing my back molars. There is no charging indicator on the unit, so there's no way of knowing whether it is charging or not. I will say, however, I do prefer the brush head size/shape in comparison to Sonicare's shape/size. I was even using the compact brush head's with my Sonicare, but the Oral-B's are just more comfortable and do a better job reaching my back molars. While I wouldn't buy this model again, I will most likely step up to a higher priced model to see if the noise gets any quieter and the motor stronger. All in all, it was worth it to find out I prefer the brush head shape/size over Sonicare's. Also, the price of the replacement brushes are much more reasonable. Granted you change these heads ever 3 mths v. 6 mths with the Sonicare, it's still a significant savings.

title: The Real "Miracle In A Jar" For Me!
text:
I've been a user of the Alpha Hydrox products for several years. I'm 38 going on 39, and some people still mistake me for 25 to early 30's. I especially love the 12% Souffle cream. Trust me, if you purchase this product, it will work SO well that you may take it for granted someday. Don't! I made that mistake, and it almost cost me my skin!

I had run out of the souffle and was lazy one day when repurchasing my skin care products, so I bought a drugstore brand of a popular new "Simply Radiant" skin care system with fancy "Soy Proteins" in it. I wanted to even out my skin tone (African-American, with a couple of dark dots left over from a few small pimples). After using the moisturizer for a week, I started developing cystic acne-type bumps on my face!! BIG pus-filled lumps that developed in clusters on my cheeks and forehead. I was horrified. I immediately stopped using the moisturizer, and the cysts stopped developing, but the damage was done; I had slowly-healing cystic acne bumps on my face. When I returned the cream to the drug store, the clerk took one look at me and quickly gave me my money back; the bad skin reaction was that obvious.

I ordered the Alpha Hydrox 12% Souffle as soon as I could, along with the Alpha Hydrox 14% AHA swipes to help accelerate my skin exfoliation. I used the swipes 3 times a week, and the souffle morning and night. After a month, I finally got the acne under control. After two months, my skin was smooth again. After six months, I was able to take the most gorgeous headshots I've ever had done, and the graphic artist only had to retouch "shine" on my forehead and chin. There's only a pinhead-sized indentation left over from the acne scars, and all the deep-colored hyperpigmented spots have completely healed and disappeared. My skin is baby-smooth, even toned, and if I had told you that approximately eight months ago I had deep acne scars on my face, you would never believe me.

I'm back to just the Souffle morning and evening for maintenance, but I'll NEVER take using my Alpha Hydrox products for granted ever again!

All-in-all, if you are looking for a quick way to have fun, flirty lashes during a makeup tutorial, quick pics, etc. grab a pair and have fun. But, if you’re looking for a long lasting night out, I’d opt for real glue.

title: Not 100% Agran Oil, OK for Hair Use, maybe not skin or face
text:
This is no criticism of the distributor of this product, they do tell you the ingredients on the selling page: Cyclopentasiloxane, Dimethicone, Cyclomethicone, Butylphenyl Methylpropional, Argania Spinoza, Kernel Oil(Argan Oil), Linum Usitatissimum (linseed) Extract, Parfum (Fragrance). However, you expect this product to be mostly argan oil, and I don't think it is. First, 100% argan oil usually has a very earthy scent. This product is heavily perfumed. And, if you're trying to reduce the 'cones in your hair styling or skin routine, you can clearly see that Dimethicone and Cyclomethicone are one of the first ingredients, before argan oil.

I did use it on my hair after shampooing and conditioning. I'm not a "no-poo" person, so I don't mind using this for my hair. It did make my hair smooth and shiny with blow-drying. However, there is a lot of fragrance in this product, which stayed with me and on my pillowcase for quite a while. There is also a coating to my hair, unlike pure argan oil which usually sinks in my hair. Some people like that coated feeling on their hair, but I only use those types of products on days where I'll be prone to frizzies.

This product is just OK for me. I would use caution using it on the skin because there is a lot of perfume and additives, so spot check first. I'll just be using it for my hair.

Just for fun, I shaved my face again with my Braun Synchro, to my surprise, I heard cutting noise...  Apparently, the Braun can save even closer than the Norelco.  After a quick shave with the Braun Synchro, my face felt even more smooth.  I am not pro Braun per se, but it seems the Braun Synchro shaves way better.  One more thing, if you keep certain facial hair, like goatee, you will find the big head of the Norelco to be a problem, you can't get a precision shave, where as the Braun has a narrow rectangle shaving surface, is much easier to control.  I was always pretty neutral about Braun and Norelco, but now I clearly found the winner--Braun Synchro.

The foam itself does not remove makeup -- you'll still have to use a cleansing oil first. It's more of a 2nd step cleanser in your dual cleansing routine. If it were not in the shape of a rose, i highly doubt re-buying this --the performance is quite ordinary/basic. But the ROSE! adorable.

For me, the visual gimmick wore off after a while, and I found myself using a normal cleansing foam in a tube, as it was faster and easier than using two hands to pump out the rose each time. Fun to experience one time, but not a re-buy for me.

This Kneipp lavender lotion is thick, but it’s not a heavy or greasy lotion. This probably provides moderate hydration for normal skin, but for me it feels quite lightweight. I think it’s a nice cream, but I prefer a richer lotion or cream that comforts my dry skin more and provides longer lasting hydration. When I’ve applied this after an evening shower, my skin feels reasonably moisturized for a few hours but it’s not enough moisture to last all night so I need to reapply before bed. This seems best for those who don’t need heavy hydration and enjoy a lavender scent.

This lotion does have a moderately strong lavender scent that even lingers on my hands after washing. It smells nice and doesn’t bother me, but it may bother those sensitive to fragrance as this is just in the range of what I can tolerate as strong lavender has been a headache trigger for me. This lotion has retinyl palmitate, which is especially risky mixed with sun exposure. This lotion seems best for evening use given that lavender can be relaxing and retinyl palmitate doesn’t mix well with sun. Like it. 4 stars.

title: Nice facial steaming product, with handy portable misting device.  Decent performance.
text:
At a spa, people go into the steamroom to relax muscles, open pores and detoxify. This device isn't a steamroom but aims at providing some of the same benefits to the face and neck, especially regarding the skin and pores. This device heats water up to 104F, creating steam which is expelled from the golden rim outlet. Unfortunately it cannot handle the addition of essential oils, recommending only pure water (or weak alkaline mineral water). This would have been a fantastic ability and function. Oh well. As a pure water streaming device, it is a decent performer.
It does not take long for the water to heat, about 30 seconds, and a fine steam mist is pushed out from the device. The optimum range is 6 - 10 inches away from the steam port. It's a good idea to start at a 12 inch distance, and ease your face closer, gauging your skins tolerance.
(Note: you can add toner that can fully dissolve into the water. The key is not to have a viscous liquid, or particulates, which will adversely affect the atomization.)
We found operation to be fairly simple and easy. Fill the water reservoir, put reservoir back into it's position. turn on the unit, within 30 seconds face gets a spa steam experience.
Is this as effective as those face steamers that have a cone that keeps the steam contained? No, because the steam floats freely. But, it's also multiples cheaper than those kinds of facial steaming devices. This is a credible portable device, that is compact enough that it won't take up much counter space. It's minimalist design will allow it to fit in with most decor.
It's easy to set up and operate. It's acceptably effective.
Also included with this steaming device is a mini misting device, a headband (with pink ears) and 4 skin care tools (intended to help treat acne and blackheads).
The mini misting device does not heat the water you put in it. Rather, via a rechargeable battery, a touch of the button will spray a fine mist. This is very handy in the summer, when you might want a spritz of water to help cool you when outside. It's an apt complement to the facial steaming device.
I found the facial steaming device to be capable of decent performance. If you have realistic expectations, you'll enjoy this product. And, I like the rechargeable portable misting device.
Overall, a worthwhile product set, which earns a 4.5 - 4.75 star rating, with a high level recommendation.

The device does work kind of like a squeegee, but of course, doesn't take care of everything. I like that it is made of a hard plastic because it is durable. I fear that the more flexible silicone products might not last long. This little puppy seems like it will last forever. After use, I simply shook it off and wrapped it in a handkerchief. I kept in nearby at all times and never once smelled any unpleasant odors.

If you are a camper/backpacker, this is, in my opinion, the only device you need. It is light-weight, effective and durable. It made my camping experience so much more enjoyable. It's kind of hard to tell in the pictures, but it is about as long as your hand from wrist to fingertips. Easy to pack in an outside pocket on your pack, or to simply stick in the back pocket of your pants. I could go on forever about how much I love this. Happy peeing, ladies!

I used 6-8 curlers for my whole head.

My curls last three days minimum.
I DO NOT use hair products on my hair ever.
Curls are soft and natural feeling.
Caruso Steamer does not damage hair. Stopped perms many years ago after finding this steamer. This amazing steamer adds shine to my curls. I can run my fingers through my hair as much as I want.
There is never those bent ends of hair, curls just fall, I shake my head, move a curl or two with my fingers and I am out the door.

I love the bright colors. My absolute favorite thing about them is that they are large enough to fit all my hair. My hair isn't terribly long--three inches or so past my shoulders, and it's of medium thickness, I would say. Generally, my hair is too long for the typical hair wrap and an inch or so peaks out at the end of the twist. Not with these! These hold all my hair and there is maybe an extra inch of material, so they can hold even longer hair! And because they are so much bigger than the typical ones I use, they don't pull my hair so tight, which can result in a weird kink in the hair around my face, especially my bangs.

These don't completely dry your hair, but they do suck up a lot of the water. The longer you leave them on, the more they absorb. I usually only leave them on for ten minutes out of habit (see the weird kink in my hair the other kind leave). They are really nice!

I was pretty bummed that trying a different type of hair tie was a failure, perhaps it would work better with those with not so thick hair.

title: Look no further you found your brush
text:
I had been thinking about getting a new brush for a while. I have had an Oral-B Sonicare for about 4 years. It still works, but I had been thinking there may be something better with the advance of technology the last few years. The Sonicare brush vibrated from side to side, which I have always like much better than the brushes that rotate in a circle so I was very nervous about giving this brush a shot. All I can say is, WOW!

This brush is amazing. The Sonicare never seem to brush hard enough, whereas the top setting on this brush is exactly what I hoped it would be. I was also always a bit confused how firm I should hold the brush against my teeth and the 4000 series essentially makes that dummy proof as a giant red light comes on when you are pressing to firm.

The best comparison I can make is to describe this as the cordless version of the brush your dentist uses. It's that swirling brush that leaves your teeth feeling like you just left Dr. Dental's office each day. For folks that don't like as firm or rough a brush, there's enough settings to tone it down, but I have found that most brushes don't have a setting firm enough rather than delicate enough. This brush solves that problem.

I read some complaints about the handle, the charger, etc. I can't imagine why people could even complain as it's the last thing I would notice nor do I think either are a problem. The charging stand is nice and you can remove the holding case that attaches to it if you're worried about counter space. You also get a nice travel case, which is a huge plus because every time I took my sonicare on vacation, I would have to bring it with my carry on or else the on button would also get pushed in the suitcase and end up basically dead by the time I arrive.

I had a tough time justifying buying a new brush when I had one that worked fine. I couldn't be happier I took a chance as I firmly believe this brush will leave me much healthier teeth. I have to believe the Oral-B brand will last as my brush from 4 years ago is still going strong.

title: Probably performs as advertised
text:
I tried it out on my legs as shown in the marketing image and video. The surface of the product is like a fine silicone sandpaper, and it creates some not-uncomfortable friction against the skin as you vigorously rub in the area you want to eliminate hair from. I saw only minimal results with light rubbing so I rubbed up and down as shown in the video with more pressure until it became uncomfortable. I don't have a high pain tolerance, so it is entirely possible someone else with a higher one would be able to rub harder. As it was, I saw better results with this increased pressure, but it still only got about 1/3 of the hair from my leg, which is pale and thin with about 5 days' growth. My skin turned red temporarily, and I did end up having to shave per usual to achieve total hair removal. title: Worth it!
text:
My daughter has Shirley Temple hair; red, thick and tight curls. So we go through detangler and curl products like crazy. Recently I’ve noticed I have better results with her hair if I use a leave in conditioner opposed to detangler, but I did want a spray version of the leave in conditioner I like for her hair. That’s where this bottle comes in. I just fill it with water, squirt a little bit of the leave in conditioner into the bottle, pop the top back on, shake it up, and I’m good to go. Even though for the first few hours, the conditioner has discoed completely, I do not have any issues with clogging. The spray seems to handle the thickness without issue. Because I only need a small amount of the conditioner to mix with the water, I’m actually saving a ton of money. I used to buy detangler every other week, if not sooner. But now I have a bottle of conditioner that I can use with this spray bottle, and it’ll last me months! Thank goodness.

My favorite part of this spray bottle is that it can be sprayed two different ways. If you just pump it once, it’ll have a long mist/spray of the product. But if you pump the trigger several times, you have a continuous spray. I use regular spray bottles, so continuously pumping is something that is just a habit to do. But this spray bottle gives a continuous spray as you keep pumping, resulting in more product being released! It’s also an easy trigger so I find my hand/arm doesn’t get as tired as it usually does when doing my daughters hair.

The only reason I deducted a star was because I wish it came in a bigger size. I feel like I am refilling this often because it doesn’t hold all that much. It’s not a huge set back, but it might be bothersome to someone who needs this spray bottle in use more often. Like a hairdresser. If you need a bigger bottle, this might not be for you.

title: One professional haircut LAST MARCH 2020
text:
As I write my review on August 7, it has been more than 5 months since I've been to a barber shop. The corona virus could do me in because I have a compromised immune system and I'm an old codger. I bought this cordless cutter thinking I could skip a trip to the barber and go half as often as I normally do, but this cutter has worked so well for me (with just a little help from my wife) that I might just go the entire year skipping the barber shop.

Despite having bursitis in both of my shoulders and arthritis everywhere, I'm able to "manipulate" and maneuver the cutter to give myself a "not too bad looking" haircut. The cutter comes with enough attachments that you can select the depth of the desired cut you need for different areas of hair needing trimming.

I'm impressed with how long the cutter can be turned on and used on a single charge, and the way the cutter is shaped, it is easy to hold. It pretty much conforms to my decrepit hands and is comfortable to hold.

If I were having to make a speech, or giving away a daughter at a wedding, I'd go to a professional barber for a "real" haircut, but for an "old codger" who often doesn't get off of the ranch much these days, this cutter does the job for cutting my own hair, during the "scare" of Covid-19.

title: you will see results if you commit to it
text:
I've been using this for 3 months now and I do think this works with longterm use. You obviously aren't going to see overnight results but if you keep at it you will notice a difference on your wrinkles. Luckily I don't have too many yet but I did use it on the little areas where I'm starting to see wrinkles. I noticed a tightening of the areas I used the laser on for the past 3 months. I really liked the hyaluronic acid serum that was included in the set - the serum felt gentle and has no smell (fragrance free). On some days where I didn't use the laser I would still use the serum to moisturize my face. I looked into purchasing just the serum, which they do have for sale, as I really like the product. The laser is easy to operate and charge (usb). I didn't use this daily as I wanted to give my skin a rest, but I think if you used this religiously then you would see results at a much faster rate. It isn't painful, but you feel a little zap. I would equate it to the same level of "pain" as a derma roller, that spikey/zappy feeling - not painful, not super uncomfortable. That of course, will depend on your skin sensitivity. I recommend using the lowest setting first then working your way up as your skin sensitivity will allow. Don't force your skin into what it cannot handle - listen to your body's reaction!

I've seen so many of these laser type products for the skin/body, and never tried it because I didn't trust it. Nira is the first at home laser product that I decided to give a chance to, as I trust it. Overall I am not disappointed but do know that you need to commit to it if you want to see results. If you are going to use it once every few weeks then it will be a while before you see results, if ever. I plan to keep using this to stimulate my skin.

title: Engineered to fail
text:
This product is good while it lasts; it'll clean your teeth better than almost anything out there (unless you have tartar, then you'll need something with a bit more power) and stimulate your gums. However, having autopsied this model, I am convinced that it was engineered to fail under typical conditions after a time, perhaps to motivate the purchase of a more expensive model, which will itself become useless when the irreplaceable batteries go out.

The first one I bought lasted a year, and even that long only after I learned that you have to plug the two holes in the back of the battery compartment to prevent the corrosion from taking place. By the end, batteries were lasting one week tops, at 2x use per day. I also learned that you have to hit it against hard objects when it won't turn on and sometimes then it'll go. You also need to scrape off any rust from the battery contacts occasionally.

Knowing these quirks, I bought another one and immediately plugged up the holes in the back and put tape around the battery cap. However, it has now lasted only a month. There's no rust or corrosion to speak of, however, it just doesn't turn on anymore.

Today I autopsied the first sonicare to see why it had failed (the new one is still on warranty). In taking it apart, it's clear that most of your money goes into buying a tank-like shell around the $1 worth of electronics. This would be a good thing, if there were not two gaping holes in the battery cap that let water in anyway and the shoddy rubber seal. After taking it apart, it's clear why the corrosion so quickly leads the failure. They protect everything on the circuit-board from corrosion by putting glue over it, except the battery contacts, and the contacts and wires that lead to the solenoid coil (that makes the brush vibrate). The contacts that lead to the solenoid and the battery contacts are also strategically located next to each other on the circuit board, so they can corrode together quickly using any moisture from the adjacent battery-terminal holes, while the non-essentials like the timer are located on the other side of the board and completely sealed off from the ambient air by glue. This also explains why hitting it sometimes allows it to start; you're shaking some of the corrosion loose.

The switch is also of questionable design, being nothing more than a paper-thin piece of plastic with some kind ring on it that's slightly more conductive than the plastic.

If the replacement that I get out of the warranty fails, I think I'll try a cybersonic or an oral-b; hopefully their teams of engineers weren't paid to make something less reliable than a politician.

Why can't they make a sonic toothbrush with no batteries, that plugs into the wall, and lasts a lifetime? Or just quit making these to fail so readily?

title: Easy use
text:
I like having my nails done but I have no patience with painting them and letting them dry. Even when I go to salons, I rush and at least 1 nail gets messed up. That being said I have started to use nail strips recently and love them. I usually use color street but I decided to try out these ones.

First off, I love the color, it looked just like the picture online. The blue is a calming baby blue, almost like a light wash denim. They were easy to apply. I did have to trim one of them because I have a more boxy nail shape on one of my fingers but that's nothing a pair of scissors can't fix. The alcohol prep pad was very thick and easy to use. The nail file was also solid quality for a disposable file. The strips were able to be applied removed, and readjusted without messing up the strip or your nail.

Now for some negatives. Most of this stuff is not bad, its just coming from someone who has been using color street for a few years now. First off, these are single sided nail strips so you cant easily get 2 uses out per side. Separating the nail strips from each other is a bit of a challenge since the protective plastic is a little thick. Overall these strips were a little thick, so filing was hard. Lastly, the blue almost seems printed on, if you stretch the nails a little, the color shows up more white and it looks printed and not solid nail polish.

With all that in mind, I would say none of the negatives are deal breakers. I just wanted to list them so you knew what you were getting into. The sunflowers are nail stickers that I bought off Amazon.

text:
I bought this item for my wife, as she was getting into DE shaving and wanted a brush & razor stand. I figured for $8, it was a good buy, and certainly cheaper than everywhere else I'd seen shaving stands.

Well, you get what you pay for.

There are several issues with this:

- The acrylic bowl is SMALL. It barely fits my Art of Shaving badger brush, which is smaller than most other brushes I've seen; my wife's Omega boar brush takes up all available space and she's unable to get a good lather going in the bowl itself.

- The neck to hold a brush? It doesn't fit any of the brushes I tried except for my small badger brush, which has a knot size of something like 18mm. I can get my wife's Omega brush to fit in the stand, but I have to bend the bars out, and it's just not a good fit.

- The two loops at the back to hold the razor? Apparently you have to have a REALLY skinny handle on it. It does not fit my Muehle R89 razor, my Gillette NEW open comb razor from 1932, nor my wife's Maggard MRP. I'm not sure what razor it WOULD fit...

I'd return it, but it wasn't fulfilled by Amazon, and it'll end up costing me more in shipping to send it back; I think I'm going to use it as a giveaway for a contest I've got going and see if someone else can use it; I'll be buying the wife a new razor stand that will, for sure, fit her razor and brush...

It was purple, too, although thicker and lighter in color than the shampoo. As I rubbed the conditioner into my hair, the wonderful floral scent of the conditioner filled my shower--what a delightful sensory treat! I checked my hair again when I got out of the shower and dried off--still no purple hair, thank goodness. However, when I squirted some shampoo into my hand to take a photo, there was a big purple stain on my hand when I washed the shampoo off. I squirted the conditioner in a different spot on my hand for that photo, and it did the same thing. I've washed my hands several times since then, and the purple stains are still there. So...even though the product information online says it works fine with gray and white hair, I look down at my purple stains on my hand and I have to wonder. Since I love the smell of this shampoo and conditioner and how incredibly soft it leaves my hair, I'm going to continue using it. title: It's pretty ok. I tend to like products like this ...
text:
I am always on the search for a new brightening concealer pen, so I thought I would take a gamble on this one. It's pretty ok. I tend to like products like this to be pretty watery and light, but I would say this one has a slightly drier consistency than usual which makes it just a little thicker than I like. Despite the name is was also a little pinker than I thought it would be, which turned out ok on my pale irish skin but might be funky on someone with a different coloring than myself. None of these things are a huge deal breaker, but I seriously dislike the packaging. Most pens I have used like this have a dial on the end to dispense product; for this one, you have to click the end cap button a few times before applying to the face. The first time I used the pen I felt like I was clicking forever before any product was actually dispensed, which was very annoyed. Now the pen has no issue dispensing the product immediately, but it with the click mechanism I end up using more product than I would like.

tl;dr It's pretty ok, and not the worst choice for your money. But nothing special about it either, and the packaging is less than desirable.

text: Sia is a brand that I've had the opportunity to use more than once. Generally I like their products quite a bit, and this serum actually works very nicely as well. It's a small bottle as most serum bottles are, but the really nice thing about this particular formula is that a little will certainly go a long way. You do not need to overuse any abundant amount of this particular product as it spreads extremely well, and saturates very nicely too. I find it has very nice hydrating properties, as it did a great job of moisturizing my skin and leaving it feeling soft. I do have an age spot or two on my face that have appeared over the last few years, and I was hoping that this serum would do a good job to lessen the appearance of those age spots. Unfortunately I would have to report that I haven't noticed any difference after using this for about a month now. The age spots in my opinion are pretty much just as prevalent as they were from the get go. That being said as a hydrator, this serum does an excellent job of moisturizing and softening the skin. The scent is nice too, with kind of citrusy tones. It doesn't last very long however. So if it turns out that the scent is something that you don't like, it dissipates rather quickly. I've used this serum as part of my night time routine before applying moisturizer, and I liked it very much. All in all my experience was very good, so I would recommend giving it a try if this is something you were thinking about.

title: Inefficient Razor that's Rough to Use: There are much better value bargain razors out there.
text:
The Acevivi Razor : A Test and Review
I only came across this razor very recently. It intrigued me because some seemed to like it and report that it was well made. Also, like the new Fendrihan razors, it has an unusual head: Closed comb on one side; open comb on the other. I think the idea is that it offers two levels of aggression. The Lutz slant offers a similar choice of two levels of aggression.

In use I found that both sides offered about the same level of aggression. Another reason for the test is that it's a low cost razor; under $13 currently on Amazon. I'm always intrigued by potential bargains!

A further unusual feature is the exceptionally long handle. Longer than the Futur, longer than my Mergress, Schick Krona, or even my long handled Gillette Starburst, (aimed at the ladies” market); longer in fact than any razor I own. To some this is a plus, to others not so. It may be useful if ladies wish to use the razor on their legs, or other parts. The razor is well balanced so the long handle presented no problem.

The razor comes with a box of five blades. I have no idea of their origin. But since the razor is Chinese, I expect China.

The Blade used for the Test
I chose to use the Rapira Platinum Lux. I've found this blade to be consistent and reliable in just about every razor (but there are some razors where it's an indifferent pairing, say with my RR Wunderbar), and it's always good for at least four shaves, often six, in just about any razor. It's sharp, smooth, comfortable, very cheap to buy, and easily available, and my personal favorite of the Rapira line. I've also used it every DE razor I own at one time or another, and I own over 50 DE safety razors . Not my favorite blade, but a very good one in most razors. I used a brand new blade

How I Used this Razor for the Test
When using an adjustable razor, (and following advice from others on this forum, including Jim Chandler, plus my own long experimentation) I've found the best way, for the smoothest and most comfortable shave is to INCREASE the aggression with each pass. It seems counter-intuitive at first but it really works best. It's like lowering the blade on a lawn mower to get a closer cut. I increased the aggression on each pass on this test.

Since this razor supposedly offered two choices of aggression I used the Acevivi in this way: Less aggressive WTG and XTG, then more aggressive ATG and for buffing. I'm assuming that closed comb is less aggressive, though as some have reported with the Fendrihan, this is not always the case.

Now in previous reviews, I notice that some people seem to miss this point. I really believe that this is the best way to get a very smooth, comfortable, and importantly irritation-free shave with an adjustable razor. I have a complete thread on this method. Please review the thread and give it a whirl, and report what you find please!

The Routine
For testing I go through the same routine. I clean my face and wet the beard by washing with a glycerin soap. I rinse off the soap, wet it thoroughly and apply two drops of a pre-shave oil.

By the way, I believe good pre-shave prep not only produces a better shave, but reduces irritation, and keeps you skin in good condition. I know of one rather famous reviewer whose skin frankly looks irritated, red, blotchy and awful, especially on his neck. I don't doubt he gets close shaves, but at what cost?

I use an Arko shave stick applied directly to the beard and lather with a Stirling Synthetic “Kong” brush. I rinse and lather again between passes. I thoroughly rinse the head of the razor between passes.

I remove the blade from the razor when I'm done. I dry it with a microfiber cloth. Naturally I dry the razor too when I'm done.

I finish with an Alum block, which is a good indicator of razor burn or irritation. Then after washing it off , I apply Thayer's Alcohol Free Witch Hazel.

The Shave
I shaved 22 hours before doing a test comparison of the Parker Variant and Ming Shi 2000s, so my face had a little less than average growth.

First Pass WTG: Closed Comb Side
Fairly smooth, reasonably efficient. Not good enough for a one pass shave.

Second Pass XTG: Closed Com Side
Not especially smooth and after the pass I wasn't especially happy with the hair removal. It still felt like there was a lot of hair, but I press on! Still not good enough even for everyday.

Third Pass ATG: Open Comb Side
Quite scratchy. I could feel the blade and I didn't enjoy the pass much. A lost of hair remained. Quite disappointing. Not a good shave at all.

Buff up and J-hooking
I would have had to spend an age buffing and cleaning up because the beard was still quite rough, and frankly my face already felt quite irritated. So I did not buff with the Acevivi. There are limits to my testing zeal!

Finishing the Shave:
Sometimes a specific blade is no good. In the interests of fairness, I took the blade out and put it in my most efficient razor, the RR Wunderbar slant (which incidentally is not a blade this razor likes a lot) and had to shave again, because the shave with the Acevivi was just not good enough even for everyday.

I then did another ATG pass, and boy, was there a lot to remove! The jawline and neck still had a lot of growth. The blade performed well in the Wunderbar, so I don't think one can't blame the blade.

Now I'm not comparing a $13 razor to a $130. That would be grossly unfair. I just wanted to see if the blade was to blame, and frankly I didn't want to irritate my face more than necessary.

I did a clean up and buffing pass, using the Wunderbar and got a BBS shave. However the feedback from alum block revealed a lot of irritation, not surprising given three indifferent and inefficient passes with the Acevivi, followed by another ATG pass and cleanup with the Wunderbar, though I don't blame the latter. No nicks, cuts, or weepers, but definite neck irritation.

Conclusion:
The razor is well made, and low in price, and I admire the innovation, but I cannot recommend the Acevivi, unless you want to get a very long handle that's well made for under $13. It's possible that it will do better with other blades, but my initial impression is that it's not really worth testing. It's a fairly mild and quite inefficient razor.

Is it good value? No! The Ming Shi 2000s Adjustable is cheaper (aroud $10 from China) and better in every possible way. The following razors, all under $20 are much, much better: The RazoRock (RR) German 37 Slant, the Phoenix Artisan Accoutrements Bakelite slant, the RR Slab, the RR Mission, the RR Old Type, the RR Jaws (if you can get it), and probably some others too.

It's a pretty poor razor, and even at the low price not worth it. I wouldn't recommend it to newbies, because it will put them off DE shaving. Here's one to pass.

title: I love this toothbrush, but...
text:
1. I don't understand these reviews that complain about getting water into the battery compartment and corroding the batteries. I've never had this problem. It would seem that one would have to be really careless for this to happen. Don't submerge it or pour water over it, and you should be fine.
2. Don't worry about battery life. Get some Eneloop rechargeables, and swap them out anywhere from a couple weeks to a couple months and you'll be fine.
3. This does such a good job, my dentist assumes I'm flossing like I'm supposed to be. I'm not. I do use a waterpic, but only a couple times a week these days. My dentist gave me an A+ on my last visit (part of this is because of the fluoride rinse that's been helping strengthen my teeth, but that's another review).

So now to the reason I only gave it three stars.

I had one of these that we bought years ago. I don't remember how long, but it's been probably 5 years. I'm not exactly sure, but it's been awhile. It's always worked great and still does. We finally got tired of sharing, and when we saw they were only $20 on Amazon we got another one.

This second one has had to be replaced under warranty twice in about a year and a half. It just stopped working, both times. No corrosion in the battery compartment or anything. The unit looks pristine, it just stopped working.

The first one lasted about 8 months. The second one only about 6 months.

So while this is a great product (functionally) and I would still likely buy it again if my current one died out of warranty (can't beat $20) I'm getting concerned about the quality. Here's hoping third time's a charm.

title: I LOVE these!
text:
I just have to say it, I HATE WEARING A MASK! I have glasses that fog up terribly with most all traditional fabric masks. I have low-grade asthma and wearing a mask where I am breathing in my own air makes me very anxious and I end up being unable to breathe well at all. Thankfully I found that I didn't have to worry about any of that once I began wearing a face shield instead of a fabric mask. Because I began working in retail around the holidays and was required to wear a mask for 8 hours a day, I was able to survive with the shield. But I really didn't like the way that I had to wear the elastic band around my head over my hair, and it was much like wearing two pair of glasses, since I had to view the world through my glass lenses as well as the plastic of the shield.

One day I saw a woman in my store wearing one of these masks and I immediately became a fan. I found this seller online and I can't believe how much I love wearing this! It feels almost like I have no mask on at all - in fact, I was once heading into a store and the greeter there offered to give me a mask, not realizing that I had this one on until I got closer to her. It is great that you can sanitize this between wearings very easily without having to put it through the laundry, and I just keep it hanging from my rearview mirror and use hand wipes to clean it.

However, there are a couple of things that I'd prefer on this mask. The plastic is a hard, formed plastic rather than a pliable one. I no longer work in retail and am no longer required to wear a mask at my new job, but I feel like if I had to wear this one 8 hours a day like before, it might break within a few days. Although it does not fog up my glasses at all, it actually fogs up when I am wearing it outside. Once I enter the store and an ambient temperature though, the fog goes away and it is clear once again. I am sure that this mask would not be allowed on an airplane, but then neither are many other styles of masks out there. The other thing that is a bit bothersome is that when you are talking or singing with this mask on, it moves with the movement of your mouth since it holds onto your face with a chin guard that keeps the plastic away from your mouth. But all in all it is worth it to be able to breath and remain compliant with the current laws of my City regarding masks. For those reasons though, I gave it a 4 rather than a 5 rating.

title: The trays alone are worth buying this kit
text:
In researching teeth whitening products on Amazon, it quickly became clear to me that a custom teeth whitening tray would be the best solution. My teeth are straight enough that my parents and I decided against my getting braces as a child, but they are crooked enough (especially my mostly-hidden bottom teeth) that I worried other whitening products (like white strips) would not whiten evenly.

I went out on a limb and ordered this kit. At the time it was only $50 on Amazon. It came packaged as reported. I took my teeth impressions, the process was pretty easy, and sent them off to the lab in the pre-paid envelope. Then I crossed my fingers. I had every confidence that the initial package would arrive since it had the backing of Amazon, but I was a little dubious sending my impressions off to some random lab that's not affiliated with Amazon. I had decided just to wait until I got my customs trays to start using the whitening gel, rather than mess with the boil and bite trays.

Well, it was over a month and I was beginning to lose hope that my teeth trays would ever come, when I got an email that my trays were on their way! I had no idea when I ordered this kit how long the trays would take, and I don't think a month or two is an unreasonable amount of time to wait... so that's why I'm writing this review, to let customers know that they should be prepared to wait several weeks for the trays to arrive. But they do arrive! And I'm very happy with the result. The fit is precise and snug.

As for the 22% gel... I've been using it for about three weeks now, roughly 20 minutes to 30 minutes a day. It appears to have made my teeth brighter... not sure if it's made them all that much whiter. I'm a big coffee and tea drinker, so this gel is up against a lot of persistent staining. Looking up close in the mirror, I still see the yellow cast of my teeth stains, but the enamel underneath appears brighter. I'm probably going to try the 35% gel after I'm done with the gels that came with this kit.

But that's okay, because I have custom trays, now, and even if the gel they came with isn't sufficient, the trays (which, as I understand, would have cost a few hundred dollars from a dentist) are worth the price of the kit. Now that I have them I can order any gels I want from Amazon.

title: Research before you buy
text:
Common sense right? Well, it’s not that I didn’t try, but it’s not exactly made as easy as it could be.

Regarding the seller: Don’t buy these without being 100% sure they’re for your clippers, because you can’t return these.

Regarding the manufacturer: Wahl doesn’t do a great job identifying their physical products. I bought a clipper second hand, thinking “Great, it’s hardly used and all it needs is a new blade.” Turns out, if you don’t have an exact model number it’s extremely difficult to figure out what blade kits will work because Wahl doesn’t actually put the exact model number on all of their products. There’s also slight variations for common parts, like screws. Not sure why you’d spec an entirely different screw when manufacturing a like part used in multiple product lines, but hey, what do I know. You might only get the name of the series or product line, or in my case, an abbreviation of it. I’m not sure why, considering every other professional tool manufacturer stamps or at least prints a model name, number, and serial number on every unit. I’ve had an easier time sourcing parts for 10 year old discontinued power tools.

title: Almost perfect
text:
I purchased an sleep mask just like this in a store and, when it went missing, searched for it high and low until I found it here on Amazon. The mask blocks light well with little or no light leaking in around your nose and none around the eyes. The contoured eye coverings place no pressure on your eyelids. I never felt comfortable sleeping in a traditional sleep mask until I used this style. I can even open my eyes in my mask and my lashes don't even brush it.

The comfort in wearing meant I quickly adjusted to its use and now can't hardly sleep without it. As someone who has had trouble sleeping and finds napping almost impossible, having the routine of perfect dark when I sleep at night has allowed me to build a trigger. Now, when I need to sleep early, want to catch a nap, find myself in a plane, or other times I might ordinarily find it hard to sleep, I can place my mask on and it signals sleep perfectly. It's improved my sleep length and frequency, as well as reduced the time it takes me to fall asleep, which I think anyone could appreciate.

My only gripe is that, while I thought this one was exactly like my previous mask, there's a little difference. There's a little plastic piece on the side of the elastic that joins loops for the adjustment system and they sit very near my ears. I can sometimes feel it digging in and I never remember feeling that on my previous mask. For occasional use, you may not notice it, but using them nightly, the little part can bother me sometimes. My solution plan involves breaking the part and replacing it with something soft or hand-sewing that connection point. Customization is a very small price to pay for the amazingly comfortable contoured foam that makes up the main body of the mask.

title: Best electric shaver I've ever used
text:
This is the first rotary shaver I've owned, and it is by far the most comfortable shaver I've ever used. I have very curly whiskers, so they're essentially flat ribbons that tend to confound normally-shaped shavers and make it difficult for me to get a close shave when using a razor. With this shaver, I can go in a circular motion, much more easily catching the whiskers on any part of my face or neck. While I need to use a pre-shave (like Lectric Shave), I've needed that for every shaver I've used.

Cleaning is much easier with this one than any other I've used. Simply open the heads and rinse with hot water. I previously used a Braun Activator, which was self-cleaning but required special cleaning cartridges that cost anywhere from $8 - $12 for a 2-pack; over 4 years of use and regular cleaning, that brought the total cost of ownership of the unit to at least twice what I initially paid for it.

The only caveat with this shaver is the tiny trimmer; since I only use it for my sideburns it isn't a big deal for me. However, if you have a moustache and/or beard you need to trim, you might need a separate trimmer.

Overall I believe this is an excellent shaver for the price.

title: Big, Bigger, and Biggest
text:
This is an interesting set of mascara. I have my own favorite brand mascara but I was looking to lower the cost of my makeup budget and these mascara set fit the bill.

It is interesting to see that the company packed those containers in a way from right to left: big, bigger, and biggest and you can tell which is which by the sizing of those tubes.

"Big", the teal tube, is for natural days when I need a soft oomph to my eyelashes and it fit the bill. Very nice and it held up well during long days.

"Bigger" ,the yellow tube, is for between natural to thicker lashes, not necessarily long but it is nice to get extra fluffy lashes for days I want to show off my blue eyes. It had good lasting power but it did flake a bit after a very long day.

"Biggest", the purple tube" is the bomb. It has fibers in solution making eyelashes lengthen and thicken and it really makes my blue eyes pop. It flaked off a bit at the end of the day due to fibers but it's very minor compared to making my eyes look big and gorgeous.

I can choose which mascara that I want without guessing due to its different sizing even though I could just read the names on the tube but they are rather confusing.

I really like the ease of these mascara and they're so easy to remove with makeup wipes. You can even get the mascara to last longer by using makeup setting spray.

Yup, I will purchase them in the future and my budget will be easier to manage.

title: Base coat was almost dried up, but the powders  are AMAZING!
text:
The powders are beautiful. Since I wasn’t ready to redo my own nails, I offered to do my six year old daughter’s with dip for the first time. She chose the pink. The powder is VERY fine, and needed three coats to become opaque, and I probably could have done four. The fine powder smoothed out really nicely tough - I barely had to file, and was able to do it all by hand, without firing up my nail drill. Took a while longer than normal to dry, but that could have been because I had to use a different base that came in a separate kit that I don’t really like. The one that came with this one, while sealed, was very thick and past the point of no return. I was so disappointed about that. I do like that they included the extra brushes and pretty little strange case. I appreciate the slightly larger jars of powder too, though I noticed the white seemed to not be as full as the others. Sure enough when I put the other jars on a scale, they weighed in between 18 and 19 grams. The white weighed just over 16.

Not sure on staying power since we just did them this morning, but if they can hold up for a week on the fingers of a six year old girl who likes to climb trees and dig in the mud for worms, I’ll be impressed.

I have yet to try any other colors, but if they’re anything like the pink, these are my new favorite for dip powders. I’ll stick to Latrice for my liquids though. These weren’t bad, I’ll use them, I just like the Latrice liquids better.

Oh! Bonus - my daughter discovered tonight that the pink glows in the dark!! She was literally jumping up and down with excitement. I will definitely be using these on myself when my current set needs to be redone. Overall, I’m pretty happy, because the price was right. Just wish I had gotten everything I paid for.

title: Non-greasy and natural looking! Great hair cream for men!
text:
This comes in a large container. It was a lot larger than I was expecting. It works well. It is a little hard to get out because of its tackiness and hardness. However, you just push your finger in and scrape some up and you will have it. You do not need to use much for most styles, depending on what type of style you're going for. I rub a little bit of this cream in between my fingertips and then rub it into the area of my hair that I want. It holds very well. I used this on my son's hair when he wanted a particular style. It turned out quite well. This is not sticky or greasy at all. It also does not get stiff. It looks and feels natural. It has a nice scent for men. My son likes it a lot and he uses it most days. I used it a couple times too. The scent is not strong or noticeable.

I like how natural your hair looks after using this. It does not leave your hair shiny or greasy. It looks very natural, as if you used nothing at all. Remember not to grab too much. However, if a little bit doesn't seem like enough for your particular hairstyle, then you can always grab some more. Rub it into your palms or fingertips first before applying it. I have bought the professional hair salon pomades and hair creams before. This works just as well as any of those, maybe even better since it's non-greasy and looks natural. Furthermore, this package is a lot bigger than what you usually get in the hair salons. So I think you definitely get your money's worth from this. I was so glad to be able to buy this product while they had a promotion going on. I think this is a great cream for getting that particular look or definition you want. They give you plenty of it too. This is well worth your money. In addition, it does not leave any white flakes in your hair. I have experienced that from other products. This review is a reflection of my own personal experience with this product.

Ps. If this product is too solid or hard for you to use, just add a teaspoon of water and mix. You may want to let it sit with the water overnight to help soften it up. It then should be easy to use.

text:
To me, the "high" setting felt exactly like treatments I have received in the dr's office. My skin was very smooth and felt wonderful after use. I was on the fence regarding whether or not to buy this product because I thought that there must be some gimmick-- else why would so many women go to get this done professionally if they could have a machine at home? I'm glad I purchased because I get the same result for much less money, not to mention time wasted making weekly appointments. Keep in mind:

*Crystal refills are an additional expense
*The warranty card must be sent in within 10 days of purchase to be valid
*There are different settings so that you can control intensity
*Comes with instructional dvd
*One application covered my entire face and I still had a bit more than half a cartridge left--so one cartridge could last two applications if you just do your face.

I purchased my machine from a flash sale site so I got a bit of a discount but I would pay full price for this in a heartbeat--it's great. You should go to the manufacturer's website and price shop with amazon to see where you can get the best deal. the manufacturer's website also sells complementary products but I can't comment on them because I have not tried any.

title: Quick, easy, blendable & at drugstore prices....gotta love it!!
text: I think we all have days where we're looking for something quick and easy when it comes to makeup.  Anything to get us out the door looking somewhat put together with the least amount of time involved is the goal.  If you're looking for a quick eyeshadow look that takes next to no time these are one answer.  Cream eyeshadow on one end and a brush on the other.  The brush is surprisingly usable, but since I've got older eyes (which means older skin that needs to be babied) I just use one of mine.  They go on pretty smooth and creamy.  Not a ton of pigment on the first pass, but it's very buildable.  The swatches on my arm are 2 passes of each color.  They also blend out really well.  I put a couple passes on my lower lid and blend it up into my crease and I'm good to go.  There is a bit of shimmer in this one, but it's not overwhelming.  Just a bit of sparkle that looks good even on aging eyes.  They make it through the whole day, but I did notice some creasing and breakdown after about 6-8 hours. title: Fantastic quality matte black lipstick, with great depth that lasts
text:
Thick, velvet smooth and beautiful, this lipstick is some of the best I've ever tried. This stuff is very similar to Wet n Wild's "Mega Last" lipstick, which is also excellent -- the texture is almost identical and so is the lifespan, up to a couple hours if careful before reapplication is needed to keep the colour full and deep. The "Pagan Angel" black is stunning and rich, and it builds well onto the lips for full coverage. The taste and smell is completely neutral.

I really, really recommend this lipstick.

text:
Love being able to access electrolysis at home! I have been going to a professional for months now and when the 2020 pandemic began and all service providers closed up shop, I wasn't sure how I would deal with unwanted facial hair. Where other methods of hair removal can encourage stronger hair regrowth I did not want to regress. Then I found this! I have had this product several weeks now and am very happy with it. I wish I had found this earlier. Not only can I do a treatment whenever I want, I am able to target hairs when they first appear as opposed to waiting for an appointment. It is very easy to use. I was afraid I would be unable to target the follicle in the right spot but that has not been a problem. It has a high pitch buzz when the current is delivered to the follicle. Most of the time the sound is my only indication that anything is happening. I do not find this painful. I can tell it is working because when I go to remove the hair it comes out with no effort. I do keep the power at the highest setting except for the delicate area above the upper lip. That can be a painful area at home or at the salon.

My only complaint with the product is that the tweezers included are useless. Just use your own.
I bent the stylist at first so I did order extras to have in case that happens again... so far so good as I haven't ruined another. I don't think that is a product flaw as it must be very delicate to do the job right... just be careful.

If you are unfamiliar with electrolysis, do not expect that one shot will forever kill a hair. I suggest reading articles on the subject as this can be a long term process. But considering other methods are a FOREVER process... go for it !

title: My favorite non-acetone remover.
text:
For this price you get 6 individually sealed containers of remover pads. They each contain 38 thin fabric-like removal pads that are soaked in the non-acetone remover. The containers screw open and don't seem to dry out easily. The remover contains isopropyl myristate, propylene carbonate, fragrance, and water. These are ideal for anyone who doesn't like the smell of acetone since they just smell flowery. They smell wonderful, I'm someone who doesn't like many scented things, but they are all very soft pretty scents that I love.

The pads remove polish more slowly than most acetone-based nail polish removers and require a bit of scrubbing. To remove a bright red (read-as nail polish that stains) manicure I use 3-4 sheets (more if there is glitter in the polish). They do leave your nails and hands a bit greasy feeling (which means they moisturize your nails rather than drying them out like acetone) so you should always wash your hands thoroughly after using the remover pads. Overall, great product and I will buy it again (once these run out, they last forever!)

title: Great Foundation
text:
I'm 45 and my skin has changed dramatically over the past 5 years. I had to move from loose powder coverage to more of a "foundation" coverage to hid all the flaws. After trying several different products, I came across this product from Avon. So, it's a cream foundation that goes on very smooth. I only apply it in the morning and find that if I don't mess with my face too much, it stays all day. It covers very well. All the little sun damage spots, redness, etc are covered evenly and smoothly. It doesn't look like you have a foundation mask on, but I also apply it down along my jaw line and neck to make sure.

There are two cons to this product: 1) it tends to accentuate fine lines until it settles. I use a magnifying mirror and you can see the make-up in the creases. From farther away, it's not that bad. I also notice that as it settles into my skin, that seems to fade. 2) I have combination skin, and it feels oily on my skin after a few hours. It does not cause breakouts (actually, my skin is so much better since I started using this product), so I don't think it's doing anything, but just feels a little oily. It doesn't LOOK oily, it just feels oily and I can't wait to get home and wash my face. I'm not a foundation user, so this may be typical, I'm not sure.

Overall, I really like this product. The coverage is fantastic and far outweighs the minor "cons" I have listed above. Since I only apply it once a day, on work days usually, it lasts a long time. It comes with a round sponge and mirror compact. It is definitely Avon quality.

title: Great Hold and Light Scent
text:
I have been using beard oil for a while, but recently, it was not making the cut and my beard was getting a little too scraggly for work. I decided to try beard balm to see if it might be able to provide some hold and tame down some of my loose hairs. I was worried that I would need a significant trim if I couldn't find a way to bring it all together, but since starting to use this balm daily, I have been able to let it grow without any thoughts about the professionalism. Below are a few comments I have to make on different aspects of this balm.

Size: This is a fairly large container. If you are looking for some size comparisons, I would say it is about the same diameter as a coffee cup and 3/4 of an inch deep. I have been using it daily for a few weeks now and still have well over 90% of the balm remaining.

Scent: As someone switching from beard oils with fairly strong scents, I initially thought this balm was scentless. I think this can be a positive or a negative depending on your preferences. If you are using a beard oil or cologne with a scent you love, this will not clash with it, but will give you the hold and conditioning you are looking for. On the other hand, if you are looking for a balm that will double as cologne, you'll probably want to buy a beard oil or some actual cologne to supplement what this will provide.

Strength: The hold is great! My beard is about an inch and a half to two inches, and this has provided the perfect amount of hold for me. It helps me to be able to do a little bit of shaping when I need to, but mostly allows my beard to be itself. It has also left my beard feeling less dry and looking a little bit healthier.

Overall, this is a great beard balm and I would recommend it to first time users or those who have tried many before. Also, I received this balm in exchange for an honest review.

title: Not good. Maybe okay for lefties.
text:
I almost never write negative reviews, but I had this set in my wishlist for weeks waiting for it to come back in stock and unfortunately I’m just not happy with them. The set I received only has 3-4 of the designs pictured which would be okay if they were of good quality, but they’re not. My set looks like horn and doesn’t have any raised lines down the sides which would indicate that they’re molded plastic, but they could simply have been sanded down to get rid of that.
Unlike other carved hair sticks I have, these are flat on one side and therefore you cannot see the dragon, bird, etc. from both directions.. Because of this, they only look good with the carved side out and most of them need to be inserted into the bun from the left to achieve this. If you’re left handed they might be okay but that’s very awkward for me and not the way I usually make my buns. Quality hair sticks that are the same on both sides are much better because they look great no matter which direction you choose to use them, as well as from the front and the back of your head. In addition to being decorative on one side and flat on the other, several of them are curved in such a way that if I were to put them in with the right side facing out they are curved away from my head rather than towards it, making them even more awkward to use. I don’t know if they’re made this way or if they warped during shipping, which would indicate plastic.
Overall, I’m unhappy with half of them and the others are mediocre at best, so they’re not the great value I thought they were. There are other sets of carved wood hair sticks that I’ve purchased here which are fantastic, as well as other carved horn sticks that are gorgeous and functional. The only way I can really use these is to make a bun that’s held in place with pins and then add one of these as a mediocre looking decoration. They’re just not very good at holding my long, thick hair up on their own. There are much better choices out there. Not recommended.
