When I filled one jar with the liquid oil (instead of overfilling it), I didn't experience this issue.

title: Loving These Locs!
text:
[[VIDEOID:f6fe2bb4d18d1094a8c2136bc198cd5a]] I've always loved dreads, so when I saw these, I ordered them immediately! I hadn't known I could simply *install* dreads without having to grow my own hair long and then proceed to do whatever magic (and damage) was necessary to create dreads. As soon the first set of 12 arrived, I was thrilled; I also knew that 12 strands was nowhere near enough to cover my head so I ordered a second set. Each set came with a bag of random hair accessories as well as what looks similar to a crochet hook. The hook is ridiculously small, so I don't know if it's intended to pull the hair through the top loop or if it's to help maintain the dreads as they're washed and loosen up over time. There were no instructions, so after my first set arrived I scoured the Internet to find photos of loc styles as well as tutorials about how to install them. I've included a short video with this review to help people realize that the most difficult part will be installing these on the back of your head. (I don't have a fold-out mirror and I don't trust myself to do a good job, so I've got to find someone I trust to do the back of my head for me.)

While this is the first set of dreads I've handled, they're not stiff and they have no odor. (While researching dreads, I discovered that a lot of synthetic pieces have those issues but THESE do not! I mean, I loved the first set so much that I ordered another right away.) I don't plan to have my entire head in dreads, but if I did I could easily get away with only 3 to 4 sets (with leftovers) because my hair is really thin and I'd pull larger sections through the top loop as I braided each piece in.

The ends of the dreads look a little scraggly BUT I think that makes them look all the more authentic; in fact, I was surprised when I hopped back online and saw these are synthetic! The top of each has a black rubber band just below a loop of hair and you basically pull a section of your own hair through that top loop, split that hair into two sections (so with the dread and your own hair you have three separate sections). Get the dread close to your scalp, then simply braid the three sections together to secure the loc into place. You'll need a small rubber band to hold the sections together where they end and it's that simple! You can attach the little hair accessories wherever you choose.

If you've been wanting locs, these are an excellent value and the perfect way to see if the look is right for you. I do think they should come with instructions, but that doesn't take away from the perfect coloring, length, and texture!

This is a very credible cuticle care toolset. The handle/shaft can be used with one or two specialty heads inserted. You can customize it according to your specific needs, at the time. I think it's a manufacturing error, the opening not the exact same size as the 'good' opening.
The assortment of heads is impressive. They are composed of quality stainless steel, with a professional appearance.

title: PURE GOLD! MAGICAL! CANNOT LIVE WITHOUT THIS NOW!!!
text:
This stuff is magic! I have really dry, peely lips and I never wear lipstick/gloss/etc. because it always ends up looking bad. Despite my hardcore chapstick obsession (I have a drawer full of various chapsticks in my desk) I thought maybe some higher-end lip moisturizer might do the trick for me. I invested in a good lip scrub and purchased the Nuxe Rev de Miel and the Bite Beauty agave lip mask after hearing rave reviews on both (as an aside: I think the "big gun" ingredient in the agave lip mask is lanolin, which should be fairly easy to find, but for some reason I can never track down lanolin products to use on my lips). While both were nice, neither rocked my world, and so my hunt began again. I happened to stumble across [...] and her review of the laneige lip mask, which I have been curious about but have yet to bite the bullet on the $20+ price tag, and this pure smile snail lip treatment. After reading her RAVE review, I was desperate to get my hands on some, although it was a little hard to track down, but I found it for a good price here on Amazon and decided to go for it (plus free shipping, who can argue with that?!). Boy am I glad I did! This stuff is AMAZING! First, I've never really had any lip products quite like this before. There is a fruity scent underscored by a minty scent and flavor, both of which are mild and pleasant. The texture is very thick and sticky, far more than anything I have ever used before, but it doesn't bother me as I put it on then go to bed. If you rub it into your lips vigorously it will be "pushed" out to the edges of your lips and sort of gather in the corners and along the edges of your mouth, and sometimes if I do this I have to spread it around again to make sure it's really coating my lips. It feels like a protective film, and once it has absorbed in (takes awhile since it is so thick and sticky) your lips are UNBELIEVABLY soft. Like nothing I've ever experienced before! I love this stuff! I hope they never stop making it or I might be completely heartbroken.

Just one observation, I did develop a blemish on my lip line of my bottom lip a few days after I started using this, but I'm not sure if it is related. That does happen to me on occasion, and it could just be a coincidence, but worth mentioning.

text:
So far, so good! I've got very sensitive skin & this is great.

My routine:
1. Wash with 'cleansing water'. (Soaps are too much.. even sensitive ones!)
2. Wet my skin. Make sure it's dripping wet. Don't skip this step!
3. Squeeze a little hyaluronic acid onto your fingers and rub around your wet face.
4. Let it dry.
5. To finish, smooth lotion or oil (whatever you prefer) on top of your now-dry face.

This gives the hyaluronic acid moisture & locks it in. You'll love it! You can even do this at night as well.

NOTE:
This is not magic. It will not repair years of sun damage or neglect to your skin. However, if you take care of yourself & take care of your skin, this will really help with your crows feet or frown lines or general wrinkles that we all get as our skin ages.

Enjoy! Don't expect miracles... but take care of yourself and take care of your skin. Plus, this is vegan. Hooray! You can nourish your skin without hurting animals. I'm nearing 40 and this is really helping my crows feet & fairly-large frown lines.

title: Adorable, well-made, compact and portable device for face cleaning/massaging. Pricey though.
text:
This is a silicone face pusator/massager. One side features soft silicone bristles that are useful for working any topical application into your face. The other side features a few ribs and can be used for simple face massage (no creams/topicals).

You turn it on by pressing the power button on the back (massage side). You turn it off the same way. There's a travel lock you enable by pressing the + and - buttons simultaneously for three seconds. You disable the lock the same way.

The device integrates a 300 mAh LithiumIon battery. That's not huge, but it's big enough to give a rated 300 minutes of run time. So it's enough to throw into your travel bag or purse (after a full charge) and not worry about running out of juice.

It fits reasonably well in the hand. The vibration intensity can be adjusted in 8 levels using the + and - buttons. Personally, if I'm gonna use this, I'll be using the highest level, and at that level it dusts up a good amount of lather (if the topical you're using can lather). If you have sensitive skin, the lowest level is quite low--just a low hum of buzzing.

Honestly, this is a sweet face cleaner. There is a caveat here, though. And that is that this device is quite pricey for what it is (silicone with a moderate-sized battery and a small buzzing/vibrating unit inside). So whether it's worth the price will be a matter of personal preference. It's perhaps closing with a note that this comes with a two year warranty, unlike cheap similar devices, which usually with a blink and you'll miss it warranty.

Pros:
** Cute and stylish
** 300 minutes run time on a full charge
** At highest level, capable of a getting a topical (or soap) lathering well
** Lowest level is low enough to satisfy those with sensitive skin
** Travel lock-out mode
** Two year warranty

Cons:
** Expensive

title: Adorable Kid-Friendly Unicorn Headband
text:
I purchased this headband for my 4 month old. Her cousin was turning one and having a unicorn themed party. We all agreed that our little girls would dress up as unicorns for a photo op; this was perfect! I was really surprised by how well made the headband was. It arrived in a clear plastic package in a bubble wrap envelope. The headband is very durable and small enough for my baby- but flexible enough to definitely fit children up to 5 years of age. The tulle on the back (the "mane") is attached securely and flows down the back of the head without getting in the child's face. It's also a very soft tulle that is not itchy and has caused no irritation to my kiddo's sensitive skin.

The ears, flowers, and horn are also all securely fastened to the band. The ears have purple glitter, the flowers are kind of a faux satin, and the horn is a shiny silky pink material that has a plush feeling to it. Definitely VERY kid friendly and I have a feeling this is going to be a hit with my daughter when she gets a bit older and wants to play dress-up.

The actual band part is covered in a really soft white material. It was very gentle on my girl's head and she didn't seem to mind wearing it at all. In fact she was happily smiling the entire time. It was so darn cute! All in all, I'm so happy with this purchase. I'd definitely buy it again and have recommended it to friends and family who thought it was just oh-so-cute. I haven't purchased or seen any of the other unicorn headbands on Amazon- but the quality of this one was way above my expectations.

title: Great product and great results
text:
Searching for a safe and effective skin brightener is always my top priority because I have a never ending battle with skin discoloration and dark sunspots. I love the fact that this serum is gentle and does not contain the harsh chemicals that most skin lighteners do because I prefer using products that have natural and botanical ingredients as much as possible. This product comes in a dark amber dropper bottle which protects the product from sunlight exposure. It also contains Glycolic and Kojic Acids as the key ingredients which I believe will lead to clear and brighter looking skin. This serum keeps my skin smooth, shining and flake-free. It is not greasy and does not form a film. I have somewhat sensitive skin which is pone to irritation and redness, but this serum is very gentle without causing any breakouts or negative side effects. I believe it has been gradually improving my dull looking appearance by making the spots a bit lighter.

I use the product as directed after cleansing, toning my face and allowing some time to dry before topping with my regular moisturizer. This light weight clear serum not only applies smoothly and evenly, but it also has a fresh light scent that will dissipate after it dries. It has a liquid gel like texture which leaves my skin soft and smooth, not to mention it is also fast absorbing without any uncomfortable feeling and leaves my face quite moisturized. I have even started using it to lighten the sun spots on my hands and the results are impressive. Although I have not been using it for long, my skin tone has started to look more even and I have also noticed that some of my blemishes have cleared up along the way. My darker spots still exist, but they look much better and I can see some significant improvements of my lighter ones.

I am sure everyone's skin is different, but I have experienced zero sensitivity or dryness. I love how much clearer my skin looks throughout the day and my skin feels more balanced. My overall appearance is much brighter and smoother. The brown spots on my hands are slowly fading in under two weeks and I can say that I am really happy about it. In fact, everybody's skin type is different and the effects may not be the same or visible for everyone. I have used it twice a day for quite some time now and the brightening effect seems to be progressing. There is no miraculous or overnight whitening as such, but with gradual fading of sun spots, my face does appear clearer and even toned. This product does what it promises and lightens my dark spots. This is a great and reasonably priced dark spot corrector serum that I will definitely buy again and I feel quite confident to explore other products from the same line to further improve my skin conditions.

Disclosure: I purchased this dark spot corrector at a discount for my honest and unbiased review.

title: Good, but a word of caution for people with sensitive teeth
text:
The nice thing about this toothbrush is that it uses the same heads as most of Oral-B's other toothbrushes. This is a basic model, which probably cleans just as well as their other models. The battery lasted me about a week of twice a day brushing, and the battery indicator tells you when you'll need to recharge it a few brushing sessions in advance. Don't ignore it too long, because it takes about 18 hours to charge it fully, but charging it about an hour should be good enough for one brushing. The charger is small and doesn't take up much room in a drawer.

The small head really works well for cleaning the sides of your teeth and between them. Oral-B talks about the cupping action and it really works like the polishing tools most hygienists use. It even seemed to dig food particles stuck between my teeth(!), but you'll still want to floss where no toothbrush can reach. If you have gum issues, this may be the ideal toothbrush for you.

The dual clean head got my teeth acceptably clean faster, but it's noticeably bigger and the precision clean head worked better overall for me. It's nice that they included two different brush heads so you can see which you prefer.

Unfortunately, the slower pulsing action seems to irritate my teeth. A week or two after I started using this toothbrush, my molars started to ache. I ended up returning it and going back to my other Oral-B, whose head looks more like a normal toothbrush which vibrates up & down very quickly. It doesn't clean along the gum line quite as well, but seems to clean the grinding surfaces of molars slightly better.

Oral-B also sells softer toothbrush heads which people seem to like and may be better for my sensitive teeth.

I added another star for Amazon's good customer service and considering that most people don't seem to have sensitive teeth. In general, just about any electric toothbrush will do a much better job cleaning your teeth, removing plaque, etc., etc. - much better than a manual brush. Try one. If you don't like it, a different type may be better for you too.

It's not as close as a razor but to the naked eye you can't tell. It kind of feels like the stubble from a day old shave. But like I said I was impressed. You do have to go over an area several times but it didn't bother me.

There was no discomfort. There were only a couple times when it seemed to catch and the pinch was very minor. I used large circular or long sweeping motions and it was like getting a leg massage. You can do it while watching tv. I shaved on dry legs (which were extremely ashy so don't judge me) but I want to try it in the shower since it claims to be waterproof. I also love the attachments. I used the trimmer blade to do my bikini area.

The only drawbacks are A) The housing for the blades is hard to open to for cleaning, especially the middle blade. You have to twist it counterclockwise and lift. It's also hard to put back in place. B) The instructions for removing the attachments isn't clear. I was scared I was going to break the thing trying to get them off the unit (turns out you just pull them out with a little force and pop them in, no twisting).

All in all for $20, I would definitely recommend.

title: Great compact unit -- not as strong as others though
text:
Our last water flosser died -- so it was time for a replacement. This unit is VERY compact, I was actually shocked when it came because I thought there was no way it could fit in there. Lo and behold -- it did! Although this is a permanent fixture on our sink, it could easily travel with us if we went anywhere. Being a compact, travel-friendly water flosser I was surprised at how much volume it can hold. If you can't tell, I'm really impressed by the compact ability of this water flosser.

It comes with a variety of tips, enough to make this usable for a couple as my husband and I share it. It is very easy to use, the one call out if you have a more traditional water flosser is that this is a rechargeable unit! It comes with a charging cord (USB), but no base -- so you'll have to grab one of your existing ones and let this charge for about 8 hours -- so you can't use it straight out of the box.

The only complaint I have is that even at maximum pressure it is not as strong as our previous one. It does work well enough to get any extra stuff out of your teeth after brushing, however, it is not the strongest water flosser -- my husband would like something a bit more strong, but that is really the only complaint we have!

title: i wish i knew how to use ALL the brushes...
text:
I was so excited to receive this set. I already had a brush set from Mary Kay, that I love; but, I it only has 5 brushes.
Since I like to contour and highlight (subtly), I mostly needed brushes for this.
Researching sets produced a huge price range. One could spend upwards of $70.00, with comparable brush sets. Yikes!! This set is much more affordable. The brush handles are solid and bristles are firmly attached. Some brushes are softer than others.

So, if they are quality brushes and the price is reasonable, why am I only rating them 4 stars? I had no clue what each brush was for, and the internet wasn't very helpful:(
If the brushes had been labeled, or there had been an insert explaining the function/functions of each brush--it would have received 5 stars. Add pictures/diagrams for tips on use, even better. I would be willing to pay a little extra for an easy to clean roll-up case for the brushes. A girl needs to keep her brushes clean. That is a feature, I believe many look for. I travel a lot, so my roll up bag (for my other set) is essential.
As it is, Cosmopolitan magazine's website has an article on how to use different makeup brushes. It was helpful for a few of the brushes, which I now use everyday.

What I love:
*The sponges are fabulous for applying foundation and blending after you contour/highlight.
*The large, angled brush is great for applying blush, so it looks more natural.
*The large, pointed brush does a nice job, when adding bronzer to contour.
*The large, round brush is what I rely on for swirling on powder.
*The small, pointed brush is phenomenal at applying color at applying contour eye shadow.
* I use the small, tall bristled, rounded brush to blend the areas of shadow on my eyes that need softening.

What I didn't like:
*Obviously, not knowing what each brush is for.
*The eyeshadow? brushes use too much product and application is sparse. I believe it's because the bristles are stiffer than what I usually use.
*No case to keep them clean, which leads me to look for alternative solutions. Leaving them out in the air, exposed, is a bad idea. Think of the germs in the air, especially if you keep them on the bathroom sink. Eww! Bacteria grows quickly and can cause infections, such as pink eye.
User Tip: I use baby shampoo to wash my brushes. It is gentle on your brushes and it gets the job done.
I received this product at a discount, in exchange for my honest feedback and unbiased review.

title: Helps My Sensitive Skin
text:
My skin is ridiculously sensitive, so finding products that won't set off some kind of irritation, breakouts, etc., is nearly impossible. I hadn't used a cica cream before, but the reviews were positive enough that I wanted to give it a try.

The texture is interesting - it's less a cream and more like a gel that's almost runny. It absorbs fairly quickly into the skin and doesn't leave behind any kind of greasy residue. It does help with redness and dry patches, and at this point, it doesn't seem to cause breakouts.

I have to say, though, that I was hoping for longer-lasting, even cumulative results, because I apply this at night and right after I rinse my face off the next morning, it's almost like I never used the product at all. Maybe it's a matter of me having to use this twice a day (at least), but given the high price point for what is, in fact, a pretty small tube of product, I feel like I would go through the cream much too quickly that way.

Still, it does help a bit and doesn't seem to cause any issues, so this is one of the very few products that I can see myself continuing to use long-term.

title: 4/5 It's Not Bad....
text:
I've been using Bare Escentuals "Bare Minerals" mineral makeup since about 2002. I've tried other brands but till now I just didn't find anything I liked as much, let alone better. Lately though the BE makeup just hasn't been agreeing with my skin. I'm getting older and my skin is a bit more sensitive these days apparently. The one thing I never cared for with the BE makeup was their use of bismuth. Anything with bismuth it just makes my skin itch. I've been reading about the negatives of parabens too, and I decided I wanted to get away from that as much as I could.

BE doesn't have that but it does use bismuth, at least they did as of the last time I ordered a big kit. After perusing Amazon and reading ingredient lists I chose to try this kit. Mainly because of the fact that this makeup doesn't have any of that and reviews here already are mostly positive. Also because I liked the eye shadow colors in the trial kit. These are colors I'd use a lot so I didn't feel like I was wasting money on colors I'd never use just to get trials on everything else. The jars are about the size of a BE eyeshadow, a little smaller maybe. The brushes weren't bad but they are small. I put them in my purse kit. They're useful for that, but not for much else. But they're sturdy. They're not losing bristles and they seem fairly soft.

For the most part I like this makeup. It's about the same grind as the BE mineral makeup, feels a bit silkier to me actually. It smells about the same seems maybe a bit less noticeable, the smell. It blends as well, but doesn't feel quite as heavy. The finishing veil is good. I have combination skin and oil in my t-zone and it did a good job of keeping me matte all day. The foundation covers well and doesn't make my face itch at all. The bisque is okay but I don't think it's got quite the coverage of the BE bisque. I did have to use more of it to cover things the same way. I kind of wish this kit had come with sample jars of the colored concealers as I would have liked to have tried those combined with their bisque. I think it might have worked better with that combo. I'm admittedly at a point where a simple bisque concealer is probably not enough for me. I'm getting dark under eye areas and have some red I need to cover now and again.

Their "glow" mixed with the pink blush is my new blush. It's too much for me as a bronzer. I have very pale ivory skin and it just does not work for me all over. Just a little too much orange, a little too dark but it did work okay as blusher over the pink they send you. Combining both that gave me a blusher that worked well for me. The pink blush they give you is just way too light and frosted for me. It just doesn't show up at all. It was the one product in the kit I just did not care much for. I would definitely want a darker more mauve or cinnamon toned blush rather than this one. The pink on it's own is pretty useless. I had to combine the two or forget it. It didn't even look like I had any color on my cheeks.

The foundation colors are decent. Their Fair #1 is actually a near perfect match for me but I'd probably never use the Fair #2 unless it was combined with the Fair #1 maybe. My skin is never that dark, not even in Summer. But Fair #1 I must admit I like that one. It's hard for me to find a foundation that's fair enough that's not too yellow, but Fair #1 works well. Fair #2 is just a tad too dark and just a bit yellow for me.

Overall I'd have to say this kit was a positive experience except for a couple of colors being slightly off for me. I do plan on ordering a big kit but I'm also going to email them and ask if they might send a slightly darker blush and just the Fair #1 x2 instead since they're supposedly picking the cosmetics as they pack for you. Can't hurt to ask, and if they do then their "Fair" kit will work very well for me and I can see myself becoming a regular with this one. I did not expect this product to be as good as it is actually. It was a very pleasant surprise. I'm used to spending a lot more on the BE product. This is much less expensive and in some ways I think I actually like it better than BE so I probably won't be a BE customer much now that I've discovered this.

title: Only meant for gel polish! Works well when used correctly
text:
This is ONLY meant for GEL polish NOT for acrylic powder, dip powder, Poly gel, or builder gel. Why? I don’t know. I’m guessing whatever chemicals in it breakdown the gel polish won’t breakdown the acrylic powder, dip powder, Poly gel, or builder gel in the same way.

This works great! I have tried other gel polish remover before and they just don’t feel right on the nail. It’s hard to describe, but it’s just a weird feeling I get in my nail bed when I’ve applied them. I’ve been trying out different ones hoping to find one that doesn’t feel like that and works really well…I finally found one!

This is easy to use.
-USE NAIL FILE TO REMOVE TOP COAT. This step is important. A lot of people think this step isn’t necessary with a gel polish remover like this. That it’ll remove the top coat too. It might, I haven’t tried it. But, I’m guessing it wouldn’t do it as quickly and easily. Just take a nail file and lightly buff off the top coat. It doesn’t take much.
-Apply a thin coat of the gel polish remover just like you would any nail polish
-Let it sit for 3-8 minutes. It will start to crack/bubble.
-Take a cuticle pusher and use it to push off the nail polish. It should push off easily. You can always add another coat of the remover if it’s not fully off.

I found for me with 2 coats of gel polish on, it usually took me about 10 minutes from start to finish. So much easier than acetone or even a drill! As long as you remove the top coat by filing it off before applying this remover and give it time to work and soften the polish, it’s easy to scrape off!

As a side note, even though this says it’s not meant for acrylic powder, dip powder, builder gel, or Poly gels, I tried it with dip powder. It worked well but did take longer for it to crack/bubble and I had to do 2 coats of the remover. It also worked much better when it was a solid color dip powder and not a dip powder with glitter in it.

title: Good, with one Caveat
text:
I really like this shaver and I use it a lot. I write a lot of reviews on Amazon that are for fun only and not serious, but believe me, I am being serious here.

This shaver has lots of good features, and it definitely does pay for itself. I'm a guy who just likes having a crew cut, and this shaver is perfect for that. Why go to the store and pay $15 to have some stranger cut your hair (and have to waste your time waiting until they can get to you) when you can just buy this baby and do it yourself? Or better yet, have your significant other help you out and do it for you. It has already paid for itself several times over. (I like Setting 2, myself.)

Also very useful is the nose hair trimmer. This is not something that guys like to talk about very often but it happens to the best of us and there's no shame in trimming that unsightly growth out. This one is very useful. You just clip it in, turn it on, and jam that sucker up your nostril. Again, VERY useful.

The rest of the attachments were okay but not necessary, in my opinion.

So why 4 stars? Because of an accident that I had once with this thing, a manufacturer problem. I had started shaving my head and the power went out. Apparently it wasn't fully charged. So I was left with stripes of bald patches running down my hair, and it looked extremely bad.

I recharged it overnight, but had to go to work the next morning and didn't have time to finish the job before I left. So I had to go to work with my hair looking all nappy like I had been suffering from radiation fallout sickness or something. I had to hole up in my office all day, so I would not be seen.

This disaster could have been easily averted had the power supply on this thing been set up so that you can use the device while it is plugged in. Only it doesn't work that way. It is not set up to operate off of a power supply. It is only set up to operate off of its charge. So when it is plugged in, it is only charging the battery. If the battery is dead, then it won't turn on and you can't use it even when it is plugged in!

Whoever heard of such a crazy arrangement? This is totally unlike the other Norelco shaver (the 3-disc beard shaver). It makes me want to give it 1 star, but that would be unfair.

So basically here is my advice: Make sure that this thing is well-charged before you put it to your head. Otherwise, you may be sorry! Take it from somebody who has been there.

title: We Tried EVERYTHING To Get This To Work
text:
When it comes to styling devices, my family all has different preferences because we all have different hair. This looked like a really great product. Let's take a look..

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This comes in a nice box, well packed in a fancy presentation and comes with a little manual. The device has four buttons on it which are power, temp up or temp down or timer. The bent curling iron is supposed to be more handy to use.

MANUAL
The manual is bare bones. It looks fancy but never tells what temperature or time would be good to start with for different types of hair. That was very disappointing. It does tell how to basically press the buttons and what they are for, however.

HOW DID THIS PERFORM?
We tried this several times on various occasions. Each time, we set the temperature higher and higher until we were at the top temp but very few of the curls we tried making worked. The hair simply had a light bend in it. When using a different curling iron with each person, the hair looked great. Finally after trying for the last time today, we have determined that this curling iron just does not work. I am not sure if we got a bad one or what, but it just does not do hardly anything except leaving a partial bend in the hair no matter how we wind it.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Although a great concept, this curling iron did not seem to curl hair properly no matter what hair we used it on or how high or low the temperature was set.

MY RATING
TWO STARS. Great idea, just didn't work at all for us.

I bought this for my wife to help her keep her flat iron safe from damaging with heat and to tidy up the counter space. I should also note that I use this stand with her flat iron for safety when coupled with a smart plug to turn her iron on and off at specific times before she goes to work. I wanted to have her flat iron preheated for her when she was dressed for work and also to ensure she turned it off after she was done using it, as she is notorious for leaving it plugged in and worrying me about setting the house on fire.

Her flat iron is a Paul Mitchell something or other (about 1.25") and fits perfectly. The opening appears that it would hold up to a 1.5" flat iron depending on the exact dimensions. The plastic gets hot while her iron is in it, but I see no reason why it would melt or catch fire. I purposely tested it with her flat iron just sitting in the holder for 30 minutes, and while the plastic was hot to the touch (go figure her flat iron is set at 410 degrees ), it does not appear to be a safety or fire hazard.

My only complaint is that I cannot get the suction cups to stick to any smooth surface for more than 24 hours. I've tried smooth tile, the smooth granite counter, and the glass mirror for mounting surfaces. The suctions cups always fail within about a day no matter what I do to prepare the surface or the suction cups (i.e. rubbing alcohol, glass cleaner, soapy water, plain water). Once she figures out exactly how she likes it positioned and uses it that way for a while, I'll probably end up using the included anchor and screw to mount it to the wall for her.

title: Get the 130
text:
I ordered this wig in 10 inch, 180 density. I’ve had it for a little over 6 weeks. I cut mine more equal in the back, so it was more like a bob.

Pros
Very good quality hair. I’ve washed it a bunch, colored it three times (more on that further down), styled it with heat many, many times, and even slept in it a few times. It always goes right back to looking new.

Takes heat and can keep a curl.

The size of the cap is, in my opinion, perfect. It is big head friendly and long enough to go over the sideburn area in front of the ears. I’ve never owned a wig that fits me this well.

There’s basically no shedding, and it doesn’t have any matting or areas that tangle.

Very well executed ombré.

Pretty long life. I wear this a lot.

Cons
This wig is not cute out of the box. The curl that came in mine was honestly ugly. Thankfully it is not permanent. After the hair is washed and dried, it has a very nice slight natural wave.

This is not necessarily a con for me, but the lighter section is definitely brassy. I wanted mine orangey red, so this was a good starting point for me.

This wig does not dye well and the color will be mostly gone within a few washes.

The hair is not evenly distributed. I’d say the back half is 100% density, maybe 130. The hair on the lace is like no joke 400% density. There is so much hair on the lace. I’ve plucked and plucked and plucked and there’s no improvement. So the hair in the front is puffy because there’s so much hair. This wouldn’t even be entirely bad except that a lot of the hair on the lace is only 2-3 inches long so the thickness doesn’t follow through all the way down.

This is the biggest con. One of clips on the adjustable strap came broken, and I didn’t realize until I had started customizing it. Lesson learned there. I’m fine with doing some work on my wigs, so it’s not a huge deal. But someone else may not be comfortable doing so.

I give it three stars due to the weird hair distribution and broken clip. I would probably buy this wig again when this one dies. However, I would definitely recommend not paying extra for more density.

text:

Come to find out, there's a whole group of people that tend to talk about my hair and how cute it always is, the time I put into it, etc. I started dying laughing and said really guys, my hair isn't real, as I pulled it out. They were shocked! Apparently they have been jealous of my hair for awhile haha! Also, one was a hair dresser! And a good one! She never got more than3 feet from my head or I'd say she would have spotted something but still at 3 feet it Eben fooled her.
THERE ARE LITTLE TRICKS TO IT LOOKING FAKE AND REAL! Take the 2 seconds to do them! Take a mirror and look all around for threads sticking out. If it doesn't match perfect, cover up your poney rhat sticks out in the center. Fluff and fill holes. Tease little pieces if you need to to fill a spot.
As far as color, if you are a solid color you really need to match perfect. If you have highlights or multi colors in your hair you can be a bit off. Naturally if I pull up my hair the poney will only be blonde but my roots will be very dark. So as long as I match the dark, I can wear a piece with more or less blonde, more or less dark or all of either blonde or dark. Again just make sure the dark matches

title: AWESOME (and inexpensive)
text:
These polishes are AWESOME for the price. My polishes were a little thicker than the one Gelish polish I own (Red Roses), however even application was not a problem. The durability was about the same most drugstore gel polishes. I ended up taking off my polish on day 14 because I needed a change and don't like the look of a naked nail bed (not because of chipping). I used a darker color (see picture - taken on day 3 and again on day 14-with some flakies) and needed 3 coats to achieve complete opacity. Color pictured is from set 22, color #196. Polishes are easy to remove (cottonball soaked in acetone wrapped around the nail with foil for 10-15 minutes).
The downside is that these polishes ship from overseas, so can take several weeks to arrive. They are well packaged and I did not have any breakage during shipment. In my opinion, these polishes are worth the wait and will save you a ton of money on expanding your gel polish selection.

UPDATE 9/2015:
After using these polishes for several months, there are a couple more things that I wanted to comment on.
The pros: I still believe that for the price, you won't find better gel polish. The durability is excellent and the colors are beautiful.
The cons: the colors don't match exactly with the photos so if you're trying to match a color based on the photo, you will likely be disappointed. The pigment saturation is generally lower than in more expensive polishes. Meaning, while some are good two coaters, others may need up to 4 or even 5 coats (especially the microglitters in set #022 which tend to have a more jelly formula).
My conclusion is still the same, however. I will continue to buy more sets of this polish as I grow my collection.

Wrestling with this slippery wet bottle with my wet hands didn't seem to be working - I couldn't feel any give or clicks as I tried to twist the very small nozzle button in the wet - and without my glasses on I couldn't see if there were any markers or arrow directions....but I braced the slippery bottle as firmly as I could and kept trying until I suddenly noticed a stream of foamy soap coming out and dropping to the floor of the tub.
As I proceeded with my shower, I continued having challenges. This bottle has a VERY firm button. It wasn't actually locked, but my small 54 yr old female hands didn't have the strength to manage it at all (one handed). Especially as the bottle was wet and smooth and dang slippery! I ended up having to brace the bottle with one hand and push the button with the other - which left me with no palm available to catch the actual soap coming out. I wasted a bit of soap before I figure out I needed to twist the hand holding bottle to catch the stream of soap which let me catch about half.
There's definitely a design flaw in choosing that bottle and button dispenser!! It's very attractive but the tension spring for the dispenser button is crazy strong. Maybe they took the idea of masculine soap too far and have chosen bottles that can only be used by men with stronger hands too? Added with the smooth but hard bottle (metal doesn't provide any give when you squeeze hard) that becomes super slippery when it's wet (which is the expectation when taking a bath or shower) this doesn't seem very well thought out. Bad operations and marketing choices!

title: Ni-Cad battery dooms it
text:
I really wanted to love this trimmer. Especially given the hefty price tag. It trims as you would expect and the vacuum works well and is a must-have feature in my opinion.

Another must have feature is either Ni-Mh battery or the more expensive Lithium ion battery. This has Neither it is the bad/cheapo/old Ni-Cad (Nickel Cadmium) with all the memory effects and shortened life span that implies. For a device like this where you can't swap the battery yourself and you can't leave the job half done you will have to partially charge and then finish your trim. Then you will recharge it fully, boom instant battery memory and shortened life. Or maybe you re-charge it after every use? That may be even worse... I've been through this before, you are doomed to a useful life measured in months before the battery (and therefore the whole trimmer) craps out.

I researched on line and couldn't discover what type of battery it was so I went in person to my local WM and looked at the packaging, still no hint. So I bought it thinking they couldn't possibly sell it at such a high price point with such an unsuitable battery.

I got it home and found in the instructions that the battery is Ni-Cad and soldered into place and must be disposed of properly. I'll be returning it and looking for a different vacuum trimmer with a battery that will be useful for longer than a few months.

title: Super Thick formula, but it's great stuff!
text:
Okay so let me first say I didn't buy mine from Amazon. I bought mine through eSalon's Match-Up program (3 products per shipment for $30, the first month is $15) I ordered the Big Love Shampoo, Big Softie Conditioner and, Get Lifted Root Lift Spray. I have her fine thin hair so I am always on the lookout for products to boost volume without breaking the bank. I have tried all sorts of products, everything from Living Proof, to Nioxin, Aveda's Invati line, Redkin, Purology, etc. Now, I'm not saying the products from the other lines don't work, a lot of them are great, but they cal also be pretty pricey. I already use eSalon to color my hair (if you haven't tried them yet, you should) and their regular shampoo/conditioner packets they send along with your hair color are great (and smell amazing). But I need VOLUME, not southern beauty queen volume, but volume none the less. So! In comes Big Love & Big Softie. For $15 for my first order I couldn't say no. Both the shampoo and conditioner are SUPER thick. So thick I had a little trouble getting them to pump out of the bottles. I was worried that something so thick would just weigh my hair down and it would have been a waste of money. I WAS WRONG. The big test for me is "second day hair". Most volumizimg products do well the day you wash, and that's great. But, what about the next morning? The answer, NOPE. I'm on my second day hair as I wrote this and it still has some decent volume to it. I can't swear it's just the conditioner, but the shampoo/conditioner/root lifter combo worked really well. I would recommend it. Especially if you do eSalon's Match-Up. Three salon quality products, of your choice for $30 is nothing to stick your nose up at. Ill be ordering it again for sure, next time with their Volumizing mousse (just to give it a try too).

TL/DR: Give it a try, it's a very thick formula, but it works and it won't break the bank.

title: Versatile and comfortable
text:
Many times wearing a mask also comes with the discomfort that the elastic bands can cause to some one’s ears. I found that the Zelaxy Mask extenders do help with the comfort level.

The pack of Mask extenders I have contained 5 extenders; black, white, pink, green and blue. The Eagle (it has little ‘wings’ that the elastic strap wraps around) model that I have is made out of soft silicon which makes the extender comfortable to wear around a person’s head.

The extender is stretchy enough to get on fairly easily, it also has multiple ‘stops’ in order to control tightness of a mask and the extender is thick enough so it won’t snap under normal use.

The ‘standard’ way of wearing the extender, that being directly behind the ears, works fine. This extender is also versatile enough to allow the extender to be worn around the neck so that both elastic bands from the mask fall below the ear while still providing good support.

There is one unexpected issue; longer hair can sometimes complicate putting on the extender as longer hair can more easily get caught up in the ‘wings’.

The bottom-line is that, for me, the Zelaxy extenders are comfortable to wear and they do help make it more comfortable to wear a mask throughout the day.

title: Nice but could be made better
text:
This roller does indeed turn applying skin care products into a spa experience. Pop this baby in the fridge on hot summer days as a way to take your skin from tired to taut. Warm it up to help your skin absorb products more easily. It washes clean and doesn't absorb any of the products. The trouble comes from how it's put together. The metal caps that hold the rollers on each end of the wand/handle come off too easily. They aren't glued or crimped on, nor are the little metal caps snug fitting. Both ends where off when my roller arrived so I actually thought I had to assemble everything prior to each use. If I hold the roller up to where it's straight up and down, the roller that is facing the floor slides right off the handle. In a way this isn't a completely horrible thing since being able to disassemble the roller works better for travel. Just please be careful when opening your storage bag and pulling out the roller in case yours is the same way. If it were to fall onto a hard enough surface from a high enough height, the rollers could crack or shatter.

Aside from the poor craftsmanship, I do enjoy using this roller and not only for applying skincare products. Sticking the roller in the freezer for 20 minutes then using it on my face and neck when I am suffering from a migraine is a godsend. I recommend having two so that you can use one to battle your headache while the other one cools down. The rollers hold cold (or heat) for several minutes, and can be wonderful tools to help relieve pain from stuffed up sinuses as well as headaches. The little gua sha tool that is included is also wonderful for more than applying skin care products. Chilling the gua sha before use can help treat puffy eyes, headaches, small bruises, mosquito bites, foot massages, and so on. Both this and the roller are completely smooth - no rough edges or bumps.

Also included are a black velvet bag for storage, a handy booklet showing how to use both the roller and gua sha, and a hand written note thanking me for my purchase which is a really sweet gesture. All-in-all the tools are nice products, but for the price you'd think the manufacturers could afford glue to keep the rollers on the handle.

text:
I bought this product because I had gone to a new salon and forgot to ask for a clear glaze when I had my root touch up. I noticed that my hair color looked dull. I had gone through a home coloring period in my 20's that was not pretty. But, I read great reviews about this clear glaze. I still would not try to add or subtract color myself, but this just adds shine and manageability. I have fine hair and use Bumble & Bumble thickening shampoo & conditioner, which are miracle products
I didn't want to add anything that would make my hair limp. The first time I used the product, I followed directions exactly and left my conditioner on 3 minutes and the glaze on 3 minutes. And it was fabulous. Had my volume, but added smoothness (no flyaways) and shine. The second time I got busy & left my conditioner on about 10 minutes and the glaze on about 15. No bueno. My hair was stiff and flyaway. This time I repeated the first time and its all good. I only wash my hair about twice a week so I am putting it on wet, after conditioning, each time I wash. There are instructions for a once a week application in which you put it on dry hair and leave it on 20 minutes. I haven't tried that method. I am a believer in this product and will no long have to pay the added cost to have it done in the salon.,

title: weightless, non tacky, fully absorbs quickly, NO added fragrance, no scent
text:
I have Rosacea, specifically type 1 where I experience redness from flushing and visible veins (telangiectasias). Otherwise clear skin. While topicals won't really help the veins, I can use products that help even out skin tone where it is pink from flushing. Some products can initially make my skin red, then it calms down (especially if new). This ISNTREE Cica Relief Ampoule Duo Set has not irritated my skin. In fact, it has helped to minimize aggravated skin.

The serum is extremely light. I think the lightest weight product I have ever used. The bottles are small, and I feel like I am going through it quickly. I may be using too much, I dont know. I do apply to neck and chest as well as face. I already use a product with EGF (epidermal growth factor), and I thought that maybe in serum form it would feel like a more concentrated dose. I have no idea how much Isntree uses, but this product feels like the emphasis is on the Centella Asiatica Extract. That isn't necessarily a bad thing, I am just not sure yet what I think about the performance of this product for my skin. The two small bottles would be better as 1 bottle.

--super light weight
--absorbs instantly
--not tacky
--skin feels instantly smooth (I also use some on the back of my hands)
--I wouldn't use it alone as a moisturizer, especially if have dry skin (like me)
--gentle, doesn't aggravate my skin, but that very well could differ for everyone (esp those w/ damaged skin barrier)
--contains soothing centella asiatica extract
--contains EGF- worth doing some research to see the benefits and to discount myths.
--ingredients that can help build and maintain skin barrier. Especially important for those with skin conditions where they are exacerbated by a damaged skin barrier. Got super sensitive skin? work on repairing that skin barrier before anything else.
--NO added fragrance in ingredient list. No naturally occurring scent either. I cant detect any aroma.

My skin: mid 40s, smooth and clear (except for visible veins), leans dry. I follow this up with a moisturizing SPF (their sunscreens are great) or a moisturizer if using at night.

I dont think it is bad. I really just think it is ok. I would give it 3.5 stars if I could. For me it isn't quite a 4 star product, so I am going with the middle of the road rating of 3. Your experience will vary. I think it would be especially appealing to those who prefer a weightless non tacky Centella Asiatica product. While I have zero issues with this, I am not likely to repurchase it. I have preferred products, especially for EGFs. However, if I notice anything else-- good or bad, I will be sure to update. It can take at least 2 weeks for a product to show its effectiveness, and it can take that long for the skin to acclimate to a new product. I am a little early on writing this, but my skin is used to centella asiatica as well as EGFs, and with some Isntree products.

DMSO has a low toxicity rating and may very well be a “miracle” pain reliever and have many other beneficial uses, but its biggest plus is also its biggest minus—it quickly and super-effectively delivers substances through the skin and into the bloodstream, and magnifies or “potentiates” their effects. This can be beneficial in some situations, but potentially very harmful in others, and that’s likely why the research on DMSO is so contradictory.

DMSO’s super efficient through-the-skin delivery means that it has to be extremely pure to be safe. Any impurities or toxins present will be carried directly into the bloodstream. title: I must say that caring for my beard has really made it look much better than before
text:
I have been using beard products for a while now, may it be growth formulas or simple oils, I must say that caring for my beard has really made it look much better than before. As far as beard shampoo goes, I never really knew about this. I would simply use ordinary hair shampoo or even soap to wash my beard every time that I’d shower, but since I stumbled upon this, I thought to give it a try. Now for starters, this bottle is actually of a pretty decent size. It will definitely last a while if used carefully. Now the shampoo itself does its job. I have used for about 2-3 days now, and I can’t say that I have any complaints. I would give it 5 stars but there are 1-2 issues that weren’t all too convincing for me.

The smell of the product is “Bold Forest”. Now I don’t really know what that really means, but the smell doesn’t really convince me tooooo much. Sure, it’s something I can get used to, but compared to the amazing smell I receive from my beard oils, I was surely expecting for this smell to match it too. But that’s not a major issue I suppose, as long as your beard is A-OK! Another thing that wasn’t quite convincing was that you have to kinda be careful while applying the shampoo on your palm. Although the hole is small, a lot might come out so you got to be steady with that. Also, the shampoo isn’t the same as hair shampoo, it’s actually a bit gooey, which caught me by surprise, but then again, I didn’t really know what to expect when buying “beard shampoo”. Other than that, my beard these past few days has felt a bit softer and “fresher”, if I may. As far as dandruff and all goes, I’m sure that a beard shampoo is essential if you really want to grow your beard. I don’t have a huge beard myself, it’s actually a bit small. But everyone has to start somewhere, right? I use this product while showering (twice a day), and right after I shower, I towel-dry my beard and apply my beard oil (incase you were wondering). All in all, I definitely recommend this beard shampoo!

EZ Feet cleans MOST of the bottom of your foot and in between the toes, satisfactorily. With my size 12 foot, the REAR bottom of the foot is rather hard to clean with the EZ feet.

The bad: (as I see it) is that the EZ Feet doesn't clean any of the sides of your foot, being there's no bristles on the side, only on the bottom and the front part of the foot. I can't push my foot in far enough to get the rear BOTTOM of my size 12 foot. I have to wash most the top of my foot and all the sides of the foot after using the EZ Feet. It is easier cleaning my foot with the EZ Feet unit, ultimately.

EZ feet should positively add side bristles so the sides of the foot can be washed, and a larger footprint (or raise the top bristle armband slightly) so as to allow larger feet to clean the REAR bottom of the foot.

title: The only thing that holds my hair up properly
text:
I have long, very thick hair. My hair breaks heavy-duty ponytail holders regularly. My hair laughs at barrettes and clips. Every time I've had a professional updo for a formal event, the stylist has used multiple dozens of bobby pins to hold my hair in place. And I have never been able to do an updo myself and get it to stay in place, no matter how many bobby pins I use. My hair just spits them out, and the updo falls down. I'd even tried those Magic Grip curved plastic hairpins -- people claimed those held up long hair -- and if anything, they worked worse than regular bobby pins in my hair. (And yes, I used them right, first aiming them out of the bun and then twisting them around to tuck them into the bun.)

So I was skeptical when a friend recommended Spin Pins. I figured they would be another disappointment. But they are BRILLIANT.

It takes four Spin Pins to hold my hair in a bun (the package instructions say to use two, but they're written for people with normal amounts of hair). I literally just screw them into the bun so that they catch some of the hair that lies against my head, along with catching the bun itself. I figured out the best technique by my second try. I promise these aren't complicated to use. The instructions have pictures.

And once they're in, that bun stays until I take them out. I can walk, dance, shake my head around, and the bun will stay perfectly in place. I usually need to use a couple of bobby pins to tuck in a few stray ends here and there, but the Spin Pins hold the weight of my hair -- and believe me, my hair is heavy. I've made buns at the nape of my neck, on the back of my head, and on the top of my head, and all of them stay perfectly in place with these pins.

I've used them regularly for probably a year now, and they haven't bent or broken or anything, despite the large quantities of hair they are forced to hold up.

Don't panic too much about interlocking them (despite the dire package warnings). With four Spin Pins in my hair, they can't help but interlock a bit, but I have never had the slightest problem unscrewing them from my hair again. They also like to interlock in storage, but again, I've never had the slightest problem just unscrewing them from each other again.

I'm glad I was able to get the 3-pack, because now I have a couple of extras in case I lose one.

If you've never been able to get bobby pins to hold your hair up properly, do give Spin Pins a try.

title: Strong fragrance
text:
This was my first time trying shampoo or conditioner in bar form, and I had the opportunity to try both from this company's line of products. My first impressions were very positive - the ingredients looked clean and natural, as well as being cruelty-free and vegan, I love that it’s plastic free (both the lack of bottle and the packaging), and that the scent options were relatively gender neutral. The bars were a little smaller than I expected, but ergonomically they fit comfortably in the palm of my hand and don't seem to be shrinking too fast after a week or so of use. I'm glad that they have different colors, so that I can differentiate between my bar soap, shampoo, and conditioner!

My experience using them was pretty good. It felt odd at first as I've only ever used bottled products, but quickly got used to it and could definitely see myself using more bars in the future. I tried both running the conditioner bar down my hair and lathering it up a little in my hand and applying that way. Between the two, I felt that I got pretty good coverage and results. My hair felt less tangled and I was able to work a brush through pretty easily once I got out the shower. When my hair dried, it seemed softer and healthier looking than it had previously, and my curls had a little more life to them.

I only have two concerns - the first is that I'm struggling to find a place to put the bars in my shower where they won't get misted by water and disintegrate more quickly that way. The second is the smell. Although it's not unpleasant, it reminded me a little of a scented candle, and was very strong. Three different people commented on the smell of my hair that week, which is not something that usually happens to me. My husband thought that I smelled like cologne! I could see this being a pro or a con depending on how you feel about fragrances. Personally, I found it overwhelming as I'm more on the sensitive side to smells.

Overall, I would consider trying this or a similar product again in the future, but only with a less intense scent.

text:
I have never taken the time to actually review a product but I just had to for this one. Let me tell you a little bit about my skin condition and how this product has affected me.

I'm 26 years old with very fair skin. However, many of my high school/college years were spent in a tanning bed. I've always loved my skin when tan but when it finally sunk in that if I kept tanning I would look like a prune, I luckily stopped for good. However, I always hated the way my skin looked. Very blotchy, often dry, and I still get pimples at 26! I've tried every product under the sun and nothing, at least for me has lived up to its promises!

This product is truly amazing. When I first tried it, it stung my sensitive skin. I used it for about 2 weeks then stopped because I didn't think it was working. If you have acne prone skin, it will make you break out a little at first because all of those pimples will be forced to the surface. So I stopped using it. However, after reading all the good reviews, I decided to give it another shot. It's been about a month of using this product and boy have I seen drastic changes in my skin. My skin is 100 percent softer and smoother. Old acne scars that I had (my skin scars very easily) are lightening up and my complexion is much more even. And, the best part is, I get no more pimples so don't have to use drying products like benzoyl peroxide anymore!! My face is so smoothe throughout the day and it stays that way! It is truly amazing, but the trick is, you HAVE to give it about a month before you will truly see results! Be patient!!

Ok, for those with a similar skin condition to me, just want to let you know my skin care routine using this product.

Morning - wash with cetaphil daily cleanser, apply alpha hydroxy souffle, let dry then apply good moisturizer ( i use eucerine spf30) Make sure you use a noncomedogenic one with a good sunscreen!!

Evening - wash with plexion cleansing clothes (need prescription), apply alpha hydroxy souffle, then a good night cream ( i use neutrogena visibly even night cream and it's worked wonders)

I also take nicomide which is a vitamin my dermatologist prescribed for helping with acne.

Sorry this review is so long, but I just really wanted to offer my advice and let you know what has given me amazing results! If it wasn't for websites like this, I would never have known to purchase all of the products I use! I really hope this helps!!

title: Great cloth for removing makeup. Equal to the Makeup Eraser
text:
I love the idea of these makeup removing rags. It saves a lot of money to be able to buy one product that removes makeup, oil, and dirt without having to buy makeup wipes, cleanser, and all the other products that we spend money on to clean makeup off of our faces.
I will be comparing this product to the name brand Makeup Eraser http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B00KBPSUYC?psc=1&redirect=true&ref_=oh_aui_detailpage_o05_s00 that I bought off Amazon as well and have had since June 16th 2015 so I can see if they are the same of different.

Makeup Eraser Claims:

Makeup Eraser removes 100% of your makeup with just water.
Removes mascara including waterproof mascara in just seconds.
Cloth is approximately 7" wide x 16" long.
All natural, no chemicals, and machine washable.
Use up to 1000 times and everything comes clean;no stains and remains soft. Promotes healthy skin.

Makeup Remover Claims:

Reusable. Simply clean it in the wash for a brand new cloth, again and again.
Absolutely NO harsh chemicals on your face
Super soft material that is gentle on the skin
Clears away hard to remove makeup with less effort

Makeup Remover (purple) Pros and cons Vs. The Makeup Eraser (pink)
* Both cloths are soft and both sides feel the same as the other.
*The purple cloth is a tad bigger than the pink cloth which is nice.
* They both remove waterproof mascara easily along with other regular makeup.
* They both wash up the same.
* The makeup eraser feels thicker than the Makeup Remover but does not affect the makeup removers ability to remove makeup.
*The price is quite different. The Makeup Remover (purple) is around $13.00 and the Makeup Eraser is around $20.00 for pretty much the exact same thing.

If you are looking for a way to save money and want a cheaper version than the Makeup Eraser but performs the exact same, I would go with the Makeup remover. Save that extra money because this cloth performs the same thing as the Makeup Eraser.

* I was sent the makeup remover cloth at a discounted price for my ubiased review. I bought the Makeup Eraser at full price. All opinions and comparisons are my own.

Completely satisfied and even delighted!

title: Not just cotton and silk - contains polyester
text:
I won't say the product is necessarily bad, but I certainly do not like it and am not pleased with the disparity between the description and the actual product.

While the amazon page says these eye-covers are made of cotton and silk, the product packaging and tags both indicate the product is cotton, silk, AND polyester. I would not have bought these had I known this as my wife reacts to polyester. This just leaves me with another useless set of eye covers that my wife can't use.

Also, I personally find these uncomfortable. The silk is nothing like my nice soft silk shirts. It is still a shiny and smooth fabric, yet also an uncomfortably rough (I'm not sure how better to describe it -- it's like running your skin over tiny closely spaced wires), fabric that is very hot to wear on your face. Furthermore, I found that I got a headache both times I tried wearing these.

My wife has previously made some passable eye-covers out of cotton socks that we both can wear -- and I find significantly more comfortable. She's suggested that maybe she can try taking these apart and using the straps and cotton parts and making better cotton-sock eye-covers. I'm skeptical and am considering returning these. I'm certainly not happy.

If you like the really slick-abrasive feeling fabrics like cheap silks or cheap satins, and if you don't have any issue with the polyester in these, I can't really see a problem with them. They could probably benefit from being a bit larger, but they're 'pillowy'-enough (for lack of a better word) to block out most of the light and fill in the gaps around the edges. Mystery as to why they give me a headache, but they've enough good reviews that it can't be common.

I'm giving them 2 stars because I think the description is misleading and I don't like them, but also because I think a more moderate rating would get this lost among rating of people who are happy with the item. I always read some of the reviews and I wish I'd seen a review like this before purchasing.

title: The cute isn't a cover up...
text:
A good number of times when you see something as cute as this little bee-esque slicker brush, the manufacturer is covering up a shoddy product and hoping the "awwww, it's SO CUUUUUUTE!!!!!" factor will overwhelm the buyer so much they don't notice and/or care when the product gives up the ghost after only a few uses. So yes, choosing this slicker based on looks probably wasn't the smartest of choices, but in the end it seems to be a good one. This slicker brush is rather nice (and should be for the $20 price tag). It's comfortable to hold. There is weight to it so this doesn't feel flimsy to where the grooming head will break off if you try to comb out a snarl in your pet's fur, or like the body is the thinnest molded plastic they could get away with so it didn't break just removing it from the packaging. Another plus is the end of the tines are tipped/dipped in protective little drops of plastic so the sharp metal ends don't harm your pet. I've always avoided those slickers as they seem like some kind of torture device - how can bare metal ends be comfortable when raked over skin?

For taking care of loose hair, this did a bang up job on our two Maine Coons, including the one who absolutely loathes - and I mean to the depths of H.E. double hockey sticks with a side of utter disgust - being brushed. She was adopted from the shelter as an abused kitty from the home of an older cat hoarder, and whatever happened during her first six years of life there were traumatic enough that she will do her best to eviscerate anyone who tries to groom her long fur beyond the area of her neck. She actually lets us very gently use this on the rest of her back and legs and tail for around 45-60 seconds before flipping out, and that's a big improvement! Who knows, maybe she's as amused by the itty bitty bee antenna as we are, but this is the first slicker brush (even with the safety tipped teeth) she's let us use on her back, sides, and legs. The other Maine Coon (a big chonker of a guy) lays on his back with his legs stretched out and purrs like a race car when he gets groomed, so it's not a surprise that he loves this slicker as well. Cleaning the hair out is easy. Just press the button, the plastic disk pushes up, and the hair is forced off of the tines for easy removal. A few of the finer hairs may stick to the plastic or around the tines, but nothing major. When the slicker gets dirty between the base and the underside of the plastic disk, one of those super skinny reusable straw scrubby brushes and a bit of dish soap does the trick. We clip a wooden clothespin on either side of the plastic disk to keep it raised so the tines can air dry and not rust from trapped moisture. Since the tines all seem to be securely anchored to the base of the slicker head, we aren't too concerned about one being pulled out while trying to work through a tangle. It's still a good idea to check the tines every so often to make sure they are all there, none are loose, and that none of the little safety tips at the end of the tines have come off.

The only thing that could improve this slicker is a price reduction. A pair of googly eyes wouldn't hurt, either.

title: It's okay.
text:
.

Wow, it looks like I'm part of a small minority here! I'm happy that this product works for all the 5- and 4-star reviewers. For me...meh.

For starters, this feels greasy on my skin and takes longer than other moisturizers to absorb. Certainly, it is an "okay" moisturizer, hence the three stars. ("It's okay.") But for me, it's sure nothing to write home about.

I very much like the flip-top tube -- very quick and easy to open and dispense with one hand. The texture is nice. And I do appreciate the absence of scent. But an hour after I've applied it, my face feels no different than itI did before I put it on.

Having said that, I will say that I have researched the use and effects of ceramide on skin, and it does seem that, in certain strengths and when used with certain other ingredients, ceremides can help skin retain moisture. So, this product will work for some people. It just doesn't do much for me.

This product is not overly expensive, which helps, but there are a number of lower-priced moisturizers that I believe most people would find just as good as (or perhaps better than) this one. I can't recommend it as a great moisturizer, and I honestly don't know how it gets such terrific views, but that's the nature of skin care: what works for some doesn't work for others. I just can't see this one as being any kind of a magic bullet.

I can use the other epilator in all the delicate nooks and crannies, and have no fear of rashes, nicks, or bleeding. This one, on the other hand, has left me with some pretty nasty cuts in places that I won't mention. The obvious solution to the problem is to make sure you only use it on short hair, and to hold the skin very taut, before going over it. title: Not A Bad Little Eyebrow Kit!
text: I ordered this dark brown Eyebrow Stamping Kit to see if it would be any better than using the standard eyebrow pencil.  Now, granted I have barely any eyebrows due to hypothyroidism, so finding something that looks natural is key.  I love this little kit.  It comes in a very handy little plastic zip lock bag which includes, the brow powder, 24 eyebrow stencils, and 4 eyebrow/eyelash brushes.  It was a bit difficult sorting through all 24 stencils but I narrowed it down to 4 initially, then down from there to 3, then 2, then 1.  On my right eyebrow(your left in the 4th pic), I did my eyebrow with the standard eyebrow pencil how I usually shape it.  I thought by doing one to compare to, it might make it easier to find the closest shape to what I do.  After finally selecting the stencil I was going to use, it was easy to peel it off the paper and apply to my skin/eyebrow.  I may have stretched it a little, I am not sure.  The brow powder applicator doesn't twist or push up.  It just has powder in the tip automatically.  Oh, I forgot to mention that on the back of the stencil box, there are instructions.  So, I kind of dabbed the brow powder on, but I do think it helps if you have eyebrow hairs for it to cling to in the first place!  I do at the start, but my ends are gone!  The brow powder is a bit loose and a small amount fell over the sink.  I then peeled the stencil off(was easy and didn't hurt).  I show the immediate results in pic 7.  In my opinion, it was a bit thick(I'm more "old school" and like my eyebrows thin), so I took a wet tissue and wiped a bit away and made it more narrow.  I also used one of the eyebrow/eyelash brushes to feather it out a little.  Then my final results are in pic 8.  I would say NOT BAD.  From far away it does look more natural than the pencil shaped one which is thinner and more precise.  Natural brows are not like that!  I will say though, it is not exactly "water proof". text: I tried using this after 30 days of using Walmart's eyelid scrub towelettes. The Walmart eyelid scrub towelettes have the same ingredients as the OCuSOFT LID SCRUB ORIGINAL PRE-MOISTENED PADS but are about 30% cheaper and much larger in size. After that, I wipe down the eyelashes and eyelids with a small cotton pad soaked in saline water solution, the stuff that comes in a bottle for rinsing out contact lenses. This does a good job of clearing the OUST solution from my eyes because the tea tree oil in the solution does sting a little (not much) and you want to make sure you completely rinse it out -- no pain no gain if you want kill those mites and clean your eyelash pores. title: My skin went from dry/dehydrated to oily after using this toner 😔
text:
The sedum extract in this essence was quite intriguing to me. As someone with chronically dry, sometimes dehydrated skin I thought this toner could help me. "Sedum is a succulent leaf known for its intense hydration, vitamins & mineral level. It holds more hydration than watermelon and is rich in phytoestrogen that further boosts hydration and improves the skin condition." When I read that, I thought this sounded like the recipe for perfect skin, but every time I use this essence my face turns super oily. I have never experienced this kind of change from any of the hydrating essences I own.

The scent on this is light, clean, and fresh, very herbal. You should be aware that this product is fragranced with natural fruit oils & extracts. A few minutes after application though, the scent dissipates quickly. My skin is crazy reactive & very sensitive, but I did not experience any adverse reactions to the ingredients used in this essence.

There was also a generous amount of samples from Celimax included with this toner. 😀 They sent 2 Noni ampoules, 3 serum packettes, and 2 AHA/BHA exfoliating/brightening pads (labeled for underarms, but can be used elsewhere). Korean brands are so very gracious with samples! Thank you, Celimax! ❤

Both the package & bottle both come safety sealed. The bottle is of nice size (150ml) and features a shaker style spout for easy dispensing. I pour a small amount of the essence into my hands, then pat into the skin after cleansing. Then I apply my serums & moisturizer.

Though I don't find this product to be a particularly good fit for my skin right now (during the hot & humid Florida summer heat, when my oil production is already at it's peak), I think this essence may work better for me in the winter. I do think it's a nice product, so it still gets a 4 star rating from me.

title: Excellent hand cream
text:
UPDATE - 09/30/16 ========================================
Still loving this moisturizer and just ordered another package. This stuff goes on well, absorbs quickly into the skin and doesn't leave a greasy feeling! My skin feels truly moisturized. I love using it on my hands and feet before bedtime, this way it really absorbs into my skin overnight.
Love it, love it, love it!

========================================================
Not many people know this, or give it another thought sometimes - anything you put on your skin gets absorbed through the skin and ends up in the blood stream. This is why I am rather careful when picking my skin care products. I have been staying away from most hand creams for a while now just because for the most part there's at least a few potential carcinogens lurking among the ingredients. Even though the big famous brand creams make your skin feel wonderful the question is if the trade off is worth it.

Unfortunately, even so called organic products aren't always that safe. Provided, manufacturers of this goodness are disclosing all the ingredients on the label (and not hiding anything) this cream looks safe enough to eat. Therefore, I have been happily slathering it all over my hands (and any other body parts needing additional moisture) in the past few weeks and I am quite pleased with the results.

This white fluffy goodness feels surprisingly light and absorbs quickly into the skin. I must admit, it is a tad thinner in texture than I had expected but on the other hand this lightness ensures there's no oily residue left on your hands. The cream has no scent whatsoever which is a definite positive for those who are sensitive or don't particularly appreciate scented products. I'm adding a drop of essential oil of my choice (whatever I feel like that day) when I apply the cream if I feel like smelling something nice. Basically this cream is your blank canvas and leaves much room for creativity.

One thing I would probably change about this product is the packaging. (At least maybe as an option for buyers to choose from) I really think that tubes are better for hand creams - way easier to dispense and so much more hygienic (sticking your fingers into the container doesn't really help keep it germ free). Other than that I am happy to give this product my approval.

I purchased this product at a discount in exchange for an honest and unbiased review, all opinions are based on my own personal experience with the product.
