title: So weird!
text:
I never thought I would sing praise to a sponge made from konjac root. The first time I had heard of these type of sponges I thought it sounded kind of weird, yet interesting. The only experiences I have had with konjac root was when I would ingest it, in pill form, to aid in a fuller feeling belly. Gotta love diet hacks. Anyways, an offer came around for me to try a set of discounted sponges for review. I thought, “these seem crazy and awkward. I must try them!”

The second I opened up the package to take a look my daughter gasped and said, “you got those? Can I have one? I have been wanting one so bad but they are expensive.” Well, with this brand, you get the same exact product that are sold in stores for insane amounts of dollars, for a screaming, affordable price. Two sponges come in a box so I handed one over to her. She was so excited.   I have slightly oily, sensitive and acne prone skin. My daughter has very oily and is also acne prone. This sponge cleanses and exfoliates without over drying. There is something about the way it holds water that feels really soft, gentle, yet effective. It is the direct opposite of what it feels like when it is dry - hard and scratchy. It does take some time to incorporate enough water into it, for the sponge to fully absorb the water, to be soft enough to use on your face. As you rub it across your skin it feels good and soft. I use light pressure while I use it for light exfoliation. I like the flat end for my forehead, cheeks and neck and the rounded end for my chin, nose, sides of nose and cheeks (near the side of my nose) and between my eyebrows. I feel like I am able to get a good cleansing in all areas. I use a small amount of cleanser. I use my hands to apply my cleanser and then use the sponge. My face is way smoother and makeup glides on nicely. My daughter reports the same thing. She loves the sponge and its benefits it gives.

My only slight criticism is the attached string. I do not see how it can be secure for long but who am I to know? I have never used one of these. It just feels a little like one pull could rip through the sponge. I do appreciate it having a string, though. It makes it super easy to hang-dry the sponge so all sides are/can be exposed to well circulated air. It does take quite a while for it to dry. Still, it is the only sponge of its kind and as weird as it is, it works.

text: I used these for the first time last night and had very few goofs.  I have only three nails that have bubbles and that's only because I let go of the form too soon.  You should keep steady pressure on it for about 20-30 seconds before you let go and take off the excess.  I also started to leave it alone for about ten seconds before I popped it off.  I am NOT a nail tech, but I have done my own acrylics the old way two or three times.  Let me tell you I will never do it the old way again!  There are NO bumps or ridges including where the white tips were put on.  I used the clear acrylic this time instead of the pink and clear so I could figure out how to do it first.  If you look close you can see that even when you are holding pressure on the nail, there is space for the form to do the actual "molding".  I got mine at Sally Beauty supply in a kit that included everything you need (acrylic liquid, powder, tools, etc.)  for $35.  It was cheaper than buying everything separately.  On the box it says it can do up to like 15 sets or something.  Definitely recommend it.

title: Helps to detangle my wet hair in the shower but not as good as my Heeta brush
text:
These brushes are actually like eight combs strung together. I had to set the extra piece that comes with each brush to separate the tines. It was not easy to get the bar across the "combs" but eventually I managed. There are only two places the bar should be put and that is where the holes are on the back of the "brush." I assembled these brushes on the lower holes. My biggest issue with these brushes is that there are only two holes to lock the bar in place when I prefer four holes like my Heeta detangling brush (product number B0836XT7J8 since the Amazon embedded links are not working).

Once this is assembled, it glides through the hair and detangles. It works well on dry hair but even better on wet hair. I love the hard tines as it is like getting a massage on the scalp. The handle provides an okay grip but I would have preferred a silicone grip. Since the combs are separated, this brush can act as a vent brush for blow drying even though it is not of circular design. Hair can be removed easily since the tines are flat with no "ball" tip.

The only reason I rated this three stars is because of the hard time I had assembling the rod in place on each one, the lack of four holes for a secure fit, and the lack of silicone grip on the handle. Otherwise they work well. The current price of $8.99 is reasonable for two detanglers.

text: Keratin’s make the hair smoother (NOT STRAIGHT), shinier, and frizzy free for up to 8 months depending on the strength of the product. Keratin treatments rebound the keratin in your hair so that they are all put back into place. There are a lot of steps but don’t get discouraged because they’re quiet simple. To start of give 2 good shampoos with a clarifying shampoo (specifically the keratin complex one, then towel dry and blow dry the unconditioned hair. Once fully dry, make small sections and apply the treatment from roots to ends and comb through with a fine tooth comb to make sure hair is fully saturated. Let that sit for 30 minutes then blow dry again without washing out the product. Once fully dry the final step will be to straighten the hair with a flatiron so the keratin will set in your hair. After you’re completely done you won’t be able to wash your hair for up to 3 days depending on the strength in the solution.

title: Super cute AND functional!
text:
With 4 kitties who share our home- two of which are super fluffy and all four are super 'sheddy' - I'm always on the hunt for ways to manage the fur tubleweeds that roll through our home! I ordered this brush because....well....I had nothing to lose! And boy - I was happily surprised!

Pros:
* The brushing area is nice size - it allows me to brush a large area at one time, which is key when dealing with kitties who don't love to be brushed.

* The bristles have tiny rubber tips, which is a small detail that makes a huge difference! This little 'bumper' seems to be much more appealing to our older kitties - perhaps their skin is more sensitive or fragile. Also, for our younger more rambunctious crew, it's not unusual to find minor 'battle wounds' (don't worry, nothing serious and always in good fun). Having this little rubber tip protector prevents from tearing off any scabs as they heal.

* It works! The 'self cleaning' aspect of this brush DOES work! With a wide variety of fur lengths and textures in our 'pack', I can attest to the fact that it catches it all, making it so much easier to keep clean. No more digging into the spikey needley prongs, ruining your fingers as you try to fish out all the pieces of fur! Hooray!

Cons:
* This isn't TRULY a con, but rather a small detail that would have made this tool even better....a cushioned brush. Several brushes that we've liked have 'cushioned' brush heads (where the bristles attach). This allows the brush to contour better to the kitty's body. That's the only thing I can think of that would have made this brush better.

Overall, this cute brush earns 15 paws of approval from our Pack! (One is a tripawd....)

If you find this review helpful, please let us know!

title: Perfect for beginners with small hands.
text:
I’ve tried a couple e-files in the past, all of them have been a bit too bulky for me to properly hold. I always wondered how everyone managed to use e-files with ease, and didn’t fumble because they didn’t have a good grip. It always felt like I didn’t have a good hold of the e-files and it just made them hard to use properly. I never really thought I had small hands until a friend of mine suggested I look into slimmer e-files. Honestly, it seemed the slimmer e-files were more expensive so I just gave up and stuck to handle filing everything. Until recently when I came across this e-file... It’s been game changing for me.

The first thing I will say is it is SLIM and small. THANK GOODNESS! It’s so easy to hold and properly use. Which leads me to the next great thing about this e-file, the fact that it is small and slim doesn’t effect its performance at all. This things is very strong and fast. As many of you know, you’re not supposed to use your e-file on it’s fastest speed unless you absolutely need to. So when this e-file gets the job done even on its slowest setting, it’s just amazing. I’ve tried e-files that had little power, so I’m thrilled that this one is so powerful. There’s a dial on the cord that controls the speed. There’s also a switch that goes from off to on, and reverse. It also comes with two sets of bits. Both come in their own containers. You also get a dusting brush and two extra bags of sanding bands. Considering some bands can be completely shot after one full set of nails, it’s nice to be supplied with extra! To change out the bits, you just put the metal post of the bit into the hole, and push it down until you feel it’s securely in it. You don’t have to twist or lock anything into place. The bits stay securely in place while filing despite not actually being locked in place. To remove the bit, just pull it out (it doesn’t come out easily so you will have to pull a little).

I’m still very much a beginner with e-files because I never had luck with any before this one, so I can honestly say that this e-file is perfect for beginners. I had no issues with learning how to use it and Controlling it. It’s made filing and shaping my nails so much easier. I use builder gels, gel polish and dip powders. This e-file has worked wonderfully with all of those, when it come to filing, shaping or taking product off. It’s been wonderful and game changing for me. I love it and would recommend it to everyone.

The only downfall is it is powered by a USB cord. The outlet plug is not supplied so you will need one of those, but everyone has them laying around somewhere (iPhone outlet plugs). The instructions give a wattage requirement for the plug. I use my iPhone one and have had luck with that. But that Means you need to be by an outlet or power cord. Switching from hand to hand can be annoying with a cord in the way. I do think I will be upgrading to a wireless e-file down the road. But for now, this is great.

title: Makes Washing Your Hands When You Are On The Go  Convenient And Fun
text: Disney And Touchland Hydrating Hand Sanitizer makes washing your hands when you are on the go convenient and fun. The set includes four 1fl oz bottles with 500 sprays. The presentation package is truly adorable and instantly gift ready. The hand sanitizer is slightly larger than a gift card but looks like an iPod or simple cell phone with a drawing of Mickey Mouse that reminds me of an Andy Warhol sketch. There are four different fragrances: Pure Lavender Scented, Aloe You Scented, Citrus Grove Scented, and Unscented. One press of a button releases a fine mist. I ended up pressing the button two times to get a proper coverage per hand. The fragrances of the three are bright and strong. My hands felt clean, did not have any stickiness or residue remaining, with a faint perfume from the fragrance. I found that after multiple uses, I did not experience any dry or rough skin despite the product including ethyl alcohol. One negative I have is that there is no way to lock the button to keep it from accidentally spraying when in a bag, backpack, or purse. Another negative is that these adorable hand sanitizer containers cannot be refilled. Given the sturdiness of the product container and how cute it is, I really wish this was an option. When it comes to price, it is high but justifiable based on the sturdiness of the product container, the quality of the hand sanitizer, and of course acknowledging the tie in to Mickey Mouse.  The product is vegan and cruelty free. It is Made in the USA. I really love these hand sanitizers for not only their look but how well they cleaned my hands. These are a must have for any Mickey fan.

title: The Negative Reviews Don't Do This Shaver Justice ⚖
text: I will start out by saying that I did not purchase my Wahl Smart Shaver from Amazon since I found it cheaper elsewhere.  With that being said, I'd like to comment based on my usage of this shaver thus far. First of all, I just recently used a Braun 9 series shaver. Unfortunately, this shaver does not have a cleaning/charging station but I'm not convinced that is a deal breaker. I am also puzzeld by some of the negative reviews here. I literally turned on both shavers, and in my honest opinion, the Wahl was slightly quieter. The Wahl does have some similarities to a Remington shaver. For example, the two inner blades resemble the Remington as does the sound of the shaver. The outter foil seems to be very unique to the Wahl brand. So in using the Wahl Smart Shaver, I found it to be very effective on 2+ days of beard growth as it went through the facial hair with ease. The shaver head is thinner which in my opinion allowed me to get closer than both Braun and Remington shavers. The hypoallergenic foils that have symmetrical and asymmetrical foil slots provided me with an exceptionally close and clean shave. Almost 12 hours after my initial shave, and I barely felt any stubble growth. To me that speaks volumes about this shaver. I was very skeptical about trying this shaver based on the prior reviews here and the fact that the Wahl shaver was cheaper than the leading brands (e.g., Braun, Panasonic, Remington, etc..). However, for now I'm glad I took a chance and decided to give the Wahl Smart Shaver a chance. Also, if you view other sites, this shaver ranks significantly higher than it does amongst Amazon shoppers. Not sure why this is but something doesn't make sense to me. So if you want a clean shave and also don't want to go into debt buying a shaver, I suggest giving this shaver a try. By the way I'm retired military and this would've been nice to use while I was active duty. Lastly, if you're still not convinced, please take into account that Wahl guarantees this shaver for five (5) years. Take a chance. You'll be glad you did!

The masks come well sealed as a set inside another bag. My set did not come with instructions for use. The back of the packet only has ingredient information. I had to look on the Amazon product page and with my phone I could not read the instructions on the one picture they have of it- as it was blurry. So from what I think I read you use these masks daily for 20-30 minutes. 1 star was taken off for lack of instructions- there's no real reason it couldn't have been on the packet itself. I'll say when I buy these at home treatments I tend to lean more towards mud masks, gels, and lotions, the biocellulose masks are never very comfortable or fit my oval face well. The eye holes are never big enough and the masks never sit right. This is sadly no exception, I would keep pushing on it while I wore it so another star taken there. Now, the effects: they were pretty good, my face definitely had a glow about it when I removed them. Likely over time and with extended use my skin would lighten more. So at least what they said is very true. They are pricey but if they do what they say and this is the result you want they would be worth the cost. title: fun colors, easy application with a little prep
text:
These are some fun colors from INH. They are not for the timid. I had used an INH semi-permanent color (pink quartz) before and knew what to expect. This time I tried Wish Bear that is a green blue color. I have curly hair and usually just add color to a few curls around my face, but this time I was feeling crazy and did a full head application. I had mixed results with the different levels of dark and light in my hair. I would say that the image with the different results based on your starting color are accurate. If you have a mix of levels in your hair then you will get a mixed look, too. This will look best (and get you that prettiest Care Bear color) on a pre bleached platinum level hair.

Application is easy if you prep you surfaces (old towels are great) and wear gloves during application. I followed the instructions and had washed the night before so I was applying to dry unconditioned hair. I didn't use a bowl and a brush. I just used my fingers and was careful to section and saturate. I left it on for an hour because I know from using semi-permanent colors over the last year that I need longer than the usual 30 minutes. On pastel shades I usually go an hour to two hours. If you are unsure then do a strand test before you go all over crazy like I did.

My hair felt great afterwards. It is conditioning. It very much reminds me of the expensive brand that starts with an O. Would I get this particular color again? For me, probably not. I did not have light enough hair to get the Care Bear look. I also don't think the green in the blue green works on me. Would I get this brand again? I sure would.

title: Norelco 1050CC pros and cons
text:
I bought the Norelco 1050CC (shaver and cleaning system). Here is what I like and don't like:

Pros:
-Shaved great for an electric
-Cleaned up well in the automatic cleaner
-I know others complained but I had less razor burn than other shavers

Cons:
-Beard/Sideburn trimmer is ineffective and located in a very poor place.
-The angle of the trimmer seems awkward to use.
-MOST OF ALL the recharging system is a complete disappointment. Basically you start the cleaning cycle and have to wait around to unplug the shaver so that the battery doesn't get ruined. It even tells you in the instructions not to leave it plugged in if your battery is charged--which is 90 percent of the time. VERY VERY stupid.

I would have kept this razor otherwise if it wasn't for the illogical charging/cleaning system. You pretty much have to choose between waiting 5 minutes watching your razor clean itself every morning or be okay with ruining your battery. It is enough of an inconvenience that I am returning it and going back to my Norelco quadra trac.

title: Good slip, highly recommended
text:
I was given the opportunity to review Keeva's tee tree oil shampoo and fell in love with it right after first use. I wasn't around to when they were selecting reviewers for their conditioner but now that it's available for purchase I'm glade to say I've bought it for full sale price being 20 USD. Like it's shampoo counterpart the bottle is 28oz total.

Texture: White and creamy
Scent: Pleasant and definitely not reeking of tea tree oil like it's shampoo sister
Slip: Slip is a product's ability to allow one to detangle hair effectively and not need to use too much product to do so. For the amount I used which is pretty standard across the board with all conditioners I've tried, this conditioner is rated at 5/5 for slip
Moisture: Next to none but that isn't a real issue due to most of the oils being found in Keeva's tea tree oil shampoo
Standout Ingredients: hydrolyzed keratin ( protein ), argania spinose ( Moroccan argon oil ), cetearyl alchol ( fatty alcohol )

Cons:
Cocos nucifera ( Coconut Oil ) isn't listed as an ingredient, however it is featured as an ingredient on the front of the bottle.
Melaleuca alternifolia ( Tea Tree Oil ) isn't listed as an ingredient either.
Both of these oils is on the front of the bottle being featured however, the product doesn't list the oils as ingredients.

Overall, I believe this to be a quality conditioner even better than some brands found in salons. Price of the bottle is reasonable for the quantity received. This conditioner does provide one with good slip and it doesn't leave hair feeling heavy or weighted down after rinsing. I feel that when used with it's sister shampoo, you'll benefit from this conditioner most .

title: Halloween Or Messing Around Okay, But Serious Wear, Not So Much
text:
I have been working with wigs for quite a few years now. One thing I know is a good quality vs not so great quality wig. Let's take a look at this one.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?

HAIR
This wig has some great hair. the colors are definitely platinum white and what I would call light auburn base hairs. The white hairs are about 1/3 or so longer than the auburn hairs. There is a nice kink to the hairs.

THICKNESS
That is where this wig is sadly lacking. At the top, the wefts of hair are way too far apart. The lace in the cap is a very light butter colored yellow. The hair is not too thin, but it is not quite thick enough to cover hair below. Yes, this comes with a nylon cap, but it just is not comfortable with those. If you have dark hair it will definitely show the bright colored lace and elastics through the wig when the wind blows.

BANGS/STYLE
That is where this wig is just not practical unless you don't mind looking stupid for a party or Halloween. The bangs are WAY too long for anyone to wear. That usually would not be a problem, but what you will get instead of the cool light ends on the entire head is chopped bang that is bland looking and then these white cool looking ends around the head. The bangs are best cut painstakingly so that the auburn is cut way shorter (about 2/3) than the white hairs. That takes a lot of time but worth the effort. Then you have to cut them at a staggered manner.

Other than the bangs being hard to trim so you can at least function with this wig on, the overall style is fabulous. I love how it falls and looks while on the head.

ELASTIC BANDS
Inside the wig, there are elastic bands with hooks to help hold the wig on the head. You might want to take them down to the spot you like it in as the hooks have a tendency to come undone during wearing.

WHAT I WANT IN A WIG
Believe it or not, I would actually wear a wig like this with the right outfit, and not to be silly either. I prefer wigs that look authentic,, and can be worn realistically as well as for fun.

1. I have to be able to see out of it
2. I have to be able to wear it comfortably without fussing
3. I want it to not have my real hair showing
4. I want it to look realistic
5. I want it to last for quite a few wearings

DOES THIS WIG PASS THE TEST?
I am giving this wig THREE stars because it is hard to wear and see. In order to trim this in a realistic manner, I have to take a LOT of time and that takes stars off for me. I happen to love the style and coloring, so I am wiling to put the work into it, but honestly, I think it should be a bit shorter in the bangs area since it is so hard to trim and keep it looking real. Also, the wefting on the top is just a bit too widely spaced. I wish also that the cap was made with light auburn lace and elastic instead of the icy yellow colors.

THE BOTTOM LINE
If you want to wear this for fun, it will be hard to see and hard to trim and not look silly in this. It is comfortable and the style is epic, but there will be work required. You can bandana it to help, but it still will look a bit floppy unless trimmed a little bit in the bangs/fringe area. I like this, but it takes work to wear and not look silly for me.

MY RATING
THREE STARS. The trimming of the bangs is VERY time consuming since we only have one shot at it and if it is screwed up, then the wig is toast. I wish there was more hair on top and that the lace cap did not show as easily. A darker cap underneath (light auburn color) would have been much nicer with this. I will still use this, but it could have been a bit nicer with small inexpensive changes.

title: Not too oily, but it does feel like a film
text:
I've tried to transition from chemical based sun screens to more mineral based. The main issue I ran into was that they're super oily (not what I want on my face all day). I read reviews that this one would absorb better, and (bonus) act like a primer. All of that seems to be true, however 2 complaints. One tactile, and one visual.
Perhaps it's a side effect of the mineral aspect, but I can feel this sunscreen on my skin. Not as an oil slick in the crevasse of my face, but rather as a layer permeated into the surface of my skin. It doesn't simply wash off at the end of the day, and requires a somewhat exfoliating wash. I've been getting away with mild cleansers and a good face cloth wipedown.

Visually, it does blend in with my (super pale) skin after a few minutes wait. However it also catches on any dry patches (forehead, nose, etc.) and looks a little... unpleasant on close inspection. I'm inclined to believe this is an aspect of the primer element. I don't normally wear primer, or foundation. So maybe I'm just uninitiated and this kind of reaction is normal. It's definitely not my favorite thing, but it is relatively minor.

So far it's working, and I feel good about what I'm putting on my skin and it's environmental impact. Those are major pluses in it's favor. :D

*Update*
after revamping my skincare routine I find I like this sunscreen more and more. It was catching on any rough spots on my skin, but with a improved moisturizing routine that hasn't been a problem. Instead I feel like it acts as a light primer and it's more than enough "makeup" to get me through the day. You do still want to be sure to wash it off in the evening. But that's all sunscreens. I like that this not only gives me protection, but also evens out my skin tone and lightly covers any blemishes. It's not a replacement for foundation. But if you're like me and usually go bare face, it feels just a little extra nice.

text: I have extremely sensitive and dry skin. I only used about the size of a new pencil eraser and that was more than I needed.  After a couple of hours I noticed that my left hand still looked like I had applied lotion which was a nice change.  By the end of the day, the top of my hand and the skin at the base of my thumb were still looking good.  This was pretty amazing since I must have washed my hands a dozen or more times.  I decided to go with the face today.  Again I used about the size of a new pencil eraser and that covered my whole face.  It felt good and I did not feel like I needed to add any oil to my cheeks on top of it.  Its been a good 6 hours and they still feel like they did when I first applied the cream.  Also, no redness - that is a HUGE plus.  I am really happy I took the chance to test this product.  I like that it works well and that I can give it an honest good review.

If you haven’t been using makeup primer, then you’re really missing out.

Whether you wear a full face of makeup everyday or you prefer to keep it simple with BB cream and tinted lip balm, makeup primer is a godsend when trying to combat shine or create a smooth base for foundation.

Yet, many people often skip this step because they believe they don’t really need it, are unsure of how to use it or don’t think it’s worth the investment. However, using primer underneath your makeup will make everything last longer, whether that’s on your skin or in your cosmetics bag. We asked two beauty experts to discuss the ins and outs of primer and why it’s a must-have. Here’s the deal.

Makeup primer is a base for foundation or face makeup that allows it to go on smoother and last longer.

Formulas are available in cream, gel and powder. While moisturizer softens skin, editorial and celebrity makeup artist Stephen Dimmick points out that primer prepares skin for your favorite tinted moisturizer or foundation, giving it something to hold onto so it lasts throughout the day.

Many makeup primers are formulated with silicone-based polymers like dimethicone because of their ultra-smoothing effects. But for those who struggle with cystic acne and other skin conditions, do a patch test or check with a medical professional before use, as there have been reports of allergic reactions to dimethicone.

Physicians Formula’s celebrity makeup artist Joanna Schlip adds that makeup primers can also help smooth any fine lines, wrinkles or large pores. If you are searching for a face primer to help color-correct rosacea or conceal acne spots, Schlip’s go-to is this light green primer as that hue cancels out redness.

Primers are even available just for your eyelids to prevent creasing. “I’d recommend pairing a primer with extra long-wear [eyeshadow or eyeliner] formulas for a look that will really stay put,” says Schlip. If you have oilier eylids, Dimmick advises that you use a mattifying eyelid primer.

Using your fingertips to apply makeup primer allows you to really work the product into your skin.

Schlip thinks it’s best to apply primer with fingertips for areas larger than a quarter. “If only using for small areas, I’d recommend a brush. I like to use a concealer or lip brush for this,” she said. This spot-treat technique gives the look of a more natural finish, according to Schlip.

Taking this routine a step further, Dimmick considers the process “an exercise for the face.” He explains that massaging primer onto skin with fingertips helps “to get the blood flowing underneath.” We’ll consider that the next time we’re meditating while putting on makeup.

Primer is a life-saver for getting your makeup to stay-put in extreme weather.

If you live, visit or plan on traveling anywhere that experiences hot and humid or cold and dry temperatures, Schlip suggests having primer handy to help your makeup wear longer. However, Dimmick advocates for using primer year-round. “No matter what the weather is like outside, this extra step will save you a lot of time and effort.”

Primer can even be worn on its own.
Love the fresh no-makeup look but want to look a bit more polished than when you first woke up? Primer is your answer. The product can be worn on your eyelids and double as a light eyeshadow, or it can serve as a lighter alternative to foundation.

title: Best Hair Removal Experience EVER
text:
I have tried and owned it all: razors, electric razor, the original Epilady back more than 25 years ago, the Smooth Away system, Nair, and a really nice hot wax kit. I am very sensitive to pain, but my desire to be done with hassling with hair and mess overrode that. I expected less from this epilator than it has delivered. Yes, there is what I would call discomfort with the first and most ambitious hair removal, but I suggest that you do use the "massaging" head with it. That DOES work for a first timer. I now prefer the regular attachment for efficiency, but the massager is great on the remaining sensitive areas. I am flabbergasted at how many hairs it finds. A GREAT feature is the "Smart Light" that shows me the tiniest hairs. Very satisfying to watch them disappear as the epilator goes over them. It is also a very easy to clean device! I ran out of hairs to epilate (got a little addicted to the perfection of the process), so am now waiting it out. I have had smooth, smooth legs for DAYS. Worth every cent of the 119 dollars I spent. (Note: I've not tried it in the shower yet, as I'm happy about being able to set out a towel and watch tv and have a snack while I do this thing. You are not trapped in the bathroom.)

Tips: If some hairs are shorter than 2 mm and just can't get picked up, they are not visible in any case. Wait a day, and the epilator will get them. DO exfoliate. I recommend the "bath gloves" that you can get at the grocery store, but the Body Shop has terrific exfoliating bath gloves. If a hair is stubbornly being missed, be sure to stretch the skin tight right at that area, and try again.

• It’s nice to hold and use. It’s kinda heavy and big, because it’s made cheaply. But that actually makes it easier to hold =)

title: Beautiful Razor
text: I had never even heard of SHASH prior to my seeing this razor here on Amazon. Like most, I had been looking at Parker, Merkur, Vikings Blade, Earnest James, etc. to replace my nine year-old Parker 96R razor. BTW, the Parker 96R is still working perfectly, and the only wear and tear can be seen on the black handle. I also made the change from a butterfly razor to the more classic three-piece razor. For some reason, I thought I would never buy any razor that wasn't a butterfly type. Then it slowly dawned on me that the three-piece style ain't rocket science to put together. And, sure enough, after receiving this SHASH Dean Collection razor, I have learned it's almost as easy as the butterfly style. Plus, you get a very tight and secure closure when you screw the head piece(s) & blade to the handle. I am using Wilkinson blades, and only because I like them - this razor, of course, can use any DE razor blade. In fact, this razor comes with a generous supply of 30 Astra blades which I will try at some point. All in all, I am very pleased and impressed with this SHASH razor and its craftsmanship. Hopefully it will last another nine years with no need for replacement like my old, trusty Parker 96R. (BTW, check out the difference in the underside of the two razors. Notice how the SHASH underside is an upward arc, whereas the Parker 96R and the majority of DE razors are a downward arc. I notice that the upward arc gently pulls up the skin and hair immediately prior to cutting with the blade, resulting in a more pronounced "sound" of cutting. Sounds crazy I know, but it's true. In any case, a BBS shave results.) The length of this razor is 4 3/8".

CONS

* some liquid leaks too.

This product will be good for lotion, toothpaste or shampoo/conditioner coz they have thicker consistency. But be aware that scents leaks. The reason why I gave it 3 stars is because I can’t use it for the purpose I got it for (hand sanitizers)

text:
I bought the 8040x a couple of days ago and even I am surprised at how impressed I am with the shaver. I have always been a reader of reviews on Amazon and this is but my second review. This product makes me want to recommend it to everyone I see. Wow!! First, let me tell you about the shavers I have had.

My past shavers: I have had a Braun Synchro (lost with luggage on an international trip), a Norelco Reflex that I absolutely hated (but still hung on to for emergencies) and a Braun Activator 8595 (with Clean N Charge station) that I had till recently and absolutely loved. My Braun Activator (which I had for the past 3 years) broke when it slipped from my hand last week. Hence, I was in the market for a new shaver and thought I will research the shavers available since I was going to spend some money.

My new 8040X: I used my old Norelco Reflex for a week on a temporary basis till I bought a better model and absolutely hated it. It made my skin all red. As I was researching I came across the 8040X on Amazon and was intrigued by the idea of a wet shaver (having used only foil dry ones thus far). I tried it out in the shower for the past couple of days and I must say it has absolutely blown me away. It is so convenient, and the smoothest shave I have had in several years (as good as a Mach 3 shave that I stopped years ago). My wife was super impressed and to quote another review on this site....my cheeks AND I MUST EMPHASIZE even my neck, chin feel like "Baby's bottoms". The lotion that comes along with the shaver is awesome and goes along really well with the Nivea after shave lotion that I was already used to. Cleaning is a breeze...just hold it under water and run the motor for 30 secs. No more Clean and Charge Refills (boy are they expensive)

For the past several years I have been held hostage by the Braun company consumables (Clean and Charge solutions). It is a great relief that I found a shaver that wont hold me hostage like that, save for a little bit of moisturizing lotion that goes in the shaver (you dont really need a lot if you shave in the shower or by the sink). I am planning on buying one each for both my brothers as well as my father in law. Wonderful shaver and very well worth the money.

I have no intention of returning this shaver (I bought it thinking that I will try it for 3 weeks). Go out and buy this model, save your money and do not buy the 8060...dispensing the lotion into the shaver is really easy.

I will try and refresh this review in the next few weeks.

AS PROMISED ---- UPDATED APRIL 2008 --- AFTER 6 WEEKS OF USE

It has been at least 5-6 weeks since I bought the shaver and not surprisingly, I have not returned it to Philips. This is a great shaver. I have tried using it in the shower as well at the sink.

After having read complaints about the cost of consumables that come with this shaver, I decided to put it to the test. I began by trying Edge shaving gel prior to shaving with terrible results. It resulted in a very sticky shave....not good at all. I then decided to try a small travel pack of Nivea shaving gel.... and believe it or not....it worked like a charm....as good as the shaving conditioner. Apply a very small amount and do not lather it up vigorously...just a thin film.

Here is what I do nowadays..... I apply very little of the Nivea shaving GEL (not conditioner) and apply gently, do not lather up heavily. I use the shaver with little or no conditioner and it works just as well either in the shower or at the sink. Very little irritation and smooth effective shave. Also, applying the gel on your face prior to shaving prevents spraying of debris on and around your basin.

If there is anything I do not like about this shaver, it is the power and speed of the motor. While I cannot attest or comment on previous Coolskin models, that I have never owned, I can say that I can live with the power and speed of this shaver for several reasons. It is smooth, does not irritate your skin (which is extremely important for me after having experienced other shavers and razors) and easy to use. Go get one and if possible try getting it at one of your local stores like Bed Bath Beyond or Linens n things with a 20% off coupon.

title: An expensive mixed bag
text:
There are only a few reviews on Castle Forbes' Special Reserve Neroli. A couple are on here, a few randomly online. You have to dig for them. So if you're reading this, you're more of a fragrance lover than the average Tommy Bahama fan. Put simply, CF Neroli is not a popular EDP, nor is the brand. You have to know some things about fragrance and have a specific knowledge about neroli itself, to have come searching for Castle Forbes version. This is how I came to know this brand and EDP myself.
My view is that it's not worth the cost of 160USD. That's a lot of money for a 3.4oz. bottle. CF has a nice brand image, the EDP presentation is great, and the quality of the materials used are outstanding. However, the scent alone falls short.
Neroli Reserve starts out wonderfully: crisp orange and neroli, combined with greens like pine, grass and hedges. You feel like you're at the beach, sitting just where the sand dunes meet a lush forest. This lasts for about 20 minutes. Then the "woody/musky" basenotes kick in, and this is where CF got it wrong. It deteriorates into a powdery, barbershop, very British scent. It's something your grandmother (not grandfather) would have worn if she lived in London in 1865. Designer houses today try and replicate this a bit, usually just producing a floraly, loud, baby powder vibe (see MDCI Invasion Barbare). This basenote scent is what then dominates for the next 10 hours, more if you've sprayed any arm/chest hair. The woods aren't masculine woods, just faint tree bark really.
The EDP strength is phenomenal; this stuff lasts. The only problem is whether or not you like to smell like a woman, particularly a powderpuff with flowers. I do get some faint whiffs of neroli, but it's overpowered by the floral powder. I would not recommend this for a man, and unfortunately, would recommend Tom Ford's Neroli Portofino over this. A different vibe for sure (more aquatic), but TF's neroli sustains.
Overall, 3 of 5 stars just because the ingredients are so good, but the scent isn't as much neroli as it is the musky amber that CF used. Bummer.

title: Moisturizing and smells great
text:
The packaging on this product is SO cute. It looks like yogurt in a yogurt container but on the side of the container it warns you "do not eat". It is quite tempting. It looks so creamy and smells lovely too.

The actual product itself also looks like a thick yogurt texture. The scent is quite light and not overbearing, which I like. The hairgurt goes on smoothly and my hair does feel much softer after having used it. I still do need to use product on my hair since it does tend to frizz up when I air dry it. I don't think it's a one-stop solution to frizzless hair, but it's a good quality hair masque with a great scent. I didn't feel like it left a lot of residue and my hair wasn't sticky like with some other masks.

I also appreciate that the mask is free from a lot of chemicals and sulfates. I feel better knowing it's a more natural, moisturizing product. It is rather on the expensive side, but it does come with two separate containers so you the freshness lasts longer than if you got one big tub. Overall, I like this product.

text:
I don't usually write reviews unless I'm reminded by some incentive email, but I had a hard time picking the dude out cologne, so I figured maybe this would help someone. Plus, I love solid colognes.
These are cute in that they definitely follow a wintery theme. Their subtlety is on point. The price is reasonable, so if he doesn't like one or two of them, that's fine. I took one star away because they are a little weird--and I wanted more vanilla, (literally, I was hoping Snow Leopard would have more vanilla). Here is my take on these:
Snow Leopard: Clean, crisp. Smells like dude just took a shower, and is now eating a candy cane in the shower steam. So at first, it's like: why? And where's the vanilla?
Woodland Ranger: Crisp, clean. Smells like a really fresh Christmas tree...and also that shower steam.
Uncle Jack: WTF. Smells like you are hugging a very drunk man in brand new leather jacket...who also just took a shower. Don't wear too much if you're driving. It's interesting tho, and one of the stronger scents.
Barista: Sweet, nutty. My personal fave; I'm probably giving him this one early. Smells like forgetting all your problems as you walk into a coffee house, where they make drinks with whipped cream and coco dust. Remember Barney's Coffee?
All in all, these are subtle yet manly, interesting yet familiar...srsly...I wonder if Uncle Jack has a name's sake. I hope he was a happy drunk.

After a week of use, on the older models you can see they need thorough cleaning as residue accumulates at the cutting  edge. This can only be done with a brush, AFTER you remove the blade. The Arcitec doesn't allow you to do this. No amount of rinsing in the water will clean the Arcitec heads. Those who say "cleans easily" don't realize that rinsing the cutting head only cleans it superficially. Also as others noted the razor will not hold the whiskers when shaving and will make a mess. text: I have very fair, very sensitive skin that is prone to itching and rashes.  Most bars of soap (and by most I mean 99%) are too strong for my skin so I am on the constant lookout for a product that I can use as a shower gel.  I asked myself "Who else has sensitive skin besides me?"  BABIES!!!  So I turned to looking for products created for a baby's skin. title: It works and is not messy if you follow directions!
text: I am a firm believer in alternative medicine and non-toxic, organic cleaning substances; this is one of the reasons I was intrigued by this product. I'd already been aware of the benefits of activated charcoal for other uses, so why not use it to remove toxins in the mouth? I'd read many of the positive and encouraging Amazon reviews before purchasing it from my local health food store, and do not regret this purchase for one moment. Even though I've only used it twice, thus far, my teeth already look a bit whiter and feel cleaner than with any other product I've ever used. I was initially concerned about the "messiness", but there are specific directions provided to minimize the mess. A scoop is provided for those such as I, who prefer not to dip a wet brush into the container, but there's a better option. I have a set of small-increment measuring spoons (pinch, hint, dash, smidgeon), one which scoops out the perfect amount to sprinkle onto a wet toothbrush. This worked perfectly the first time I used it with no spills in the sink. You only need a tiny amount. I then "followed the directions" and kept my lips closed while brushing for the maximum two-minutes and keeping my mouth close to the sink drain. The directions also state to NOT "spit" it out, but rather allow it to fall out of your mouth, and use your hand to transfer running water to your mouth for rinsing. The small amount of charcoal residue left in the sink cleans up quickly and easily. So if you use a small enough amount, stay close to the drain, keep your lips closed, and refrain from spitting, this should be a pleasant and satisfying experience. So far, I highly recommend it!

title: My cat lost his everloving mind...
text:
I wanted something small for grooming my short-hair cat & this was the best I could find. I'm glad I gave it a try!
It has a narrow metal comb, which works like every other comb, but it's sized right for a cat - no more stabbing him in the shoulders & haunches.
The second comb, with curved fingers, is what really makes this brush a winner. The teeth are plastic, so they're soft. My cat lost his mind when I started brushing him with it. I've never heard him purr so loud. He even made muffins. He never makes muffins. I have to hide the brush because, when he sees it, he starts patting me & looking at the brush. It's adorable. And slightly terrifying (no cat should be that smart).
There are a few downsides to the plastic comb. First, it doesn't hold the hair it knocks loose, so you have to follow each stroke of the brush with your hand to pick up all the loose hair. Second, it electrifies the cat. Every loose hair that you fail to catch floats up & sticks to you, until you look like Cousin It. And the cat looks ridiculous with such static-y fur - I've learned to keep a spray bottle or bowl or water nearby to kill the static.
Even with these drawbacks, I love this brush, if only for the joy it brings my cat.

title: An All-Natural Pain Neutralizer that gets 2 Thumbs Up in our experiences and home
text:
Let me first of all say that Pain is the body's way of telling you that something is wrong, and that you should respond with a treatment that behooves the problem. Don't expect this product to miraculously heal something that is broken or badly sprained. However, you may have good success temporarily "erasing" the pain from over-use of muscles or whatever, and may allow you to be able to sleep when that is not possible without having applied it. As you heal when you're sleeping, this can be a real advantage.
The body can quickly learn to expect a continuation of pain from a minor problem, and it will linger on and on, even becoming chronic as you change your posture or gait to accommodate the ache or pain. My experience has been that if you can reduce the pain even temporarily (especially) in acute situations, it may break the cycle and never return. People we have spoken with have also experienced relief with chronic aches and pains.
In addition, some users have reported that it is effective with masking the pain of fibromyalgia.
Some reviewers here have complained about the smell - duh - it's from the natural oils. I think it is a pleasant smell, but it is a bit oily, so if you put it on before going to bed, give it some time to soak in, and cover it to reduce the amount that transfers to your sheets. You may also want to use less than more and will find that a little goes a long way. And - oh yes- it won't cause you to fail a drug test as many OTC remedies do.
I have used this product personally for more than 10 years, have given it to older family members, and given dozens of the towelettes to strangers who were in dire need of quick relief - never with a complaint. I strongly recommend it with the above caveats.
One size doesn't fit all, but if you are one of the vast majority that are not allergic or bothered by any of the natural oils used in its manufacture, you may find comfort and relief in what it can do for you.

title: Pretty amazing...
text:
I've been using this razor since it arrived, approximately 2 weeks ago, and thinking long and hard about the score I'd give it. I actually intended to give it 4/5, the reason being that, while it's an excellent razor, the price point is rather high. In the end, though, I'm so impressed that I really need to give it a full five stars in spite of the price, with the caveat that you may want to take a look at one of the less expensive, stripped-down models; this one is the flagship, but all the models should be similarly excellent (please bear in mind this is the only one I've used).

And excellent it is. While my feelings have already been summed up in the opening paragraph, read on for similarly styled (but moderate) hyperbole.

I've never gotten such a good shave with an electric razor. Norelco does recommend that you give the razor a full 21 days of your time exclusively (i.e. not shaving with anything else) before making a judgment. I haven't had the luxury of giving it a full 21 days, as I need to get my review in; however, I've already adjusted to it so well that I can't imagine going back to my old razors. It will only get better as I get more used to it, although I'm perfectly satisfied at this point and unsure if it could get any better.

Not only do I use it to shave my face (which is obviously what it was designed for, and it does a great job), I use it to shave my head. It's not going to give you as close a shave as a traditional razor, but it's also not going to scrape against your skin like a traditional razor. You'll also save money on shaving cream (the only extra expense is buying a new razor "head" for it yearly, the price of which I am uninformed of). It works "dry". This is nice for me, as it takes a lot of cream to shave both my face and my scalp, and it does, in fact, do a decent job on my head. It's a little stubbly, even right after shaving, but honestly the only thing that would do a better job would be a blade, and that's a difficult way to shave (I was previously using a Headblade). If it can shave a head, where my hair was very thick, I imagine it would be adequate for even the bushiest of beards, and, again, it's designed for faces, not heads.

If you look at the features list, you'll see that this model is full of bells and whistles. Truthfully, they are mostly extras you could live without; the lower-end models would likely be just fine, so I strongly suggest examining them as a money-saving alternative. The meter that shows you how many minutes of the charge are remaining is sort of handy, the icon that lights to remind you to clean it is somewhat useful, but to say they're necessary would be a grave overstatement. In fact, the "wash me" icon lights up after basically every use, so its necessity is particularly dubious. (As a side note, it's marvelously easy to clean.)

In the end, the product does receive my highest recommendation. I think if you tried it out, you'd be pleased, and even if you had to send it back and didn't like it after three weeks via their guarantee (it does take time for your skin to adjust), there would be little time/money wasted. I would, however, encourage you to check out the lower-end models. Ultimately, even the high price point wasn't enough for me to downgrade to four stars. I'm normally quite critical.

text:
The frosted glass looks good. The color of the plastic and silicone parts is darker than in photos, though. Judging from the website it's supposed to be off-white, actually called "classic linen," but the ones they sent out seem to be more beige. If that doesn't suit, there's also a "midnight blue" color available, which is a sort of medium gray blue judging from the photos (which may or may not be reliable).

Or you can take the silicone skirt off this--it's made so it's removable, good for occasional cleaning--and replace the push top with whatever color you want. It's a standard size. I think it looks better without the skirt even with the beige top. Just be careful not to break the bottle. It feels pretty sturdy.

The scent of the soap is lavender with citrus. (Not coconut--that's in the photo because it's where some of the saponified oil comes from.)

It washes well, doesn't leave any noticeable residue for me, though I suppose the aloe juice is intended to moisturize some.

It comes oddly over-packaged but in cardboard that can be recycled or biodegraded.

The ingredients given at the website are:

Saponified coconut oil, saponified olive oil, potassium soap, aloe juice, citric acid, sodium chloride (table salt), natural essential oil blend, vitamin E.

It's not clear why potassium soap is listed separately from the saponified oils, since that's what potassium soap is, oils turned into soap by the addition of potassium hydroxide (potash).

title: Clean & lube your blades while running
text:
I am not a beautician or barber, just someone with 2 dogs needing regular clipping. I remember seeing this product or a similar one in barbershops where my Dad would go to get a haircut. It was in a good-sized flatish round jar and the barber would dip the tip and bottom of his clippers in it while running and they would come out shiny and hair free. Now the jar looked like a pot of disease waiting to get passed on to the next customer as it had floating bits of hair and residue from who knows what.

I had been cleaning and oiling my clipper blades after each grooming and using a coolant on them during clipping to keep the blade's surface from getting too hot. Cleaning the blades afterwards never seemed to get all the hair from between the teeth even using a tooth brush and sliding the two blades back and forth. This stuff really CLEANS all the hair off and you can hear that the blades are better lubricated by the reduced noise. I do wipe them quickly so as not to drip any of the H42 onto the dog. They are shining and humming pleasantly after dipping them into this stuff. I will continue to buy this product as I feel it will extend the life of my clippers and make for a better cutting blade.

Now for the down side and why I took off one star. This stuff still comes in the good sized flatish round "tub-like" container and is seems intended that you dip the blades (not the motor, just the blade tips and bottom) into the whole container full and continue to reuse this stuff over multiple cuts. I don't care if it is Virucidal and Anti-bacterial, that seems like a really unclean way to use this. I solve this problem by pouring a small amount into another container (at least 1/4 inch deep) and dip my clippers in that. I discard the stuff after each groom. Unfortunately the container it comes in does not pour without dripping and yes, you use more of this stuff using my method. I continue to use oil and coolant, but this stuff truly cleans off the bits that get between the teeth and seems to get the blades running much smoother. I do recommend this product, but not for using the reservoir full repeatedly over several cuts or clippings. That method just doesn't sound like a healthy way to go. So if you use clippers on humans or dogs, I feel this product may be of use to you.

title: Powder gives light wash of color. Good for someone who doesn’t need too much.
text:
A little while back I got an eyebrow stamp kit like this and loved it! The only thing I wished was that the eyebrow stamp was a little thinner. When I saw this kit and saw the stamp looked a lot thinner than the one I had, I had to try it!

This comes with the brow stamp, 24 brow stencils, and 4 spoolie brushes.

Theres a whopping 24 eyebrow stencils included in this kit! That’s crazy! So, I’m sure most everyone can find a shape that they like for their brows among these stencils. Unlike most kits that have brow stencils like these, these have adhesive backing that sticks to you. Most kits I’ve gotten like these the stencils are plastic, so reusable. I like that they stick because you don’t have to worry about holding them perfectly in place while also trying to use the stamp to fill in your brows and worry about it moving some. But, I don’t like that they aren’t really reusable like this since once you pull off the backing and stick them on, they won’t stick anymore.

The first time I tried a brow powder stamping kit I wasn’t expecting much. I kind of expected this to make ugly, thick, blocky looking eyebrows. But, this actually works great! The product in the stamp is powder, so it creates a nice, light color, and you can dab more to build it up if you want. Once you use the spoolie, it looks pretty natural. You can also add pencil to if you wanted.

I don’t have thick brows, but I don’t have extremely sparse brows. My brows are thinner, where you can see skin poking through, but there’s basically an even amount of hair all the way across. I used to just leave my brows be, but when I do a full face of makeup I do feel like my brows need a little something. So, I started doing my brows. I usually do a little tinted brow gel. It usually gives enough tint to make them look a little fuller and complete, but not so much where they look too thick. I feel like since I’m just starting to do my brows, whenever I have them filled completely I think they look too thick and weird 😂 So, I like a middle area. So, using this stamp works well for me. If I’m doing full glam, I like to apply it to get a kind of light wash of color. Then, I’ll kind of go over the tail a little with some more powder to darken it a little more. Then, I’ll take a brow pencil and do a few kind of hair like strokes in the front. Sometimes I’ll go in and do some brow gel if I feel they need more defined. This fills them out nicely, makes them look complete, but doesn’t make them look too dark or full. If I am doing a more natural look, I’ll just use the brow powder in the stamp. I do feel that there isn’t a ton of product that comes out and I’m not sure how much product is in the stamp. I don’t mind that not a lot comes out, I actually prefer it. But, if you wanted more product, it might be kind of annoying for you.

Overall, I think this is a nice little set! It is a nice way to try different brow shapes to see what you like for yourself. The product works well. The brow powder looks natural and lasts nicely in the brows. I would definitely recommend this for someone who isn’t sure about their brow shape - what they like best on their face, what shape works best, how to fill in brows, etc. This set will help with those things! If you’re someone that just likes a little wash of color and fuller, more filled out brows, this would help with that. If you’re someone who likes a lot of color in the brows, you might not like this since it just gives a wash of color. So, I would recommend it but only if you’re someone who wants to try out different brow shapes to get an idea of what works for you or if you’re someone who likes a light wash of color throughout their brows.

title: Really Excellent for Waves & Curls
text:
I have long hair that's wavy to curly, in layers. It's not kinky, is very thick, and is about average in terms of coarseness-- neither course nor fine. It is prone to frizz, and I live in the South where it is very humid.

Finding a product I like is a challenge, but I really do love this one. In the shower, I wring my hair out, then apply the product--a quarter-sized dollop, then comb it through with a wet shower comb to re-wet as directed. After applying, I often end up wrapping my hair in a towel after I get out so my hair isn't soaking, and I have not noticed this affecting my outcome. In an hour, I've got a head full of soft, shiny curls. There's no frizz, no tangles, no flaking, and no stickiness. And you've got volume at the roots-- no slicked down, weighed down, crunchy roots!

The best part is the next day or two. If I twist my hair up in a bun and go to sleep, I will get a different look in the morning-- looser waves, still soft and touchable without the greasy roots or weird stiff hair that other products give you. I love a product that doesn't require a daily do-over.

I started out with the 2 oz size to try out (I'm jaded when it comes to hair products), but I will be moving up to the 32 oz now-- that's how much I like it!

text:
For reference, I have dry, sensitive skin. I tend to be VERY careful about the cleansers I purchase because many cleansers can be very harsh; even those meant for dry skin. However, I do wear sunscreen and makeup, and both need to be fully removed at the end of the day. Most gentle cleansers do not remove makeup well. This cleanser smells a bit citrusy due to the begamot oil. It's a nice texture; not so runny it runs down my hands, but not too thick to spread on my face. I need 3-4 pumps to effectively cleanse my face. It does a great job with my (non waterproof) eye makeup as well as foundation - my face is clean! I was surprised how clean it rinsed off - no oily feeling remained at all. My face just feels soft and moisturized. I do follow with a lotion cleanser just to be sure, but you could definitely use it as a stand-alone cleanser. Sometimes I use this in the mornings when my face is feeling particularly dry and it makes my skin feel awesome!

The ingredients in it are great, the price is reasonable, and it's vegan and cruelty-free. Most importantly, it works!

I would definitely recommend this to anyone who has been searching for a way to brighten, firm, and help their complexion without success. For me, it is a game changer!

first review:

My specific need for this shampoo was try to help with extreme stress induced hair shed. The brand promises to "stimulate keratinocytes for renewed hair growth", and there were some anecdotal reports of it helping with hair loss I found in my research, so I gave it a try. I've been using it for a little over a month now, twice a week, and cannot definitely see any difference it might be making in my hair regrowth. It didn't prevent any further hair shedding though. My hair keeps falling out at about the same rate it did.

The positive is that the shampoo didn't seem to do any further damage either. It does produce a thickened look. My hair is naturally fine and even in its best days i could hardly get any volume at the root. This seems to be helping with the texture and fuller appearance. I would not call the effect "silky", as the thickening effect is achieved by making the hair coarser than my natural state. This means i have to be extra diligent with my conditioner to aid smoother results along the entire length. Oh, and it also tangles quite a bit in the shower.

All in all, I think my search for hair regrowth solution continues.

title: Kiss has the best nails! Instructions on how to make them last 10-14 days!
text:
These nails are GORGEOUS!!

Do NOT use the sticky adhesive as they make the nails not last as long. Simply:
1. Push your cuticles back
2. File down your nails
3. Lightly file your nail bed so the glue has something a little rough to hang to, it’s always easier than putting glue and a nail on a smooth surface and makes them last much longer
4. Find the 10 nails that fit you and lay them down in the order of the fingers you will put them own (pink-ring-middle-index-thumb-thumb-index-middle-ring-pinky) - they have numbers on the underneath of the nail on the tip, remember those numbers or write them down because that’s likely your size in all Kiss nails (for example, I’m 12-10-7-8-3-3-8-7-10-12, the smaller the number the bigger the mail)
5. When you’re ready to apply, place glue on the bottom of the fake nail about 1/6 inch from the bottom to the middle of the nail and make sure it’s dispersed even - DO NOT put the glue directly on the nail bed, for longevity it works best to put it on the fake nail
6. Align with the appropriate finger and place down, holding for 5-10 seconds.
7. There may be a little glue that comes out on the sides. Be careful not to smudge that on the nail itself. Just take a paper towel and dab that little bit of glue up as you go
8. Once all nails are on, file how you need/want them and you are set for about 10 days.
9. I usually get a solid 2 weeks of wear out of mine! I use either these KGN10, the almond shaped wine, or I’ll do a French or natural French short length from Kiss.
10. Carry around an extra nail or two that may fit a couple different fingers for emergencies, the glue, and the nail file. If a nail pops off and it’s not a broken nail, simply file your nail bed again and apply glue to either a new nail that fits, or the one you popped off if it’s salvageable.

Enjoy!

text:
I got these a month ago when I saw these featured on a YouTube hair video from a YouTuber I follow and generally, her advice on products is solid but these French pins?

The IDEA/CONCEPT is simple and tried and true. So no way to really mess it up, right? Well...

What I do like is the color and the paint or coding hasn't faded or chipped off. The slight curve allows for the in to rest against the curve of your head. The length is nice, and allows more versatility.

What I don't like is the material. For $10 at Target, I wasn't expecting something industrial but the material is very, very flimsy and not remotely sturdy. Not only that, maybe it's the coating on the pins, these things don't stay in for long, or at all sometimes. I have fine, long hair and these pins won't stay put if I don't use product. I usually use a leave-in conditioner so that helps to create texture and the pins seem to stay in longer. These might work better with coarse, thicker hair. It's too bad the material isn't sturdier--so don't think you can do anything while wearing them. The minute you start anything other than sitting and look pretty for however long you wear them, they will fall out without even trying. I had my hair half pined up with a barrette and then pulled the rest up in a twist and made sure the prongs were under the barrette so that it was more secure but it didn't even last half a day and I sit in a cubicle for 8 hours staring at a computer. Just getting up to get a cup of coffee or a printout from the copy machine or other basic tasks would easily loosen the pin.

These are merely okay if you're doing absolutely nothing but sticking a pencil to keep your bun in place work just as well. It's too bad since they are pretty but these are not that functional.

title: Unique. . .Maybe Too Unique
text:
This is a really neat razor that has one possible issue, which I'll get to later.

The handle is big and heavy, and its unusual shape is very stylish. It gives a nice shave, too. If you have a small face or tight features, the large head might be a bit tricky to use in some areas, but that hasn't been a major issue. I usually use an old-school double-edge razor, not a flexing cartridge razor, so the fixed head angle isn't an issue for me. If you're used to a razor with a movable head, this one might take some getting used to.

The included shaving foam smells good and works well. You don't get a lot, but you don't have to use a large amount of it.

The "stand" is just a heavy metal cylinder with a round hole in the top and a pad on the bottom. The hole is wider than the razor handle, and just deep enough that the razor doesn't topple out. It's kind of weird, like the stand was designed for something else, but I guess it works.

I'm not sure why they call this package a "travelling razor kit." It comes in a large gift box, and doesn't include any sort of travel case or bag. Plus, it's the biggest, heaviest razor I've ever seen (aside from folding straight razors). I wouldn't even think of taking this thing on a trip.

Despite all the good things about this razor, there's one major red flag: At the moment, replacement blades aren't listed on Amazon or on the Suprent website. The package includes two cartridges and a card to get a third for free, but there's no guarantee that more will be available when you need 'em. While the included cartridges are definitely good for several shaves apiece, if that's all you get, you'll soon be left with a very expensive paperweight. I rated the product based on my use of it, but recommend that you verify the availability of replacement cartridges before buying.

title: Another stellar shaver from Norelco
text:
I've read a lot of bad reviews on this shaver and I just don't understand why it gets such bad marks. Granted, I've never shaved with any other brand than a Norelco, so I may not have a lot to compare it to. For the past eight years, I shaved with a Norelco Advantage/Cool skin. I wasn't in the market to purchase a new shaver, as I loved my cool skin, but after 8 years, it began to come apart (literally). I received this shaver as a welcome and much needed birthday gift. So far it has lived up to my expectations; its precise in the way it cuts the facial hair and it does provide a closer shave on the neck region than my Advantage/Cool Skin model. In order to avoid any razor burn, I dab some Lectric Shave on my face about 30 seconds prior to shaving (great advice for any of you experiencing razor burn). Unlike the Advantage/Cool skin model, the hairs fall into the blade area neatly, which makes cleaning a breeze. All it takes is some lightly running hot water and about 30 seconds. The arcitec 1060 also has a very powerful charger; I've had it now for over two weeks and have only had to charge it once.

Yes, this is an expensive razor and it may not be worth the price you pay for it, but getting it as a gift I can honestly say that I hope to be using this shaver for years to come. It's a quality machine that does what it is supposed to do: provide a close, comfortable shave.

This is a great set! You get a good sized box full of stuff.

The packaging is great, you get a big pack of the facial cleansing wipes and five of the face masks, and it all feels great on your skin.
My skin was softer after the mask. I suggest warming it first - I tossed it in its package right into my hot bath, along with the eye gel mask. The mask can be a little drippy ( they usually are), so soaking in the bath with it on means no clean up.
The lip treatment was great! My lips were a little dry and peeling, and after the treatment, they were so soft and moisturized.
Nothing had any unpleasant fragrances, either. Which I appreciate.
I really enjoyed taking the evening to pamper myself with this kit, and it would make a great gift!
Totally recommend it.

What I did not like:
- the amount of dye. I only dyed part of my head, the rest is shaved, and I still ran out of dye. With the same amount of dye from a different brand I can almost dye my hair twice. Probably because this is rather thick

- the fact that it contains silicone. I did not see that until too late. So I’ve been washing with a clarifying shampoo in between to make sure I get them out of my hair. Of course this will affect how long it stays vibrant.

This is my first time using Amazon.com for purchases other than books and software. So after carefully examining the various razors and reading previous purchasers critiques I decided to go all out and buy the "TOP" of the range product the Philips Norelco arcItec 1090XD Men's Shaving System.
This was not a snap decision as I also physically examined the model in Booths chemist. And after admiring the self cleaning aspects of the so called "SYSTEM" I gave myself a little treat and placed the order. This order also included an extra carton of cleaning lotion and a spare set of cutters.
I duly received the product but low and behold no cleaning "POD". How can this razor be accurately described as a shaving system. Surly a top of the range "Shaving system" includes the cleaning pod.

Enough of my woes but buyers beware. Once bitten twice shy.

On the razor itself I cannot say enough to express by satisfaction with this product.
I have over the pass 40 years always used an "electric" razor. Including 2 Braun and more recently 3 Philips or Norelco models.

The razor is a joy to use. It gives a lovely and almost silent cut. It looks and feels fantastic. The humble "electric" razor has certainly come along way and progressed to the development of this model. The design is so well balanced between the cutting heads and the main body it's as if the cutters were attached to the top of your thumb. The charging system does exactly what it say on the box and is fully charged in 60mins. It does remind you to empty and clean the cutter head after every use. But this is a relatively straight forward exercise and not as off putting as other commentators have suggested. The recharging stand complements the razor in both design and usefulness. It has suction pads on the bottom to ensure that the stand and razor won't move from its correct place. OK the trimmer is not as big as on my current model. But it does exactly what I need in tidying sideburns and trimming over ears etc.
Look it's a Razor not a hair grooming machine.

Would I recommend the razor? Most definitely YES, it's a man's razor. And thankfully as previous ladies have comment on its does not suit their needs. So hopefully I will not see my wife borrowing it either.

However be careful where you buy the product and don't get stung like me.
[[ASIN:B0014N0MFK Philips Norelco arcitec 1090XD Men's Shaving System]]

title: Amount of Product Seems Deceiving, But...
text: For anyone complaining about the amount of product in this... this lip butter contains 6.2 grams. A traditional Chapstick brand lip balm in a tube and even Blistex at the drugstore has 4.25 grams. The lip butter tube is a lot wider than Chapstick, so it appears to have less product when really it contains more than what you’d typically get for a lip balm in a swivel tube. Of course it’s more expensive, but that shouldn’t come as a surprise if you choose to buy a lip balm at Sephora (I purchased mine off Amazon because it’s slightly cheaper), and I don’t feel it should be rated any less just because of the price. If you want a lip balm that simply gets the job done, there are plenty of affordable options at the drugstore. This smells absolutely amazing and leaves your lips feeling silky smooth. It also leaves a nice shine, so I love layering it on top of liquid lipsticks for added hydration and a subtle gloss. I have really full lips that tend to get chapped quickly, so lip balms are a must for me but I prefer a thicker formula like the Bite Agave Lip Balm. I know some people say that one is too thick, but I find I have to apply less whereas with the lip butter, I’m constantly applying (but I don’t mind cause it smells and makes my lips feels so good!). If this was a bit richer/thicker, I’d give it a 5/5. However if you don’t like an extremely thick formula and don’t mind fragrance in your lip balms, you’d really enjoy this!!

It was a little hard to put the elastic loop around the button but I figured it out okay. I left my hair up for a bit to see how much of the water it would absorb. I like to style my hair while it's in-between wet and damp. After about 15 minutes I pulled off the towel (again the loop and button gave me some issues but it's probably user error) and my hair was perfect! Right in-between wet and damp! title: Good overall quality but bad design
text:
This is the third of Norelco's waterproof series that I have owned.
The overall quality is just as good as previous models and other Philips/Norelco products.
The shaver is constructed well and is lighter and more compact than previous models. Charging and battery life also seem to be very good.

The main problem I find with this new design is that the heads/razors are floating and not encased as previous models and most other shavers. When using this shaver in the shower this is not a problem. However, when you use this shaver outside of the shower, the lack of casing around the heads means that as you shave, all of the hair pieces fall from the shaver to the counter or wherever else you may be (I would not recommend using this shaver in the car unless you don't mind getting yourself and your car covered with hair pieces). To me this is a major oversight and design flaw.
In short, if you only plan to use this razor in the shower this is a good choice, but if you need to use the razor outside of the shower as well, you may want to choose something else.

title: Order Ahead~
text:
The good:

Packaging is very much discreet, and inside the box was another pretty box. They sent it to me in a little black box, with some really pretty tissue paper around the jar. And a little business card.
Speaking of the jar, that's discreet, too. The label peels right off, leaving you with a simple black jar with a silver lid. The cream is filled to the TOP of the container, and it smells so wonderfully of vanilla.
Without the label, it can easily pass for any kind of body/face cream on the market.

Applying it, you really do only need a little bit, like a fingertip's worth. It's very creamy at first, and even with only a small amount it looks like you used way too much with the way it just spreads out, and then it feels and looks very oily before finally absorbing. Now I understand why 4oz is sufficient for a month supply.

I might edit in later on to share any results, seeing as there aren't any other reviews on it at all... Presuming anyone requests it anyway. (No sense wasting the time writing it up here if no one cares to know. ;p)
Their site says you can 'see results' within 2 weeks, but we all know how much that varies from person to person. However, it has Pueraria Mirifica in it, and that stuff is strong, so who knows how fast it'll work.

The bad: Delivery.

There is no "fast" option - when you order it, your only option is 5-8 days.
I placed this order July 6, on a Saturday, and it was expected to go out the following Monday or Tuesday.
It "left the facility" on Wednesday, July 10th.
It was expected to arrive between Thursday, July 11 - Tuesday, July 16.
It finally got to my post office July 18th.

Considering that I had to PAY for the shipping, unlike a good 95% of my orders on Amazon, I can't say I'm impressed with the seller's delivery speed. Of course, I don't know if their shipping is always like this, either, and it was only 2 days off of the estimated date, which is why I only docked 1 star. But for future orders through them, I will order a week or two ahead of time -- just in case -- and I suggest you do the same.

********
