I bought one entirely because it was significantly less expensive than a Sonicare. I have had it three years and have yet to be able to run the battery down, which I find remarkable ... leaving it off the charger for a week results in very little if any loss of power.

I completely disagree with the reviewers who say that it doesn't perform better than the non-sonic brushes.

The first time I went to my dentist after having used it for six months, he sat back in his chair and asked me what I was doing differently. I told him nothing but changing to a sonic toothbrush ... when he asked me what brand it was, I told him and he said "Well, don't change a thing, because this is the first time you've had zero placque."

Its not supposed to be a substitute for flossing. Flossing once a week (which is considerably less than what the dentist wants) and using this brush have improved my dental health measurably enough that my dentist remarked on it, and I doubt you can do better than that for the money.

title: A Good Deal
text:
I bought these last year after I had purchased the cheap tv stamper set that was being sold at Sally's. Don't buy that set if you can help it. Get a Konad stamper and pick someone else's plates.

These Bundle plates, just like any other project/skill/product that you use have their drawbacks.
These plates do work well, and the newer sets come with a paper backing to protect the edges. Some people state that the images don't come through, but it really depends on a couple of things, so if your images don't come through on these plates, here are some things to keep in mind:
1. try a different stamper. I bought a Konad recently and it stamped beautifully, especially the delicate full-nail leaf pattern. Came out very well.
2. it could be your polish. Some of the wet and wild stuff works, china glaze does too, as does sally hansen. but it depends on the consistency and chemicals used in the polish, so don't be discouraged! I would recommend using the same brand of top coat that you are using to do the stamping design, because some I have used seem to "melt" the base coats away after a light brush.
3. it could be your technique. press firmly but evenly as you go down. Don't press hard enough to break your finger, but a little pressure may help in transfering. Also, work quickly, as the paint on the plate or stamped will dry.
4. it could be that you didn't clean the plate properly. I thoroughly clean out every desgin with acetone nail polish remover, and make sure all the cracks are clean. DO NOT UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCE USE NAIL POLISH REMOVER WITH MOISTURIZERS. THE OILS AND CHEMICALS MAY CAUSE THE NAIL POLISH NOT TO ADHERE TO THE STAMPER AND WON'T WORK!
5. the plate could be bad. I haven't tried every design, so I can't say which are bad, but they seemed to do okay. If you work fast and you roll the stamper in an even motion across your nails in one direction, and NOT back and forth, your design should be ok.
Overall, a good stamped makes a helluva lot of difference when doing this. Otherwise, they are good plates, although the rose doesn't come out too well in my opinion, and the full nail designs are too small, as many others have said. I'm not picky. I just match up and restamp the open space on the nail and it turns out good.
Overall, okay quality for the price and interesting designs for those who are just starting out and want to have something a little different to play with. Cheers!

title: Does the Job Well
text: Those who are concerned with the latest and most effective electric toothbrush would do well to consider the ORAL-B VITALITY model.  When an electric toothbrush performs on a high level as this one, then performance trumps price, which in any case is quite reasonable. What I found useful was the dual revolving bristle head.  This twin set of bristles is a double edged sword.  True, it cleans and massages well, thus insuring the fast removal of plaque, but on the down side, the user must remember to take care not to exert too much pressure since it is easy to forget that gum tissue is far more fragile than tooth enamel.  There are several other plusses, the most notable being its portable recharger that allows one to use it in a normal manner for several days. Finally, it has the added advantage common to all electric brushes; one can easily swoop away plaque from hard to reach areas such as behind the front teeth.  When one considers the opposition, the primary reason to buy one over the other is how well the brush does its job in a safe, efficient, and reliable manner.  The ORAL-B VITALITY brush stands out.

title: excellent coverage, non cakey, doesnt settle into lines, a tad warm for fair, cool skin
text:
Primer, liquid Foundation, BB cushion, and a flat kabuki brush. I have another Phoera kit, and I like it a lot.
https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B093GFPFP9

I am not sure if Nude (#102) is the lightest shade they have or not, but if you are like me and have fair skin with cool undertones this may lean a little warm. It isn't bad, but if they had a better match available I would want to get that.
THEY DO!! this is for fair with pink undertones
https://www.amazon.com/dp/B07RZ6QZLJ/

The BB cushion is a tad lighter, and a better match for my skin. I do like both. I tend to like cushion over liquid, but both of these are fantastic. I really like how these feel, and despite being a little warm on my cool skin, the make up looks good on the skin. Doesn't settle into every nook and cranny, nor dry flakes.
My skin is 40+ so this is something I look for in make up.

The primer is fantastic. A LITTLE GOES A LONG WAY. Use less than you think you need lest you want a more oily look to seep through. I find that primers like this are great for dry skin, and for more dry feeling foundations.. but their foundations arent drying. So less is more with their primer.

The formula for the liquid foundation really impresses me. Staying power is good. Skin feels comfortable. Skin looks healthy. I can touch my skin after and it doesn't feel like there is make up on. Provides really good coverage with a little bit yet doesn't look cakey and fake. Can be built up. I would recommend this over dermablend, personally. All my redness disappears (from Type 1 Rosacea). To provide a more sheer wash, just change up your application- use a damp sponge to put it on, or use a damp sponge as last step to blend it in and lighten it up.

I really think it is worth the try. I wasn't even going to try this, but since they provided so much information in their product description it really piqued my interest. If you need coverage with a natural look.. try this!

This is the correct wheel for high speed steel turning tools.

If you listen, you will hear your cutting edges come into sharp. When you sharpen by ear, you take less material off and done sooner.

If you are not a safety nut, take all your guards and shields off and it will fit on a 6 inch bench grinder with the oneway sharpening system jigs no problem

I noticed as well that the wheel was peck drilled to balance it. It runs real real quiet. I have never been able to hear the motor in my bench grinder before while it is running.

If you are looking around for a solution to get off of stone wheels or white wheels, do this one.

I shaved them off, yet would still use a little bit of that stuff on my head hair before applying pomade as the two seem to work together well, the jelly almost functioning as a pre-styler. Once I tried the Outlaw Soaps Magic Elixir, however, I realized that it does much more for my head hair than the jelly was doing. It instantaneously tamed my curly-wavy hair, but working *with* the curls in a way that mirrored how I style my hair anyway -- it actually felt "magical." Also, it stood in for itself without me needing to use any additional product (was on my way to hot yoga and didn't want pomade liquefying and pouring over my face). Also, the smell, like all Outlaw stuff, is intoxicating and legitimate aromatherapy -- the manly, woody, nutty scent put a smile on my face. Also, it's subtle and can act as a "base" for other Outlaw products such as their solid colognes and hopefully the upcoming DEODORANTS! (While the scent has it's own woody character, it seems to provide a foundation whence you can take off either in a "woodsy" or a warm, bourbon-ey direction.)

These guys are artists -- the impeccable harmonic synthesis between quality/effectiveness and out-of-this-world scents that they've achieved sells itself. In fact, when somebody wonders what it means for a product to "sell itself," Outlaw Soaps, for the most part, is the definitive example.

title: Meet my new best friend!
text:
OMFG this brush is amazing! I have 3B style curls and I'm also biracial so my hair is really porous and a bit on the fragile side. In its curly state it's a pain to care for but the traditional blow dry and flat iron method is both tedious and damaging to my hair.

When wet to straight irons came out, I immediately hopped on board because it just made more sense that heating my hair while wet would be less damaging to it. Through this I got hooked lol. But even with that it is a bit tedious.... though it did help me figure out that I could flat iron my hair dry and skip the blow dryer.

My boyfriend has one of these brushes and I tried it as a quick way to straighten my hair in the am. I was SUPER impressed! But it had some design flaws that made me seek my own, and landed me here.

From what I've seen comparing this brush to the more popular Rinfy and his brush, they've reallly improved upon the original design concepts. Most notably, the buttons are on the front of the handle and not the sides, down near the cord instead of anywhere up near the head. This along with the way they're shaped to be concaved makes it highly unlikely they'll be pressed by accident. But even if you do press them by accident, the device automatically locks them about 30s after the temperature is set. If you want to change the temp or turn it off after that, you need to click the power button twice to unlock them.

The teeth are not only steep enough to accommodate my thick hair, but there's also way more of them packed more densely together. This seems to make this brush MUCH quicker at straightening my hair, and it can also get it board straight. The other brushes have only gotten it as close as a little wave.

Since my hair is so thick, I also have to place my hand on the bristles while I pull the brush through so it gets all my hair in it. This is the only model I've tried which hasn't burned me even once while using it so far. The teeth are so densely packed that there is no way for a finger or the side of my hand to slip down past the safety portion of it.

Quick heating? Honestly I don't know why anyone tries to claim that.... I've never seen any heated hair product heat up quickly. My stove doesn't even heat up quickly. I hardly expect my straightening iron or brush to defy the laws of physics so I don't have to wait a few minutes for it to heat up. That's why I turn it on BEFORE I'm ready to use it. 😉

All joking aside though, this really is a fantastic brush. It even FEELS high quality. Nice weight, premium plastics, slick design. It will fit right in with other hair devices no matter how pricey they are.

title: Smooth as a babies bottom!
text:
Hello All,

I purchased this razor as a replacement for my dying Norelco 4821XL which I purchased about ten years ago. I have been a loyal Norelco fan for 30+ years and with the addition of the Norelco 9160XL, I hope to continue that tradition. The first thing I noticed about the 9160 is HOW QUIET IT IS! My old razor made so much noise that it was like shaving with a hedge trimmer. The first time I turned on the 9160 I had to double check that the batteries were charge because of how quiet and smooth it runs. The next thing I am happy to report is how close and smooth a shave it produces. WOW!

The only negative I can say about the razor is that there is SO MUCH PLASTIC on it that I am concerned about how well the unit will hold up with age. In addition, the lock for the trimmer is rather difficult to get your finer on to release especially if you do not have long fingernails. I wonder if Norelco (and I hope you are reading this) could make the ridges on the trimmer release a wee bit higher so that those of us fingernail challenged people can have less trouble releasing the latch?!

Short of that minor annoyance, the razor is lightweight, quiet and produces a great close shave that will have your face as smooth as a baby's bottom. If you want a great razor I would look no further and jump on this puppy also while you are at it you might want to pickup a set of the HQ9 replacement heads so that down the road when the razor tells you that heads need replacing you have a spare set to replace them with.

Ciao!

title: No difference after three weeks of consistent use, and product won't dispense through pump.
text:
ANOTHER UPDATE:

My dermatologist told me that unless a Vitamin C serum contained the L-ascorbic acid form of Vitamin C, I was wasting my money and doing little to improve my skin. I found a serum here on Amazon that contains 17% L-ascorbic acid, and I've been using it for approx. 3 weeks. What a difference! I can definitely feel it working for one thing (it burns for about 5 seconds), but more importantly, I can SEE the difference in my skin already. At first I thought my eyesight was going downhill, but then I realized my skin really did look smoother and had a new glow. Do an Amazon search for L-ascorbic Vitamin C serum to get the good stuff.

Having said all this, I have added a LOT more spinach to my daily regimen lately, so I'm sure that's contributing to my skin's appearance too.

UPDATE:

I finished the bottle which gave me about 5 weeks of use. If it made any difference in my skin, it's at a microscopic level. I'm buying another bottle - mainly because there's got to be SOME truth to all the 5-star reviews. But if, after another month or so of use, I still don't see improvement in my skin, I'm asking a dermatologist for a Rx for Retin-A.

ORIGINAL REVIEW:

I've been using this product for three weeks, and I have yet to see any improvement in my skin. I'm amazed (and not a little skeptical) about some people seeing results in two weeks. I also wonder how many 5-star reviews were written by people who were given the product to try.

I'm very methodical about using new products on my skin. I use a 10x magnifying mirror, establish a "baseline" area of my skin to observe over time, and take close-up "selfies" of my skin to compare with photos taken a few weeks later. No difference so far, but I'll continue to use this product until it's gone.

I DO like that this retinol doesn't irritate my skin, which is highly unusual. So unusual, it makes me wonder if it indeed contains any retinol.

In conclusion, and not a critique of the product itself, but the product won't dispense through the pump. It's too thick. I'm having to pull the cap off and shake the serum on to my fingertips. I wish it came with a dropper instead. I changed out out the pump with a dropper from another bottle of serum. I'm surprised I haven't read about this problem in other reviews. Another reason I'm leery of all the glowing comments.

I'll update with my progress, or lack thereof, at a later date.

title: Interesting Gritty Texture And Strong Clove Scent
text:
This Spa-Da Immunity Support Soap is one of the more interesting soaps I have tried. You get a pack of 6 small shield shaped soaps in a resealable plastic bag. The soaps are about 2.75 inches in length.

The scent is strong when you open the bag and especially in the shower. Some of the oils and ingredients included are cloves, cinnamon, oregano, peppermint, parsley, eucalyptus, and rosemary. If you don’t like the smell of cloves, then do not order this because that is the most predominant smell in my opinion. I like it though- it has a nice spicy kick.

The soap definitely feels different than I expected. It doesn’t feel really smooth like many soaps. When dry, they were slightly powdery when I ran my finger across. They are slightly gritty feeling which I noticed more once the soap became wet in the shower. This could be nice if you like a slight scrubby feeling. I typically rub it onto my mesh bath sponge or silicone sponge so I don’t really care about the grittiness either way. I found that it lathers and suds up very well with both my mesh and silicone sponges.

I just started using, so I’m not sure how many showers I’ll be able to get out of each bar. Honestly, I thought they might disintegrate and get used up fast simply based on how powdery they felt when dry. I don’t think it will last as long as some other soaps, but I was still surprised that I could somewhat see the outline of where the shallow cross was imprinted on the soap even after my first shower-and I did intentionally scrub my sponges all over that side pretty vigorously. I took a picture of what the soap looked like after one shower compared to unused bars.

Anyway, my skin feels very clean, perhaps even a little moisturized after using and I haven’t experienced any irritation to my sensitive skin (I have eczema).

I like that this soap is natural and free from harmful chemicals. I also love that it is made in the USA-Ohio specifically, which is where I am from.

I’ll be sure to update my review if any issues arise like if I find that the bars do in fact get used far too quickly. I hope my review was helpful in some way, and if so, I would love to know- thanks!!!

title: Surprisingly Good
text:
I’m really glad I gave this one a second chance. I bought it, used it twice, decided I didn’t like the way it coated my face, and shoved it into a corner for about a month.
On a whim, I tried it again one day after a shower. What I noticed is that the light coating it provides made my moisturizer glide on like silk. As the day goes on, my face stays looking hydrated. So, I’ve been using it ever since for about two months. Now I feel like my routine would be incomplete without it.

You could, if you have oilier skin, use this as your only moisturizer in a pinch. I like that it primes my face so beautifully, even though I don’t wear makeup. It makes the moisturizer glide and settle nicely.

I *think* it also creates a sort of plump look to the skin. I am not sure that lessens scars or deals with discoloration yet. I do know, however, that it makes my skin look dewy and refreshed.

I’ve experienced no irritable or breakouts. My skin is hyper-sensitive, it reacts to fragrances even before they touch my skin. Sometimes it burns slightly upon application, but it does not irritate or damage the skin in any way.

It creates a very, very light coating on the face. But I have applied topical acne medication in spots over it and it didn’t prevent the treatment from penetrating. It plays well with niacinamide, which is in my la Roche Posay moisturizer, BP, and BHAs.

I wrote elta asking if I could apply it before applying my retinoid at night. They said they don’t know and told me to consult my derm. Therefore, I only use it in daytime, after my morning cleansing. I would like to try it as a buffer to my Tazorac at night, but until my derm says it’s okay, I won’t.

I think toners are absolutely necessary when you live in a hard water area like I do. But it has taken me years to find one that doesn’t break me out. Prior to this, I used rose water occasionally or no toner at all. I’m actually terrified elta will stop making this. Above all, its main benefit is that it removes residue from hard water and facial cleanser and restores the ph balance. That is all you should expect of a toner. But the added benefits listed above make this a keeper.

It even tells you to do that on the little paper included in the box.  I expect the people who didn't have results didn't do their do diligence and read the paper. By the time I remove my gel polish I normally have 5 or more coats on, so I use this product two times to get most of the polish off and then gently file off the rest. title: A nice, all in one set
text:
Everything in this set is clearly labeled, and most everything that you need is included. (I also used a dish to mix the dye, toothpicks, Q-tips, and some cotton pads.)
Because my eyes are easily irritated, I don't like wearing mascara for more than a couple of hours and started dying my eyelashes. However, this was my first attempt at a lash lift. Let me just say--if I can do it, you can do it!
If you are an expert at this, the directions on the back would probably be enough. I watched a couple of YouTube tutorials and found one where the presenter did this herself, which was very helpful. Because I was doing this to myself, I did one eye at a time, which worked out fine. Also, I didn't want anything too dramatic for my first time, so I used the Medium-1 lift pad; next time I might go a size smaller.
One thing I noticed is that the solution times for this set are longer than some. (Perm/#1--18-20 minutes; Fixation/#2--10-15 minutes; Black Dye/#6+7--25-30 minutes.) Because I didn't want to fry my eyelashes the first time, I didn't leave the solutions on as long. (#1--12 minutes; #2--8 minutes; #6+7--5 to 20 minutes.) One reason I think less time might be okay is that I dyed my first eyelashes just over 20 minutes, but for the second eye I must have gotten the dye a little too close, and my eye became irritated. I washed the dye off after only about 5 minutes, but both sets of eyelashes look the same depth of black several days later. The lift is also staying quite nicely and looks better than mascara for me.
This kit comes with supplies to do 5 eyelash and eyebrow treatments. Only using this for my eyelashes, I think I'll be able to do this at least 12 times. (And doing this only every 6 weeks, it's going to last a while.)
Finally, I'd recommend using Castor Oil as part of your daily routine. Applying it to my eyes/lashes once a day has helped keep them healthier (even with treatments) and has helped my lashes grow longer. Anyways, have fun!

Pros:

Easy to turn on and off, simply press a button.

Looks good and when it works, it does a decent job.

Cons:

Lasts only 10-15 min max before you have to plug it in overnight to charge.

Does do as good of job as I thought it would actually shaving.

Recommendation:

Save you money and buy a better shaver. If if you can't afford something nicer, a bag of disposable razors will do a better job.

title: Works well on my thick, long hair

The brush worked well combing my hair out after she took it down from last week's braid. That was on dry hair. It also worked well after she washed my hair and went to brush it out. She was afraid that the bristles on the brush were scratching my head but I felt no discomfort. In fact it felt good having my hair brushed.

The only negative is that the brush kept slipping out of her hands because of the configuration of the handle. The handle needs to be a little bit longer.

I received this brush in exchange for my honest review. I liked it so well that I ordered two more for my daughter-in-law and my granddaughter – both who have long, curly hair that is hard to brush out (I was thrilled with all of the color choices). The brushes will be in their Christmas stockings and I hope they like them as much as I like mine.

text:
[[VIDEOID:5be0c2275f0579b3fea94237db2d7551]] Holy WOW! I'm not a huge makeup person so I have zero patience for these kinds of things, but I do have a couple kabuki brushes I use for my BB cream. I have some silicone cleaning pads to use to clean them with. Even though that works just fine, the process is arduous and I still have to wait overnight (and sometimes for more than a day) for the brushes to dry, while they lay precariously on some window sill or on the counter. For that reason, I have two brushes so that I can alternate them, but frankly it takes a little time and I'm lazy, so for the last two or three weeks, both brushes have been dirty and I've just been applying the bb cream with clean fingers instead. The cream doesn't apply as well with fingers as it does with a kabuki brush; it looks heavier when I apply with fingers and I like a more natural look, so I decided to do a bit of research.

I ordered this product and WOW. It only took a few minutes to ended up with TOTALLY CLEAN AND COMPLETLEY DRY BRUSHES! What would have taken me about 15 minutes for each brush (so 30 minutes), plus some elbow grease and a ton of cleaning product, and a day or day and a half to dry, was done in less than a 5 minutes for each brushes. (It's actually more like only a few minutes each.) And now I will clean my brushes more often because of it.

The kit also comes with two brushes, a bunch of adaptors for any sized brush, and a cleaning liquid for non water-soluble makeup (like foundations). I didn't pay enough attention to know it would come with the cleaner and brushes, so that was a bonus!

I rarely if ever give high stars or such emphatic reviews, but I am seriously amazed. I also just ordered one for my sister.

I included pics of what my dirty brush looked like compared to a clean brush, a video of the cleaning, and a post-cleaning brush pic. Bear with my video as I can probably get better at the process, and also it's hard to hold up a phone videoing and do this at the same time. I'm just SO amazed, that I had to document it and share :)

It could also be a cool way to store/display your makeup brushes and have them keep their shape (versus throwing them into a cup/holder/drawer). title: Not 100% human hair
text:
This wig isn't 100% human hair.
I tried to lighten it with powder bleach using a strong developer and saw hardly any results at all.
It lifted / lightened maybe 2 shades after processing for almost an hour.
To no avail, I covered the test strand with foil and used my blow dryer to help it lighten. Nothing happened.

Using the same formula, I would've gotten completely different results on a 100% human hair wig or on living persons head of hair.
I have 39 years experience in the hair industry, including coloring human hair wigs and hair extensions. I have never had this problem before.

I wanted the wig for a chemotherapy client who had curly hair, same length with a center part. The only problem was the color.
Unfortunately, I went by what the description is of the wig, which is 100% human hair. I ordered it, recieved it on time. Tried to lighten it as promised for my client with a disasterous result.
Now I have the upsetting task of telling my client that I can not achieve the same hair color she had because the wig isnt processing the same way human hair should.
This is after I reassured her I COULD achieve it given the facts stated and description of the wig.
My personal conclusion and professional opinion with 39 years experience is that this wig is not 100% human hair.
Theres no reason why I could not achieve a lighter color for my client other than that the wig is made up of something that resembles human hair, and not 100% human hair as the description states that it is.

It's not an overly thick wig, but has enough hair to scrunch and create a full look.
Curl formation is smooth.

3 stars for the style, curl and length of the wig. Pictures of it are somewhat accurate.
0 stars for the misrepresentation that its 100% human hair.
In addition to me, I will have a very upset client.
I'm at loss as to what to do now as she wanted and I reassured her that she could have this wig for the holiday.
It's too late now to order a different one and start this process over again.

The price it’s twice of what my to go deodorant usually is, however I have been looking for a more effective deodorant, I workout everyday and I am extremely conscious of the my smell, I do not have a strong humor so I tend to forget to apply deodorant after I shower and it is usually until I am halfway through my workout where the smell of sweat reminds me I forgot. Also, most deodorants contain very strong fragrance that are not always the must skin friendly because they do only mask the smell and neutralize the bacteria waste but do not actually address the issue, so I personally can over look the fact that this deodorant does not smell like perfume just because I am looking for a deodorant and not a nice scent, I would hate to smell like peaches and roses with a strong hint of bacteria waste-byproduct (armpit smell). title: I'm not seeing it
text:
These are essentially giant temporary tattoos very similar to the ones you sometimes get as novelty gifts and promotional material.
Like those, you simply peel off the protective cover, press the design where you want it, then wet the back of the paper holding the tattoo, until it transfers to your skin.
Rubbing alcohol helps wipe the tattoo off, if wear and tear and sweat don't take it out first.

The reasons I personally did not care for these:
- A lot less vivid on my skin, than in photos or against the paper
- There is no precut opening for your mouth; FYI, you get the best result cutting (carefully) an opening after you put the tattoo on, not before
- Very difficult to line up with your own mouth
- If you wear these over your mouth, the activity of talking, drinking, eating, etc... rapidly degrades the tattoo, causing wrinkles, gaps, tears, etc...

In my opinion, the best use of these temporary tattoos would be to create the illusion of a fake mouth somewhere else on you body, like your tummy, neck, back, hand, etc...
Honestly, I was just really disappointed with these all around.

title: Love This Shaver
text:
I replaced my Norelco Spectra with this Smart-Touch 9190 XL and it works as advertised. I liked the Spectra, but compared to it the XL simply outclasses the old one.

The XL takes less time, shaves closer and is quieter. It also has a much bigger chamber to hold the cut hair. And the trimmer works well. According to the manual, it takes up to 3 weeks to conform to your skin and you may get some irritation until it gets broken in. I set it to sensitive and have had very little skin irritation from day one.

It has some nice features including a screen that tells you how many minutes you have used and how many you have left. Or, you can change the display to a battery indicator. It also tells you when to rinse, charge the razor and change the blades. Another nice feature is the travel lock. You hold the power button for 3 seconds and it locks which prevents it from accidentally turning on. The charging base has a little clock, but I do not see the point in that.

My old razor had the digital information screen so that is what I wanted in a new razor. However, if you do not need or want that feature then I would suggest getting the cheaper model. I think all the other features are the same on both, plus you would save a lot of money. Personally, I like the 9190XL but the choice is up to you.

Pros:

Faster shave.

Closer shave.

Information screen.

Easily rinses clean.

Holds charge for a long time.

Quiet operation.

title: Good product, excellent customer service!
text:
I'm not new to hair extensions. I've worn them for a few years quite a while ago when growing out a short cut. Once again, I went a little balayage bleach crazy and fried my longer hair which caused a ton of my length to break off. I decided to go this route again while growing my length back out. I have fine hair, but a lot of it, so I got 2 packs. I could probably use a few more for fullness but 20 sets looks fine. My hair is currently color treated dark red at the roots and the color fades to magenta at the ends. I got the light brown to blonde extensions so I could custom dye them to match. The extensions took the dye very well and you can't tell a color difference between my hair and the extensions at all.

The claim that they are thick from root to tip isn't true. Most extensions claim this though and I expected it, so I got longer hair than I really wanted so I could trim it and get rid of the thinning in the ends. I've had minimal shedding so all in all, that is a plus.

They come super straight out of the pack but have some natural wave to them when you wash them. Not a problem as my natural hair does too so they blend well there too. They are soft and as long as you use a leave in oil they will stay frizz free. They hold curl really well too. I curled them and they stayed curled over two days, long after the curl fell out of my natural hair. I've had some tapes separate after install, and removed some due to my own misplacement, but replaced them with tape I had before. Most of the original tape has been replaced at this point so I can't speak to its quality or longevity.

I'm not totally blown away but am happy enough with my purchase to wear them until it's time to replace them.

Edit 6/7/21: I was contacted by Easyouth customer service because my review wasnt a 100% satisfied review. They offered to send me a free pack and provide a discount code for my next purchase to update my review. I will say that they have gone above and beyond what I would expect from a seller. Given I wasnt disappointed in the product, but had a similar experience to what I'm used to from other experiences with extensions. They were very responsive, very quickly. That's something I appreciate.

The new pack I was sent was packaged differently than the two packs I ordered. They came in a branded cardboard box. The extensions were packaged nicely in a plastic sleeve and inside the sleeve the wefts were attached to a thinner paper card and tucked into a little hair net to keep them from tangling. (My first order was just attached to a long, thick paper sleeve.) The hair is still beautiful. I also ordered a halo using the code I was provided. So I plan to dye all of my new extensions to match my natural hair once it arrives.

Thanks for the great product and excellent customer service!

text:
When I try out a new electric toothbrush, I test it by using disclosing tablets. Using them, you can see the plaque on your teeth, and measure how much your brush leaves behind. This brush removed absolutely nothing. It's exactly like a standard manual toothbrush that buzzes.

The bristles on sonic toothbrushes vibrate in an up and down motion at high speed. They don't move far, but the speed they're traveling at allows them to scrub the surfaces of your teeth very efficiently. My old Sonicare (purchased before Philips bought them out) left NO plaque film behind.

Curious about the Oral-B's non-effectiveness, I held the bristles lightly against my tongue, and could feel no motion whatever. It's as though the handle vibrates, but the bristles remain stationary.

Fortunately, the brush is inexpensive, so I won't feel too bad about throwing it in the trash.

Yes, the packaging is gimmicky and I totally fell for it, but I make no apologies. I bought 3 shades--PK01, CR01, and OR01--and they're all quite nice. That said, the PK01 is a bit lighter than I expected so I'll probably get more wear out of the other two.

The tints are pretty long-lasting. I was able to wear the OR01 all day yesterday, and even through lunch and drinking mugs of tea I didn't need to touch it up 'til the end of the day. (And, truthfully, since it was the end of the day and there was still a hint of color, I was lazy and just didn't bother.) The tints aren't noticeably drying, either--although I'm a balm addict and usually put some on over the color throughout the day. Luckily, this doesn't seem to have a terribly detrimental effect on the color. There is a slight taste, which is neither unpleasant nor pleasant--I didn't especially like it, but it didn't bother me. I'm not a wine drinker, but my guess is they don't really taste like wine, just kind of fruity.

The only other true tints/stains I've used are the Tony Moly ones and I think these compare favorably to those in terms of ease of application (I think these are more forgiving), durability, drying, and taste (the TMs had a more chemical taste). I don't dislike the TM's, but these are just better, IMO.

I'd recommend these tints, and will probably buy again, especially to try out the other other colors.

title: A Great Shave
text:
First off let me start off by saying that like most 17 year old males, I have very sensitive skin. Before buying the Norelco Advantage, I could not find a simple solution to getting a nice quick shave without all the hassle that comes along with it. I did not really have a problem at the time, with the length of time that shaving took, but rather, the razor-burn afterwards. I went through about 10-12 different types of creams, and 6-7 different razors, trying to find the right combination. It wasn't until a good friend of mine recommended this, that I decided to try an electric razor. The Norelco definately lived up to it's reputation, as one of the best electric razors out there. Two things that stuck out about it was that you could get a good clean shave in hardly any time at all, and in my case, the gel worked wonders on my previous razor burn.

Now, there are however a few things that could have been improved on. None of these however seriously demote the quality of this razor. The first thing that I noticed is that it is not good with multiple day stubble. If I go for a few days without shaving, I end up having to switch to the beard trimmer, and then back again to the regular blade, in order to get a good shave. This can get quite tedious and annoying in a hurry. Another thing that I noticed is that the blades tend to gunk up quite easily making cleaning almost a weekly thing. The last thing is that unless at full charge, the blades tend miss some of the longer hairs.

All around this is a great product for those of you out there who are looking for a nice quick close shave. Dollar for dollar this is one of the better products that I have bought, but I look foward to seeing an upgrade on this Electric.

title: Decent cleansing conditioner for dry, damaged hair
text:
I have very dry, very damaged hair, and am CONSTANTLY on the search for the "perfect" products for my hair. I have now tried just about every shampoo and conditioner available, ranging from very cheap drugstore products, to very expensive salon products. I've also tried a few infomercial products. While I have found several products I do like very much, I am still on the search...

Having heard that Pantene Co-Wash might be a good alternative to my expensive infomercial cleansing conditioner, I purchased the large bottle and gave it a go. After following the directions to wash into my hair and then let it sit for a minute before rinsing, I towel-dried my hair and then let it dry naturally (my wavy, frizzy hair usually does better air-drying than it does being dried via hair dryer). My hair was definitely easy to brush, but I feel it didn't get my roots very clean.

So I tried it again. And then again. Each time, I felt it did a good job detangling, but not such a good job cleaning. My hair looked fine for about 8 hours before it began to look greasy. Getting my very dry hair to look greasy is not an easy feat!

Overall, I would say this is a decent cleansing conditioner for dry, damaged hair, but it might leave some people's hair (mine included) looking a bit greasy, especially after a few hours.

Although this product is marketed for African-American hair, it works for other textures of hair, as well. I have very fine, dry, damaged Caucasian hair, and it works for my hair texture, as well.

I love the Laura Mercier line, but I've found the sweet-scented lotions, like Creme Brulee, to be overpowering. I'm willing to keep trying, though, and I'm glad I did. I love the Ambre Vanille Souffle Body Crème

Ambre Vanille Souffle Body Creme comes in a heavy, clear glass jar. The silver lid easily screws off and on and the label is elegant and attached to the front of the jar. It’s pretty and I love having it on my counter.

I'm used to the thick texture of body butter, so I was surprised by the lightness of the Souffle Body Creme. It has the texture and appearance of whipped cream--only it smells much richer! The creme goes on a little white, but once it's rubbed in you can no longer see it. My skin feels soft and smooth and not at all greasy

I find this fragrance to be much more subtle than the Creme Brulee Hand Crème, but it’s still pretty strong. I'm not certain what Amber smells like, but I definitely smell the coconut, vanilla, and sandalwood. As much as I like this fragrance, I do think it's too much for me to wear during the day, so I've switched to using it at night. I drift off to sleep to the scent of Ambre Vanille

I suspect that the Ambre Vanille fragrance isn't for everyone and at these prices, you really want to make sure that you love the scent before investing in it. The souffle texture is a nice change of pace from my usual body butter.

title: Absolutely stunning polish
text:
This is the best gel polish I have ever used. The colors are all absolutely gorgeous and true to the picture, they are low scent and apply with ease.

This gel polish is so easy to work with and didn't flood my cuticles at all an leveled very well. I have always struggled with gel polish and never found one I liked until now. The blue color in the picture is literally only one coat and it looks that good, it is full coverage , bright and so shiny (I have zero top coat on and it is shiner than most top coats I own). The white is just like most whites in that it is a bit sheer on the first coat but, I only had to do two coats which is way better than other whites I have used in the past. I was just testing these colors out but, I am so comfortable with the coverage and shine I can leave them just like this and be happy. Most of the colors though I would recommend two coats just to get the most even pigmented color you can. The polish once dry is very sticky but, the stickiness comes right off when you use rubbing alcohol over top of the nail leaving the nail smooth and insanely shiny. These polishes pair beautifully with most gel top coats and do not peel or chip. The color does not fade and easily can stay on for a week or two.

Removal of this polish is very easy as well. You can either sand it off like I do or use remover and soak the nail and it will come off quick and easy.

You receive a good amount of polish in each bottle so they will last you a while. Overall this is an amazing gel polish kit and the only one I will be using from now on! The price, the pigmentation, the ease of application and removal as well as the shine and ability to skip a topcoat if you choose makes these polishes a total win in my book!

title: STICKY SITUATION
text:
When I first received the item I was pretty excited. Tried opening it out of the outer plastic bag, but it was sticky. I thought it might have been a leak, and sure enough the product had sticky goo all over the cardboard packaging. It was pretty bad even for a leak, so I examined it over the sink, but then realized the ENTIRE top half of the spirit gum adhesive bottle had broken off and half the glue was filling the clear plastic cover attached to the cardboard.

At this point I was worried about glass cuts but I tried to salvage what remained of the glue. Using a scissor, I tried extracting the glue remover so at least I can use it to clean up all the stickiness resulting from the sticky situation. When I cut the packaging open, all the glue started dripping out into the sink. Long story short, the glue got everywhere and it was a mess cleaning up because THE REMOVER DIDN'T WORK EITHER! As there was a lot of glue, I also applied the remover liberally, including pouring out enough to cover my hand and soaking a cloth to scrape with. I had to later resort to using citric acid using lemons and that seemed to work better but still tough to remove.

I considered buying a new one but at that point I really didn't think it was worth it given my experience. All in all it took maybe 2 hours to clean up, and to begin with I have an extreme dislike for sticky substances on my hands.

I've always liked the "triple head" configuration of the Norelco shavers and this one is the best yet, with the settings for more sensitivity, and the heads that flex with your face so you don't miss anything. For me, the "normal" setting is sensitive enough to use, but it's nice to know you can make adjustments if needed.

The battery life is quite good; I took it on a recent three week business trip and only needed to charge it once!

My only criticism of the product is about the trimmer attached. It really doesn't do a wonderful job. It's not horrible, but it's just not as good as the rest of the shaver. The trimmer is a bit small and awkward to handle. I still keep my old Panasonic around when I want to do trimming! Otherwise, it was well worth the investment!

Recommended.

text:
I have been using this product nightly for 3 weeks and I can already tell my teeth are getting whiter! I have struggled with tooth sensitivity from whitening strips in the past, but this product gives me no sensitivity problems whatsoever. I'm so excited to have found a natural product that delivers on its promises!

I have not experienced any major messes as other users have. I find that when I follow the directions included in MMM exactly as stated, the product is virtually mess-free. My advice:
1. Use half of a scoop, as the directions tell you. Trust me, a little goes a long way. I hold my toothbrush over the pot as I pour the product on my toothbrush to waste as little product as possible and to avoid messes.
2. Buy an extra soft toothbrush to use exclusively for the Magic Mud. This product WILL stain the bristles, so no use in using your expensive electric toothbrush.
3. Brush the product on your teeth in small, gentle, circular motions, focusing on the outsides of your teeth (the ones you want white). KEEP YOUR MOUTH SHUT as best you can, once again, as the directions tell you.
4. Put on some fun or relaxing music while you brush - 2 minutes goes by very quickly that way.
5. Spit SLOWLY with the water running, spitting as close as you can to the drain. Less mud will splash up your sink that way.
6. Swish water around in your mouth to get extra mud out from your gums and teeth. Slowly spit again. I then brush with my electric toothbrush with toothpaste as normal.

title: WORTH THEY BUY!
text:
First off and to the bottom line, for quality and price point totally WORTH THE BUY!!

For reference, I ordered the 22 inch Color #2 Darkest Brown. I am 5'11" and ordered a length similar to my own hair.

Now for the background: I am mid 40s and I have always had SUPER thick, curly hair until an autoimmune thing kicked in at which point I lost 3/4s of that volume over a year. So I've been playing around with hair extensions. If we can dye out grays, do our nails, etc. to feel better about ourselves, why not hair extensions?? This particular piece is AMAZING! Honestly, it could be thicker, but then I feel it would be too heavy. It's perfect for me.

The color matches perfectly. The length is accurate. The sheen is beautiful. Some other reviewers complained about it tangling, and although it does, it doesn't tangle more than my own hair and brushes out back to original form with ease. ...Some other reviewers said it doesn't stay in place and I personally disagree. I straighten my hair, put it up in a ponytail at the height I want, clip in the extension, wrap the extra piece and secure with 3-4 bobby pins around the base. That may sound like a lot of work, but really it isn't (especially since I only wash my hair every third day or so, and in between days, I just shower without wetting my hair). It took me a couple tries to perfect it, but since, I have it down and wear it for 12-14 hours continuously without an issue. No headache, no slipping. My hair blends with the extension and you can't tell which strands are "real". ...Admittedly, I haven't played around with curling it or anything so I can't commit or advise on that.

All in all, I feel this is a cheap, quick and easy way to feel beautiful. And everyone deserves to feel beautiful! Hope this review helped :)

title: I love snails!
text:
I love snail slime. I have been reading about it for a while and am so glad I pulled the trigger to purchase it. I get occasional acne and scar easily. After two uses I saw a profound improvement in my skin. Nothing works that fast.I am a believer and am buying up all the slime I can find. The use of snail slime to improve skin dates back to ancient Greece, where Hippocrates, the famous physician, reportedly prescribed crushed snails and sour milk as a way to rid the skin of inflammation. In more recent times, the use of snail creams started when Chilean farmers who handled snails for the French market noticed their skin was visibly smoother. Nowadays, it is the secreted slime discovered by these farmers that is harvested to produce snail cream, not crushed up snails.
How the Slime Works
When snails are agitated, they excrete a thick fluid as a means to protect themselves. It may sound odd to use something like that on your skin, but remember that humans and most other animals also excrete oils as a way to protect their skin. In fact, the oil your body excretes to moisturize your skin is made up of lipids, sebum oil, and dead skin cells. As a snail protects itself, the slime that is excreted from its body is packed with nutrients like hyaluronic acid, glycoprotein enzymes, antimicrobial and copper peptides, and proteoglycans. All of these nutrients are already commonly added to beauty products and are thought to provide many benefits to skin.
The science behind snail slime as a viable beauty cream is mostly derived from lab studies where the effects of the slime have been tested on a variety of cell cultures. In these studies, research suggests that snail slime will stimulate the production of elastin and collagen, increase fibronectin protein production, and stimulate increased proliferation of fibroblasts. While all of these traits could be beneficial for skin, there have yet to be significant cosmetic trials or research into how snail slime actually affects the skin, and how long those effects last. In fact, there haven’t been any significant clinical trials on how a specific beauty product containing snail slime actually works on this skin – just the slime itself.
One of the main difficulties in conducting clinical trials on the benefits of snail slime is that the market has not fully figured out how to guarantee the results of testing. After all, if snail creams are to be effective, then the slime has to have a consistent concentration of the various chemical compounds, but this is difficult to guarantee. Because the success of trials leans heavily on the quality of snail extract used, the concentration of slime and the way it is excreted and processed, test results can sometimes be misleading. Some companies that manufacture snail creams do choose to keep a steady supply of their own snails so they can better regulate the extraction and formulation of the slime.

title: Newer is not better
text:
Well, I've owned this razor for over a year now and I think I'm going back to my old Norelco 9160XL (similar to the current 8200 series). What don't I like about the Arcitec model?

1) It's loud--loud enough for my wife to complain in the morning when she is still trying to sleep. It is much louder than my 9160 which is nearly silent.
2) I don't think this new HQ10 blade set cuts as well as the HQ9 set. I believe I get a closer cut from the old razor, and with less effort. I find it easier to shave my neck with the 9160, which is exactly what I had hoped the Arcitec would do better, but it doesn't.
3) I don't like the hair trimmer design. The design on the 9160 (and current 8200) is much better. It's much more convenient to use and it trims better.
4) It's nearly double the price of the 8200 series.

What do I like about the Arcitec?

1) I like the design of the handle much better. It's thinner, longer, and feels better in your hand.
2) I can get about 1 month of daily use out of a single charge.

If it was quieter and it cut better I'd highly recommend it; but it doesn't. If I had to purchase a new razor today I'd buy the 8240. By the way, I've been using Norelco razors for decades. I've not had any problem whatsoever with my razors since they moved away from NiCad batteries (at least 5 years ago). The old razors batteries used to die and they were not replaceable, so you'd have to throw the whole thing away. But this is now very much a thing of the past. I highly recommend the brand.

title: Effective Lotion for Intense Skin Needs
text:
There is much to appreciate about this Zeroid Intensive Lotion for Severe Dry & Disordered Skin. This is a Korean-made product and I do tend to be a fan of most Korean skin care products.

This arrives in a 6.76 ounce bottle. It was nicely sealed. I was modestly concerned about the product's clearly labeled manufacturing date 3/11/2020 indicating I'm receiving it over 16 months after the manufacturing date. While this isn't always an issue, it doesn't particularly instill confidence.

This lotion uses what the manufacturer calls MLE Technology along with Defensamide and Ceramides along with Squalane for moisturizing. It is noted as being good for all ages including babies and children.

While I had some concerns, I'm overall pleased with the product's performance. This is a white, smooth lotion that applies easily. I'd actually just had some seasonal allergy reactions on my skin while working in the yard and opted to use this on my skin. It soothed my skin greatly and has gone to work surprisingly rapidly to calm down my inflamed, swollen skin. I'm actually quite impressed.

There's no scent that I can detect.

In terms of value, this is fairly modest. While this is being advertised as somewhat of a premium lotion, I'm not sure I can justify continued use - we'll see how it continues to do and if I notice a definite improvement over other products. However, I definitely can't deny that it's effective and it is definitely making my skin look and feel better.

Zeroid is noted as the #1 Dermacosmetic in Korea for the last decade. It's easy to understand why as this product works incredibly well and surprisingly quickly.

Overall, while I am a bit concerned about the manufacturing date and the price point is a touch high I'll continue to use and compare it to other available products. For now, I'll say I'm impressed and happy with the lotion's performance on my troubled skin.

title: Same great smell I remember, just LESS of it.
text:
I started buying this when it first came out and because it became unavailable for time, switched to a different fragrance. A few years later (March of 2017), after finally running out of my previously ordered multi Apollo spray pack, I was reminded of the Kilo (after finding the Apollo was now temporarily unavailable) and and ordered it in quantity. After receiving it I noticed it had the same great scent I remember, that will always linger on clothes (always spray on clothes, NOT on skin), but also noticed it had been repackaged in a new kind of spray can. Knowing what I do about the corporate world of business I immediately compared the content amount to the previous can that still sat discarded in my bathroom trash container. Sure enough AXE had reduced the amount of content in the can by an ounce and redesigned it so that side by side it APPEARED to be almost the same size. Of course the slight reduction in price doesn't match up to the per ounce value (ROUGHLY previous price of $4.25 for 5oz vs now approximately, $4.34 per can; though buying in quantity as I did can reduce it up to$2.86 per can when purchasing an 8 pack). This is just the nature of the corporate beast. Promised profits + general greed = f the consumer.

None the less, if you need it I'd recommend buying it in quantity before they reduce it to 3 ounces. It's still a great product and a good value, when purchased in bulk.

title: I wanted to love these...
text:
I really did want to love these. I had to cut off a bunch of hair after a bleach accident, and I HATE having short hair, so I've been curling it just to make it a little less awful. I obviously don't want to use heat when I'm trying to nurse my hair back to health, so my only real option is sleeping in curlers. Foam rods make great curls, but they are horribly uncomfortable, and my hair is too slippery for rag curlers when it's this short. These looked like a happy medium.

These are pretty easy to use - they roll well, and the wires keep them in place pretty well. They are much, much more comfortable to sleep in than foam rods. I understand that they have to be squishy to be comfortable; however they are just too small! I tried them every night for two weeks, and I never got the curls I wanted. They almost always ended up much too tight, except when I tried rolling larger sections, which ended up really uneven - tight in places and barely curled in others. I'm going for a defined curl, not soft waves, but these were ridiculous.

I ended up removing the foam and replacing it with cut-up foam rods, which was a slight improvement over just the foam rods. I'm currently testing (second night) foam rods that are very big but made of super squishy, comfortable foam. If they don't work, I'll go back to the hybrid of these and fosm rods til I find something better, do they aren't totally worthless, but I wouldn't buy them again.

title: Disappointed - went back to my T800
text:
I bought a T800 quite a few years ago when I found the Austrian-made unit on sale at the local Target store. It lasted very well, and I was somewhat disappointed when the battery eventually would no longer accept a charge, though it continued to work while plugged in.
After carefully looking into alternatives, I went with a T970 from Amazon.com, hoping for the same quality. Major letdown! This Chinese-made unit just is not up to the same standard as my T800. The charger is a seperate seperate and bulky transformer, instead of the simple cord of the T800. The T970 is larger, more awkward to hold and to use, and more fragile in every possible way. The vacuum, which was one of the initial attractions, works, but only marginally well, and the unit is unstable when laid down on a solid surface. If the mile-long charging cord is attached, expect to have to prop the unit against a wall to prevent it rolling over.
I spent $6.00 on a top-quality replacement cell for my T800 (shipping was $4.00, for a 700mA Sanyo AA), and after careful disassembly and reassembly, successfully replaced the ailing cell without breaking anything. Unbelievably, The T800 now outlasts the T970 two-fold.
I wish I'd stuck it out with the T800 in the first place.
.
Updated June 29, 2009.
After about two years of irregular use and the resulting regular complete self-discharges, the T970 stopped functioning even while plugged in, unless first given time to recharge. Initial time to start working after plugging in has increased to the point where it no longer works even being plugged in for 24 hours.

title: An Evolutionary Upgrade That Pays off BIG
text:
I've used Oral B toothbrushes for years now. I have always been more than satisfied. I purchased my most recent professional series over 6 years ago. I've always watched them and from appearances, nothing seemed to change. I was wrong! When the brand new 4000 series came out it piqued my invest. I bought one at announcement and when I opened it I was pleased by several differences:
1. The new spare toothbrush holder is better thought out and works much better than the old 'stand up' one.
2. The charging base itself is flatter and more attractive.
3. Unlike the old charging base, there is no where for gunk to pool and become unwashable. Sounds like a small thing, but who wants to look at a mess on their kitchen counter?
When I used it I found out that the improvements were more than skin deep. This is a better toothbrush. I cannot quantify it, but it does clean better, not a little bit, but a lot. In addition there were some positive functional changes.
1. The standard two minute cycle with beeps every 30 seconds has been augmented with a ' deep cleaning' cycle that simply uses the same brushing action with a three minute cycle and beeps every 45 seconds.
2. A separate polishing cycle has been added.
3. A sensitive cycle has been added. For people first converting to an electric toothbrush, especially kids, this is a plus.
4. A pressure alarm light that is easily visible has been added. This was a plus for me since I saw that I had been brushing too hard at the very back of my gums.
Is this an entirely new and revolutionary product for cleaning your teeth? No. Is a very real upgrade resulting from refining that which was already good? Yes. If your Oral B is several years old, you may want to consider upgrading.

title: Good features; disappointing results
text:
I have had this razor for 6 weeks now (that's past the 3 week adjustment period) and overall I am disappointed with it.

First, what I like about the razor:

The quick rinse cleaning is a very nice feature and the reason why I choose this razor. I am not very good about cleaning the razors.

The trimmer is on a spring release that works much better than my old Norelco's trimmer that took some force to open.

Indicators to let you know when to recharge and when the razor is at full charge.

What I did not like about the razor:

For the other posts who said the larger blades did not seem to make a difference from older razors, I must agree.

The charger light is only a light, not a gauge.

On the subject of charging, the manual says that you should not let the razor sit in the charger to preserve the internal battery. This can be a real problem since I shave close to the time I am leaving. So, I don't have the time to wait and remembering to charge it when I get home usually doesn't happen.

I wasn't sure what to expect from this, I anticipated a reasonably "scrubby" exfoliator due to the name and though it does provide some scrubbing action it certainly isn't as...abrasive?...as I thought it might be. In any form, vitamin C, MSM, hyaluronic acid, green tea, rosehip oil and Coenzyme Q10 from Ove Beauty provide potent antioxidant protection, shielding skin from damaging free radicals—those pesky rogue molecules that promote premature aging. The most abundant forms of free-radical damage are environmental factors we can’t escape—think sun damage, pollution and oxygen—that assault skin on a daily basis, but that’s where topical vitamin C can help.

When incorporated into your daily skincare lineup, well-formulated products containing vitamin C and these other other ingredients can provide a range of benefits that keep your skin younger-looking, longer. They can reduce the appearance of brown spots and other types of sun damage

The toothbrushes themselves are good, but I don't feel they will last very long with one charger already broken within 1.5 days and having to share the other charger

Update: the other charger broke now too. The prongs on the charger create a caustic blue substance (I'm no chemist, I'm sure there's a name for it) while the toothbrushes charge and then they break off. All fine if two prongs make contact with the contact points on the bottom of the brush, which are both on the same side, while there are 4 prongs on the charger. If two prongs on opposite side break off, you're out of luck. I'd like my money back for both of these. Even if they sent new chargers, they'd have the same flaw. The toothbrushes really should have either a better charging design or a secondary way to charge them.

I'd have to restart... and restart ... and restart .... and restart ... cut some knots out ... restart ... etc.

I was really looking forward to wearing blonde-pink-purple ombre braids for Valentine's week, and I tried to stick with it. But I realized I'd probably have to spend another 4 hours fighting a pink and purple rat's nest on a Saturday afternoon. I quit and actually took the braids I did manage to wrangle in out. By that point, I had been throwing away so much of the hair, I didn't think I would have enough to finish. That big nappy mess in the pic is probably a bundle's worth of hair that was un-salvageable because of the tangles.

Whoever manufactures this hair needs to find better quality fiber. The colors are beautiful, yes, but the fiber quality is trash. Why they are charging $20 for this pretty but low quality stuff is beyond me. I usually pay about $5/3 bundles at my local beauty store (and that stuff doesn't tangle anywhere near as bad). I understand the coloring probably increases the manufacturing cost, but that's only if the fiber was good quality to begin with. This hair would be worth $20 if the fiber were better.

I got this epilator about a year and a half ago and I've used it in average once a week on my legs, bikini area and armpits.

I like that it is wireless, so it gives you freedom to use it in different rooms and the cord does not get on the way. I also like that is a good size and easy to hold. The moving part is easy to clean (with the brush, included) and it can be washed with soap and water (I air dry it after that).

The epilator can only be used wireless, so if the battery is low and you haven't finished the job, you have to wait until it is fully charged again before being able to turn it on.

Mine takes about 30 minutes to fully charge and gives me about 45 mins of wireless use. However, a couple of weeks ago I noticed that even when it was fully charged, the red light (signaling low battery) started flashing after about 15 mins of use. I guess the battery wears out eventually, and as it cannot be used while it is plugged in, it will rend the whole epilator useless.

title: Not thrilled so far
text:
I just picked this up this evening and unboxed it a few minutes ago. I'm already a bit disappointed with it so far. I had read the reviews here on Amazon, and knew that some people were finding a rough shave with it. I haven't had a chance to try that yet ... but the cleaning system is a bit of a disappointment.

First off, the cleaning solution that they provide contains no alcohol. My Remington with cleaning system had an alcohol-based solution, and I was always sure my razor was clean and sterilized. But this? No alcohol? Hmm.

Secondly - my Remington (and the Brauns, too) had a small filter packet that was supposed to catch all the little bits of whiskers that were going through the cleaning solution. This one? No such thing. So you mean weeks-old whiskers are going to be floating around in the non-alcohol based cleaning solution? No thanks.

The "unplug after it's fully charged" thing will probably be a bit annoying - but I have a feeling some people are worrying a bit too much about this. I left my Remington in the stand constantly for 5 years. Eventually the battery burned out - and I realize it was probably my fault (I didn't read the manual) but I don't think you need to get obsessive like some reviewers have here and get it unplugged *immediately* after it's done with its cycle. When you get home from work in the evening would probably be find. Just give it a full charge once every several days.

Even though I haven't even given it a full charge yet, I have a feeling it's going to be going back and I'll be buying the Braun instead - even though my face seems to prefer a rotary.

title: Highly Recommended
text:
I replaced a different manufacturer's very old electric razor with the Arcitec 1050, and have been using it for about three weeks. My primary shaving method has been the razor blade, supplemented by the electric for a fast shave now and then. I am so satisfied with the new Norelco that it has become my primary shaver. It delivers results virtually as close as a blade, and sometimes I think it is just as good. I don't feel that I need to use a blade to get a close shave any more, and I'm really amazed by the results. I didn't think that an electric could ever come this close to a blade. I guess that the technology has improved over the last twenty years, like everything else!

The shaver is not perfect, but the disadvantages are minor in my opinion. It does produce hair shavings, so I just shave over the sink. I don't mind cleaning up a little. The trimmer is quite small, but it does work well enough to clean the sideburns with an up and down motion. I have found that the shave is quite comfortable if you don't overdo it - just shave until you are clean, and use an after-shave cream to avoid minor irritation. I would prefer being able to leave the plug in the shaver, rather than remove it right after the charge is complete. It's a small inconvenience for such a great shave. And it is more economical than blades in the long run.

My T980 does almost everything perfectly: it holds a charge for weeks; its vacuum reduces the number of trimmed hairs around the sink by about 70%; it feels wonderful and it works quickly.

However, my T980 does NOT stay at the level I set it at. If I don't firmly grip the length setting wheel it will jump from, say, a 5 to a 3 -- as it did this morning -- embarrassing me either by giving me a patchy trim or by forcing me to shorten my beard length.

This problem doesn't seem to be a result of the way I'm, say, holding the trimmer -- I used the [[ASIN:B0001HYL0M T765]] for four years without having this problem -- but rather a flaw in the trimmer itself. From these reviews, it seems like only a few of the T980s have this problem; still, you might want to try the [[ASIN:B000FED5D0 T780]], which doesn't seem to have this problem -- I wish I had.

Update 3/12/08: Make me look like a fool once, shame on me; make me look like a fool twice, shame on you.

I've used this trimmer about 12 times since writing this review, and by a combination of duct tape, a pinch grip, and a good deal of vigilance I had been able to avoid too many embarrassing shifts in beard length.

...until this morning, when it shifted silently from a 5 (Late Winter Academic Beard) to 3 (Peach Fuzz) in mid-shave. Two options: shave my entire beard to a 3, which is inappropriate for my face type, or look deranged because half of my face is at 5 and half is at 3.

I threw my T980 in the garbage ten minutes ago.

-No silicones. It's specifically described as being silicone-free.

title: It isn't even close to natural bristle
text:
I wanted to try a synthetic fiber brush since it is impossible to dry your natural bristle brush sufficiently before packing it up on the day of travel. I was looking for a brush that I can use, shake out and pack within minutes. For use at home, I've had over the years a couple of natural badger brushes of varying quality, ranging from lower grade black only brushes to very fine silvertip. So, trust me, I know how they feel.
This brush is for me virtually unusable.
When i try to lather up, i spray water and soap all over the bathroom. Try as i may, i couldn't prevent the spray. When these synthetic bristles are deflected even only a little, they spring back with a snap. It appears that the spring back force increases linearly with the amount of deflection. And all the fibers move almost in unison.

This is very different in natural bristles where more force bends the hair further, but it isn't like a linear increase in force. During the lather, the bristles conform to your face and the circular action seems to gently bent the hairs in one or the other direction. The brush also spreads a bit, as fibers are pushed and bent a little. Once you lift the natural hair brush off your face, the bristles don't string back all at once. Some fibers may return to their approximate straight form, but the water and soap mixture will clump some of them together.

I want to be clear that I don’t object to a different brush feel. As long as it does the job of lathering up and isn’t so coarse to feel like sandpaper, I’m fine. This synthetic fiber, on the other hand, are best compared to very playable, soft steel springs. Even when I tried to lather up very slowly and gingerly, each fiber literally snapped back to its original position. When you lift the brush off your face, all the bristles are back in place as if you just upacked the brush.

In summary, this brush is far from coming close to the feel of badger bristles. I cant use it without spraying soap all over and I wish I could return it, but it appears I’m stuck with this thing.

title: Weightless, Skin Feels Silky, Makeup Lasts Longer, Blurs Lines-Odd Smell, Skin Gets Weird Sensation
text:
This Grown Alchemist Anti-Pollution Primer has a gel texture that feels weightless on my skin. This doesn’t have a lot of ingredients and lacks chemical fragrance, but I find the scent is moderately strong. I assume it’s mostly from natural lavender, rose and grapefruit oils. I really don’t love the scent as it smells odd to me, but it mellows out and doesn’t really bother me. The lavender and grapefruit oils are potential irritants, but my sensitive skin hasn’t had any visible reaction or real discomfort using this primer.

I have dry skin and when I apply the primer my skin feels a weird initial sensation that reminds me of alcohol, but so far it hasn’t caused any visible dryness. I do always apply a hydrating essence, serum and cream before the primer and I see the primer has glycerin, so that may be why I don’t see dryness or maybe something in this just feels mildly irritating to my skin. This does have benzyl alcohol pretty low on the list, so maybe I’m feeling that but the good part is that I haven’t had any real issue. I can’t say if daily use might dry my skin.

This primer is super lightweight, so sheer it’s invisible and I don’t feel any sticky residue. It makes my skin feel silky, and my cream and liquid foundations spread smoothly and evenly over it. I do notice a blurring effect, especially around my mouth area where I need all the help I can get. My makeup holds up well all day even though the weather has been so really hot lately. Other than that weird sensation I get that does eventually pass, my skin generally feels comfortable. Like it. 4 stars. Made in Australia.

Ingredients: Aqua/Water/Eau, Sodium Acrylates Crosspolymer-2, Acetyl Heptapeptide-4 (Prebiotic-Peptide/Peptides Prébiotiques), Caprylyl Glycol, Glycerin (*Plant/Plante), Fructose, Withania Somnifera Root Extract (*Plant/Plante), Ganoderma Lucidum ( Mushroom) Extract, Citrus Paradisi (Grapefruit) Peel Oil, Lavandula Angustifolia (Lavender) Oil, Rosa Damascena (Rose Absolute/Rose Absolue) Flower Oil, Benzyl Alcohol, Dehydroacetic Acid. title: LOVE THIS STUFF!
text: I used to buy Vikki Lamotta Wonderlift YEARS and YEARS ago in New York, and then stopped using it to try a lot of other brands.  Hers was the original, and it still works great.  HOWEVER, you DO need to play around with it for a while to get it to look natural and so that your face isn't all powdery looking.  I use a very light moisturizing lotion on my face FIRST and let it completely absorb before I apply the Vikki Lamota Wonderlift, and then I let the Wonderlift DRY FOR HALF AN HOUR AT LEAST until it is fully firmed up, after which a slight white chalky look is on my skin...  THEN, I get my hands damp under the faucet (shake off all the excess water) and rub MORE of the moisturizing lotion into my hands and mix it with the little bit of water in the palms of my hands and then lightly PAT my hands all over my face where it appears white or chalky looking. I only use a tiny bit of make-up as a TOUCH UP ONLY on places that have blotches or redness, because you CANNOT rub makeup over your face once the Wonderlift has dried or it will simply ball up and take the Wonderlift OFF!  It takes some practice, but if you are dedicated to looking YEARS YOUNGER (as I am!!) then this will do the trick!

title: Looks nice and easy to use...jury’s still out on results.
text:
This thing looks very nice, and feels even nicer! It’s beautiful, and very easy to use. However, it is difficult to grip at times, especially if your hands are wet or moisturized. There are two clipped corners to allow for optimal grip location, so that is a much-appreciated design feature. Nevertheless, the smooth glass edges can make it tricky to get a consistent, sturdy grip. I wear nitrile gloves while using it, so that I feel more confident in the hold I’ve got on it, especially over a hard surface. So, keep that in mind. That being said, though, it is far more aesthetically appealing, user-friendly, and gentler than the traditional pumice stones or foot graters.

A protective storage case would be a great addition to this item. I saved all the packaging and have been placing the file back into the plastic packaging tray and then placing that tray back into the outer plastic packaging box. Something similar to a travel bar soap container or a retainer case would be perfect (slimmer, of course, to fit the file)! The storage case with drainage holes for drying would minimize the risk of breaking the file during cleaning, drying, and storing it. For the current price point, I personally think a reusable storage case should be included.

All that aside, my only real concern, and the reason for the current rating, is that my feet actually felt and looked dryer and rougher several days to a week after the first use. I realize this may be due to my own user error, as I followed the exfoliation with my usual moisturization regimen. It is reasonable to assume I should have taken extra steps to protect and care for me feet immediately following the exfoliation, as the delicate, softer skin was exposed. So, I am going to try it again, this is over-moisturizing and wearing plush socks for the few days afterward. I will update my review with my new results!

Overall, I currently recommend this foot file. I find it to be worth trying out, and is a better alternative to the more abrasive methods. I have included photos showing the packaging and tray in which I keep it stored, as well as close-ups of the smooth top size and gritty underside. Hope they help!
