title: Jet Clean is a gimmick; any Norelco model is just as good
text:
If you don't own a Norelco triple-head razor, stop reading now and just buy one -- any one. Or if you own an ancient Norelco double-header, or a triple-header before the Lift'n'Cut heads, sure, get a new one. But if, like me, you have an old model, do your utmost to replace its parts and you'll be just as happy. (I replaced heads and two solder-tab NiCd's.) Here's why (echoing other reviewers' sentiments):
(i) This particular model is no faster than my old one, its "Speed XL" moniker notwithstanding. Maybe that's because of the new blade size/design, or maybe the old motor turns faster. (Seemingly, old AC and NiCd models spin faster than old NiMH models; YMMV.)
(ii) This model is no more adjustable (N/M/S) for closeness of shave than my old adjustable model (1-10). The heads do indeed rock more than the old spring suspension, but I still must stretch my skin with the other hand to get a close shave over the bumps.
(iii) The cleaning system leaves stubble-grit on the rubber bits. Also mine required repairs after 5 months, because the washer mechanism got stuck. (It has a 2-year warranty (yay!), alas they insisted on shipping the razor back, too (aargh!).) Norelco's attempt to "Gillette up a revenue stream" with consumables, i.e. cleanser fluid, is a little transparent.
(iv) The cleaning system leaves you with a damp razor, even if you shake it and let it stand for an entire day -- it's the shaving equivalent of a wet willie in the morning. Worse, the small quantity of liquid remaining is just enough to create a jumpy slide across the face -- not as even as completely dry, nor as smooth as a lubricated wet shave.

On the plus side, the battery life on this razor is excellent, and longer than old Norelcos. If you live out of a suitacase, you won't have to pack the cord. Which is good, because the charger circuit has been pulled out of the razor body and into a wall wart.

The razor rates 4 stars (not 5 because they have made better razors before, and hopefully will hence). The cleaning system gets 1 star. So don't get a CC model, but definitely do buy a Norelco razor. If you switch from blade or foil electric, please do as the manual says: give it two weeks of rotary use before judging the closeness of the shave. But especially if it's your first razor, grasshopper, you will be hooked for life!

title: This GUY absolutely loves this luxury body wash!
text:
I hate to say it, but I could care less about what kind of body wash I use and the ingredients it contains. My favorite brands to date are Axe, Dove, and Old Spice.

Having the opportunity to try this Hask Body Wash was an eye-opening experience for me. I really didn't think I was going to be impressed by a hypoallergenic wash that stripped away all the drying additives that I had become accustomed to applying to my skin on a daily basis.

The first positive impression was the fact that this Body Wash arrives as a pump product. It allows me to put it in the corner of the shower and not have to constantly turn the bottle upside down and squeeze out the contents.

The next positive impression was from pump to skin. This stuff is nice and creamy. It lathers very well as you sponge it across your body. For that reason, a relatively small amount goes a long way.

What impressed me the most was the lasting effect this Body Wash had on my skin after the shower was over. My skin wasn't dried out. It was smooth, with a refreshing coconut, vanilla scent.

While two of these bottles are more expensive than the body wash brands (and the like) I mentioned above, I do feel that the price is justified in that this is definitely a "luxury" body wash that will give you an entirely different kind of cleaning experience free of additives and filled with natural moisturizers that will hydrate your skin rather than dry it out.

title: Smells great, works better
text:
I purchased my first bottle of Castle Forbes Lime Oil Aftershave Balm in October of 2011, and I am just now replacing it with a new one. Yes, this stuff is a little pricey, but it is well worth the price to me.

This balm comes packaged in a very nice box, and inside you will find the actual bottle. It is a heavy, solid bottle, with a nice cap, and it looks very attractive sitting on your counter or in your medicine cabinet.

The first thing you will probably notice when using it is the delicious lime smell. It smells wonderful, but is not overpowering once on your skin. It is a fresh, light scent that I enjoy all year.

The balm itself is very high quality, and makes my skin feel great after even the closest straight razor or double edge shave. In the past, I used several different "sensitive skin" aftershave balms from all the big names you find in chain drug stores, and non of them work as well as the Castle Forbes. This balm works so much better that I can actually use less than the big brands, and my skin still feels more moisturized and less irritated. While a bottle of the competitors balms would last me a month, maybe two tops, the Castle Forbes has lasted me 9 months as of now, and I still have about a month's worth left in the bottle!

After using this, I have no redness, no irritation, and no razor burn. It leaves my skin feeling soft and moisturized, without being greasy. If you apply too much, it can make your face feel "sticky" for a while after, but that just means you applied more than you need. With a product as high quality as this, less is more!

Overall, yes it is expensive, but you can use much less than competitor's offerings, it smells great, it feels great, and most importantly, it works!!

title: Great e file with a dust collector and light, all in a compact package.
text:
I do my own nails at home, and this item is perfect. When I tried a different e file I learned really fast that a dust collector was essential — the dust got *everywhere*. I thought having everything in one machine would be a compromise, but all three functions work great. The light is nice and bright and I can put it exactly where I need it, for both application and filing. The fan is a little loud (too loud to hear the tv), but I don’t have anything to compare it to and I don’t mind anyway because it does such a great job with the dust.

The e file is way better than the cheap one that is the most popular on here (you know the one). I bought and tried both and kept this one, so I will compare the two. The hand piece on this one is smaller, lighter, with less vibration and it’s quieter too. The speed adjustment is incredibly smooth and accurate, and it will spin at a very low speed. The other one will spin slow but it’s tough to adjust the speed accurately, and the lighted display on that one doesn’t tell you anything. I also like that this one has an “off” position on the rotation switch in between “forward” and “reverse”, so it’s impossible to harm the motor by switching too fast between forward and reverse. The motor is plenty strong too.

If you want a less expensive e file then this is the one to get. If you get a cheap e file and a dust collector separately it would be the same price, and with this one you have higher quality and a lamp too.

title: Best shower cap I've found thus far and been searching for a bit
text: I often wonder if the reviews I read are actually real sometimes bc I see so many that are both rated best to worst for the exact same product. I've been on the hunt for a decent shower cap. Never did I think it would be so hard to find the right one to do only one simple thing - cover head and keep hair dry while in shower. I have long hair so need mine to fit and accommodate my hair length. I don't need it to do anything more amazing than that. I bought some in local stores only to return bc as strange as it sounds, they didn't do that one simple task.  They actually were either too big (in an awkward way) or too small (pulled hair and fit like a cap made for swimming) It was weird that I was finding it so hard to find a normal shower cap that works. One I bought for $14 had this strange design where it was way too narrow and tight but also too long. Strangest thing!  And I also found to some degree you do get what you pay for. So ok, this one is a smidge pricey I guess as some complained but there are some, I see that are over $30 so $12 seems much better. It fits fine and even allows for tightening for those with a smaller head. It accommodates my long hair and bow is just added for some degree of cuteness bc let's face it hard to feel the least bit attractive when wearing a shower cap. And contrary to another review I read the bow stays in place just fine - I can't fathom how hers didn't and sagged bc material is stiff. Only thing I will say it isn't as ample as picture leads you to believe. I understand we all have different sized heads, but it's shown to be extra poofy on pretty young model. Id share a picture of me wearing it but well that may scare people off and I do wish to leave a favorable review bc this cap actually does what it is meant to do - fit head and keep hair dry. End of story. Happy Bathing Ladies :)

They felt tight for a couple of hours, like my feet were too big for my skin, but it wasn't uncomfortable - just noticeable. I forgot about it for a couple of days, and by the Saturday after (so 4 days) HUGE chunks of skin were peeling off of my feet. I had an appointment for my first pedicure in a year on Sunday, and the technician was somewhat appalled at the amount of skin she was removing from my feet. Today is Monday, and despite the thorough job the pedicurist did removing the skin, I'm still peeling a bit. I expect this will be done in a couple of days, but the result is unbelievably smooth, soft feet. I will absolutely use these again (and will probably combine with a pedicure again so I don't have to do all the skin peeling myself). The only downside (and this is mentioned on the instructions) is that my feet are a lot more sensitive to temperature and sunlight. So walking around barefoot on the hot concrete at the pool is rather painful, and I had to use higher SPF sunscreen on my feet because the new skin felt like it was frying in the sun. It didn't burn, it was just uncomfortable. Overall, I'm very pleased with the product and will absolutely purchase again!

title: Warning - product is not as portrayed on site
text:
I purchased 4 of these as a gift to my mother and grandmother. I turned them onto Ruby Stone years ago, but they are not able to find them locally anymore. This set had the buffer added which they didn't need, but wouldn't mind if it was in the package; the real purchase here was the Ruby Stone file itself.

The picture shows the Ruby Stone like I expected to receive it - a pullout version like I have used in the past. It's always been very easy to use and, most importantly easy to handle and gentle. There are arthritic hands in play here. Instead the file is some sort of flip out side-sheath with a very point top. I guess you are supposed to be able to flip it out or pull it out completely (since whenever I flip it it just end up coming out all the way) and then put it back. I found it hard to get out (the plastic is cheap and curves in to grab the file) and almost impossible to get back in. There is no way that arthritic hands could handle. I think the pointy end, combined with the difficulty to manage, only makes this a dangerous combo. Sure, if someone removes the file for them the first time they can ditch the case but I hate that then there is nothing protecting the stone file from breaking (this version is much thinner than past versions as well, by about half the thickness. And, not that this makes any difference but is nice to know, it is white vs the original pink).

Overall, I am very disappointed. I tried to return the files but will have to pay shipping even though I was misled. So now I am stuck with them. I will scour local stores to find something different for my mother and grandmother.

I do not recommend this product unless you cannot find any other ruby stone alternative. And I hope the image gets updated so others are not misled and left to hold the expense for a product they don't want like I was.

The brushes as a whole are a great set! I don't use all of them, but I do use most every morning as part of my daily makeup routine. The bigger brushes are a good girth and feel good to use in my hand. The thinner brushes are better for more detailed work like eyebrows, concealer or eye shadow. The brushes come with a recommended guide for how to use each brush with different kinds of makeup - this was very helpful for my mother (who'd never had a complete brush set) when I bought this set for her as well. The case is very pretty and perfect for travelling!

My only complaint: the part of the handles where the wood is glued into the metal piece is very weak, and starts to detach after only a couple uses. I accidentally dropped one of the larger brushes on my counter, and the wood piece completely detached from the metal piece and I could see they were only attached with a minimal amount of glue. title: Great but, get the cheaper one. Just as good.
text:
Do you have migraines or Meniere's disease or just have a sensitive head? Don't get any of the pulsating Oral B brushes. They will just make you nauseous or trigger a headache.

I have used the classic Oral B electric brush for many years. A fantastic simple white design by Braun of Germany - since discontinued after Braun was bought by an American company. Now I have the simple low end non pulsing model. Essentially the same guts and head as the classic but with an ugly, over stylized, blue body.

When the battery started to die on my classic model, I picked up a pulsating Oral B. It is really banging away at your teeth and does as good a job as the non pulsatinging. But it vibrates your jaw and skull like, well, a vibrating electric tooth brush! After a month, it was just too much for me. I went back to the dieing battery original, but soon got its replacement as a gift.

The verdict: I'm in my 40s and I've had about 6 different dentists (moving from job to job) in 5 different states. One was a professor at a dental college. After each visit, they all proclaim my teeth are in excellent shape. I use the cheapest Oral B electric brush (non pulsating) in the morning and before bed with Colgate Total. I also floss just one time before bed and use the Crest rinse for night time. I get them cleaned every 6-9 months.

Save your money and get the cheapest Oral B electric toothbrush. I think it is on sale sometimes for about $10.

title: Once You Learn How To Use, It's Great
text:
I know it says "Men's" on there, but I am a woman, and I use this razor. I just happen to have very coarse hair on my legs. Lady shavers don't do it for me. In fact, I've always had to use 2 razors, a men's for the legs and a women's for the underarms. I know, more information than you wanted, but it's relevant.

This razor is the only one I have ever had that works for everything. Oh, I had some really nasty razor burn before I got the hang of it, but since then, it's been great! No cleaning and maintaining 2 razors any more.

I have found with this razor, that putting pressure on it is a big no-no. If I do that, it will tear up my skin big time. I have to just sort of guide/glide it over the area, no pressure on it, and it does a beautiful job without the razor burn. Now, I honestly don't know how that would go for a guy and his face, but that's how it works for me on ALL parts I shave.

This razor only needs charged about every two to three weeks. There is no indicator system on this razor, and when it needs charged, it just quits. If you keep playing with the on/off button, it will run for 2 or 3 more minutes, but that's it. It takes one hour (about) to recharge, much better than any razor I ever had before.

This razor is easy to clean, just run the head under the sink, shake the water off, and let it dry out. I do that once a week. Easy peasy.

Like I said, I've no idea how my experience might translate for a guy. I gave it 4 stars because of the lack of a recharge indicator. Other that, it is wonderful for me.

This is the second set of hair clips I bought from Shemay and I am very pleased that this set is as high quality as the first one. The clips came in a zip-lock bag on the scheduled delivery date. # They are the right size for my daughter. She is only 14 months old now and is really tiny. Big ribbon bows are just not matched to her size. I found that she gets more compliment when wearing tiny hair bows than wearing bigger ones.

Bottom line:
I am very happy with this high quality hair clips and I think I will buy a second set in the near future to make pigtails for my daughter.

title: Not tested in animals; Hypoalergenic and sulfate free!
text:
I'm a person that loves fragrances, specially natural oils.
I have a diffuser, I add natural essential oils to all my homemade lotions, shampoos, conditioners, body scrubs. My favorite scents are peppermint, sandalwood and argan.

I have tried a few other brands of argan shampoo, and as someone who loves skin and hair products, i'm always on the lookout for brands I haven't tried yet. The ones that work best for my skin and hair, I become a recurring customer.

I have other products from Pure Body Naturals; I like the fact that their products strive to use natural ingredients, mostly are hypoallergenic, and this shampoo is sulfate free.
This shampoo is very thick and dense, you don't need to use much to wash your hair; it doesn't lather - because it's sulfate free. I have no problem with it not lathering. If you think products need to lather to clean, you're mistaken. Sulfate strips your hair of it's natural oils, making it much weaker, brittle, and dry, that's why you need conditioner after a sulfate full shampoo.
I did not use conditioner after this shampoo, and i wash my hair twice, once to remove dirt, and second to rinse and coat my hair with the "goodies" in this shampoo; specially because i work in the elements and with animals, my hair and scalp need good cleaning.

My hair smells absolutely amazing, looks healthy, shiny, strong and clean. It brushed easily, no snagging, no knots. Very silky and soft.

I love the pump, a couple of squirts and no lid to close, and if it falls in the shower, it won't spill everywhere.

Very well made product, great natural ingredients, awesome smell! Highly satisfied!!! OH! Very important: NOT tested on animals!
Although i've received this product discounted, my review is an expression of the uses i put it through.

title: A good, no-frills electric razor

I've been using this Norelco 6423 Reflex Plus corded electric razor for about 2 1/2 weeks now, and so far, I'm glad I decided to buy it.

My old Panasonic rechargeable razor didn't seem to be holding a charge for very long anymore, plus it was time to replace the foil and cutting heads again. For about the same amount I would have spent to replace the worn parts on my old razor (not even including the cost of replacing the battery), I got a brand new Norelco razor!

The first thing I noticed about the Norelco is that it's MUCH quieter than my old Panasonic. My Panasonic sounded like a Dustbuster when it was on. Another plus to the Norelco is that it does a much better job of shaving underneath my jaw line and on my neck. I have not had any problem with the cord coming out of the razor while shaving. It fits in there nice and snug. I also have had no problem with the razor grabbing my skin. Just make sure you don't press down too hard on your skin while shaving, and use your free hand to pull your skin tight while shaving your neck, as suggested in the accompanying booklet.

If you don't need a fancy, expensive razor that cleans itself or is rechargeable, give this one a try.

title: Close, comfortable, and convenient
text:
Other reviewers have covered just about everything that I would have to say, so let me just add a "me, too" to what I consider to be the most important points.

1) Very, very comfortable shave, the most comfortable I've ever had. (I will qualify that by saying that this is the first electric shaver I've used in the shower, so as far as that type of shaving goes, my experience is limited.) It's not as close as a blade -- almost, but not quite.

2) It's very easy to clean, charges fast, and holds a charge for a pretty good length of time (probably about 45 minutes or so of shaving time).

3) The gel and lotion packs are a neat idea and are very convenient, but they are exceptionally pricey. They're about $1.25 each, and they last only about a week. I do use them when I travel for the convenience, but at home, I use regular shaving gel, and I encourage you to try the same. It saves a lot of money.

4) As with any new shaving technique, you will need to experiment a bit to find out what works at what doesn't as far as direction of motion, amount of pressure, and the like. They do say in the manual that you should give it three weeks, so if you don't like it at first, give it some time and try different shaving methods.

5) I've never actually dropped mine, so I can't confirm or deny whether it breaks as easily as others have said it does, but the shaver does look a little delicate, so being careful is probably prudent.

6) I don't use the trimmer, either, but I can see how having to change the attachment would be annoying, as others have reported.

All in all, I'm very pleased with the shaver. It makes shaving easy, convenient, and even fun -- so much so that, for the first time since I started shaving over twenty years ago, I'm actually shaving every day. For me, that says more about the shaver than anything else could.

title: Norelco Quality Going Downhill
text:
The Good

9170XLCC gives an excellent shave in about 5 minutes. It'll take about 2 weeks of daily use for your beard to adjust to the razor heads, but after that it's as close and clean as any blade shave.

The Bad:

1. It's cheaply made. Norelco has outsourced manufacturing & it shows. The frame holding the razor heads is plastic; every other Norelco I've owned (over 30 years) has been metal. The frame is supported by these weird plastic-bubble "shock absorbers" that will probably go in a year or two. The shaver has a junky, cheap feel to it. I have always gotten 5-6 years of use out of my past Norelcos; this one feels like it'll last about two years.

2. Cleaning tank is a marketing gimmick to sell $[...]/bottle cleaning solution. Way overkill. It does work OK, but the shaver gets just as clean if you rinse it under hot tap water (which you will have to do anyway because the cleaning solution leaves the razor heads coated with a slimy residue). You can pretty much throw it out after the free bottle of solution is used up.

3. I'm already on my second unit. The chip that controls the battery level indicator, recharging, etc. is flakey. The first one I had never could accurately display battery level even after 3 complete charge-discharge-recharge cycles. It'd show 15-20 minutes remaining, then just die in the middle of the shave; battery tapped out. Also, it would sometimes illuminate for no reason at all; had to turn on-off to clear it. If it happened during the night, the battery would be fully discharged by morning. So I returned it to Amazon.com (thx Amazon for great customer service!!!).

The second one that they sent to me recharges continuously when you use it with the cleaning tank -- it's not supposed to charge during the 55-minute cleaning cycle, but mine does. That means that you have to catch it about 5 minutes into the cycle, after it's done it's dunking in the tank, or it'll recharge completely after every shave (which the instructions tell you not to do because it shortens battery life). More reason to toss the cleaning unit. Ridiculous on a shaver this expensive that they'd ship junk to their customers before fixing these problems.

4. The travel case is worthless for protecting the shaver on the road. It's nothing but a zippered nylon sack. You'll have to put the shaver into something else if you pack it in checked luggage or it'll be a pile of parts when you unpack.

5. They don't include a stand so when you're done shaving you lay it on the bathroom countertop. I'm using the one from my old Norelco, but if you don't have one, storage between shaves is just setting it down somewhere.

Sad to see a fine old company like Norelco cheapening it's flagship product like this. I've been a customer for 30+ years, but next time I'm in the market for a shaver I will definitely comparison-shop the competition.

Two stars because it does give a good shave; the rest is a mess.

title: OK, but outperformed by a $10 foil electric
text:
I got this shaver in early January of 2007. For the first month or so that I had it, it worked decently. The shave was relatively close and it did get most of the hair, but it did take a few passes over the skin, and a touch-up using the on-board trimmer to get the ones it missed. I also found myself having the stretch the skin quite a bit to get a close enough shave. However, it did offer an irritation-free shave (I have sensitive skin, thus why I stay away from blade razors).

Over the next few months, though, I noticed that the shave started to get more irritating: more 'pulling' instead of cutting (had always pulled a little, but got more frequent), takes more passes to cut what it once would, etc. I changed the blades after 3 months (short period, yes, but I tried anyway). It helped a little, but it still wasn't as good as it once was. Then, I started to realize that the shaver wasn't holding as strong a charge as it once did. It would come off the charger and be 'full power' for less than one shave, and would need to go back on the charger after 6 shaves (far less than the advertised two weeks). A call to Norelco led nowhere, as they said it was 'expected' for the battery to wear down over time (4 months?).

I kept using the razor as I wasn't about to waste the $90 investment. On a trip in late July, I had forgotten to pack the shaver, so I purchased a $10 Remington battery-operated foil razor at a local convenience store. Sad to say, but from Day 1 that foil razor has outperformed the Norelco by leaps and bounds in all areas (closer shave, gets all areas better, less passes needed, etc.). Also on a sad note, the Remington is kicking the bucket (a year later), and I am forced to go back to the Norelco for the time being while I look for an acceptable foil shaver as a replacement.

In short, this razor performed decently at first, but it seems as though compared to a $10 battery operated razor, this $70 shaver isn't a good value for the investment.

title: Cavin Schon Fuller's Earth & Bentonite Combo Clay (3 Pack)
text:
Cavin Schon Fuller's Earth & Bentonite Combo Clay is chemical free, preservative free, metallic free, pesticide free, peroxide free, ammonia free, and cruelty free. It is used to leave skin and hair softer, as a deep pore cleaner that draws out toxins, and as a treatment for acne and scars. One package (this comes in a set of 3) weighs approximately 100 grams. The product is made in India. Each bag of clay comes in a resealable pouch to keep it fresh (and from making a mess). The directions say to not use a metal bowl when you are using this product (probably due to absorption issues). I used a styrofoam bowl and plastic spoon which I discarded after use. First of all, I believe the directions say to use 1-2 teaspoons of clay to equal parts water. I recommend using MUCH LESS. I followed these directions and had leftover clay that lasted for two weeks! (I kept adding water to the remainder to soften the clay each time I used it). The clay is fairly easy to mix as it is not sandy or gritty - but becomes more of a "putty" type mixture. I used the clay on my face only, as I did not want to deal with the mess of having it in my hair. On each application, I left the clay on for about 15-20 minutes (recommended amount of time). After about 10 minutes, you can feel the clay tighten on your skin. This doesn't hurt, but just feels strange, and at least for me - was a tiny bit itchy. The clay comes off fairly easy with a warm washcloth. There is one thing to note about this clay and it is even mentioned on the product instructions - this clay can (and did) make your face appear red after removal. I encountered this issue each time I used the product - even decreasing the time to about 12 minutes or so. The redness looks like a very light sunburn and doesn't hurt. It takes anywhere from 30 minutes to 1 hour to go away (at least in my case). Since it didn't hurt and was only appearance - I didn't worry too much about it, and just followed up with moisturizer afterwards. After the applications, I noticed that my skin felt much smoother, but the feeling only lasted that night (and sometimes only for a few hours). If you are not used to clay masks - this will make a mess! When applying the clay, I had some that fell off of my fingers and plopped into the sink. When trying to clean it up, it only smeared - making matters worse. The product does as it is intended, but I do not think that clay masks are for me. I did not like the tightening feeling when it was drying, after the first application- the redness was a little weird, even after reading the warning/precaution, and I prefer easier/simpler techniques such as creams, ointments, or serums. I have seen some reviews that state that the clay does not smell. I have to differ on this, as it does smell like - well CLAY! It has an earthy, dirt smell to it. Nothing bad or extreme, but it is noticeable. After using the product for 2 weeks straight - I did not notice much of a difference in my pores. The amount of product that you receive (3 bags) should last for quite a while! I had the leftover in the bowl that I mixed, and I still had 3/4 of a bag left from the one pack. I gave the rest of this bag to my mom and sent the other two sealed bags/packs to a friend.
I received this product in exchange for my honest and unbiased review.

title: Beautiful Summer Polish
text:
While this has been discontinued and hard to find, if found at all, I did purchase it when it was available. I am a China Glaze fan and have purchased many of their polishes here on Amazon and other places, and have been given bottles of China Glaze polishes. My hobby is nail art, and I have many bottles of polishes from many brands, but for the most part China Glaze is one of my favorites. I love it because it allows me to grow out my nails because it contains a nail hardener in it which I appreciate. I used to have acrylic overlays and when I removed the overlays, what was left were weak, damaged nails that would bend and break into the nail bed--very painful! However, while using China Glaze polishes, it strengthened my nails enough to grow out and now they look amazing! For this, I will always love this brand.

I love spring and summer colored polish. In fact, most of my vast collection are mainly spring and summer colors. The color of this is what drew me first. I use it in the Summer with my teals and aquas. It is a textured polish and contains a glitter-ry finish-highly reflective as is, and even more so when top coated. Without top coat it leaves a rough finish as all textured polishes do. With top coat because it is porous it absorbs the top coat and more than one coat is needed. I have worn it both with and without top coat and in the sun this is really beautiful. My only complaint but not just aimed at this polish, but all textured polish is removal. It is most difficult with regular polish remover like glitter so I use acetone to remove.

I would recommend this if you can still find it. I wanted to buy the whole set because of the colors, but was only able to get two and no luck finding the rest at present time. It sold out and was discontinued some time ago. However, if you can find it and like textured polish, again, I would recommend it.

I also used to have problems with ingrown hairs (while using my Remington epilator) & it has gotten so much better since I started using the new one. I also like that it's cordless & the charging time is reasonable (it usually charges within an hour) & I can get both of my legs done without having to charge it again.

I would purchase it again & recommend it to a friend.

title: Long fine hair has shape and style!
text:
I have abundant long, fine hair which is stick straight unless it’s on vacation in say, Sanibel Island FL, Cancun, or on summer days in Washington DC. I work from home most of the time, so my hair is generally air dried and worn down, but I wanted a tool that would help me style my hair - some way, any way! - while on business trips without devoting precious carry on space to both a blow dryer and a round brush.
This device has given me exactly what I wished for! I pack it in my bag, air dry my hair as usual, brush it out carefully with a hair bristle brush, and then start hot brushing. I don’t do anything fancy, just turn my head upside down to get some volume at the crown, then run the brush through my hair to get it orderly. I might wrap a few ends around the barrel to get some shape, and style it away from my face, but this device is far less technically demanding than a round brush/dryer set up or a traditional curling iron. I like that I can use this spontaneously, so if I get sucked into some other task while my hair dries, I haven’t missed the chance to style it. My fine hair is prone to tangling so I am an admitted frequent user of silicone, so it was important to me that I not style my hair every day - just when I need to look nice.
Two caveats: I tried to add volume at the roots by wrapping my hair around the barrel all the way to the bottom, or wrapping just the bottom, but both approaches led to terrifying tangle-ups. As someone who has had to have her boyfriend physically cut the bristles off a round brush to free her, perhaps I’m just lacking technique. But if you get your hair wrapped around this barrel going two directions, you’d better turn this baby off quick or your roots will get scorched.
Secondly, having learned how to use a straightener to create attractive curls, I’d hoped that the straightener feature of this device combined with the bristles would allow me to follow the same procedure with smoother results. Not so. This didn’t work for me at all. If you used this device in straightener mode to achieve curls, I may need lessons from you. It might just be a matter of how willing my hair is to hold curl (not very).
Anyway, while this device didn’t let me create straightener curls, it’s otherwise been great!

title: Really like it - no more stubble, razor burn, or nicks
text:
Bottom line: This thing is great. It is a bit uncomfortable to use the first time, but it gets easier. If you can get a tattoo, you can easily use this thing.
What I'm glad it has: The exfoliation brush is really useful. It keeps me from getting ingrown hairs and makes my legs even smoother.
What I wish it had: It would be nice if there was a suction cup holder for the shower. If I use it in the shower, I have to turn off the water in order to put it on the floor outside the shower without flooding my bathroom.

I spent about two weeks researching epilators and reading hundreds of reviews and finally decided on the Braun Silk-epil 9. It has a big head, different attachments that are useful, and can be used wet or dry. I noticed that a lot of reviewers got it free, so I went to the BzzAgent site they reference, took some surveys, and thanks to my good karma, they sent me one to try out! Score! As soon as I got it, I scanned the instructions and held my breath as I held it up to my shin. I was worried it was going to be really painful, but it was just like a rubber band snap. It was a little uncomfortable, but not bad. As I got closer to my ankles, it hurt a little bit, but nothing too bad.

So, after successful use on my legs, I got cocky and decided to do my upper lip. I put on the other cap and brought it up to my upper lip. Oh mother of pearl! I couldn't do it. I've never waxed my lip and wasn't prepared for it. Not sure if you remember the first time you plucked your eyebrows, but it was a similar sensation. My eyes watered and I couldn't go through with it. I went online and did some research and saw that some people used lidocaine cream to numb the area. I tried that on my upper lip and bikini line and didn't feel a thing. I've been using the exfoliating brush and haven't had any ingrown hairs. I've use the epilator a few more times since and it's really not been bad at all.

One word of caution: If you have bug bites on your legs, be careful. I didn't realize that this little hair puller could also cut skin if it's swollen from a bug bite. That's why I gave it four stars instead of five.

Overall, I'm really happy with this epilator. I was completely prepared to buy it and, had I bought it instead of being awarded it, would have kept it. I have no desire to go back to shaving, razor burn, and nicks on my legs!

title: Atomic Pink is fantastic
text:
After reading many reviews on Atomic Pink, I went with this color for the first time ever dying my hair pink. I found some tips online that I followed before I dyed it and I'll relay some of them here.

One thing that is pretty common knowledge is that the more damaged or processed your hair is, the EASIER the color will take to your hair.

So knowing that, I bleached my hair (Using Manic Panic's amplified bleach kit) to get my hair as light as color (It made my hair near-white but it would probably still give a decent color even at the light orange stage) and after rinsing the bleach out, I avoided conditioning my hair as I usually do after a bleach job.

Tips I was given:
1- Make your hair damp. it helps the dye to cover evenly and considering the last time I tried dying my hair a funky color it ended up splotchy despite being in a similar bleached state, I think it definitely helped.

2- Mix the dye with conditioner in a small tub (I personally rinsed the little tupperware that came with the bleach kit since it has a lid and I could cover any I didn't use). Conditioner was said to make the color last longer and it also helps to repair your hair since you've likely just bleached the hell out of it.

3- If mixing with conditioner (It didn't dillute the color at all for me but if you use a signifigant amount it just might), start with just a couple of teaspoons of dye at a time to make sure you don't waste any. I ended up making two "batches" and still had some leftover, and barely used any of the bottle, but my hair is very short.

4- Cover your hair with a plastic bag (or shower cap) when waiting for the dye to take. It'll keep your hair from drying out and also keeps the mess off your neck and clothes

5- A tip I was given but didn't try was to blast your hair with hot air with a hair dryer right before you wash it out. Highly suggested if you use a red or blue.

When washing out your hair the first time, don't use shampoo. Even the second time you wash your hair, don't use shampoo. Only use shampoo when your hair looks dirty. Invest in some dry shampoo to use between washings. Less washing means a longer lasting color! That said, I dyed my hair on Valentine's Day and I've washed it three times since then and the color is still as vibrant as when I first dyed it.

REMEMBER just because color is washing out of your hair doesn't mean your hair still has dye in it. Your hair is likely to bleed for awhile. Don't use your best towels or pillow cases or wear light colored shirts for awhile.

If your color does start to fade, just mix up some more dye and conditioner to refresh it. You can also mix a tiny bit of dye into your conditioner and shake it up and use that regularly.

title: Extremely Impressed
text: i have something between 2c/3a hair, with my curls always being dry and frizzy and my scalp oily and quick to form build up. i used whatever moisturizing shampoo for curly hair that was decently priced for years. i decided to stop with the matching shampoo and conditioner thing because well, my scalp doesn’t need moisturizing like that. with regular liquid shampoo, id have to wash my hair every other day at least, and going 2 days would leave my hair a greasy mess, any longer was even worse. I made the switch to this bar shampoo a month ago. I use the purifying bar, it is kinda small but pretty thick. I wanted to test the product for a decent amount of time and see if there were any noticeable changes, and there have been! I was a little confused the first attempt, I couldn’t get the bar to lather properly but by the second wash I had it down. The bar has a very light scent on my hair, the bar itself doesnt smell amazing but I dont care about that.  I noticed immediately that when my hair was dried it was incredibly soft, softer than with anything I've used before. I have also noticed that my build up is MUCH slower to come back, i went from having to wash my hair every other day to twice a week max! Very happy about that. There is no waxy feeling left on my hands or hair either. Overall very happy with this purchase, and i’ll be coming back for more when I run out (: I encourage  anyone thinking of making the switch.

title: my new favorite
text:
I have very blonde lashes, so mascara is something I wear daily, and because my natural lash color is so light, it's really easy for me to tell when my mascara has worn off. This mascara has good staying power, and it gives me the feathery, long, full lash look that I love. I worked as a Clinique Business Manager for many years, and in addition to all the free make-up Clinique gave us, I was also able to try many different high-end mascaras I normally wouldn't have purchased, such as Lancome, Chanel, & Dior. My favorite back then was Clinique's Long Pretty Lashes which has since been discontinued, and ever since then, I've been on the hunt for my perfect mascara...one that stays on without flaking or clumping, no raccoon eyes, one that has buildable coverage and can also be reapplied without getting gunky. I do not like mascaras that give you twiggy lashes, and because I like my lashes defined and separated, feathery soft and full, I prefer a natural bristle brush over silicone brushes.

So as you can tell, I'm very particular about mascara! My favorite before trying this one was Neutrogena's Healthy Volume mascara and Guerlain's Cils D'enfer was a close second, although too pricey IMO. I love this Mamey mascara even more! I had read an interview of Salma Hayek's about Mamey Seed oil which is what led me to this mascara. Although my natural lashes are fairly long, they are also thin and getting sparse with age, so if this stuff helps to regrow them, that will be wonderful! In the meantime though, just using this makes my lashes look amazing! It does feel like my lashes absorb some of the product -- they don't look quite as thick 8 hours or so later, so if I'm going out in the evening, I will reapply, and I love that this goes on so smoothly and clump-free, even hours after the initial application. My lashes also hold a curl much better, and I've never found a mascara that does that for me. I've been using this for a little over a week now and have worn it every day except yesterday when I tried my Neutrogena again just to compare (and it wasn't nearly as good). I don't write a lot of reviews but this Mamey mascara has seriously impressed me - I'll buy it as long as they make it!

title: So much better than 5 magnet eyelashes
text:
After trying several of the 5 magnet type, I found these and I'm so glad I did! The 5 magnet type never worked after I tried to cut them to the right size because there was never a magnet on the end, which made it impossible to get them to stay on without using glue. I found these with 10 smaller magnets and thought I would give them a try! I was able to cut them to the right size and still have magnets on both ends, so they would stay on. I am not very good at applying liquid liner, but I was able to get this liner to work just fine. I used these for my wedding and they stayed on all day/evening and weren't too heavy feeling like some lashes. They really made my eyes pop and stand out beautifully in pictures! In the photos, the close ups were before the wedding to try them out, and although the one end wouldn't stay on that time, I was able to get it to stay on the wedding day.

The only thing I didn't like (which is the same with all of these magnetic liners) is that the liner is difficult to remove. The lashes themselves came off fine, but the liner was not easy to remove (from my skin or the lashes). I don't like to use makeup removers, so I used coconut oil. It took some time to get it off. But I don't think that's anything specific to this liner, it's the magnetic liners in general.

I recommend these lashes over all of those 5 magnet ones!

text: Okay, this one is new to me. I’ve seen so many videos about these and with the corona virus shutdowns, I haven’t been in for a pedicure in much longer than I care to admit. I needed to try something. Arrived in a timely manner; 2 days sooner than initially quoted. Instructions are easy enough. I washed and dried my feet, then put these bad boys on. Recommended time is for 50-90 minutes; longer for feet more in need (my heels are so cracked and flakey I wasn’t about to have photographic evidence). I was aiming for 90 minutes. I massaged them around in my feet to ensure that the product was all over. At about 80 minutes I started noticing a tingling and so rinsed the product, as described, to avoid any sensitivity or rashes. And that was that. Day 1: no noticeable difference. Day 2: The skin on my feet is noticeably tight. The left foot has very slight flaking around the toes and the right foot has a spot starting to obviously peel. Took a shower, no extra attention to the feet other than regular wash and now there is obvious peeling on both feet. Day 3: noticeable itchiness and more peeling to be had on the soles of my feet. Day 4: Ok, this peeling is gross! Holy smokes, everything is peeling it even feels like the tops of my feet may start peeling. Day 5: OMG all the peeling. Day 6: Peeling has calmed down on the bottom of the foot and around the toes but the tops of the feet haven’t started at all but it looks and feels like it is going to. Day 7: I cheated. I soaked my feet and gave them a very light pumice scrub to get the skin from the tops of my feet off and to touch up a dry patch on one heel. Final verdict: totally worth it. Recommendations: After reading through use and reviews of other similar products, I would recommend soaking your feet every day. It may help avoid the issue I had with the skin on the tops of my feet.

title: Gives light coverage that evens out skin, can be built up. Hydrating and smooth
text:
These come with 3 product boxes wrapped with plastic around them holding them together. All 3 of the outer product boxes look exactly the same, so initially I thought they had sent me the wrong thing - 3 foundations - instead of 2 foundations with sponges. But, once I took off the plastic wrapping and felt the 3 boxes, I could tell that 1 had sponges in it. Kind of weird they put them inside one of their foundation boxes. Not sure how comfortable I am with them not being wrapped on their own, but rather handled someone and placed into a foundation box? But, I guess either a machine or person normally handles makeup sponges in order to get them in their packaging, so this isn’t that weird 🤷‍♀️ Then, I took the sponges out and they looked like they had lint/paper or something all over them. I always wash my sponges before use anyways, and these felt soft and bouncy, so I figured I’d give them a try once I washed them. They worked really well so I’m glad I didn’t toss them right away. They are really soft and bouncy and increase in size once wet. Even though I really like them, I took a star off for them coming in a foundation box and having paper/lint all over them.

This comes in a thick frosted glass bottle with a dropper to dispense. It’s a nice clean way of dispensing product and to be able to control the amount of product you get out, which I like.

It claims to be made from natural ingredients. The ingredients are listed here on the product page and on the box. I put them at the end of this review. There were some ingredients that were listed oddly. When I first saw them listed I didn’t recognize them, so I looked them up. I’m not sure if they had to be translated and they got messed up that way or what, but they just weren’t written completely correct. Like I said, I put the ingredients at the end of my review. First, I put them exactly how they’re listed on the product page and the box. Then, below that, I wrote out what ingredients I felt were written the wrong way and wrote out what they should have been written as. If you want to look them up, it definitely makes it easier looking them up written the right way, at least for me it did. The ingredients can come from natural things. It does include parabens (methylparaben and propylparaben). I know a lot of people now are against parabens and now a lot of companies are producing “paraben free” products, but parabens are used preservatives. If they aren’t using parabens, which have been used regularly in products for many years, for the preservatives, they’re going to be using something else. Methylparaben occurs naturally in a handful of fruits (like blueberries), but it can also be created synthetically. Propylparaben is also a natural substance found in many plants and some insects.

I had gotten another foundation from Amazon that came in a glass bottle with a dropper to dispense similar to this one. I got that one in the lightest shade and it ended up being way too warm for me. I got this one in #2 because looking at the swatches it seemed lighter than #1. #1 seemed darker and warmer than #2 and #3. #2 and #3 seemed to be the lightest shades, with #2 looking more pink and #3 more yellow. I decided to go with #2. I always hate when companies make their #1 shade darker than the ones that come after it! I never understand that! But, I’m glad they had swatches to look at!

#2 is light enough for me, and like it seemed in the product photo of swatches, it has a pink tone to it. I did a swatch comparing this foundation in #2 to Maybelline Fit Me Matte+Poreless in 110 Porecelain. As you can tell, Maybelline one is more warm toned and this foundation is more cool toned.

It gives a nice natural, slightly dewy finish. It gives okay coverage. One thin layer just evens out my skin tone, but you can build it up some and/or use a brush instead of a sponge and get more application. With a foundation like this, that is a thinner consistency, if you want the most amount of coverage you can get from it, I recommend using a short haired, dense foundation brush. If you want to blend it seamlessly into the skin where it just evens out skin tone, you can use a sponge or use a fluffier brush to blend it onto the skin (I like using a fluffy dual fiber brush or my luxie 522 brush - it’s called a tapered highlighting brush, but I love the look it gives when I use it to blend in a thin consistency foundation! It just looks so seamless!). I usually don’t powder my face completely, only where I absolutely need to. But, with this foundation, I definitely recommend powdering! If I do a thin layer and powder, I don’t get much transfer at all.

Overall, I think it’s an okay foundation. If you like a natural but dewy finish, like a foundation that you can even out your skin tone with or build it up for a little more coverage, and don’t mind that you have to powder it to keep the transfer down, this would work for you. Personally for me, I like how hydrating this feels. It doesn’t cling to dry patches at all. Where a lot of foundations, even dewy ones, will sometimes look dry or cakey (like between my eyebrows, no matter how hard I try I can’t get foundation to look smooth and good there 😠), this one doesn’t do that! It looks nice and smooth there! I like using it on days where I just need to even out my skin.

INGREDIENTS
AS LISTED ON BOX AND ON AMAZON PRODUCT PAGE
Water, glycerin, propylene glycol, poly two methyl siloxane ring five, titanium dioxide, palmitic acid ethyl ester, liquid paraffin, PEG-30 two poly hydroxy stearic acid ester, poly two methyl siloxane cross-linked polymer, petrolatum, C12-15 alcohol benzoate, magnesium sulfate, avocado fruit fat, beeswax, rose flower extract, lanolin, magnesium stearate, polysorbate -80, methylparaben and propylparaben, phenoxyethanol ethylhexylglycerin, rose oil, iron oxides.

MY CHANGE OF HOW SOME INGREDIENTS ARE LISTED
“Poly two methyl siloxane ring five” - Cyclopentasiloxane D5 (Cyclo = ring, penta = 5, dimethyl = 2 methyls)
“PEG-30 Two Poly Hydroxy Stearic Acid Ester” - PEG-30 Dipolyhydroxystearate (di = 2, stearate = salt or ester of stearic acid)
“Poly Two Methyl Siloxane Cross-Linked Polymer” - Polydimethylsiloxane
“C12-15 Alcohol Benzoate” - I think it means C12-15 Alkyl benzoate

My skin looked nice, but I always see the real effects the next day...and I did. I'm nice and even, "glowy" (for lack of a better adjective), and my cheeks are smooth! The scent is a little too sweet for me (smells more like cocoa or vanilla than honey, but maybe that's it) but it doesn't last long and it's tolerable once it's on my face. I'm glad I gave this a shot, I really like it. There are no directions on how often to use it, so my esthetician training tells me probably 2 - 3 times a week, depending on skin type. I used it once it wasn’t snagging all my hair and breaking it off, and it did work. Heat was coming out of the “tips of the fingers” and my roots were dried, and the rest of my hair could air dry in all its undisturbed curl pattern glory. But it was still kind of snaggy and I was just so over sanding this thing as it took way longer than it should have, which honestly, it should have not had to be done at all! If I had to do it all over again, it’d just buy the bright green name brand one that was double (maybe more?) the cost of this, and not waste time screwing around with sanding this thing.

title: GREAT SHAMPOO
text:
When I first saw this product on Amazon, I was wary of all of it's good reviews. I have long hair that is prone to dryness and breakage, and have tried just about every shampoo and conditioner on the market to improve hair health. I am pleasantly surprised that this shampoo lives up to it's claims.

I want everyone to understand that this is, in fact, a shampoo; it is NOT a cleansing conditioner. In my opinion, that is a plus, as it's important to cleanse your scalp and hair follicles without adding buildup that a "cleansing conditioner" often imparts. This shampoo is sulfate-free and gives a mild lather. I feel like it cleans my scalp and hair sufficiently, without stripping. I color-treat my hair, and this shampoo has never stripped or lightened my color.

As far as moisture is concerned, this adds hydration without weighing my hair down. Yet, it is NOT drying to my hair as so many shampoos are. I have long, fine hair, so that's a significant point. If you read the ingredient list, you will see that this product contains many natural oils and humectants. Given that, I am continually surprised that it doesn't weight my hair down.

After use, my wet hair feels smooth and sleek, but I still need to follow with a conditioner for detangling. Again, this is a shampoo; it is not a cleansing conditioner. Since there is no matching Pure Body Naturals daily conditioner for this shampoo, I have been experimenting with some other argan oil conditioners sold here on Amazon.

No matter your hair type, I think this shampoo can add to your hair health. I highly recommend trying it.

title: Review of 51S foil and cutter for Braun shaver
text: Just my .2 cents. I have a Braun model #8985 Series 5. After a year of satisfactory use, I thought I should replace the foil and cutters. I got the one recommended for my shaver, the 51S. I started to use it, and after just a few shaves, I noticed the shaves were not as smooth, and more irritation to my face, than I was getting with my original shaver I had for the past year. Now just after a few shaves, I noticed my cutter was starting to dull. I stuck with it a few more months, and then I started looking for a better cutting block for it. I came on Amazon and read some reviews, and there were many satisfied users of the 30B kit. . I even called Braun, and told them my situation, and asked if I could change over to the 30B, instead of staying with the 51S. NO WAY said the rep, use only the cartridge recommended by Braun, the 51S. Well, I decided otherwise, and went to "Target", and got the 30B replacement foil and cutter. Boy, what a difference. It fits right in, no problem with the foil or the cutter fitting, I even like the foil better than the 51S, seems to roll over my fact smoother. The shaves seem so much better. Now to be honest, I have not used the razor much yet, but I'll get back to you with my thoughts when I do. On my #8985 there is a light that comes on, and it says "change foil", which came on right then when I changed the foil over to the 30B, it lite up. There is a reset button right there, and if you push it with a pen or pencil point, the light goes out after blinking a few times. Maybe the 30B is the way to go, and the 30B is about $15 cheaper than the 51S. I don't know what Braun is doing, but it is not making me buy a new Braun. If I get upset with their shaver, I'm not going to buy a new Braun, I will switch brands. Hate to say this folks, but every manufacturer out there is trying to rip us off today! Regards, TC

title: Much better than expected!
text:
I bought this at a discount store, not on Amazon, but decided to review it since it doesn't have a lot of reviews. It cost me about $9, which is why I bought it. I was just starting a k-beauty routine and picked this out totally randomly, simply because I knew I needed a night cream and I liked the ingredients.

I liked a lot of things about it--how it feels thick and creamy, yet cooling, and it soaks right into my skin and doesn't leave it feeling oily like many other products do. I have dehydrated skin (live in the desert, at high altitude), but it also still gets oily at times. I like how this soaks into my skin and does not make it feel oily, even though I put it on as my final night step after several other treatments and essences.

But because I'm new to the whole system and trying several different products at once, I didn't realize quite how good this was. I thought, yeah, feels nice, not greasy, but otherwise unimpressive. But then I had surgery and wasn't following all the k-beauty steps as much as I had been, and particularly been not using this and I realized....wow, this stuff is actually pretty good. It was THIS cream that has been giving my skin such a silky feel! And I certainly noticed it when I wasn't using it--my skin didn't feel nearly as good, and I'd only been using it for a few weeks. So, guess I'm sol--it's really nice, at least as part of a multi-treatment skin care routine. I'm going to buy it again when I finish this pot. I do go through it fairly quickly, but I'm also putting it on my neck and hands, and it's not that expensive and really is a nice cream.

title: Works well
text:
My usual sun protection is avoidance. I have sensitive, allergic, rosacea skin. I'm allergic to most chemical sunscreens, so decided that I would make my own this Spring. Actually went to a presentation by one of the big mlm essential oil companies, because they were going to present recipe for using EOs in a natural sunscreen (later research told me that EOs don't have sun prevention qualities.) The bad news is that the presentation was appalling (safety and lack of ingredient knowledge), the good news was it made me do research and take two online courses from a reputable online aromatherapy institute. One of which was a Butters & Balms course. Make a lot of my own skin products now. I had previously ought all of the ingredients to make my own sunscreen, but then decided to buy some to see how it worked for me. It did. Got one on Etsy. It was fine. There were some times during the summer that my skin was so awful that nothing wouldn't have upset it. It's a firmer consistency, I used it MANY times and barely made a dent in the jar. Bought a natural sunscreen lotion on Amazon, it had an SPF of 32. Because it contained so much of the zinc oxide, it made my face chalk white. The Tropical Sands Sunscreen only has an SPF of 8, so no white face.

The Tropical Sands All Natural Sunscreen is a lotion consistency. I'm not ready to make my own products with a water base because they need a preservative system. Lotion is easier to apply and make sure you cover the body parts completely. Probably a better consistency for sunscreen. The bottle is 8oz. It recommends application every 40 minutes if swimming or sweating. Even with the frequent application, it should still last a while. It's also the most reasonable price of all the ones I've tried.

Many sunscreens that contain non nano zinc oxide or titanium dioxide call themselves "nearly natural." Did some research because I thought they were chemicals, they are minerals. They provide a physical block rather then a chemical block. The biggest problem with the products that contain mineral blocks is that they make your face white--the more minerals, the whiter your face gets. Before the rosacea, I was light skinned, but not that porcelain white. It's December and while the weather is warmer then normal, it's not suntan weather, so my face doesn't have any other color. The Tropical Sands was fine, didn't change my skin color.

As with any new product on my face, I did a sample application. Put a little on the side where my hair would cover a reaction. It didn't make my skin reactive negatively, so I tried it on my nose and cheeks (most reactive part of my face.) I didn't have a negative reaction there. I'll definitely have to experiment with it during the prime sun time because there are times I have to be out in the sun.

I received this product at a discount for an honest review.

The solvent base contains Ethyl Acetate & Isopropyl Mistrate. I wouldn't use this as my first defense against removing glitter lacquers, and I wouldn't use it to soak off gel polish at all. Plant Therapy products are proudly made in the USA! 🇺🇸

text: I bought this product after seeing a beauty blogger's review about it. Since I have hyper pigmentation from not using sun screen in my youth, I've been trying to find ways to stop or reverse it. I also bought and tried out other products in conjunction with this one as part of a skin care routine, but I noticed that my skin would break out in very small pimples sometimes. After testing and leaving out products to figure out what was making my skin like this, I discovered that when I stopped using this product, I no longer got those small pimples. My skin is somewhat sensitive, so maybe that's one of the reasons, or some ingredient I'm slightly allergic to? I'm not sure. But I wasn't completely surprised as I did notice my face felt just a tad tingly and extra sensitive after using it (even with just one drop, no more than two, each night). During the time I did use it, which was for a few weeks, I have about half the bottle left, I didn't notice my spots lightening or even staying the same. Actually, they got very slightly darker; even though, I used sun screen. I don't necessarily attribute that occurrence to this product though, but certainly I was disappointed that this did nothing for me even after being patient and using it consistently for a while to see its effects. title: Patience required, and rewarded, by good results.
text:
Does exactly what it is supposed to do. A couple tips and tricks I've picked up along the way:
1) There is a continuity buzzer that will let you know that you have completed a good circuit (remember the saltwater on your fingers!)
--> The buzzer length is about 8 seconds and then repeats. You can use this to keep the probe in for the recommended 15 seconds (two long beeps)
2) The tweezers are just ok. A person with 120 grit sandpaper and a bit of patience can get the surfaces mating perfectly and give the tweezers a positive grip
3) There are two included probes, and the super-thin probe wires are reasonably stiff, but also brittle. I've broken one already trying to straighten the wire after I bent it.
4) The process is NOT instantaneous... after treatment the hair will still feel firmly attached. Give it an hour or two for the chemical reaction you created to break down the follicle.
5) The process will almost certainly only kill "many" of the hair producing cells in the follicle, but not "all". You will see regrowth, albeit much finer hairs, which should fade with additional treatments.

Note: this is not one of those I-got-this-for-free-and-am-writing-a-glowing-review reviews. I am really sick of those, by the way.

I self-tan after nearly every shower. I live in California and have to look the part, you know? But after two years with Fake Bake, I decided it was time to try to find something a little more low maintenance (Fake Bake is great, but the mitt is 100% necessary and the extra accessory to deal with is frustrating).

I went on Amazon, quickly scanned reviews, and ordered this. Then, while waiting for its arrival, I read the reviews and was frustrated to find that nearly all were written by sponsored users, and are therefore untrustworthy (I don't care if you say the review is "honest", I just cannot give the benefit of the doubt to a trend more associated with scams than hot tips). Nevertheless, I decided to give it a shot.

This WAY exceeded my low expectations. It blends really easily (almost no streaks!), smells relatively good, isn't sticky at all, DOESN'T RUB OFF MUCH ON SHEETS / CLOTHING (a little is to be expected from all skin dyes, but some are noticeably awful *cough*fakebake*cough*), and gives a pretty realistic tan, assuming you're not ghost white to start. Totally worth the adventure away from Fake Bake in my book.

HOWEVER, if you use your hands to apply this, you better have a stack of sandpaper nearby because this will instantly dye your palms brown. I haven't tried using plastic gloves, but I am a little disappointed that a mitt is once more necessary. At least in dire circumstances my hands are a possibility, unlike Fake Bake.

Will probably buy again

title: WOW! Get it now! You won’t be disappointed!
text:
I’ve forever been a fan of the Real Techniques sponges. They’re soft, they work great, they clean well, they last pretty well, and they didn’t soak up too much of my foundation. So, they were a win for me. I’ve tried many other sponges, but never found ones I loved as much or more than my Real Techniques sponges…UNTIL NOW!

Initially what caught my eye with this sponge was the shape. I loved it had a thin, pointed tip I could use for concealer and areas like around my nose. I loved the 2 angled sides so I can apply cream blush or bronzer or for when I want to apply powder. The sides would work great to apply my foundation. I was hoping the shape would work as well as it seemed like it would, and it did! I was a little worried about the size. Usually, I like to use those little mini sponges for under my eyes. I just never found a sponge, even with a pointy tip, that gets under my eyes to blend my concealer as well as the mini sponges do. So, I was hoping this would still work as a great all around sponge, and, like I said, it did!

The sponge is AMAZING! It’s so soft, but dense so it doesn’t seem to absorb hardly any product. That makes it so easy to clean! I’m the kind of person that hates when my sponges have product stains on them. After I use them, I clean them and keep working at it until all the product is out of it and it looks new again. This can be hard on my sponges and cause them to tear after a few washes. My Real Techniques sponges held up well during my washings, but still would start tearing after about a month of regular washes. I LOVE that this sponge is dense enough that it doesn’t absorb hardly any product, so it’s easy to clean and I don’t have to scrub it for a while, but it’s still so soft and bouncy!

It does get bigger when it’s wet, and it’s already a good size when dry. But, the point on it is thin enough that it gets under my eyes to blend my concealer the way I like it! I don’t have to switch to a mini sponge to do my concealer! I love that!

The sides work great to apply my foundation. It blends it so easily and it looks so smooth and beautiful!

The angled edges work great to apply cream blush/bronzer/contour. It blends them out great and doesn’t lift product underneath it!

It works great to apply powder too!

This is such a great sponge that does everything I need it to and I don’t need to switch to different sponges to do different things! This one sponge has enough different shapes that it does everything I need! I definitely recommend it!

title: Good mascara with a tweak
text:
This is a good mascara. The brush is a little curve so it can help with the application.

My first impression wasn't that good, since the mascara felt so thin that looks like I wasn't really wearing almost anything. It dried so fast that when I tried to apply the second layer, it wouldn't let me because it was already dry and the brush wouldn't run nice and soft through my lashes. However, I added 2-3 drops of castor oil (you can also use almond oil or any other natural oil that you like) and it was a game changer. I instantly felt the brush was running smoothly on my lashes, and was able to apply a second and even third layer with no problem. Lashes looked way better (not to mention they were also being lubricated with the added oil).

Pros:
- Does not smudge
- Easy to remove with makeup remover or even in the shower
- When removed, it comes out in small flakes which is great because it does not leave you with raccoon eyes

Cons:
- Very thin mascara (although this might be a pro for some people)
- Felt a little dry at the beginning but manage to "enhance" it with castor oil (as mentioned above)

Take your free hand and hold the section of hair that you are brushing tightly enough so that there is less pulling of the hair from your scalp. title: I am a new fan!!! Love, love, love this straightener.
text:
Okay, this might be a long review but I hope it helps!
Back in the mid 2000’s, when the Chi was selling like hot pancakes, I had such a hard time finding one available, that one day I ended up buying a Paul Mitchell iron. I fell in love with it and never again tried to buy a Chi. After 13 years of using my PM, it finally started having issues with the electrical cord. My sweet husband, seeing how much I was struggling to flat iron my hair, got on Amazon and bought me this Titanium hair straightener. I didn’t want to stop using my Paul Mitchell (was kinda sentimental about it), but I finally put it away and gave this one a try... BEST decision ever!!!! I hadn’t realized how long it actually would take my old straightener to do the job. I though 20-30 minutes straightening my hair was normal. This titanium iron is the real deal. I have super long (almost to my waist), medium thickness hair. Not thin, not coarse... but if I don’t flat iron it, I look like a lion on a bad hair day. Very frizzy. This iron heats up so quickly and it goes up to 450F. I have seriously straightened my whole hair in less than 15 minutes. More like 10 minutes. A little more if I want to flip it and curl the ends. I seriously love this titanium straightener. And no, I didn’t get the product for free just to review it. Like I said, my husband did his homework researching and bought me this for my birthday.

The only thing that I would suggest is that you might have to wear a heat glove if you are using it to curl your hair, since the outside of the plates does get hot, and when you use it to curl, you have to grab the hot end.

Anyway.. I hope it last 13 years or more like my old straightener!

title: Vegetal, messy flower balls; not sure why anyone would use this for anything but tea
text:
I thought these were bath bombs when I ordered them. However, that is not what this is at all. There are 10 tiny balls of compressed flowers wrapped in various colored foils. They can be used as a tea, which is what I use them for, or they can be put in a bath. I have no idea how anyone would use this for baking as per the Amazon title.

Nevertheless, all but the purple and red balls have a purely vegetal scent. The purple and red smell flowery. I have used tea balls before and never cared for them but did like how most stayed together. However, these balls expand into many little flower particles that float in the water. If one were to put this in a bath, it would clog the drain unless the flower debris was scooped out with a skimmer.  I used the blue ball to brew into a tea and it was tasteless. I also had to use a strainer and remove the lid on my pot to keep the spout from clogging.

Besides the mess and lackluster flavor, there are absolutely no brewing instructions, no information on what tea ball is what flower.  The Amazon site has a list of the flower and the balls but does not show the foil color. It is almost impossible to reconcile that list with what is in front of me.

Shame on the vendor for not creating an insert or package label that says what is inside and which tea ball is what flower. I personally do not care for this at all and will probably throw this in the garbage.

This is not worth it to me at any price. It is certainly not a bath bomb, I can't see how it can be used for baking, and as a tea it is tasteless and messy. There is no fragrance, so its use as a bath bomb would be for romantic or ambiance purposes only.

At the current price of $9.88 for 10 balls it comes to almost $1 per tea ball.

The power cord is much too short and I had to use an extension cord to give myself some wiggle room away from the wall outlet.  Some of the bits' textures do a better job than the others, while some don't do anything at all.  The over all look and feel of the set isn't worth the price, in my opinion. title: Give these a try!!
text:
I've bought 3 different styles of these and I had a hard time choosing which ones to get so I hope this review will help others. Sorry I don't have any pictures, I tried but I suck at that so I'll try to be as detailed as possible. First of all, these really do work if you make sure to put a couple coats of magnetic liner on, let it dry in between coats and before you put the lashes on. I bought the expensive liquid liner from Moxie and that seems to work better than the cheap stuff I've bought. However, I prefer these lashes over the ones from Moxie and they cost a heck of a lot less! I bought style 232 first and they are great for going out, they are long and thick but not so much that they touch my eyebrows or anything. I wanted a pair for everyday so I tried style 229. They are slightly shorter (not much) but thicker than 232 and do not flare or taper at the ends (same length lash all the way across). I really liked these also but they still seemed like a bit much for work, so then I tried style 234. These are perfect for everyday lashes! They are still decently long and full but they aren't too dramatic. They just look like you have a great set of natural lashes and a good mascara. (Keep in mind that my natural lashes are short and light.)

I had lash extensions for years and I loved them but they are costly to maintain and take a lot of time. I decided to take a break from them but they have taken a toll on my natural lashes and I had gotten used to the way I looked with them so I needed to find a replacement. I could never get the hang of using strips with the glue so when I saw the magnetic lashes I wanted to give them a try. I started with the expensive ones and loved the concept but had a hard time finding a pair of lashes that weren't too short or too long. I'm so glad I found these! I didn't give 5 stars because one of the pairs I bought had lashes that were 2 different lengths in the package (as a pair) so I cannot wear those.

title: Moisturizing eye cream, irritates my picky skin
text:
UPDATE: I have reduced my rating to three stars after more use. This cream turned out in the longer term to irritate my eyes, make them swollen, red, and painful. It's in good company though; I have found that everything designed to be an eye cream to help skin health and appearance has irritated my eyes (this is one of four products that have recently had the same effect). So while I cannot personally recommend this cream, my experience of it may be far from universal. I did like how it felt going on, and actually liked the jasmine scent.

ORIGINAL REVIEW (4 stars): The Penebella Brighten & Repair Eye Cream includes a lot of ingredients that are really good for your skin: retinol, hyaluronic acid, aloe, and Vitamin E, among others. It does also contain jasmine essential oil, which is an odd choice to me. I am sensitive to scents, and to floral scents in particular, but this jasmine does not bother me at all, which is surprising. I actually find it to be subtle and pleasant, but nonetheless would not choose to have any fragrance added to a product meant for some of your most sensitive skin around your eyes. It strikes me as unnecessary at best.

This cream does feel light and moisturizing. The very fine needle nose dispenser makes it easy to get precisely the amount of product you intend, which is important when using relatively small amounts of relatively expensive products. I haven't ever ended up with more product than I intended or could use well for application.

When I began using this product, the skin around my eyes were swollen and sensitive from the dry winter air and indoor allergies. After about a week of consistent use, my eyes still feel swollen and sensitive. Honestly, the much simpler, cheaper basic lotion I have for my eyes relieves that feeling better. However, this cream has ingredients that make it better for long term use and improvement. So I will continue to use it and appreciate it for the anti-aging effects, but won't rely on it for daily relief from irritated eyes. If using it longer affects my judgment of this, I will update my review accordingly.
