text:
[[ASIN:B01F7K1CRC Stone Crop Serum for Face - Natural Skin Lightening Reduces Pigmentation & Dark Spots on Skin, Attacks Wrinkles & Fine Lines - Vitamin C, E & B Complex - 1oz]]

I was looking for a good serum to help my face look good for my upcoming wedding. I am a little older than my fiance but I didn't want my face to show it on my special day. I take the best care of my skin to try to keep it as youthful as possible, so when I had the opportunity to try this serum, I was happy to do so. The serum comes in a screw top and eye dropper dispenser. The bottle is a dark amber colored glass bottle. There is one fluid ounce in the bottle. The serum has a sort of medicinal scent, not unpleasant and not too strong. It leave behind no real scent once it absorbs in. The serum feels refreshing and absorbs quickly and thoroughly into my skin. I feel an immediate pleasant tightening effect and the skin looks smooth and supple almost immediately. I've been using the stone crop serum for two weeks which is not really enough time to be able to tell the full effect of the serum on fine lines and wrinkles, but I do notice softening in expression lines in my forehead and in fine lines and that my skin stays better hydrated throughout the day. There is no burning, redness or irritation with the use of the serum and no product residue left behind. The manufacturer offers a 100% Money-Back Guarantee which I appreciate but have never had a problem with Eva Naturals products before. I am enjoying the serum and consider it a good value at under 19.00 delivered to my door and by the fact that a little goes a long way with only one dropper full of serum enough to do my entire face.

title: I have fallen in love with Artic Fox
text:
Wow, wow WOW! I have fallen in love with Artic Fox! I was so excited to try it, after seeing it demonstrated by a YouTuber I follow.

I tried Wrath on my own hair last week, so picked up an 8oz bottle of Violet Dream for my 20 year old daughter, who has bleached, waist-length hair. She did MP's Purple Haze two months ago and it did not hold long at all, which was disappointing.

We applied to damp, towel-dried hair and the 8oz was just enough. We put on a plastic cap and wrapped her hair in the towel. We left it on for two hours and it looks amazing!

Tips for those new to this type of haircolor...if your hair is not previously bleached, freshly bleached or very damaged, it's not going to give you the same intensity of the color you see on the box or in the pictures. So you might want to try a strand test if this is important to you. For instance, if you have dark blond hair and you put a green or green-ish blue over it, it's likely to look very muddy and grayish and not in a nice way. Cool colors especially work best on very lightened hair. Also, don't wash after rinsing out...just condition and then wait a couple days to wash if you can. Make sure to use a gentle, sulfate-free colors-afe shampoo. And skip shampoo often, and just rinse and condition (you can wash your scalp with conditioner). Also, "strip" your hair before applying...use a clarifying shampoo so remove any oils or build-up that will keep the color from getting info your hair! This is how I get my color to stay well for a couple months. :D

title: Great shave from an electric....solution to annoying unplugging.
text:
This new Norelco Arcitec razor provides a great shave with little irritation. I had a Braun Syncro previously, and it would leave little hairs everywhere on my neck. This new designed head flexs and pivots in all different ways to have more contact with the skin.

The jet clean station works good and is interesting to watch. It does a good job of cleaning the razor heads of hair and debris. There is however, one annoying issue. Norelco says you should not charge the razor until it needs it to maximize battery life. The jet clean system however, automatically goes into the charge cycle after cleaning and a two hour dry time!! If your like me, you will probably be at work two hours after shaving.

My solution to the unplugging is:

I picked up a plug in rocker switch at Home Depot to go between the wall outlet and the Norelco Transformer plug. I then shave a little earlier in my morning routine and clean the razor in the jet clean system. I then turn the switch off while the system is in the 2 hour drying cycle. This is ok since the razor is basically air/drip drying anyway. If it needs charged, I turn the switch on while I know I'm going to be home for and hour then turn back off. This is a bit annoying, but if I spent almost $200 on a razor then I want it to last. You could also just unplug it during the drying mode, but I like the switch so I don't have plugs and cords everywhere.

title: NOT actually silicone lined!!
text:
BE WARNED, THESE ARE NOT SILICONE LINED - contrary to what the listing says!!

I ended up purchasing these twice - when the first ones arrived and clearly did not have any silicone, I figured maybe they'd just made an error. Needing a product that was available with Prime, but finding extremely limited choices for this particular item, I ended up (stupidly) just trying again, hoping they'd get it right. They didn't.

I started to use these beads anyway, but am VERY glad I stopped after just a dozen strands or so! Because they don't have the silicone lining to protect the hair (and decrease slip) you're literally using needlenosed pliers to smash a tiny piece of unfinished metal in half, tightly around an already very tiny strand of your own hair, WITH another piece of metal in the middle! It's like a teeny tiny little car crash with your hair in the middle! If I'd tried to keep these things in for any length of time, I have no doubt they would have done serious damage. Just trying to remove the few I applied was extremely difficult and anxiety-inducing; none of the beads actually bent back in the opposite direction, like what you experience on a larger scale with the micro beads. When I could finally get each bead positioned to "un-crimp" it (getting it to stop slipping from between the pliers was no easy task) the only way they released was because they broke into tiny pieces, many took strands of my hair with them.

This is a long review for what probably seems like a totally inconsequential item, but I'm sure I'm not the only person who has made this mistake because they didn't know. Hopefully this will help prevent another DIY-er from having to deal with the same headache, and damage!

title: I really wanted to LOVE this wig like some of the other reviewers
text:
I really wanted to LOVE this wig like some of the other reviewers, but I ran into some problems with it for my Halloween costume (Daenerys Targaryen). Don't get me wrong, it helpped me execute my costume wonderfully, but fell short in my opinion in three categories.
First, when I initially opened the wig, the fibers at the part/crown were for lack of better words bent in a strange way that could not be corrected, even with light heat from my flat iron (luckily for me this was a non-issue for my costume because I needed to pull the front pieces of hair back into braids, but re-wear is going to look a little strange). Second, because you are purchasing a light colored fiber wig that is woven on to a nude headpiece, some of your natural hair/the wig cap is bound to show through. My issue was that you could starkly see the edging of my nude wig cap through the wig. Lucky for me, I naturally have very light blonde hair, but I couldn't imagine what show through would look like with someone with dark hair (just something to keep in mind). Third, thank the lord I remembered my brush. This thing got crazy tangled, now I knew some would come because of the length I went with, but I was brushing at least once an hour to keep a "fresh look."
With all that being said, I would purchase this wig again (just hopefully ending up with one that has a better crown/part). It looks 10X better and more realistic than anything I could have picked up at a Halloween store for my costume, especially keeping cost in mind at $43.

title: Thank You, Earth Therapeutics!!
text:
My bedroom faces the east and has an uncovered half-moon window above the one with blinds. In the summer the light begins to pour in before 5 AM and, being a light sleeper, I would wake up and have a difficult time getting back to sleep afterwards, which eventually, led me to search for a sleep mask.

I purchased these masks and another, molded one that came with earplugs. This is my very favorite and I shared the second of the set with my night-shift working daughter, as I felt it might help her get more rest during the day as well. I've been using mine for a few months now and absolutely love it.

It does take a little bit of getting used to, just to the feel of something on your face and around your head. I've felt a little irritation on my ears occasionally but can easily adjust it to relieve that. It fits my face and stays in place quite well without having the band on tightly. I am a "tummy sleeper", and this mask is so soft that it doesn't feel uncomfortable against my pillow. It's just wonderful!

I have not noticed any scent on the ones that I received, and I checked because of the other reviewers comments. I've hand-washed it numerous times now, then let it air dry and it's ready to go again. If anything, it's just become softer but has not shown any signs of wear beyond that. I'm now looking to order more, just to have on hand when this one is ready to be replaced.

The other, molded one seems a bit bigger but sits off your eyes, if that sensation would bother you. I have a little more difficulty getting it to block all the light as well as this one, but it could be more attractive for larger faces or folks that are bothered by having something constantly touching their eyes like this one does. Just my thoughts on that. . .

I've read many articles recently on the importance of getting adequate sleep for your mental and physical health. If you are looking at sleep masks, you're probably wanting to improve your rest for some reason. I'd recommend you give this mask a try. I don't understand why some seem scented and some aren't, but I am 100% pleased with the masks I received. Most of those reviews are pretty old if you note that.

title: Palm oil - pore clogging - failed applicator
text:
Not so good: Tube design failed, pore clogging, not 2-in-1
Good: color
Unknown: lasting?

I was glad I read a few reviews before I opened it, then I opened it carefully, pushed gently, and it burst out the sides all the same. I wasn't sure if it was because the on/off was marked on the lid but not the tube, maybe I just turned it the wrong amount? ½ turn seemed reasonable, so I turned it tighter and more came out the sides. For what it's worth, the instructions just have us dabbing a couple dots on with the sponge and blending with the fingers or brush. The sponge is an entirely unnecessary addition.

As you can see from the photo, this did allow me to put a nice and thick layer on my arm just in case anyone is looking to see how dramatic it can be. I do like the color, it's a good match, but I wouldn't use it on my eyes or my lips because the product says 'liquid blush.' There is a graphic on this page that says 2-in-1, despite showing eyes/blush/lips on the very same graphic, which I am pretty sure would be 3-in-1.

The last issue is the ingredients. The top ingredient is Ethylhexyl Palmitate, which is a pretty well known comedogenic (pore clogging) problem, so it's not great if you have breakouts. That's why I don't know how long it lasts or well it holds up over time, it's not worth the high risk of breakouts so I didn't wear it long. You might have guessed that 'palmitate' is also a derivative of Palm Oil, which is an industry that is destroying many biodiverse forests.

Two stars for color, texture feels nice, but I would only recommend this to people with clear skin that don't really have any desire to use the applicator sponge.

I will also add that accutane makes skin highly sensitive, vulnerable, and very dry, but this product did not further irritate or dry my skin. title: A good shave...but...
text:
I've used electric shavers for 30 years. My last was a Panasonic wet/dry and two Brauns before that. This one shaves fairly closely; gives a pretty good shave. It's ergonomic and fits well in my hands; comfortable to hold while shaving. I have a "tough" beard and it has also performed well after a two day beard growth; takes a little longer but a pretty close shave. The only time it has "grabbed" or "pulled" is with the two day growth; but only minimally.

But, in this day and age of "green" and trying to save energy, this one is not cool. The instructions call for rinsing in hot water; a waste of energy. Yes, one can use the little brush, or just blow it out. But Philips says use hot water. As stated by several (or most) reviewers, the trimmer is the really weak point. If you have a mustache, this one just doesn't perform well at all; just too small and hard to use. Even with the head removed, it barely trims my mustache. I guess it's okay for occasional side-burn trimming.

I bought this shaver as an Amazon daily deal. So, for almost half off retail it was a good deal. But, if you have a mustache and paying retail, I think I'd shop for another shaver.

title: Beyond all other shavers
text:
I was acutally hired to test this along with two other rotary models and 5 other electric straight edges (remington-like) in a recent product test. All of us in the test group came back with the overwhelming nod toward the Spectra in every category -- comfort, closeness and easy of use.
I've personally used a Norelco (the low end model) for a few years. Good but not great. This is a completely different animal with better cutting design for both better closeness on the face and more comfort on the neck and other angles. After a week of testing I really didn't want to return it.
The 'extra' features didn't matter much to me when I started, but my opinion quickly changed. Have a 'minutes remaining' to recharge was very useful when travelling. I knew whether I needed to bring the cord or not. That it is water resistant meant a little less worry when working near the wet sink. (I've also had this strange anxiety about it accidentally kerplunking into the toilet...now that fear is gone.)
There are not too many devices I use everyday, and that's how I'd justify the price. My cheaper norelco has been with me for about 5 years and I expect at least the same for this guy, so it can be amortized to about 10 cents a day.
I have tried and compared it to the others. Truly the best one out there, and I think you'd sacrifice a great deal taking a step down in price.

title: Clever and Simple Design Idea
text:
I don't know if this listing will last because it is (at the time of my order and review) a four pack for the price of a pair elsewhere. But you do indeed get four. So I thought I'd throw a review up.

I really like the design behind these. You can mount them with screws on a flat surface or corner. And with the included double sided sticky 3M pads, you can do the same without making holes. Plus probably get them on a round pole like a leg of a piece of furniture. The plastic spikes are a good balance of stiff and flexible, though between the two descriptors I'd lean towards stiff. I mounted a couple on my big cat tree (one on a corner and one on the base flat). They obviously blend in fine there. But they're small enough that they would be discrete even if they were put somewhere more out in the open. My cat likes them well enough. She isn't as enamored with them as I had hoped but I've caught her getting the side of her mouth on them more than once already.

Between the cheap price and the non damaging sticky pad option, they're worth trying out if you think your cat would like them. If not, no big loss.

title: it's ok but I would not recommend it
text:
It was tough to decide whether or not to give this product one or two stars, but I gave it two because it doesn't completely suck, it's just not as good as other razors that aren't as expensive The manufacturer recommends waiting 21 days before deciding to keep this product or send it back. I would also give the same recommendation to people who are looking at purchasing this. I bought it because I needed to replace my old razor. My old Remington titanium R9710 was a good razor but it ripped the hair out of my neck area and left me with very irritated skin. The thing about my old razor is that it had floating heads and it handled long hairs pretty well if I was lazy and didn't shave. This new Arcitec worked very well when I first got it but I really wanted to try it out and only had stubble on my face at the time. It worked very well with short hairs and left me with no irritated skin on my neck.

Well I wanted to see what it would act like if I let my hair grow a little and it did not perform like I thought it would. It took a long time to shave and I had to go over the area multiple times in multiple directions and with different pressures just to get a few long hairs. This new head style has really been a downgrade because when you apply pressure, the heads seem to pull away from your face on the outside part of it and it makes it harder to shave. It was either that or the fact that it doesn't have a hair collection area. It fills up with hair rather quickly so maybe that has an impact on how well it shaves. Cleaning the unit was very simple but I think I would have the cleaning system of one of the speed XL models over this. You have to pop open three separate chambers rather than flip the whole head up to clean each blade. A nice feature of this razor is the tube trimmer. You can take the razor head right off and pop out the trimmer. There really isn't much else to say about the trimmer other than I thought it worked great.

Overall, this is a very nice looking razor, but the functionality of the razor itself is pretty bad. It does come with a nice travel case and charging stand as well. The travel case is made of hard plastic and does not have room for the charger, but it does have the capability to charge the razor, so you do not need to bring along the charging stand. If you want to try this product I would say go for it because Norelco has such a generous return policy and maybe you will like it better than I did. If you think you like the functions of this razor but really aren't sure about it, I would not recommend it because it doesn't work like I think a razor should (it takes a long time to shave and it doesn't work well on longer hairs). It looks nice and has nice features, but I think its functionality isn't worth the high price tag.

title: Exfoliate your skin without ruining your hands
text:
This is a pretty great exfoliating pad/mitt with one key feature I have not seen before.
The thing that sets this apart from similar products is that the inside is lined with terry cloth.
That small addition makes a major difference when it comes to using the mitt because you don't end up exfoliating your hand the entire time you are trying to exfoliate you body.

The external material does a pretty good job exfoliating.
It's rough, but not painful, so it should work for a wide range of skin types.
Obviously, you can also pair it with soaps and scrubs to enhance its ability to exfoliate.
Personally, I find this gentle enough to use every shower, yet textured enough to remove a lot of dead skin.

If there is one extra change I wish the makers of this mitt would consider for future iterations,
it would be to add a loop of some sort to hang it by, so it can be left to dry on a hook.
Still, I can add something like that myself or just hang it over a towel rack, so it's not a big deal.

I would definitely recommend this mitt to someone in the market for one.
It's perfect for a bath or shower, offering good exfoliation for your skin, while protecting your hand from unnecessary wear and tear.

title: Works ok, but a wet/dry trimmer is the way to go!
text:
Had this trimmer for 2 years and it died last week after sliding into the bathroom sink under running water....

While it was working it was a good trimmer overall, though I really didn't like have to switch out the trimmer heads for the standard and then the detail sized cutters--on more than one occasion I was in a hurry and fumbling around looking for the other cutter assembly than what was on the trimmer. Another issue was that it was relatively easy to move the height adjustment by accident when taking off and replacing the plastic trimmer guard, which you need to do in order to switch cutting heads. It wasn't a really big deal, but a lot of times I wouldn't remember which number I had the hair length set on, and then I would have to guess what setting I had it one the last time I used it.....The vacuum feature was nice I guess in that it doesn't get too many little beard trimmings all over the sink, but then again it's really easy to just turn on the sink and rinse it, or, use the trimmer over a rug where you'll never see the small trimmings.....

But the big lesson here is to be sure buy a wet/dry beard trimmer that won't die if it gets a little wet. I just bought the Panasonic ER224S All-in-One Cordless Hair and Beard Trimmer [[ASIN:B000F4USF8 Panasonic ER224S All-in-One Cordless Hair and Beard Trimmer (Silver)]] which was almost half the price of the Phillips Norelco unit and it's a wet/dry trimmer that you can use in the shower. It also has a built-in detail trimmer so you don't have to switch cutter heads and worry about loosing attachments. When I went to replace the T980 that died, I avoided the latest Phillips/Norelco version because I think a wet/dry is beard trimmer is really the only way to go. So far I really like the Panasonic, and I wish I had bought one of these to start with.......

title: Most Excellent
text:
This mask is unlike any other I've used. Unopened, it sounds like a heavy liquid when the container is shaken; I'm used to masks that are "solid" and extremely thick, but was looking for an exfoliating mask because my skin gets very dry and flaky in winter. Got this one because I was offered a discount in exchange for an honest review. Used it last night for the first time...

It should probably be well-shaken before each use, and it looks very strange. Kind of a greenish-grey pearlescence, and it is a "runny" mask. A little goes a long way, too! I was surprised. There must be at *least* 20 treatments in this little jar. Required less than two teaspoons to do my entire face and under the jawline.

It feels strange. Kind of an icy-hot sting in the beginning; interesting, but not uncomfortable. It doesn't feel as though it would do a lot of exfoliating, and it doesn't dry quickly (maybe it's not supposed to dry, at all). The instructions said to leave it on for 20 minutes, but I left it on for an hour. At that point, it was flaky. Rather than simply rinse it off, I rubbed it off with my fingers, and THAT was definitely exfoliating. This wouldn't work with any of the other masks I've used, and I really liked being able to easily/gently rub every bit off using my fingers. Post-rub, my face felt very dry, but after rinsing with warm water that feeling went away and my skin was SO soft.

Today when I awoke, my skin felt great. No dry patches. I did still apply my usual three or four drops of cold argan oil, just because the humidity is so low right now.

As-is, I like this mask much more than I thought I would when I first opened the jar (though it smells wonderful, again, it's very "liquid," which seemed strange before I'd actually used it). That said, I'll probably alternate between using it straight out of the jar and adding some bentonite to make it a bit thicker. Very happy to have this organic mask!

title: Not ideal for very pale skin, but usable
text:
For the record, I am a longtime Physicians Formula wearer, and their products can be hit or miss. I am not being paid to leave a review, or representing anyone but myself here. This is the first time I tried PF's countouring powder, and I've used it for about three seasons. I like it. I don't love it.

I have very pale skin with pink undertones that is uber-sensitive and I have to be very careful about sun exposure. Anything can make me break out in hives or eczema, at any time, even if I used it daily for years. Thankfully, PF products have never done that to me, in almost a decade.

As for this product, the shades are where I take some issue. They worked best for my tone in summer, but now, in winter -- I'm shopping for a different product.

* The dark shade is really mahogany-like, so I have to blend, blend, blend in daylight or risk looking like I smeared mud on my face. It's good for shading jawline and cheekbones with a light touch at temples if you need it. Beware, though. If you are very pale, you want a very light touch with this one.

*The medium shade is very subtle and helps blend and soften the dark. It also works well as a matte bronzer, around sides of the nose, and wherever you need just a little definition. This is the best shade of the bunch, honestly. At least for my skin tone.

* The light shade is, frankly, worthless to me. It gives my skin a pasty, chalky look and looks heavy. Yuck. I occasionally use it in tiny spots as a concealer, but as a contour powder, it just looks like I put on way too much setting powder or something. Instead, I use my lightest shade of matte eyeshadow (also a PF product) and a higher-end illuminator for highlighting. Those results are beautiful, frankly, even on my 38 year old skin.

All in all, PF's contour colors are suitable for pale skin, but may be better on other slightly darker or warmer skin tones, or on summer tanned skin.

title: Leave In?
text: When I first sprayed this product on my hair, I noticed the smell right away. It's not bad at all, but one can't help but notice the chemical-like smell at the end of the almond note. I used it in combination with a water and oil mixture as well as some flaxseed gel to bring out and define my curl pattern. I did this for several days straight since the leave-in states it's light enough for daily use. I live in a very dry climate, so keeping my hair moisturized is important because my hair dries out quick and feels becomes brittle. I think this leave-in conditioner dried my hair out faster!!! And I would say the butylene glycol, which is the fourth ingredient, is the culprit. It probably contributed to the chemical smell as well. It's unfortunate because finding alcohol-free hair products is comparable to searching for a unicorn. But living in a  dry climate, I really don't need another hair product drying out my hair. Luckily, I bought another leave-in conditioner in unison and it's actually containing the moisture in my hair so much better. So overall, I'd give this product three stars. It doesn't really look (or smell) all that much like a leave-in...at least compared to the ones I've used in the past...but it did help with detangling, the smell was still decent, it was light on my hair with the few days I applied it, and I like that it didn't contain a bunch of harmful ingredients.

title: The fat
text:
This is a classic. Having tried a few hard soaps and creams and also having heard that "the fat" has a cult-like following, I had to try it.
The smell is nothing short of awesome. Kind of a powdery linen clean smell. And it's a pervasive smell too, that will carry with you after your shave.
But the magic of MWF is the lanolin, a natural wax that the sheep exude to protect their wool... The original Mitchell noticed that wool shearers' hands were always soft and supple, and thankfully decided to try a shaving product based in it.
You will notice the lanolin effect right after your shave as you're rinsing off your face. It will be smooth and moist and will feel awesome.
MWF can be tough to lather, but after a few tries and watching a few videos online you'll get the hang of it. For best results try skipping the bowl/scuttle and just face-lather. It'll create a luscious, moisturizing, delicious smelling lather that is like no other.

text:
When I went through chemotherapy, I lost most of my hair, and as a woman this was a real blow to my self image. This trio of products was recommended to me by the woman who runs our local health food store, and along with taking an oral biotin supplement (5,000 mcg per day), I used this three-step system (shampoo, conditioner, and leave-in serum) to wash and condition my hair. Between the two approaches, both oral and topical, I re-grew all of my original hair, and now my hairdresser swears that I have more hair now than I did before I was diagnosed with cancer and went through chemotherapy. It does feel thicker to me now, too, and my husband has also remarked that my hair has never looked better.

The only caveat is that if you have longer hair you may need an extra conditioner for the ends. title: All the strength of traditional arylic without the bulk or salon. Stronger and easier DIY then gel
text:
I have always coveted long nails, but with weak, bendy nails that peal and break easily it was never achievable. I'm a DIY girl when it comes to nails. I have been doing my own gel manicures for years and most recently have been using Brisa lite smoothing gel for added strength. It helped but manicures still started chipping at the 10 day mark and as soon as my nails got to the desired length they would start breaking.
By comparison this stuff is amazing! Its all the strength without the bulk of regular acrylic. They are my real nails but nothing will break them.The process itself is faster since you don't have to cure for two minutes each time. The coats between and after powder are just thin glue. Its also more forgiving as the coats are all even and solidly applied. You buff and clean up in the middle of the process which makes everything even and your edges perfect. I've also filed and such after they are done without issue.
I actually ordered from Revel itself, but read the reviews here first. Revel colors are also cheaper then gel's options, with a one ounce jar of color only costing about $8. One ounce jar is probably like 8-10 manicures. Sure beats paying a salon $40 every two weeks.
Removal is slightly different. I use the cotton ball with nail caps method and find it slightly more time consuming then gel, but I think that's only because I'm still getting used to it. When exposed to acetone the dip turns into a chewed gum consistency. So unlike my CND shellac that peals off I'm rubbing off sticky blobs. But I also probably just need to try soaking it an extra 5 minutes and stop being impatient.
But the extra removal time is totally worth it when you consider the manicures last longer, are stronger, and allow me to finally have my dream long nails.

I do have to commend the company for their packaging. While the bottle did leak during transport, the company was aware that this would happen ahead of time and packaged this well. This polish remover comes in the same type of bottle most store brands do. There is no special scent and it is typical remover.

This polish removes regular nail polish (not talking about gel here) very well. It does not leave nails too stripped.

Five stars. It does what it is supposed to to without excessive problems or smells.

title: War on Friction
text:
This product is sold on several different pages on Amazon.com. Whether it’s listed as being for wall clocks, folding knives or typewriters, it’s all the same stuff.

And it’s pretty good stuff. I recently rebuilt an antique record player. I wanted to update it with a modern cartridge that uses as lot less pressure and that meant that I needed the tonearm to have a lot less friction.

I initially did the rebuild with standard 3-in-1 oil. It was partially successful. Warped or off center records wouldn’t play. I decided to tear down and try again with Liquid Bearings and it worked. I can play any record now.

I like the precision needle tip. It’s a lot easier to use than the usual spout on 3-in-1 oil cans.

I bought a small bottle and only used a small fraction of it. I tossed my can of 3-in-1 and kept the Liquid Bearings. It worked for me! 5 Stars.

{I purchased these replacement blades directly from Philips, because I had a discount code. While not purchased from Amazon, these are the same blades I received from Philips.}
I used the SH50 replacement blades for a 4100 series Philips razor. I use my razor not just for my face, but also to maintain my shiny bald head! Therefore, the razor and blades get quite a work out. I wanted to replace the blades some time ago, but the negative reviews concerned me enough that I delayed. Finally, I had to move forward.
I wanted to make sure that I was not going to get blades made by a 3rd party, so I contacted Philips directly to ensure I was getting their blades. Upon arrival, I over-analyzed the replacement process because of comments I had read here. At least for the 4100, the replacement was an absolute breeze, and I would have been better off not worrying. You do need to align each of the blades a little, but if you pay attention when you pop out the previous blades, it's simple. The next time I do this, it will take me less than 60 seconds.
In case I didn't like the new blades, I set the old ones aside. Then I waited--3 days--so there was a solid amount of growth to give these new blades a right proper test! As I write this, that test was just completed. The blades passed with flying colors. It's like the razor was brand new again. There was no pulling at all. The shave was smooth, and so is my head. I'm very pleased with how these blades work with the 4100 model.

title: Just kind of average
text:
I don't used to use skin-care products often. As a male, it's just not something I used to give much thought to. However, as I get older, I do suffer from dry skin in the winter months as the lower humidity in my house tends to cause my skin to flake and break out in spots.

So I thought I would try this vegan oil for dry skin and I'm not entirely impressed.

First thoughts are that the bottle is very nice. I love the green color of the oil. When the light hits it just right, it looks very pleasing. The bottle comes with a lid attached to a dropper for application, which makes it a little difficult to apply. You have to hold the dropper with one hand and apply it to the other and rub it in. My concern with this method is how difficult it will be to pull up more oil when the bottle gets low, but I guess that remains to be seen.

The oil itself is very greasy feeling. It literally feels like a lower viscosity motor oil and also has a sandy/gritty texture to it when applied. The scent is very strange as well. To me, it smells 100% like rubber. It's not a bad smell, but it's also not a pleasant smell. It's just a smell. If you've ever smelled rubber, you know what I mean.

As for its effectiveness? Again, not impressed.

I've been using it for about a week now, and I haven't really noticed any huge effects from the lotion. My skin is still peeling and dry in most of the places where I have applied this, but I would say there is a slight improvement. However, I'm not sure it's worth the price. I have used other, much cheaper, lotions/oils that have provided better results.

Overall, this is just average to me. I'm just not sure it's worth the price of admission.

text:
This is probably about the 100th brand I have tried for an eye mask if I exaggerate a bit.
I use under eye patches almost everyday, sometimes twice a day not only for under eye but also for my neck lines and forehead.
So I am not kidding when I say I have tried 10s of different brands of under eye patches from Amazon.
To be honest, under eye patches are for a rather temporary fix, in that you have to use them everyday or for a long period to have more permanent effects. But that’s how all skin care products work in my opinion. I use it to reduce very fine lines under my eyes (you can’t really see it unless you look in the mirror closely but it bugs me), and prevent my neck and forehead lines from getting worse (and hopefully to improve).
This one didn’t stay well at all on my neck, and I felt it dried out too quickly.
FYI, I don’t have dark circles, so my rate of effectiveness is solely for fine lines and such.
For my neck lines, I think most eye patches are at par in terms of quality, to be honest. Of course, from time to time, there are brands with quite inferior quality to others. I wouldn’t know about this one, as it kept falling off.
The last straw was that it just ripped apart when I tried to move the slipped mask back to the intended spot. It was annoying. After a couple of times, I just took it all off from my face.
The bottom line is that this product doesn’t have any price advantage to overlook its rather inferior quality compared to similar quality eye masks in this price range either.
I got so many other eye masks right now, I am not going to use this one unless I run out of eye masks between shipments or something (highly unlikely though).
Overall, 2.5/5 from me based on my experience of trying this mask for the very first time, and I won’t be recommending this.

title: Will it outperform my 7 year old Norelco?
text:
I am generally happy with my new Norelco 7180XL, it is nice to have a new shaver, it is amazingly quiet, and gives a close and quick shave.

But I feel that Norelco needs to improve both their instruction manual, and their customer support. Neither of these were in tune with my first experience with the 7180XL, as far as initial charging, and what the green charging light and red low battery light were doing.

The manual calls for a 12 hour initial charge before using the shaver. When fully charged, the green light is supposed to blink. Well, on my initial charge, the light started blinking after 30 minutes. I did continue the charge for 12 hours anyway, the green light blinking the whole time.

I called Norelco support, and was informed the manual was not correct, and that I had not damaged my shaver by completing the 12 hour charge. But no further explanation.

Then I started using the shaver, and after just 2 shaves, the red low battery light came on. I went back to the Norelco website, and found a page on charging that said if the shaver did that, you should use it until the motor stops. They omit the obvious next step of charging it in these instructions, but say you will have no problem with the red light coming on too soon after following their directions.

Well, I have done that, and it remains to be seen if my new Norelco will eventually sort itself out and work right.

I must say I have my doubts after this initial experience, that it will last as long as my 7 year old model 5841XL did. I've used Norelco shavers for about 40 years, and never had any problems like this.

title: Provides subtle, consistent improvement. Effects aren't striking -- but it works.
text:
I received a discounted sample of this product to provide a review on amazon.

I am a healthy 64-year old male with skin that appears tighter and healthier than that of many peers. While I tanned during the first half of my life, I phased it out during the second. I only use lotion under my eyes where skin is noticeably loose and darker than the rest. Over the past five or six years -- part of this is genetic -- the skin at the front of the neck has become especially loose, while the furrowed lines on my forehead have begun to look alarming. I wanted to try Puressant Neck Firming Cream to see what effect it might have on these two issues.

After a three-week trial, during which I applied the product at least once per day, I've seen a subtle but real tightening of the skin on my neck, which appears to have reached maximum effect. I will assume that to continue this trend I might have to use the product indefinitely, but received no indication from product instructions about this. In any case, there are few products I use indefinitely and particularly those with such an extensive list of known and unknown ingredients. Having said that, I might use the product at intervals to reduce symptoms periodically.

The product has had no effect on my wrinkly forehead, at least not yet. I'll just have to live with it.

The cream has a clean, subtle fragrance (I wish it had none) and rather heavy consistency: A little goes a long way. I've not yet noticed any staining of clothes after application nor any side effects. If not for its moisturizing qualities, I might have awarded this product three stars, but it generates enough cosmetic improvement at a low price to merit four.

title: Duped by the Chinese! They are on my Wall of SHAME again!
text:
When I ordered the HQ6 replacement heads for my Norelco Shaver, I knew that I was NOT purchasing a genuine Norelco product. So I was WARNED!

I installed the new heads and they immediately rattled around in my shaver and there appeared to be more of a gap around the Chinese replacement heads than my genuine Norelco head. So, I took them out and measured the outside diameter of the genuine Norelco head at .812" in diameter. My new Chinese replacement HQ6 head only measured .806" in diameter. (.006" smaller in diameter) This may not seem like much, but when you are dealing with a small precision instrument, a .006" difference is NOT acceptable. I'm not planning on returning the heads because it simply is not worth my time and effort, but it's another life lesson learned. You get what you pay for and I was told they were not genuine. This is JUST THE TRUTH!! Shame.

title: Amazing Fragrances. Definitely Worth It! (Detailed Review)
text:
I’ve been on the search for a few fragrances recently, and was introduced to various reviews on YouTube about brands such as Swiss Arabian, Rasasi, Al-Rehab etc. I usually stick to Nemat’s perfume oils but this times I wanted to take a risk. Therefore, I decided to grab some samples. Initially I was intimidated by the fact that there’s the idea that perfumes that are manufactured in the Middle East can be heavy (which they can be), but great because they are long lasting. And let me tell you, I’ve fallen in love with these.

La Yuqawam Pour Femme is a definite dupe for Black Orchid by Tom Ford. It’s feminine, floral, peppery and spicy. This perfume is perfect for a night in the town, a date night, or to simply uplift your mood. This perfume is up there with Narciso Rodriguez’s For Her, Dior’s J’Adore and all the other popular perfumes that are titans in the perfume industry. I loved this very much. A must for fall/winter. 10/10

La Yuqawam Jasmine Wisp is sweet, floral and has quite an island-like feel to it. I imagine being on an island vacation. The notes of coconut and fruity notes makes this perfume a delicious addition to your collection. It’s quite the fragrance for a girly young woman but also has an element of sophistication too. I’d say that this is for spring/summer but can be used sparingly for fall/winter. 10/10

La Yuqawam Orchid Prairie is one that is so hard to describe..which is why I love it so much. I definitely get an enigmatic, unusual but a captivating impression from this perfume. I remember this perfume being described as “grape juice spilled over wet wood.” And I do think that’s quite true. Again, it’s hard to describe, but I imagine this smell as like being in the middle of a misty forest and you catch the scent of berries and rich, deep colored fruit mixed with moss and amber. I imagine this scent being something that is so rare, unusual, unique and exotic and otherworldly that people will definitely want to know about it, but you have to keep it a secret. Even if people don’t know you the wearer, they’d know that you were in the room. This perfume is exactly that. This perfume is definitely for a woman who is sensual, unusual, and rare.. a woman who is in the world but not of it. 12/10

In all, if you are looking for a captivating sample set of niche perfumes from the Middle East, these perfume samples will never fail you. They haven’t for me. So take a risk, take a chance and buy it. Also, you can always give these samples away as a gift if you don’t like them. These samples are just enough to carry in your purse, and just enough if you want to try out a scent without the full price.

Enjoy!

title: THE BEST!  Better than Super Blue, Glam Seamless Tape, and Satin Strands.  Try it!
text:
I have had tape-in extensions for several years and these are BY FAR the BEST replacement tapes I have used. I only use Glam Seamless extension hair and these fit those pieces really well. I love that these can easily be split in half because when I place my extensions I use a single piece and fold it in half, rather than sandwiching 2 pieces, to put less weight on my baby fine hair.

I have tried many types of replacement tapes including the "Super Blue", and in a pinch the super cheap (quality, not cost!) Satin Strands, and these far outshine them all. With all other tapes I always lose 1-2 pieces every time I wash my hair (which is only 1x/week), and the rest slip a little with each wash. So because of that I always put them in as close to the scalp as possible. To my surprise, not only did I not lose any with this tape, they didn't slip at all, not even a little! So I had nearly 2 weeks of my extensions remaining really tight to my head! I almost pulled them out because they were getting uncomfortable, but I ended up sticking it out.

It has now been just about 6 weeks and I am going to pull them out and reset them within the week. They still haven't slipped very much, and I still haven't lost a single one! By this point with any other tape, half of them would have come out by now! I could easily leave these in another month without much issue, but my baby fine hair knots easily when there is any outgrowth.

This tape is a little bit thicker than other tapes, which is likely why it holds so well. When putting the two pieces together, really press down and squish them together to ensure there is a secure contact with both sides. Then heat set the pieces between a hot iron on low for 5-10 seconds - this is not in the instructions but is recommended on the product's website, so I did it, and got really great results!

Because these have such a strong hold, I just ordered the C-22 solvent to remove them. I normally use coconut oil, but suspected I might need something a bit more to remove these. I will update my review once I remove them and share whether or not it was more difficult, compared to other tapes.

title: Decent product!
text:
So I don’t own a blow dryer or a hair straightener. I know. I bought this to hopefully replace the need for both of them. Pictured: my hair styled when damp, my hair styled and natural side-by-side, and my hair styled when dry (tie-dye shirt).

Some pros: I have very wavy, long, fine hair, but a ton of it, and can dry/style my hair in under 30 minutes with this. Yes the brush size is huge, but with how much hair I have, I need it to be large. The style it produced was beautiful! I will be keeping this for sure!

Some cons: I deducted a star mainly because this brush doesn’t get very hot. I guess this could be a pro since it won’t damage your hair as much over time. But for me, I noticed that some parts of my hair were still wavy, and that the style didn’t hold perfectly over time.

Some tips: definitely use this tool on damp hair. It semi-straightened my dry hair, but the style did not hold over time and my hair went right back to wavy in an hour. I had to go over my damp hair a few times, but make sure to maintain tension when you pull. That’s the best way I was able to get my hair straight. Another reason I deducted a star was because I still feel like I need a flat iron to do touch ups—around my roots specifically. But this product is definitely better than using a flat iron all over!

Verdict: worth $20! Glad I purchased.

title: A True Gentleman's Walking Stick
text:
Alpacca is also named German Silver or Nickle Silver. Consisting mostly of copper, nickle and zinc content. In my brief research I find that Alpacca does not contain any actual silver. Though some may be silver plated. But do not think of it as cheap imitation silver. It is more akin to a subset of brass.

This Alpacca cane is the pricier big brother to the plastic headed walking stick of the same design. The plastic brethren of this stick was love at first sight. The flared head and modest fluting simply screams elegance. Nowhere have I found a more elegant walking stick for the 'top hat' era.

As reported with flared head sticks, it is better suited for show. The slightly rounded top makes putting any kind of real pressure uncomfortable without leather gloves. However, it does provide modest balance if weight bearing is not your walking issue. The silvery smooth head does not make the cane top heavy.

The rubber tip is pretty standard and is useful for standing the 3/4" wide cane on flat surfaces. On the negative side, it takes away from the distinctiveness and gives an "old man" quality. I ordered my cane through a vendor who does silver ferrules (plated brass tips) and upgraded the business end of this cane to become a "Gentleman's Walking Stick". Silver ferrules raise the value and elevate the distinctive beauty.

This Alpacca cane lacks the distinctive charm of a chrome collar. My vendor states he routinely heats up such heads for removal, but the extra cost hardly seems worth the upgrade. It was mostly due to removal of the head. Unlike the screw top plastic cane, the Alpacca head is hollow and intended for permanent mounting, using pitch.

As it stands, this cane is suited for mild assisted walking. Use it more for classy strolls, theater, special occasions and dancing. Do not forget the white leather gloves!

Addendum:
On Saturday, 2/7/2015 I finally revealed this walking stick for a big birthday celebration. My black and white clothing style makes me look good, but there is a "whoa" factor when seen with this stick and a pair of white leather gloves. It helps that I had the tip refined with a ferrule and small rubber tip. I love it.

title: The coverage is pretty darn thick
text:
The coverage is pretty darn thick, definitely for people who are into normal to heavier coverage. It has a sort of matte but moist finish, which I really like because it lends a nice glow to my skin, and definitely lasts all day - huge staying power. It does slide into my fine lines, and does not really have many pore-filling qualities. It will minimize pores at first, like right after you finish applying, bu by the end of the day your pores will be rather obvious. BUT, in pictures your skin will look flawless and fairly matte regardless of how odd it looks up close in person! So at least you'll always look on point in pictures, and as long as nobody stares too closely. The product has also been a little pore clogging for me, but I find that it's somewhat manageable with dedication to a skincare routine.

The cushion inside does dry out a little faster than one would expect, but that is probably also because of the product being thicker than most cushion compacts. The puff applicator is so pleasant and soft to touch, but for me it also deposits way too much product onto my skin. I always have to go back with a beauty blender and try to make the coverage thinner, because when I don't the product looks SUPER cakey.

As for the sun protection purpose, it works pretty well, and is convenient for when traveling or running errands on a sunny day, if you're like me and like to carry a cushion around in order to reapply throughout the day. However, as I said the product can, and consistently has, been cakey when applied with the puff that comes with it, and is already a rather thick/borderline cakey. So even though it's supposed to be convenient, it's also a little counter intuitive.

title: Good razor
text:
I've used the Arcitec 1050 for about 3 months and like it with a few caveats. The shave is a good, close shave. Most days I shave as soon as I stumble out of bed at 4:30AM, without so much as washing my face. The shave is good, stubble starts to show by late afternoon. The days I shower first, 12 hours later it is like I just shaved. I am getting 25 shaves per recharge, better than advertised.

As stated by Norelco, it took several weeks for the razor to be really comfortable. May not have helped that those first few weeks were very cold and dry. I have used a Norelco for 15 years, didn't expect to need the 3 week break in, but I did.

I am not thrilled that the razor has to be washed daily, but it is easy to do. However, it means the razor sits open drying most of the time which is no real problem, but annoys me. On the plus side, after 2 months I poured a little isopropanol in the cup I got with Norelco cleaner fluid 15 years ago, stuck the razor head in it and ran the 1050 for 30 seconds. Much easier than having the take all the heads out and swish them one at a time as with my old 7825. The shave improved too, so periodic thorough cleaning is (as with all Norelcos) a must.

The trimmer is fair. It's fine for sideburns, terrible for my mustache. I bought a mustache trimmer, which works much much better than any razor's trimmer. So maybe that the poor 1050 performance was a good thing.

My one big concern. The first 1050 I bought died after 18 shaves. Just would not turn on. Would not charge. I returned it to the store and exchanged it, and the second 1050 has had no problems. But there are more electronics in the Arcitec than in my car. I suspect that caused the failure. So I am concerned about the robustness of the design. Although electronics tend to die early, or last a long time.

Oh, and the shape is the easiest I've ever handled.

title: Easy & Painless, Temporary Smoothing w/ Serum-Enjoy It But Can’t Gauge Long Term Benefit
text:
﻿I’ve been using the NIRA Skincare Laser & Hyaluronic Acid Serum for a couple weeks and can’t yet gauge whether the laser is effective at increasing collagen production and smoothing wrinkles as a long term benefit. I get good results from the hyaluronic acid (HA) serum as it gives quick but temporary plumping and smoothing of wrinkles, as do other good HA serums. I also suspect the warmth created by Nira laser may increase absorption of the HA serum and boost its short term benefits (though I can’t say for sure).

I assume it will take regular use for at least 60 days (and likely 90 days) to judge Nira‘s benefits beyond the temporary HA plumping. Nira’s own before and after photos are from the 90-day mark. While I’ll continue use of the Nira laser to see if it helps, I question the extent of any long term benefits based on Nira’s own photos that show a smiling before photo and a rather solemn after photo; clearly, we more lines are evident when smiling so I feel photos would be more credible if they showed someone with the same or similar expression in the before and after photos.

Still, I like the Nira laser as it holds a charge well and is quick and easy to use. It gives feedback via beeps. Nira states it has FDA clearance (which I haven’t verified) for wrinkle treatment around the eyes. I’m cautious about the eye area, so I’m initially trying Nira on less sensitive skin between my eyebrows where I have fine lines and slight sagging and also on my neck where I have a weird wrinkle likely from looking down at my tablet. I started using Nira on fine lines around my mouth, but I may hold off until I feel confident it won’t exacerbate existing pigmentation issues.

Nira is painless and I only feel warming on setting 2 or 3 (depending on area). The skin around my mouth is drier and only tolerates a 2, and it turns red temporarily. I’ve tried a 4 between the eyebrows and it stings, so I’ll need to work up. I use the HA serum after use, and it’s a clear gel like serum that’s calming and my redness goes away quickly. I get a quick plumping effect that temporarily helps smooths lines, but I can’t say if Nira will provide a long term benefit over time. I do like using it with the serum, so I’m rating it 4 stars. I’ll update as appropriate.

text: What woman doesn't love cosmetics and everything that entails? I'm always keeping my eyes open for beneficial face creams and serums. Algae can quite possibly reduce the breakdown of hyaluronic acid within the skin. Algae subspecies have anti-aging benefits. Maltol and POLYQUATERNIUM-80 (plant-based) is used in cosmetics regularly and deemed safe.  NMF (Natural Moisturizing Factor) components work to keep skin supple and hydrated. The combination of these ingredients is a friend to the skin's health. Understanding what's in our products ensures that we are buying serums we actually want to put on our faces. title: I think it's workng:)
text:
I have sensitive, reactive, allergic, rosacea skin. I ordered this product for both myself and my two year old granddaughter. While she doesn't have any of my DNA (stepson's daughter), she has especially sensitive skin. I've done aromatherapy the last six months. Have taken an online Butters & Balms course, so am interested in available products. I'm a little conflicted with the ingredients. There are some incredible natural ingredients (the oils and extracts) and some ingredients that I can't use on my face (Methylsulfonylmethane (Msm) and Hyaluronic Acid), a place where I can use a lot of soothing.

Recently, I've been experimenting with products that are supposed to deal with skin issues. My skin has not reacted well to many of them. Not sure about the culprit for this one, but I think it's the soap that draws out impurities. I had switched to using natural deodorant with good success. Thought my armpits would be a good place for a soap like that. A few days later, I had some large, painful, red bumps under one arm. I used the soothing diaper balm twice a day and it's really helped a lot. The bumps are almost gone three days later. I will continue to try it on my body, as I have these kind of issues--which aren't infrequent. I will also give some to my granddaughter to see if it helps heal some of her skin issues.

I received this product at a discount for an honest review.

title: Work great for fine, thin hair
text:
I have long, very fine, very thin hair so getting volume is always a problem for me. The only way I could get any sort of volume was to go the salon and get a blow out which, for obvious financial reasons, I can't do every day. I had a list of requitements for a round brush and this set checks every box!
They are sturdy and won't fall apart like the cheap ones you get at the big box stores. The hollow barrel is ceramic coated for better heat conduction without the extra damage to your hair you get from a metal barrel. The bristles are plastic but flexible and keep your hair smooth amd shiney. As a fun bonus, I adore the color! The set of 3 give you 1-1/4", 1-3/4" and 2" sizes. It also comes in an aesthetically pleasing box that is perfect for wrapping if this is intended as a gift.
If you don't know how to use a round brush I suggest looking up some tips. I was making it much harder than it needed to be! Biggest tip, don't try to do a blowout on wet hair! Your hair should be damp at best, like 80% dry. Otherwise it becomes a tangled disaster.

text: I purchased this to repair a model G Black limited edition clipper, which is basically a GTX. The GTO uses a 2 wire cord (without a ground) and we order those direct from Andis along with all of the other Andis products we sell or use to repair and sharpen equipment. They claim the 3 wire cord is only for Canada (and would not supply them to us), but many barbers in SoCal have the GTX and they need to be repaired no matter where it was intended to be sold. Some people think the heavier cord helps the performance of the clipper, but they would be wrong. At 10-12 watts, the amperage draw is far less than what a small wire is capable of handling. I did not measure the gauge of the wire in this cord to see how it compares to the GTO cords, but the only benefit of a heavier wire is that it will take longer for fatigue to cause the wire to break at the clipper. [[VIDEOID:e7a30e00ac346d7528a89979e60ae651]] This curler is big in size compared to most classic curlers. That doesn't stop us from using it in our house though! It does come in a variety of colors and I chose pink because it is my favorite color. It just takes a couple of minutes for the curler to get hot and the best part about that is you can control how hot you want it. The curler has a nice display to show you what the temperature is and there is a nice on/off sliding switch to it as well. The other buttons on the handle are for the temperature settings, curl direction, and the time setting. The curl direction is pretty flipping neat as you can control which direction it will curl your hair. You can have it make your curls go right, left, or set it to auto curl. The time setting is pretty easy to figure out, it controls how long you want the curler to actually hold the hair and how much of a curl you want. You can set it to hold the strand of hair that you are curling up to 15 seconds. You hold the blacker part toward your head when you are curling and you can start anywhere you want to. If you want more of a curl, you will go closer to the base of the strand. If you don't want a lot of curl, then you can start in the middle. It is pretty simple to use, all you have to do is slide the strand of hair into the curler and clamp it down. It will automatically gather the strand on the inside of the curler and set the curl. It is quite an amazing little gadget! You always want to make sure you are using a type of heat protectant on your hair to keep it healthy. The other thing is that it will automatically shut off after non use but always try to remember to unplug your stylers. I honestly wasn't sure what to expect but now I am going to have to fight with my daughter to use it!

This is the worst eyebrow pencil I’ve tried at this price, and it’s even worse than the e.l.f. version that’s similar. I know that’s dramatic but the reason why I wanted to write this review is because I’m just so frustrated with the quality compared to the price. It’s just not okay!

I’ve been using the nyx precision brow pencil, but this was a few dollars cheaper at ulta at the time and so I got it because the nyx one is like 10 bucks. My brows are the makeup I wear most consistently, so I’m always trying different brow pencils to try to cut down on the cost. But I go back to nyx every time. Maybe the morphe one is okay but it’s pretty hard and waxy so not really. Now I know the importance of the extra two dollars for the nyx.

This pencil is so soft, it wears down so quickly and also because of how soft it is, it’s not precise at all. And it’s not pigmented either, so I end up using a larger amount of product because of that. To do both my brows, and I fill them in pretty lightly, I use about 1/8” of product each time. The nyx one I use less than 1/16” and it’s more pigmented.

I would compare this to the elf one in terms of pigmentation and texture. Except the elf one is like $3. So at this price point I expected it to be way better than something that’s less than half its price.

And after using it a few times, the spoolie end came off when I was trying to take the cap off to use it. The main body of the pencil cracked on that end. So now I have to use a spoolie from another brow pencil, good thing I have one. And this has just been on my desk, not banging around in a makeup bag or anything like that. So definitely don’t get this if you need to take it places it can’t handle it.

This is one of the few times I would return a makeup product, it’s just so egregiously bad.

title: which is very nice, and the scent is subtle
text:
I'm a hair dye junkie, and I've dyed my mohawk almost every color in the crayon box. I heard of Iroiro through an Instagram ad, touting its "all-natural" formula. Since I'm always game to try a new dye brand, I gave it a shot.
Pros:
1. Scent - It says "Yuzu-cranberry" on the packaging, but it smells closer to a fruit punch-bubblegum hybrid. Either way, no plasticy nor ammonia smell, which is very nice, and the scent is subtle.
2. Thinkness - This has a thick opaque cream consistency slightly thicker than Manic Panic or Jerome Russell Punky Colors. No drips nor runniness! This can be used in large-mouth dye bottles, but the bowl&brush method works best.
3. Longevity - My hair is thin and porous, thus dye fades to pastel usually within ten days (even with sulfate-free shampoo and every-other-day washing). Ten days after using this dye, my hair is still a nice royal purple with only slight fading. That surprised me.
4. Conditioning - This dye has coconut oil as a conditioner, so I was concerned it'd make my hair greasy. Nope! Hair came out soft and nicely conditioned with very little limpness.
5. Color Match - The sticker label on the front suggests Iro Violet is a royal purple with a hint of dark blue; I applied the dye to bleached (level 9) hair. The end result looked like the sticker color. So, no color shift here. It will appear slightly different on non-bleached hair, but that is expected.
Neutral:
1. Packaging - The pouch is quite light, plus it does not take up much shelf space when stored upright. So far, the tip does not clog. However, the cap is difficult to open at first, you can't put the dye back in the pouch once it is out (measure carefully!), and the instructions are in a very small print.
2. Heat Requirements - The instructions say that, for best results, heat should be used neat the end of the hair dying phase. I didn't use heat, but left the dye in slightly longer than the instructions. Have a blow dryer handy.
Cons:
1. Staining - This stuff is HIGHLY pigmented, so it will stain anything it touches. Wear gloves!!! Only Splat! stains worse than this dye. You need to cover work surfaces with plastic or else you'll have permanent purple spots everywhere. I even had issues removing staining from my skin, even with rubbing alcohol! It will also permanently stain pillowcases, clothes, towels, and bath mats. Also, I don't recommend rinsing in a tile or porcelain shower or sink because of high stainage; use a laundry sink, steel sink, bucket, or other slop sink area.
2. Rinsing - This stuff takes a bit of time and effort to rinse out, and you still will get dye-tinted water with every hair wash. This dye isn't as notorious to rinse out as Splat!, but it takes longer than Manic Panic or Punky Colors or Pravana.
3. Extra Equipment - This comes with just the dye pouch. You will need your own gloves, dye bowl, dye brush, clips, shower cap, and foils (if you are doing highlights).

Overall, this is an excellent dye for experienced hair dyers, but may be a bit tricky for dye rookies. For an all-natural hair dye, this was surprisingly great! I just bought Iro Pink and I hope it is as good as Iro Purple.

I see a lot of mixed reviews with this product and what I learned over the last year is - all hair is different and what’s amazing for some is not amazing for all. But I would say definitely give it a chance, especially if you have over processed brittle hair you are desperate to save.

title: solid antibacterial, astringent and anti inflammatory qualities
text:
Tamanu oil is extracted from the seeds of the Calophyllum inophyllum tree (a large evergreen native to East Africa and some regions of India and Australia). Long used in certain systems of traditional medicine (including African and Asian traditional medicine), tamanu oil is applied directly to the skin.

This tamanu oil is manufactured by Gio Naturals, and is 100% PURE ORGANIC COLD PRESSED & UNREFINED! The oil comes in a 4 ounce amber colored bottle with treatment pump. It is USDA & ECO Certified Organic. Tamanu oil is renowned for it's skin regenerating and healing properties. Since the oil is proven to have solid antibacterial, astringent and anti inflammatory qualities, you really can't go wrong by adding it to your facial care routine. I make a night time facial serum from Grape Seed Oil, Tamanu Oil, Argan Oil, Rosehip Seed Oil, Lemongrass essential oil, Tea Tree oil and Vitamin E oil. Tamanu oil absorbs quickly, even though the oil is thick (and dark green). It does have a strong nutty / earthy scent but the lemongrass in my recipe kind of masks it, plus you get used to the scent with continued use. It is pretty strong if you use it as a stand alone oil, but again it is highly effective so you need to balance the pros (many) and cons (scent) to decide if it is right for you. Personally it is my go to oil for facial products.

Tamanu oil is touted as a natural remedy for the following conditions: acne, athlete's foot, eczema, psoriasis, and sunburn. Since tamanu oil is said to alleviate pain, the oil is also used topically to relieve the pain caused by conditions like sciatica, shingles, and rheumatism. Some proponents also claim that tamanu oil can help aid in the regeneration of skin. For this reason, tamanu oil is thought to help reduce the appearance of stretch marks and scars. In addition, tamanu oil is said to promote the healing of burns, blisters, cuts, and scrapes. It is a great, all-purpose therapeutic oil. Works well for my sensitive, acne prone skin.

I received this product at a discount. I have provided an honest and unbiased review based on my personal experience with this product. I am not affiliated with the company in any way and my star rating is based on my personal experience and use of the product.

text: I received a gift set in a cute little silver mesh, drawstring bag from Keomi Skincare in exchange for my honest feedback and opinion. Inside the bag were 4 neatly wrapped soap bars. I love that these soaps are 100% vegan, gluten free, cruelty free, sulfate/paraben/petrochemical-free, and contain no artificial fragrances or colors. What more could you ask for in a soap? title: More shaving surface is better.
text:
After using a Braun, Panasonic, and a Norelco (with only single blades) I thought I would try the new design with 3 blades in each of the three heads.

The best feature of the Braun was the ability to lock the on/off switch when traveling.

I bought the Panasonic because of the Linear motor. It also had the fastest motor speed. It doesn't get slower as the battery drains. I think the motor was actually too fast to get a great shave.

My old single blade Norelco (8894XL) is great. The motor seems too slow at first and the shave takes a little longer, but I liked the results and the way it looks and feels. It was time to replace the blades again, so I decided to go for newer technology.

The new one (9160XL) has more shaving surface and is quieter. It doesn't have a digital readout like my last one, but it can work with a cord if I don't re-charge it in time. It still has that great Norelco feel. I don't think it's any faster, but I get a better shave in the same amount of time. I need to re-charge it about once a month. I checked around for price. Amazon won by $30.

title: Easy and Comfortable to Use
text:
I was very hesitant to order this, feeling a little intimidated both by the technology and the potential for pain. Would it be "safe" enough to do laser hair removal on your own?

I was pleasantly surprised that it was both easy to use and virtually painless. You power on the unit, wait for it to indicate that it's ready, place against the surface of your skin until a light indicates proper contact, and then pull the trigger. Depending on the power setting you've selected, you'll feel anything from nothing at all to a brief surge of heat. Even on the strongest setting on denser patches of hair it wasn't unpleasant for me. I didn't notice any redness and didn't require gel or lotion after using, and I have fairly sensitive skin.

Making it even more painless to use, they've included a "cooling" mode you can switch on that will pre-cool the area where it makes contact with your skin, helping to make it more comfortable when operating. This is definitely a plus when working on sensitive areas or denser/darker patches of hair.

It has 5 strength settings and an "automatic" mode. I don't feel comfortable enough yet operating it to try the "automatic" mode, preferring to make sure it's positioned properly and ready before pulling the trigger, but I imagine it could make things go much quicker for large areas like the legs. I might give it a try when I'm a little more practiced.

The unit has two sizes of lenses - one for large areas (built-in) and one for small areas (attachment). The smaller lens is helpful when you need more precision.

It's important to read the instructions and tips before operating and especially important to wear eye protection (tinted glasses) which they've generously included. You should avoid ever looking at the laser during operation, and probably should operate this in privacy unless the people with you are also wearing eye protection. You shouldn't use it anywhere near your eyes to avoid risk of injury - I'd say nothing above the tip of your nose. One safety feature I like is that it won't operate unless the lens is pressed directly against the skin at a right angle, preventing excess laser light from "spilling out".

This isn't suitable for darker skin (including a dark tan) and also won't help with light-colored hair. You should also avoid using it where there might be a dark area on your skin, such as a mole or tattoo.

One thing I can't comment on yet is how effective this is at hair removal. It takes a few months to really notice a difference, and I've only had it for a week. My rating is based solely on ease of use, comfort, functionality, quality of materials and pricing. I'm optimistic on effectiveness, but may come back and edit this review if either it proves disappointing or exceeds my expectations. Assuming it performs as advertised, I feel comfortable recommending this with a 4-star rating.

I've been using this quality product now for several weeks and have not been disappointed by Paloma Skin Therapy. The fine lines around my eyes and mouth area truly do seem less noticeable. Enough so that I'm encouraged to continue to use this cream year round, along with my sunscreen.

Overall, I'm very pleased with the results and am happy to have been given the opportunity to purchase Paloma's skin firming cream during a recent company promotion, in exchange for my fair and unbiased review. title: Norelco is great, this one is just OK
text:
I have used Norelco shavers for many years and prefer them to all other models I have tried. This review comes from much experience with the brand.

This Arcitec design looks fancy and works well, but gets three average stars because it really works no better than the previous non-space-age, less expensive designs. The 1050, 1060, and 1090 all operate the same, they just have a different display: none is better than the other, and don't waste money on the Cleaner accessory. It is fairly comfortable to hold (I prefer the feel of the original model because this is one is smaller), and looks fancy sitting on the counter, but it does not do a better job. It requires cleaning after each use as there is no space for the hairs. I have always cleaned my shavers after each use anyway. Unless you just want the apperance, it is not worth the extra money.

Technically: The triple-blade per round head (each cutter has three spinning blade areas) does not do any better than a double cutting blade. Kind of like a Saturday Night Live skit in the 70's, Jim Belushi said, "Buy a triple bladed razor. For those that will believe anything". Lift-and-cut is a ridiculous concept and a marketing ploy, but Norelco's do a nice job. Norelco went back to more diagonal openings with this model, which is good. Many other newer models have lots of little pin-holes which are worthless, as the hairs have no time to enter a small hole with shaving motion. You would have to set it directly on a hair to cut it. The less pin-holes the better.

Feel: The head design feels better on the neck, and has not caused razor-burn if I do not stretch the skin tight like I need to with the original model. It takes the same time to shave as my older unit, and I get no better results, no faster. It takes the same time to get a smooth shave, and the same persistance in some areas.

Function: It is a little bit easier to shave under the nose, above my mustache, but not a major difference. It is much harder to trim my sideburns with this unit as the heads almost cut my hair on my head above the ears the way it is shaped. Very poorly designed trimmer, so I use my older shaver for that.

Battery: Early, new battery life is good, as with most new battery devices. But, it states to not over-charge. Meaning, you need to be around when recharging to unplug it after it is charged; not good for those that shave and must go to work. The other units would shut off after charging.

Cleaner/Charger: Again, one needs to be around when it is finished to not over-charge. The cleaner is not necessary and a waste of time, money, and chemicals. I use a razor brush from an older unit, brush it out quickly over the wastebasket (one can't blow it out without getting hair dust all over the bathroom, and it can't be shaken into the wastebasket as easily as the older models), and I spray it quickly with Remington Silicone Lubricant (I can only find it at Wal-Mart, which is the only thing I ever go there for, by the way).

Overall: Buy it for looks and keep your old one in the drawer for sideburns. Nicer on the neck.

I would return it, BUT, it was a gift, AND I like the look of it. I know, I know!!

Update 12-29-07
I purchased a Braun 9595 through J&R on Amazon, and it has a 60 day trial return guarantee. This is the first micro-screen razor I have used and it is better in all respects to the Norelco Arcitec except for the fancy styling. It is fast and comfortable, and my face feels razor smooth. I was able to return the Arcitec and am really happy with this Braun 9595 model.
