title: Much easier to use than I thought it was going to be.
text:
At first I wasn't interested in an IPL because I had tried epilators and figured this was going to hurt. Then I read a few things on it and women were saying that it didn't hurt at all, in fact they said it was like blasts of ice cold air. So I decided to give it a try. Right out of the box I was impressed with the quality of this IPL hair remover. It is a solid unit and feels great in your hand! I love the overlay of gold accents contrasted by the neutral white color. The device is very aesthetically pleasing and looks like it could compete easily with the much more expensive ones. I do wish it came with a nice carrying bag or storage bag. But, I really can't criticize it for that because it is so reasonably priced!
Once you understand how to use this device, it is very simple to use. Getting to that place is rather hard because the instructions are not as clear as they could be and the print is super small. I went online and read up on how to use this machine before it ever got here, and I'm really glad that I did because it really helped me. I found out that are things you need to know before you ever order this unit, so you may want to check out some information online beforehand.
I didn't feel like it was an ice blast, you can feel the heat from this device while using it, so you know if you're going to burn yourself. In my opinion you would have to purposely have to ignore the pain to burn yourself because you feel the heat intensify as you leave it in one spot. This one only comes with one size head so it is a little tricky to use around your mouth area. It also came with sunglasses which I did end up using because the flashes were rather bright. They also don't recommend using an electric razor before because it can cause a rash, so they say to shave in the shower before hand.
I am very satisfied with this device and plan on using it about 3 times a week for the first few weeks, dropping down to 2 times a week for the next couple of weeks, and then down to 1 time until I don't notice the hair coming back in. Overall, I really like it more than I thought I would.

title: Soft to the Touch
text:
I am only in my early 40's, Is there a need for me to use this cream? My curiosity has gotten into me ... besides, there's a fine line forming on my forehead so; I decided to give this product a try. I do not usually apply new products on my skin because I am prone to breakouts but, I dare myself to use this anyway.

So, I got the product with in two days after I ordered it. The shipping and handling was great and the #Miracalis product arrived in good condition. The product looks exactly the same as shown in the picture so; I am truly happy and thrilled to finally try it.

The Texture and Smell

The texture is creamy and I like the feel of my skin after the application. It is really soft to the touch and doesn't have that oily feeling or dry skin after every application. I just truly love to use it especially before bedtime. It makes my skin relax because it has that cool sensation. Anyway, after few weeks of using this product, the fine lines on my forehead are still there and I did not see any difference. If it is fading a little bit, I cannot tell if it does.

I will be brutally honest with you that when it comes to the smell, I am not a big fan of this product. I am hoping that in the future, they will add a pleasant fragrance to this anti-aging cream. It has a smell ... not strong though but, not really pleasant to my nose. It would have been perfect for me.

Does my skin look younger, attractive and glowing? That would have been very nice but, I cannot answer that at this time. All I know is that after each application, my skin is truly soft to the touch and I have no breakouts considering I have a sensitive skin.

title: A Very Nice Hydrating, Soothing, Barrier-Repairing Antioxidant Serum
text:
(Ingredients list is at the bottom of this review.)

I have really enjoyed using the Celleanser Vegan Clean Serum, and my skin seems to like it too. I also tried the Celleanser Clean Toner Mist, and the Celleanser Clean Cream. They all worked nicely for my dry, sensitive skin, and they worked nicely together.

This serum is creamy with a viscous gel-like texture that provides an extra layer of hydration, moisture, and antioxidants on the skin. It is applied before moisturizer. The serum is smooth and cooling when applied. It soaks in well, but it does leave a nice layer of extra hydration on the skin. It is not sticky, and it layers perfectly with other products. The scent is sort of lightly herbal or earthy, similar to many Korean skincare brands.

I will say that the finish isn't my go-to. It isn't really dewy or glowy. But I wouldn't call it extremely matte either. Maybe somewhere in-between, but more toward the matte side. I typically like to use dewy, glowy skincare, so I would probably use this product at night for that reason.

The packaging is very nice with a unique-looking, tall, slim plastic bottle with a very functional pump. A little goes a long way, and I imagine this bottle will last me a while. At $19.99 for 30ml / 1.01 fl. oz., it's a pretty good deal. Especially because the ingredient list is nice.

I haven't been using it long enough to speak on the long-term results, but I do like the serum so far, and I will definitely continue to use it. I would recommend this to anyone who likes the ingredient list and wants to give it a try.

title: I liked the idea better than the product
text:
With four cats and a large dog, I am always looking for good grooming tools. I liked the idea of this brush, but the actual product really wasn't all that. First of all, this thing is much larger than any other slicker style brush I have. This is a great feature for my large dog, but it was just ridiculous trying to groom my cats with this large, unyielding wire brush. So, not a good choice for the cats.

Unfortunately, not a good choice for my dog either, as she has a short coat with little to no undercoat and she was really uncomfortable with wires dragging on her skin. She's more of a rubber curry comb type gal, I guess. Besides the size and wire bristle problems, the plastic itself felt a little brittle and cheap and when you add in the mechanics of retractable bristles... I think higher quality material would have been a better choice because that slider for the bristles is very basic. Finally, while I loved the idea of the easy-to-clean retractable bristles, they really aren't necessary and if those wires become crooked or bent it will cause all kinds of problems with the retraction. I've made it decades by just pulling the fur out of my slicker brushes-- it literally takes 2-3 seconds-- and while the thought of retractable bristles is nice, it totally isn't necessary. It's not a practical tool for me and doesn't work for any of my animals due to its size and the wire bristles. It also doesn't seem terribly well-made nor is it made of high-quality materials, and for the price it should be.

title: The better ones, Soapwalla (my previous favorite)
text:
Over the past year and a half, I've been searching for a non-commercial deodorant that would work for me. Due to formulation changes over the past 10-15 years, it has gotten to a point where I can only use around 3 different commercial deodorants that do not cause chemical burns to my pits with long use. I've used many other popular and not so popular alternatives and haven't found that "perfect" product yet. The better ones, Soapwalla (my previous favorite), Piper Kai, and Primal Pit Paste, all cause serious irritation after 2-4 weeks and I discovered that baking soda and some essential oils cause serious irritation and eventually makes my pits raw which causes my skin to peel away. I've recently retried some Soapwalla I had for a pinch and it actually caused my pits to severely break out only one day (which surprised me). Evidently, my sensitivity to baking soda has increased over the past year.
I've used this Fat and The Moon deodorant for 2.5 weeks now and am very pleased with it. It only causes some minor bumps under my pits which is really good for me since these aren't getting worse. This is a deodorant, not an antiperspirant, so I do sweat a lot. However, I've noticed that even after exercise I'm not very stinky. With most of the other deodorants I've used, workout stank is always a problem. A couple have actually intensified the stank by adding their own. Not so here.
The only cons I have with this product so far are that I do notice it can stain some shirts with oil discoloration, but so far have been treatable. (I've used products that have stained shirts MUCH worse to where it wasn't treatable.) The other con I have about this is the smell. I'm a guy and I'm okay with this scent, but sometimes it's a bit too "earthy" smelling for me. I might even go for an unscented version of this if that is possible.

But even with the cons, I do like this product and I'm going to reorder this deodorant in the full 2 ounce size.

title: Doesn't fade but bleach is rough
text:
I have been using bright hair colors for about 18 years. In the past I used Manic Panic and it faded - this stuff does NOT fade very quickly at all! I dyed my hair purple in October 2011 and it was still there nine months later! I bleached it and it STILL stayed, except it turned pink. This color will show through even if you dye over it, so be sure you want that color!!

I currently have white hair with blue and pink on the top. The pink is still vibrant and the blue is very dark.

Two words of caution:
The bleach is rough. Really really rough. Not too bad on the hair but very bad on the skin. It makes my whole head burn. Other bleach kits do not do this and I do not have sensitive skin. It does not, however, seem to do damage to the skin. No redness or anything. It just hurts till you wash it off.

The second thing is that you will think this is all washing out. For the first five or six washes, you'll see a LOT of color in the sink. If part of your hair is still white or natural color, protect it the first few washes - coat all the hair except the colored portions by rubbing in conditioner while the hair is dry. That way, when you wash, you won't get the color residue on the other hair.

I give this product four stars simply because of the bleach - the color itself is great. I have used purple, blue, and pink.

title: Made in USA. Smells fresh and energizing, nice lather, rinses clean
text:
Three pack of individually boxed hard soap bars that smell wonderful and fresh. Quite an uplifting aroma. thyme, rosemary, sage, lemongrass..mmm. Natural chlorophyll and organic cloves create a deep green color. The soap has lather, soft clean feel. I use this as a hand soap, but it can be used all over anytime- very nice soap that inspired me to see what else they have to offer. Not knowing anything about Elsha, I learned that it is a USA company that was established in 1935 offering cologne products, and eventually perfume and soaps. These soaps are handmade in USA. Although the eagle on a flag shield screams, "'merica!", the product listing would do well to say this (their other listings do). The box that the soaps come in are gray with an Elsha sticker on it. No information as to what it is, what is in it, where it is is from, etc. If there was at least an insert of information I would feel better about buying this as a gift. The website had produced just enough information to make me feel better about trying this soap, otherwise I had no idea what was in it or where it originated. That being said, it is a good soap and I would consider it again.

title: Same Results as Dunking in a Bowl of Water
text: If you're a dog owner, its practically guaranteed at some point, you will have to deal with your dog having dirty, muddy paws. Happens often with our bichon Mac. (Naturally, it recently happened right after I cleaned and mopped the house! lol)  I ordered the Mr. Ros automatic cleaner for small/medium dogs. Its very sturdy and durable, not at all flimsy.  Its roughly 8"tall  and has a removable mat with silicone bristles in the interior which is easily removable for cleaning purposes.  The bristles are very soft and not at all hard or sharp. It arrived already charged. A USB cord is included. To operate, simply add water to the washer-(2-3 cups per instructions) Liquid soap may be added as well. (I didn't use soap) Turn the washer on-it does make noise though its  not terribly loud at all-and place the dog's paw in the washer for 1-2 minutes. Dry each paw with a towel after cleaning. Mac wasn't thrilled throughout the cleaning process but he also wasn't really scared by it. My husband started to pour out the dirty water before I could stop him so you won't see much,  but you can see in my photo the water is discolored a bit following the cleaning.  If a wet towel isn't enough to clean Mac's muddy/dirty paws, my regular cleaning method is to put some lukewarm water in a small bowl , dunk each paw one at a time and use my hand to remove the dirt from his fur while submerged. Quite honestly, I really don't see much of a difference between that cleaning method and the Dr. Ros paw washer. Perhaps results vary depending on the breed of dog but for our bichon, I really don't see a  difference.

Just make sure that you get the original and not a cheap imitation. I've ordered a dozen of them, although each one will easily last you for months with regular / daily use. Gave a couple to my mum and sis. Not too harsh, not too soft, just right. It does a great job exfoliating the surface dead skin cells away; the scrub also helps with (blood) circulation, leaving at the end of your wash the largest body organ (your skin!) feeling really clean and rejuvenated! Makes ample of foam with a small amount of soap on it and maintains it well throughout your wash. A couple of little tips: Wet thoroughly the scrubber before applying soap on it (use soap sparingly on it, a little amount goes a long way with this scrubber as I've happily discovered - you save on soap too!) After you apply soap on the scrubber, shut your shower off during the scrubbing process, otherwise the running water can and will readily and easily wash the foaming soap away from the scrubber. You can see a difference in the design of the heads. The picture on the right are my old lift and cut heads with the new HQ8 blades installed inside them from this HQ8 package. I have a deep clawfoot soaking tub, and tend to soak for 45 minutes or so (adding more hot water now and then as I go along). For that I put a cup and half or so of the salts in, and it ends up being a wonderful bath! Put on some mellow music, burn a little incense alongside, and you'll be in heaven.

Skin becomes super soft and hydrated, not in the least bit 'perfumey', and my entire body/mind/spirit is so relaxed after. It's absolutely therapeutic!

It's probably more expensive than most, but very high quality, and worth not having chemical perfumes and additives. If you buy the larger 8lb bags, a few at a time, the cost approaches what most other products might cost and that's a very fair bargain for what you get.

title: Good.  However, probably not for oily skin
text:
This foundation has potential IF you use a good primer with it. I have combination skin and, like many foundations, this can settle into pores and creases. Some foundations are better than others in terms of this tendency, and I'd say this one is about "par for the course" with regard to settling in pores and creases. Primer will help.

This does seem to have a lot of moisture in it (as I've found with many foundations that have "satin" in the title). For me, I feel a bit dewy and not quite clean enough in this -- especially when I look in my 10X magnification mirror.

However, I'd venture to guess that people with dry skin might actually appreciate this. Whereas people with oil prone skin and/or visible pores -- will NOT appreciate this so much.

I ordered the Fair color and I'm an NC20 or NC25. The color is great (not orange and not pink). Nice neutral color. It was just slightly lighter than my natural skin color and looked great with a light dusting of bronzer / blush. I always prefer to err lighter than my natural color than to go to darker, and end up looking like and orange pumpkin.

NOTE >>>Be sure to shake this well before each use<<< I noticed if I don't shake this, the first spray is mostly moisture and has a shiny greasy effect. Product applies much better if it is well shaken first. This should be in bold print on the front of the can.

I spray this into a little eyelash tray (or back of hand, or where ever) and dab my make-up brush into it. Then, apply to face.

Its a good foundation. However, getting up into this price point, I felt some of the above minor gripes warranted removing a star.

title: Good and bad - But I have notes to increase success.
text:
I applied this to my 5 year olds blonde hair. I did not want to spend a future at a salon because.... she is five!
She DOES love the end result but I will say, if you want a successful process I have several important notes.
1. I can NOT speak to the bleach because we did NOT use it. I hear BAD things about it.... so, read other reviews if applicable.
2. Product is messy! That said; count on the NEED for 2 person application. Do NOT attempt to self apply this product. Will absolutely regret it and ruin your home and clothes.
3. Count on purchasing extra items AND plan for 3 hours from prep start to finish. I will explain why.
EXTRA ITEMS: This product will ABSOLUTELY stain hand, face and scalp. Purchase: extra gloves, vaseline, and hair dye removal!
GLOVES: It only comes with one crappy pair of gloves. For best result, swing by Sally's beauty and buy SEVERAL good pairs of gloves. OR buy some of those thick bathroom cleaning gloves that come to your elbows. this way you can use them and take them off and on easily to both apply AND rinse hair.
VASELINE: COMPLETELY coat ears, forehead, neck, etc with a THICK coat of vaseline to avoid staining
DYE REMOVAL: Swing by sally's and buy a bottle of hair dye remover BEFORE you start. This will get on skin and you will NOT get it off otherwise.
EXTRA TIME TO APPLY: I have applied this product in 4 different colors to both my own hair and others hair. I have NEVER gotten good coverage without having to apply it TWICE. (including this application. pictures attached are product of applying BOTH colors twice for an hour each time) For the vibrant color you will want, count on applying, waiting an hour to rinse. Blow dry and reapply for ANOTHER hour. Do not think you will "quickly" apply this product like a box of normal 20 minute color. You will be disappointed.

Overall, as I said, my daughter is happy with the turn out and I saved money so in my case, it worked out.
However, I have experience with this product so it was successful based on ALL the above notes.
Also, I DID experience severe staining to her scalp and it will NOT come off so far even with the hair dye remover. I did not apply it close to scalp but she is young and her hair is so thin, it bleed right through and left big nasty looking spots all over her little head. That said, I ONLY applied this to the underneath of her hair as an ombre look... so I can keep working on getting it off in the next few days.
I would be much more upset if I had this all over her head.

title: 192 lash clusters, 12mm-18mm
text:
The Bodermincer lash clusters, mix 12mm-18mm with 4 rows of each size were not my favorite. First off, the case that they arrived in was quite large, almost the size of a small tablet with 2 latches that are supposed to lock so the case doesn’t come open but neither works. The adhesive strip that the clusters are attached to, I had one of the clusters rip apart when trying to remove it from the adhesive strip with eyelash tweezers (grabbed by band like always). The lash clusters are also very top heavy as you can see from my side shot above picture where the lash drifted out of place after being glued (you need to supply your own glue, not included). I held each cluster in place with lash tweezers until glue was set because I was having trouble keeping them where I wanted them. The lash clusters themselves are more of a U shape and very thick at the band with a slight flair going up/out. They do have a slightly variegated length to them but it’s not super noticeable and the curl on them was more of a C than a D. Clusters are soft but the band holding them together is sharp and slightly uncomfortable when wearing (I always glue lash clusters underneath eyelid, I think it blends better).

When removing the lashes at the end of the day most of the clusters either fell apart of several individual lashes came off the bands. I would not recommend this particular set of lash clusters.

title: My journey of finding my love in wooden brushes
text:
Before I came across this type of brush, I was using those typical plastic brushes that you would buy at the store--that was at least 3 years ago, if not, more than that. Eventually, I got tired of plastic brushes because of the way it pulls, the static that it creates, and worst of all, the way it made my hair smell. I can't stress this enough, no matter how nice smelling my shampoo is, my hair would smell unpleasant (I cannot describe), almost like plastic after it dried. And so, I made my first step to healthier hair by changing brushes; I discovered about the boar bristle brush, and bought one that I found at the store. It was fine, it made my hair soft, but was it life changing? Kind of, but I grew out of it. I liked how it made my hair feel, especially at the ends, however I could not comb from root to end, because my hair type is thick and I was not feeling the scalp massage. I even thought about saving my money for a Mason Pearson, and had it on my wishlist for a while. I found an affordable boar bristle brush, but I never bought it yet, as it sits in the wishlist.
Another problem I had with my hair is that it is unmanageable. Everytime I got out of the shower, I needed to brush my hair, no matter how unhealthy it is, I needed to. Otherwise, my hair is all tangled and I will be irritable (just kidding). Well, brushes do no justice, so I went with a detangler, I bought one at the store (once again) for about a couple dollars, and I have used it for a while. You could say, I was trying to be gentle to my hair, by starting at the ends and work my way up. For now, it was the only way to keep my hair at bay, and I still use the boar bristle brush to fix my hair a little.

Until recently, I succumbed to realizing how important hair is, and so I watched videos and videos of hair routines, until I came across holistichabit's video about her hair routine/how to get long healthy hair naturally. I kind of regretted now, not watching it when I first found her channel, but now I am obsessed about her ways of maintaining healthy hair. When she mentioned about using a wooden brush, I was almost confused, but was curious as how it benefitted her hair. Though the brushes she recommends were expensive, she did hint that Europeans make the best brushes. That is when I began my hunt for a reasonable priced, yet high quality and came across this aethethically pleasing brush. Since it was made in Germany, I had to put it at my highest priority; a few days later, I couldn't contain my impulses and just bought this brush.

TL;DR
At first use, I'm totally impressed with how it distributed my oils, and I really enjoyed that scalp massage: it's amazing. I will say, that you do not need to apply a lot of pressure to your scalp, as it massage just effectively. I decided that I should wait until I shower after, that I began using. Today came around, and first use on wet hair, I was literally blown away! I was just in awe at how soft it made my hair, and I had been waiting for this moment for my scalp massage. I LOVE EVERY SINGLE MOMENT OF THE SCALP MASSAGE! A few hours later, and my hair feels so soft, it's almost heavenly. My hair strands and ends feel evenly distributed with oil, however, I'm not sure if the back of my head feels greasy and chunky because I use a sulfate-free shampoo, and it happens almost every time. Another thing to add, my hair smells of oak/maple wood; maybe I'm just weird but I do not mind it, in fact I appreciate the smell. I cannot say if this is durable, but it is real wood, so it is important to keep the brush handle part as dry as possible. If it is wet, you can wipe it with a towel.
Overall, I am so in love with this brush and this is the only brush I will use. I know I paid less than $20, but the quality of this brush makes me want to treat it with care. The brush looks so simple and minimalist, that it just adds a touch of simplicity in your space.
I will add pictures soon; if not, maybe this week.

This is my honest and first impression of this product. I know it's pretty long, but I am just so in love, that I had to write one! I hope this helps and I recommend this product to first time users who are looking a brush that is high quality. If anything, just buy this brush already, you will love it to pieces like I did. I might make an update on this product in a few weeks, stay tuned!

Update; 5/14/20:

I still use this product, and over the years, it has aged naturally, to which it developed "rings" or natural word markings. It still holds up very well, because I am careful about the sensitivity of water to wood. However, as lazy as I am, I do not clean the bristles of my brush often, so it has developed some dirt and smell, from my hair. Evermore, I am grateful that I discovered this product, and will keep using it until it reaches its mileage. :)

About five months ago, I was offered a free Zakora Head Shaver for review via the Amazon Vine Program, and I accepted.

title: Excellent quality rose quartz massage roller. White/very pale pink, with hints of pink.
text:
This is a typical rose quartz massage roller, but it's crafted with quality rose quartz and excellent manufacture. The presentation lifts it's value as a gifting option. While there is a natural variation of the rose quartz, and there's no way to tell if you'll get the same rose quartz colors that I got, I love the almost white/very pale pink color, with hints and shades of light pink interspersed faintly in the roller. The color is the first thing you notice about massage rollers, and this is an eye catcher.
This product is not perfect, though. The handle seems to be composed of a resin/plastic. It is very light weight. Use of the resin/plastic magnifies the imbalance of the product. The color matches the stone rollers, though. If the handle was also rose quartz, this would be at least a 5 star product.
The rollers have the plastic grommets that are found on properly designed/manufactured massage rollers. It serves to protect the stone and metal arm/axle from rubbing against each other. It also acts like a bearing, enabling a smoother rolling motion. The massage rollers without these grommets i place are sub par products. Thankfully, this feature is mentioned in the product details, and indeed is found on each of the connecting points.
Overall, the massage roller displays quality aspects and is visually impressive. Except for the resin/plastic handle, it's a fantastic product. For me, the balance is an important element. But, when I encounter a beautifully constructed tool, a structural miscue become more pronounced. Still, it's amongst the premium level of this product genre. As such, it merits a 4.75 - 5 star rating, with a very high level recommendation.

title: I.love.my.epilator
text:
So, I HATED shaving my legs and did not have the bank account/ patience that professional waxing requires. It was this burning hatred of hair and relative certainty that laser hair removal is nowhere in my immediate future that motivated me to look into epilation. Also I am kind of addicted to self-tanning and shaving and waxing totally ruins a great faux tan.

I bought this epilator.

After using it on my arms and thighs for about a week with minimal discomfort, I downed a couple shots of vodka and began to epilate my calves.OUCH.Even after hanging out in a steamy shower for a half hour AND using it IN the shower, this was SUPER painful. But I kept going...

The couple days of doing my calves was intense (cursing, screaming, alarming my husband with my obsessive mission to rip the hair out of my legs), and there's no way I could get everything in one sitting since I have zero tolerance for pain. Anyhow I am so glad that I didn't stop!!!!

10 months later, I epilate once per week for about 15 minutes while watching tv (I no longer need to use the "wet" mode unless I wait 2 weeks between uses, more hair=more pain). It would have been nice if someone had given me one of these when I was like 15...thinking about all the money&time I have wasted on shaving is depressing.

Pros:

*Price- this is a great deal for all the money and time you will save
*Wet/Dry function- if you don't handle pain well, this is the ONLY thing that will get you through the early days
*Rechargable- No cords, no batteries.
*Multifunction- you can use it as a shaver or trimmer if you're so inclined
*Regrowth is not scary- your hair will be finer and tapered at the end, not angry and spikey like shaved hair

Cons:

*If you are new to epilation, it's going to hurt (but only the first couple of times)
*Grip-In the shower I've dropped it before because the grip isn't rubberized
*It's difficult to be 100% smooth(but you won't care because the remaining hairs are so fine)

I've read people complain about the battery...I plug mine in for an hour every couple of uses and it's fine. Also ingrown hairs seems to be a recurring theme...this hasn't been an issue for me, and if you exfoliate regularly you should be fine.

Of course I totally recommend this epilator to all my friends and family. I think it's great for beginners or even for the more experienced epilator-user who doesn't wish to be stuck next to an outlet.

title: Tiny plastic covers on the bristles make it more comfortable for some cats
text:
We have three cats with three very different coats. The black cat's coat is sleek, shiny, and seems to have fine little hairs. He barely sheds, and his hairs are short. He loves being brushed with just about any brush, for the interaction, the petting/grooming connection and the scratching action. However, he doesn't really need to be brushed.
Our medium-to-long haired snowshoe Siamese seems to have sensitive skin; she Hates being brushed near her achy back hips, and will complain and whip around to smack at you if you brush her very hard at all. However, she sheds a TON, and needs to be brushed almost every day, so she doesn't get clumps by her arthritic haunches (she actually gets dandruff flakes that her hair clumps around and knots up). She is at least 14 years old (we're not exactly sure), and just can't reach to groom her back end well, any longer. She loves being brushed around her head and neck though, even with our old "scratchier" long-tined brush. You can fill that brush 2-3 times easily, brushing her for just a few minutes, every day. This one, because of the tiny soft covers on the ends of the tines, doesn't seem to dig at her as much, and you don't have to brush her nearly as gently - meaning that you get far more of the clumps out when they are small and just beginning to build.
Our orange cat has extremely soft, short-to-medium hair, and you hardly notice that she sheds much. But when you brush her with the longer-tined, flexible but sharper-ended bristles of our old brush, you fill up the brush surprisingly quickly, and she lets you brush all over. So, she may be the only one that we continue to use the old brush on.
Our old brush sort of pulls the bristles into it, towards the handle, when you push the button on the back of it, to clean it off. The bristles disappear inside the brush, and you can peel the hair off like a little blanket and throw it away.
With this new brush, it is more like the flat base with holes around the bristle seats, comes forward, to the end of the bristles; when you push the button on the back, it pushes that base away from the handle. This may end up bending the bristles less, and keeping the brush usable longer. But it also doesn't compact the hair and make it just "peel off" in one fell swoop. It is more likely that you will leave some hair behind on the brush with this one. It is Worth the trade-off of it being slightly less easy to clean well, because our older, sensitive cat likes it soooo much better, and she is the one who really needs to be brushed the most. This brush is lighter, and feels less substantial than our old brush. Again, we will keep the old brush for the kitten. But this new one is perfect for Sagwa (the old cat), and I am very glad we tried it. If it does crack or bristles break off, because it seems less sturdy, I would buy another one just to keep her happy.

title: It actually does something.
text:
So, essences have always been a bit of a mystery to me (and, honestly, seemed like hokum) but my curiosity always led me back to research them. I've even bought them over the years and abandoned them because I just didn't know how to use them or if they were working. (And these are other best sellers with high price tags.) I finally revisited essences, caved in, and bought this super seller just to see if there was a fuss to be made over it. There is.

The very first time I applied it, I had a minor healing blemish on my cheekbone and it tingled at that spot. (Cool, it's not just water, lol.) I applied all my other stuff and knew it at least imparted moisture - my skin felt supple and hydrated. I noticed a change after just about a week using this - my skin was more even, a bit smoother (I have roughness on my cheeks that never seems to go away, no matter what), and dewy. I went camping for a few days - the dirty kind - and, after neglecting it, my skin needed help. I noticed everything bounced back much faster than it ordinarily would. I typically get a breakout after a trip like that but my skin stayed clear, it was just rough and sallow. Once home and finished with my usual routine, everything was back to normal and radiant again.

I know there are conflicting thoughts on how best to apply it; I won't put it on a cotton pad as I feel that would just waste too much product. (I first used this on May 6th and the picture is from 3 days ago - that's ALL I've used in about a month.) Right now I'm using one little drip of product for my whole face and neck; I just pour it in my hand, pat my hands together, and apply to a slightly damp face after toner. I must be experiencing what people are describing as a "water burst," because I put that tiny amount on my face and it's like I'm splashing water from a running faucet, that's the only way I can think to describe it; like the amount of wetness I'm getting exceeds the amount of product I used. I'm going to put some in a spray bottle with a fine-mist nozzle and use it that way, which is also how I'm going to travel with it. (Though, I've traveled with this large bottle and it's never leaked - and it lays on its side in my bag.)

For the price and the small amount I use, I will absolutely be repurchasing this.
(For reference, my once very-oily skin became dry then combo over this last winter, and now it's back to moderately oily, so it runs the gamut. I also have some unevenness, roughness on my cheeks, and dullness - all of which are improving everyday, and even my one or two monthly hormonal blemishes have been minimal and, if I get any small breakout, it's gone in a day or two and never fully forms to begin with.)

I have sensitive skin due to eczema, and I have tried so many body washes making sure they do not contain sodium laureth sulfate (this is ingredient is a trigger for a flare up). But after trying this cleanser my flare ups have minimized considerably.

This is what I do to minimize flare ups:
1) use unscented laundry detergent for sensitive skin. Dropps or Tide are both excellent brands.
2) DO NOT use fabric softners or dryer sheets, they are toxic for our skin.
3) use 1/3 cup baking soda as fabric softener
4) use unscented body wash and lotions and make sure they do not contain SLS (Sodium Laureth sulfate)
5) avoid tight fitting clothing whenever possible, especially when sleeping.

title: Works well, easy to use, one drawback is tricky to take apart and put back together for cleaning
text:
We purchased Pet Electric Hair Clipper: professional tools for your love pets/grooming clipper, from Caleegi.

Everything appears to be quite well made, of sturdy construction. The scissors and nail trimmers came out of the box sharp, and have a good weight to them. The nail trimmers have a good locking mechanism, metal, not plastic; I think it will last. The set comes with a convenient little storage pouch, which I hadn't noticed on the item description specs list. I like the colors of the pouch. They're cute. The pouch easily fits everything in the kit, except the brush. You can make the brush fit, but I dont think you can make the brush and electric clippers fit. I couldn't. The electric clippers come with a usb powered charger cord, but not a charger block. This is not a standard charger. If you lose this charge cord, you may be hard pressed to find a replacement.

The brush is of good construction, and the ergonomic handle grip is a joy to hold. For real, it just feels good in your hand. I like the push button hair dislodger for easy brush cleaning. Our dog is fairly short haired, straight and wirey, and our cat is fluffy but on the short side of medium length hair. It took very little hair off them, and I haven't found a product better than the Furminator for brushing them. But I've had and worked with longer haired dogs, and for a Great Pyrenees, Burnese Mountain Dog, or Saint Bernard, I think this would be the perfect brush.

The nail file worked great. The comb I intend to keep for myself- it's perfect for my wiry, sometimes wavy, sometimes curly, always disobedient hair.

The electric clipper charged fairly quickly, enough that I could take it for a test spin about 15-20 minutes after plugging it in. I love the electronic digital display, showing how far along in its charging it is, and the RPMs of the clipper blades. I love that it came with a little bottle of lubricant solution for the blades (none of my personal trimmers ever have). The little obligatory cleaning brush to sweep between the blades looks much the same that any electric trimmer does, but I found it shed a wire or two with every pass throughthe blades, which my personal trimmer brushes do not.

I tried the electric clippers out on myself first. I was a little bummed that the nearly universal gaurds that come with clippers designed for people did not fit. The clippers are much more quiet then most clippers, which is good for not startling pets. I used the clippers with the guard on the sides of my head and with no gaurd to shave my face. It went easily through my hair, had no trouble, and gave me a close, even shave. And I went a little rough to see if there was any danger of maybe cutting a squirming or struggling pet, and it seems very safe.

The clipper blades came off pretty easy for cleaning, but were kind of tricky to put back on, and in trying to do so, I hit at a funny angle and the entire clipper assembly fell apart in to 4 pieces. That was annoying, but after messing around with it for about a half hour, I was able to put it back together, and it still worked fine. I would be hesitant to take it apart for cleaning again, though I'm sure I will. Despite this one design flaw, I still think overall this is a pretty quality product.

I was a little skeptical about purchasing an acrylic stamping plate, as all my many others are the usual metal, and I knew nothing at all about plates made from anything else. Moreover, it meant buying a non-acetone polish remover, as acetone (which is used to clean metal plates) is the kiss of death for acrylics. But it wasn’t expensive, so I went ahead and bought a bottle, in preparation for the arrival of this plate. This plate had so many simple designs that I wanted, but didn’t have, like a basic chevron, diagonal lines, vertical and horizontal lines, and gradient dots. I loved the diminutive leopard print, since many of those designs are too big for my tiny nails. And a complete upper case and lower case alphabet?? Count me in!

The plate arrived just a few days before Christmas, so when I got it, I stashed it away, intending to play with it later. Later came today, and I’m in love! I tried out several stamping polishes with it, and most all of the designs. Even the polishes that have given me trouble in the past on metal plates picked up perfectly! The designs are all sharp and distinct. I believe that is due to the depth at which the designs are etched. They are nice and generous, meaning that even the smallest and finest of lines and features come out bold and beautiful.

Clean up is truly a breeze using the non-acetone remover on a cotton ball. And there is no chilling effect from acetone, which tends to dry out your stamping polish on the plate faster.

Often, trying something outside of the ordinary can yield stellar results. This is one such case. This plate is so good that I’m currently checking out all the other H la Cosedora plates here on Amazon. And of course, I’m going to pick up another bottle of non-acetone remover!

title: Good dry shave
text:
After about 3 years this razor is still giving consistently good and close shaves and the battery is still just as good as the day I got it. I switched to electric razors a few years ago when my face couldn't handle blades anymore. I thought I'd have to sacrifice a close shave in order to get a healthier face but this hasn't been the case with this shaver. The shave is almost as close as a blade and I have absolutely no irritation. I upgraded to one of the speed XL models and this one is slightly slower, but not so bad.

There are only 2 downsides: It takes 8 hours to charge and you can't use it corded. This is not that big of a deal though since you'll still have plenty of time to finish when the low battery indicator goes off.

At this point I couldn't recommend this shaver if you have already used a rotary and know you like them and for a very simple reason: it is obsolete and buying replacement heads is almost as much as a new razor. However, if you are looking for a traveling razor or want to give rotaries a shot then this might be the right choice. A few years ago I would have highly recommended it.

title: Best value in $/oz for a true believer
text:
I bought this giant pack after trying the 16oz tea tree oil cleansing conditioner and did some crazy calculation on the total/average cost of different ways of purchasing this really expensive hair cleansing product from multiple sources.

Obviously, you can tell I'm quite convinced by this product, or else I wouldn't invest so much work/resources into getting it. Because these things take a while to use, I will be updating my review as I finish each flavor included in this set. I will not be using the Sweet Almond Mint, which is too oily for me and I'm sure you can find plenty of review on other package sizes.

* Overall Impression *

1. Great reduction in hair loss
2. Great increase in manageability
3. Quite expensive for regular use

A lot of people say "this product changed my life!" I don't want to exaggerate my excitement. I think to be very fair this product made me discover something I never experienced with other commercial shampoos - "near zero hair loss after wash".

I was a heavy shedder and I was used to losing a lot of hair everyday. With this product, I hardly lose any piece of hair at all during the day, with everything else being the same as my old-shampoo days. I have to say I don't know how it will compare to shampoo during hair wash with an equal comparison (i.e. same washing technique). WEN requires you to comb your hair during washing, which causes hair to shed when I wash my hair. I did not comb my hair while I was using shampoos so I didn't know if combing in wash would be the same. All else being the same, I lose about the same amount of hair during washing using shampoo or WEN. The no hair loss during the day is amazing though. I might have been allergic to the commercial shampoos and never knew it. My hair now feels significantly thicker when putting into a pony tail.

Another great discovery is that WEN makes my hair very smooth, light but not necessarily shiny. It dries faster after wash. It also feels easier to manage - my hair now stays in the right shape - this is especially true after the 24 hours. My hair would have started to feel lumpy and oily if I had used shampoo, but WEN keeps my scalp evenly moist a little longer. With these two improvements, I no longer use styling products or a blow dryer.

* Impression on the Flavors I Have Tried *

Tea Tree 5 of 5
Fig 5 of 5
Cucumber Aloe 3 of 5

Very short, I would recommend people with oily/combination skin type stay away from the Cucumber Aloe. Somehow it feels more water-based I had to use more to wash each time. At the same time, even though I make sure to wash it off completely, my scalp/hair started to feel oily sooner than when I use tea tree and fig versions. Both Tea Tree and Fig are great for oily/combination type. They make my hair feel clean and refreshed. Fig makes my hair feels extra smooth and it is the richest/densest of the three.

* How Long Does a 32oz Bottle Last? *

When the WEN TV infomercial says the 12oz starter version is a "30-day" supply, you need to understand that it is for people with very short, thin, or little hair. For someone like me with long, very thick Asian hair going to mid back, the 16oz tea tree bottle survived barely one month with washing at least every other day.

Two other things to keep in mind:
The 32oz pump holds more than a 16oz pump, but less than twice the amount.
Each flavor varies in its moisture strength. As mentioned earlier, I had to use more Cucumber Aloe to achieve the same effect I can do with Tea Tree and Fig.

I made a chart documenting my process of finishing up the 32oz Cucumber Aloe bottle. In total there were about 250 pumps, which lasted me 50 days with 30 washes, average 8 pumps per wash.

* How Much Should You Use For Each Wash? *

I definitely recommend strictly following the WEN instructions when you begin. That is, use the large amount as instructed by WEN, follow the steps to rinse, massage, comb, leave in, rinse off. This will help you see how the proper use can really change your hair as they've claimed. However, this is an expensive product so we all want to use it efficiently. Once you have formed the proper washing habit, start reducing the pump number little by little until you find your optimal dose. I found my optimal to be about 1/2 of the recommended amount for my hair length. Given the amount of hair I have, I'm sure many people can save more once you've started using it.

On average I use:
Tea Tree 16oz - 15 pumps per wash (haven't started the 32oz bottle yet)
Cucumber Aloe 32oz - 8-9 pumps per wash
Fig 32oz - 7 pumps per wash

title: Versache meets the "modern" market...
text:
As the product is marketed for, it should only be used for casual affairs seeing as how while it is complex enough for formal affairs, it smells too much like something you'd wear with jeans as opposed to a suit and tie.

As previously mentioned this product is slightly complex featuring sharp characteristics that designer brands typically have, as opposed to more mellow notes commonly thought to be the key success behind marketing casual-use perfumes. In that regard I think Versache lives up to its name with this product: they manage to deliver something highly creative, if not long lasting.

It's extremely hard to define what the fragrance notes for this product are, I can only say that it is most certainly not velvety (not remotely), or musky as the designer would indicate. Instead it is extremely citrus and acidy... but this isn't to say it is too "sharp" for comfort.

So wait, absolutely no "velvet" characteristic like the designer noted? Well the mellow aspect comes with the highly distinctive scent of a "jeans" which is released over time as you wear, it making the fragrance a bit more mellow and yet still remain within the world of "distinctive" (and narrowly escaping being called "pungent" - a term I used to describe L'eau d'Issey by Issey Miyake, a characteristic I find extremely negative). Being highly distinctive and sharp from the get-go, I'd say that this product is pretty easy to forget about a few weeks after using it... seeing as how there are fans of such heavily distinctive fragrances (who obviously do not mind a sharp nose at first), this product should certainly be sampled by such individuals.

I like this product quite a bit so I'm going to give it a 4, hopefully encouraging others to try it. However as I previously noted it is easy to forget and I must admit that I do not wear it as frequently as I used to (I'd give it a 3 for a personal opinion if I could and a 4 for overall product quality and general appeal).

title: 3 Pack (White/Slate/Lake blue) of the Niutop Watchband Style Band for Fitbit One
text:
This review is for the 3 Pack (White/Slate/Lake blue) of the Niutop Watchband Style Band for Fitbit One. I received a promotional discount on this item in exchange for providing a review. I have been using this item daily for a little over a month and wanted to share my experience.

First Impressions
* The items were exactly as pictured, the colors really bright and crisp.
* It took some work getting the FitBit One in and out of the band. It gets a little easier the more you use it. I do not view this as a problem as I know its not going to fall out.
* Was not easy to insert the fasteners on the one end of the band to the connectors on the other. This is still and issue, but again, I do not view this as a negative as I can trust that it will remain secure, but it can be a pain, easier with help, to fasten it.

Observations from wearing.
* The FitBit One was very secure in the band, never worried nor experienced it falling out, coming loose, etc.
* Once fastened securely the band never unsnapped by accident.
* After the first week or so I started to get a rash on my wrist. I switched it to the other wrist and experienced the same thing. I took off the band, removed the FitBit, then washed the band in soap and water. I wore it for several weeks after this, on the same wrist, and did not experience any issues.
* I was used to clipping my FitBit to my pocket or shirt, and do not normally wear a watch. I did not have any problem wearing it, was very comfortable and often forgot I even had it on. It did take some getting used to, remember to remove for a shower, and not getting it overly wet while washing my hands, but I got used to it very quickly.
* I did notice a few occasions that if I made exaggerated arm movements it would trigger as steps on my FitBit one.

Overall
I would recommend this for anyone looking for a watchband style carry for their FitBit. I use mine daily and I not even considered going back to clip style carry. I do recommend that when you first receive it that you wash it with soap and water, rinse and let dry before using. You will never need to worry about the FitBit becoming unsecured from the band.

title: Isopropyl-based hand sanitizer that meets both CDC & WHO guidelines
text:
Much of the hand sanitizer we have been using is ETHYL alcohol (ethanol) based. THIS sanitizer is ISOPROPYL alcohol based. Note that historically most hand sanitizer has been based on isopropyl alcohol whereas ethanol has been used in things like alcohol that you drink of as a gasoline additive for oxygenated fuels (for environmental purposes) as well as other purposes. Isopropyl has been used in hand sanitizer and "rubbing alcohol" among other things. Both are now approved for use in hand sanitizer. Ethynol-based sanitzers are becoming much more common due to high demand and supply constraints on Isopropyl-based sanitizers.

The interesting thing is that the CDC and WHO have different guidelines for hand sanitizer effectiveness for these two types of alcohol:
CDC: Ethyl - at least 60%, Isopropyl - at least 70%
WHO: Ethyl - at least 80%, Isopropyl - at least 75%
You can see that it is interesting that the CDC recommends higher concentrations of Isopropyl whereas WHO recommends higher concentrations of Ethyl. Curious. Rather than dig into too many details on the difference, the easiest thing is to find a way to meet both...

The most common ethyl alcohol hand sanitizers that we have been getting (and the most common out there) are 70% -- which exceeds CDC 60% threshold, but is below the 80% WHO threshold.

THIS SANITIZER has an ISOPROPYL concentration of 75% which exceeds the CDC 70% threshold and meets the WHO 75% threshold.

Clearly these thresholds are not hard limits as indicated by the difference of opinion between CDC and WHO, but it is mildly comforting to meet both recommendations if you can do so with no downside or extra expense.

WHAT I LIKE:
* Easily squeezes out of bottle in controlled amount as a gel
* Rubs in easily and absorbs within less than a minute to leave no noticeable residue or tackiness on your hands
* Aloe helps to keep your hands moist, fighting the drying effects of the alcohol
* Small bottles are easy to take in car, backpack, purse, etc.
* Scent is minor and dissipates quickly (we're not using this for its smell after all)

SUMMARY:
A cost effective way to keep you hands sanitized when you can't use soap & water. Meets both CDC and WHO guidelines for effective hand sanitizer formulations.

title: (Check wikipedia if you are unclear where this stuff comes from -- way cool. ) Anyway
text:
I once bought a kilo jar of flakes from some craft outlet. The flakes are neat because you can see that the chip still have the imprints of the palm leaves. (Check wikipedia if you are unclear where this stuff comes from -- way cool.) Anyway, the 1 lb bags are the same quality Carnauba wax but more finely powdered. Probably that is good for some things. I am using this stuff two ways. Use 1) I use an electric iron to saturate very thin cloth and make collages. It is a neat effect. Most recently I have used the same process to cover very thin plywood to make pieces for a mobile. See pictures.

Use 2: Melt in a double boiler 1 part Carnauba wax to 2 parts walnut oil. The result is a hard paste wax that is terrific for finishing wood. Don't use much, just rub it on, wait an hour, and then buff with a clean cloth. The stuff doesn't contain any drying agents like commercial paste waxes so it doesn't dry nearly as quickly. But it works great. It is a little stiff for lubricating screws for power driving but it will do the job. Furthermore, I have used it has lip balm -- perfectly safe -- but to be honest bees wax melted with olive oil works better.

title: Easy and friendly on my skin
text:
It took a couple practice runs to get the hang of using this, but it did an awesome job removing both glitter and regular polish. What I figured out is this: Use a cotton pad to apply it to each nail. Make sure the nail looks wet when you have done it - the more soaks in, the easier it gets to remove. Wait a few minutes. Use the same soaked cotton pad to remove the polish. A little gentle rubbing will do it. Done this way, it takes a few moments, but it works. I usually leave it to soak a little longer after I've wiped the polish away, because it really does seem to do a great job of conditioning my fingers (which are otherwise prone to being dry and developing hangnails). Then I wash my hands and apply fresh polish.

It's quicker and less scrubbing than my old acetone-based routine, and it does a more thorough job on the hard-to-reach edges. It leaves my skin in good shape and my nails look happy.

title: Stylist tips here
text:
Wash your hands with dawn to remove any access oils or lotions. (Do not apply lotion sooner than 2 hours after application, they need time to adhere) Make sure your nails are completely dry before applying after wash. Nail prep is key! Buff your nails so you have no ridges and push the cuticles back and use an alcohol swab for cleanliness and longer wear. Do not apply on skin or cuticle. Wooden cuticle sticks are great to help trim access, rubber tip cuticle sticks to smooth out. Improper preparation and application can result in peeling.
If peeling still occurs after proper preparation, I recommend a nail hardener polish as a base coat to help.
Removal- I recommend non ace tone Mineral Fusion nail polish remover. If you have an further questions or issues please reach out to a stylist. Also, Am6 prices are over the Color Street website prices. Solid-11, Solid Glitter-12, Glitter dipped and designs- 13, French manicure- 14. title: Hair glides through effortlessly
text:
I had my previous flat iron for many years and never had a problem with it despite the fact that my husband accidently dropped it in the toilet tank. I let it dry out for a few months and it worked like a charm until recently. The plates began to loose their finish and when I was done doing my hair I had a bunch of fly always and loose hairs sticking straight up. It was very noticeable which bothered me. It also became difficult to keep clean so it was time for a new one.

The peacock design is what attracted me, I thought it was pretty. This flat iron does a great job. It heats up quickly, it can heat up to 450 but I usually use it at about 400. I am Hispanic and have naturally frizzy hair but it also has a lot of body. I dye my hair it's it's a little on the dry side. This flat iron straightens my hair effortless. My hair glides through the plates easily, I don't hear dragging or crunching sounds and it does not pull my hair. It usually only takes a few pass-throughs until my section of hair is nice, straight and bouncy. The plates are ceramic so they heat up evenly meaning the temperature should be the same on the front tip of the plates as it on the center and back of the plates. The ionic technology reduces fizziness and fly-away hairs. The cord has a 360 turn and is long which I really like and it's very user friendly. The packaging is divine, it comes in a beautiful box with a magnetic closure with a comb and a felt type sleeve for travel.

I really like this product but there a few cons. My biggest con would be the cord. It's made up of very stiff plastic material that has a lot of memory and I'm worried that it will eventually crack. The curling iron I had previously had a supple rubber material and never experienced cracking or breakage but it didn't have the 360 swivel cord like this flat iron. The location of the on/off switch and temperature dial is located in between the plates by the hinge. I thought this was an odd place and worry it will eventually be effected by the heat of the plates. All in all I am happy with my purchase.

I was granted the opportunity to purchase this product at a discounted rate in exchange for my honest review.

title: Good working product (with a remote) for the price.
text:
The Diffuser comes packed in a box [images on the box are not of the actual product] along with a USB cable [No Adapter], Remote Control [2 AAA Batteries not included], measuring jar [~150 ml] and an instructions manual [poorly written instructions].

The Diffuser is functionally working. Looks good and is sturdy but has a plastic feel.

I like this product because for the price it is a working essential oil diffuser with a remote control and almost no sound while working.

Nice to haves:
- There is a hole on the top for the cool mist but it would be better to have a raised spout like design.
- Please add an adapter [see notes below]
- Update the labeling of the product from 200ml to definitely less than 200ml but more than 150ml.
- It would be nicer for the packaging box to show the actual image of the product instead of 2 images of 2 different diffusers.

Notes:
When I tried to use the Apple wall Adapter [Output: 5V 1A] for this product - it did not work.
The diffuser lights would start but when I pressed the mist button the product would complete stop in about 2-3 seconds.
I used a second Apple Adapter - results same as first.

I then used a different Adapter [ratings: Output: 5V 2A 10W AC Adapter] and the product works - no issues.

title: Salon eyebrow-tinting is now a thing of the past
text:
I have brown hair but was born with naturally light and sparse eyebrows. I used to spend obscene amounts of money getting my brows done for up to $20 at the salon (oftentimes they didn't get it as dark as I wanted), but since purchasing this product I haven't been back! Since I know how I like my brows better than any esthetician would, I apply the dye as I would fill in my brows with a pencil or eyeshadow. I let the dye sit for about 2-3 minutes, then wipe it off with a rag (caution: the dye DOES stain rags!). The dye is inevitably on my skin for a day or 2, but since I fill in only where I'd actually put makeup, it's like I have makeup on and they actually look fuller (just use caution when applying). The box comes with at least 20 or so capsules of dye (which are the hardest to open without getting powder in my sink), so that means I can literally dye my brows 20 different times. The dye lasts about 2 weeks at a time. Overall, if you have lightly-colored eyebrows and want them to be darker, I highly recommend this. It's saved me time, money, and hassle!

I attached 2 photos to this review: Picture #1 is my natural brows, before dying, and picture #2 is shortly after dying, with my brows brushed upwards with some drugstore brow gel. The first is taken with my iPhone and 2nd picture with my Canon DSLR, but the sparsity of my natural eyebrows should definitely be apparent in the first photo despite the lower-quality.

text:
This product is absolutely fantastic. I have the kind of fair skin that is so pale that I have LITERALLY never found a foundation (drugstore or high end) that has a color light enough for me. I have the kind of fair skin that allows me to artificially color my hair a level 8 copper reddish blonde and people think it's my natural hair color. So anyway, I researched forever to try to figure out how to lighten up my foundation and found this product. I am currently using Urban Decay's Naked Skin foundation (another silicone-based product) in 0.5 (their lightest shade). The Zero Minus blends in perfectly and I apply the concoction on prepped (moisturizer and MOM on my T-zone) and primed (Monistat Anti-Chafe Gel) skin with my Beauty Blender and set it with Nars's light reflecting loose setting powder all over and Tarte's Smooth Operator Amazonian Clay finishing powder on my T-zone (I have extreme combination skin). I set it with MUFE's Mist and Fix setting spray. It lasts ALL DAY and BONUS: it doesn't look like a mask because it's actually the right color!!!

I was having some issues in the beginning with it separating on my skin after about an hour (mostly on my T-zone), but it hasn't been doing this since I changed setting powders (originally, I was using Too Faced's Prepped and Primed, which is a fine product that I love, but on my skin it doesn't seem compatible with my foundation when I add Zero Minus). Like other silicone-based products, this gives a semi-matte finish that is very natural looking.

So what are you waiting for!? If you're so white that you make a polar bear jealous, buy this product! It is high quality, long-lasting, and blends beautifully with other silicone-based foundations. title: and they are versatile enough to be perfect all on their own
text:
i am a hair stylist. i work in a busy salon and i always have someone in my chair. i have guests from all walks of life, all ethnicities, and all hair types. quality tools and appliances are a must, something i don't compromise on.

i have used three different types of clips in the salon. i have used smooth metal clips, plastic butterfly clips, and croc clips. the smooth metal clips work well for holding foils in place, but they don't do well for sectioning off large sections of hair. butterfly clips work well for sectioning off hair but not for holding foils in place. butterfly clips are also limited by their size. they come in two sizes but even the larger size isn't always big enough for some sections of hair. croc clips will do everything. they are long enough to hold foils, strong enough to hold large sections of hair (they have the expansion bar that bends to allow them to grip and hold large, bulky sections of hair), and they are versatile enough to be perfect all on their own. with croc clips, i don't have to have some of all the others in my station drawers. croc clips are the other clips all rolled into one. i don't foresee that i will ever use a different clip.

the Rioa croc clips are pretty standard. they are stamped with the brand name of "toni & guy," a well-known name in the styling community. i have purchased several sets of "toni & guy" croc clips from other merchants (including professional beauty supply stores) and the Rioa clips are equivalent to those.

text: When I started using mineral makeup I started with the more well known big brand line, I don't know if I can say their name, but the 'Bare' kind ;) But I'm a full-time student and reordering that brand was a little more than I wanted to be paying. And I had switched to the Matte formula which I loved but it was less product for a higher price. So I started looking to see what other mineral makeups were out there. I found another before IQ and they were ok, but when I tried IQ Natural mineral makeup I was sold. Great price, great product! I have been using them for over a year now, and I can't see me changing. As far as the product - great coverage from the mineral foundations (I use their IQ natural acne moisturizer before putting on the foundation and it works sort of like a primer, and it is great for my skin. One of the reasons I switched to the other brand's Matte formula was to avoid the bismuth oxychloride in the original formula. I had heard that bismuth oxychloride contributes to acne, and I believe it does. IQ's products do not have bismuth oxychloride and I love that! One tip that I recently learned from a youtube video is after you put on your mineral foundation and veil slowly and evenly press the side of your powder brush on your skin to kind of help 'set' it. I use a kabuki to put on the foundation and a much softer large brush for the veil. I've been doing this for the last couple weeks and I think it helps keep the product on longer. title: Great scent, great lather. And a great price (at WallyWorld).
text:
Palmer's/E.T. Browne has a lot of above-average products in its line. This is one of them, for sure.

The scent is scrumptious. Not much like "coconut sun-tan oil at the beach" … much more like "fresh coconut cream pie desert!"

I say above-average because, if you scour the ingredient list on Palmer's products, you will typically find SOME natural & luxurious ingredients … and also some fairly common chemicals. So many of their products are of a higher quality than common store-shelf items … but not exactly in the category of seriously premium and/or upscale products.

For example, this product's main ingredient is Sodium olefin sulfonate. That's a common ingredient in bath & body products that used to make them lather. And Palmer's has been very generous with it, in that this shampoo really REALLY lathers up! The next major ingredient is coconut fruit extract. Many manufacturers won't use coconut oils or extracts in their bath & body products because straight-up palm oils and extracts are cheaper. After that there's a list of many other common chemical sounding ingredients. But also there's coconut oil, Tahitian gardenia extract, keratin-protein and glycerin. Those too are premium ingredients that common bath & body products usually won't contain. And this shampoo contains NO sulfates, parabens, mineral oil, dyes, gluten or phthalates.

That's a lot of quality, given the price … that being $4.36 at WallyWorld for a 14 ounce bottle… and, as of this writing, with instant "$2 off" coupons attached. That's a lot less expensive than other "big brand name" shampoos that offer less and cost more.

There's also a matching body wash product. In use, and in the ingredient list, they are almost exactly the same product. And there's a matching bar soap, though I found it far less interesting - meh - than this shampoo and its matching body wash.

This shampoo seems far better suited for dry hair; it conditions, moisturizes and protects. But I have oily hair. So I sometimes resort to using my bar soap on my hair as a first pass, to "cut through" a lot of the oil, before actually using this shampoo as a second application.

In any case, for a mere $2.36, you can pick up a bottle of this stuff at WallyWorld and see how this shampoo suits you yourself.

title: Bought for use with UV Resin
text:
I didn't buy this for nails, but for curing UV Resin. And it works like a charm. I'm using resin from the Sophie & Toffee brand at the moment, and I leave it in for roughly 10min each cure. It's given me consistent hard cures each time.

The lamp is really lightweight and isn't any heavy duty plastic but if you're a bit careful and don't drop it, drop things on it, throw it, or otherwise abuse it I don't think it's a problem. It is a little big but nothing extreme, and in the case of resin work it's better that way because you can fit larger molds in. I'd hazard a guess that molds the size of the Mod Podge molds would fit (all of mine are smaller at the moment).

It's not noisy, it doesn't produce heat that I've noticed, and the bottom tray/panel does come out (it doesn't always slide easily). It did come with the bulbs packaged with styrofoam inserts to keep them from breaking. They were installed already and it worked straight out of the box. There aren't any instructions but they've got those here on this page so it's not an issue.

title: VERY Small Bottle, But Works Well
text:
I have been looking for some shampoos to help with cleaning hair, but also making the scalp heal for nice hair growth and also flaking.

HOW THIS COMES
This comes wrapped tight in plastic with the pump down.

HOW TO USE
Once the plastic is open, you turn the pump to make it pop up and then you can dispense the shampoo.

SIZE
The bottle is only 6 inches from the base to the top of the pump. It is pretty small.

SCENT
My mom found a really old bottle of shampoo in her attic that was by Fabrege called Farrah Fawcett shampoo. This scent reminds me of that. It is a really nice smelling shampoo.

SCALP
I did feel some tingling in my scalp when using this. It did not burn or hurt at all, it felt nice.

HAIR CLEAN?
I have very fine hair which is easily weighed down. It is hard to find a shampoo that encourages volume, does not make my hair look flat, and that does not make it full of static. This shampoo leaves my hair clean for a few days and it somewhat encourages waves. I can not comment on static, as it is not near winter yet. My hair was not left dry or frizzy at all.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a nice shampoo. It is a small bottle, but a little bit goes a long way. It makes my scalp feel better and leaves my hair nice and clean.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. I wish the bottle was not so small, but I do like the shampoo. I was going to give this to my daughter (she has scalp issues) but I think I will buy her a 2nd one and keep this one for me.

text: I'm somewhat fair skinned but went with Medium/Tan, glad I did.  Especially with summer near.  My first experience with loose minerals makeup.  I like it so far. This way I can easily find them in the order I want to use them.  I decided to set each one on the counter before opening, and just turn the lid, rather than holding them up to open them in case I drop them (would lose the entire contents). I do have to let my moisturizer dry completely before applying the loose minerals, but no problem so far.  Not sure how it may be in the heat of summer when my bathroom's warm though. text:

Even after a few tries, it just wouldn’t hold any oils/serums/or creams. Unfortunately, it just didn’t work out.
However, the wash cloths were decent. They were quite durable and I use them to wipe off makeup/soap after I wash my face. Again, it’s not thick at all. It’s very very thin, so I have to use 2-3 cloths each time. The fact that they’re dry and wrapped in tiny packaging makes it super convenient. I always carry a few in my purse and spill some water on them to use on my hands, face, or just any surface.
The price is low and great, which is why I purchased it... but not worth the money since I couldn’t use it for what I intended.
The additional items that came with it were nothing of importance. The headband works quite well, but I would t expect it to last long.

This beard balm has a flowery, feminine scent.  I can't smell cedar, sandalwood, musk, or leather in it.  I find it suspicious when a "natural" company doesn't list the names of the fragrance oils it uses in its product.  The scent ingredients on the can simply say "scented with premium grade essential OR fragrance oils."  "OR?" So which is it?  Fragrance oils are what people sell on the subway, and that's what this beard balm smells like: a generic, perfume-y scent.  You know when a product at, say, Rite Aid, says it's "mint eucalyptus" but when you get it home and smell it, it doesn't smell anything remotely like either of those things?  That's what the scent of this product reminded me of.  Flowery and feminine, no "old west" "leather" "outlaw" here.  If you want a feminine scent, get this product. This is my third high end Philips/Norelco shaver in the past 10 years. I bought this arcitec 1090 with high hopes that it would do an even better job than my previous 8894xl.

I'm sorry to say that after 3 months of using it almost every day... I consider this a step backwards from the 8894xl. In their quest for a really cool design, and I have to admit it does look really good, they have lost sight of the fact that it actually results in a worse shave.

I find myself having to cover the same ground many more times than in the past and have to concentrate much more to check for missed hairs and spots that I have to go over even more. Also, the statement that the new design improves the ability to shave your neck is not true, I think it is also worse in this regard.

My advice, dont bother with the cool Arcitec design, buy the top of the line traditional Philips/Norelco model instead.

title: TLDR: Great Gift!
text:
I recieved the green one of these as a belated "birthday gift." Although to be clear, I picked it out and asked for it by link, because parents can be clueless sometimes.

Despite that I was concerned about this item for a few reasons, first being that I've been taught brushes should dry with the bristles pointed down in order to prolong the brush life. The second, which is somewhat tied in to the first, is that I have a variety of brushes ranging from 20+ y/o Arbonne brushes from mom's old WFH days, to the dollar store mermaid tale brushes my own little girls gave me last mothers day after they had destroyed a few of the Arbonne ones. I also have some random singles from Ulta and a couple double ended ones Walmart. All in all there were 13 ends I had to clean, including a spoolie.

I used my Simple brand moisturizing face wash as soap this time (I usually switch between this and coconut or olive oil every other week), and just put a dab of it on each section of the scrub side. Then I got the brush wet, and took it to the scrub side using a swirling motion. I did each brush one at a time and adding soap or water as necessary.

As you can kind of see in the pictures a few hairs from one of my Arbonne brushes got tangled in the scrub side. But other than that it seems like there was far less hair lost over all.

IMO the bottom half of the scrub side worked better for smaller brushes, eyeshadow, concealer, spoolie, etc. Where as the bigger brushes did best on the top half of the scrub side.

When I was done with all the brushes I rinsed the scrub side, shook it off, flipped it over and it was ready to go. To finish up the brushes I gently squeezed out the excess water. Then I pressed them with a paper towel a bit more firmly. Finally I arranged them in the stand in front of a fan. They dried pretty quickly and I haven't had any hairs fall out yet, so I don't think the glue inside was effected. If this changes in the future I'll come back and adjust this review.

All in all, I was pleasantly surprised by this thing. At first the scrub side didn't seem to be large enough over all or section wise, and the brush stand circles all looked to be too large for my brushes. But after having put it to the test, my brushes are cleaner than ever. I even washed one brush that I swore was clean. I was, as the kids say, shook. This thing helps you get deep in the bristles. And while I wouldn't recommend using the scrub side on your sponges/beauty blenders, the stand does well for holding them to dry too and they seem to dry quicker this way which I think has something to do with the fact that air can circulate underneath them.

Finally the brush color change sponge, is fantastic. I tested it out with my most pigmented dark glittery purple eyeshadow, followed immediately by my most matte nude shade. Worked perfectly. It's a great addition to a great product.

My only complaint is that this thing is called bear shaped. Now it may be because mine is green, but I swear it's a frog. But either way, I love it. I think this set, with some brush cleaner and a nice set of makeup brushes would make a great present, especially for a young lady who might not even be aware brushes need washing!
