title: SO Many Uses For Both Oils! I LOVE Them!
text:
I am finding SO many uses for Shiny Leaf's coconut and sweet almond oil! I do have some experience with coconut oil but this is my first time using sweet almond oil. Thanks the labels on the bottles, reviews and internet searches, I'm finding SO many ways to use these oils...sometimes together, sometimes individually.

Because I have terribly dry, sensitive skin, my main goal was to see how one or both oils could help protect my skin, especially now that winter has arrived and my skin is REALLY taking a beating. Both oils work well to hydrate and moisturize, so I mixed a few ounces of each in a mist bottle. After I bathe, I mist a combo of the oils over my skin to help hydrate and moisturize. The oils absorb quickly and do not leave an oily/greasy look OR feel to my skin. I'm already seeing a decrease in my dry skin/itchy red patches of skin. I experience NO discomfort whatsoever when misting these oils onto my sensitive skin. Both oils also work wonders on hair by moisturizing, hydrating, improving hair texture/strength, stimulate hair growth /thicken hair, and nourish the scalp to prevent dry, itchy flakes. In addition to using my combo of oils after bathing, I also give my hair a spray or two with the mister and sure enough, I'm seeing less hair in the drain and on my hairbrush after brushing. My hair is soft, smooth and shiny WITHOUT looking or feeling oily/greasy from the oil combo.

I use the coconut oil (alone) to help remove makeup, under and around my eyes to soften and reduce fine lines, I rub a small amount into my scalp (as does my husband) to help stimulate hair growth, on the kid's faces after their baths to soften (especially in cold weather!), on my nail beds every couple of days and a light amount on any patches of eczema/red skin. (It relieves the itching/burning and redness from eczema quickly!)

I use the sweet almond oil (alone) on dark circles under my eyes, a SMALL amount on split ends in my hair, a drop on chapped lips, I'm just starting to tinker with it for aromatherapy purposes. I recently learned that it can help fade scars so I've begun to rub some sweet almond oil into a scar on my finger to see what happens. If it helps, I'll then move on to a small facial scar I have. I'm also trying something on my own; just started doing this a few days ago. I get nosebleeds every single day, at least once a day, throughout the winter when the heat is on in the house. This started when I was 2 years old, I'm now 49 so I've experienced this my entire life. I now rub a small amount of sweet almond oil under my nostrils before bed. Since starting this, I continue to have nosebleeds. Yesterday, I had only one and it involved just a few drops of blood. I didn't whip through numerous tissues like normal. ONE tissue took care of it. (that's huge for me!) I have NO clue if its just a coincidence or if the sweet almond oil is helping in any way but I'm going to continue using it.

These oils are phenomenal! Both bottles are 16oz. I love the fact that they have normal caps on them but pumps for each bottle are included as well. The liquid of each is thinner oil than I expected, which I prefer. Both absorb quickly. Neither has a scent. I've found SO many uses for these oils, I can't wait to discover more. ( I'm SO happy with these oils, I recently purchased Shiny Leaf's biotin hair conditioner and cannot wait to try it! ) I find the price to be incredibly reasonable, especially since you're getting TWO bottles of oils! HIGHLY recommended!

title: Tightening and moisturizing serum
text:
This is such a great anti-aging serum that provides moisturizing and tightening effect to my face in the short time since I have followed the instructions and included the serum in my twice a day skincare routine. Hyaluronic Acid helps the skin hold in more moisture; Vitamin C helps brighten and even skin tone. Together, they work magic and indeed are the best ingredients to fight signs of aging. This product leaves the skin feeling silky soft and really helps with diminishing the appearance of fine lines. The serum has worked well with my other facial products and there is no conflicts in over application of ingredients or mixture of fragrances. My skin does not look quite as tired as before and it has continued to look better.

I love the pump dispenser because it is more sterile than taking it out of a jar or regular container. Aside from the convenience of its portability, after reading all of the benefits, I have been adding it to my daily routine and using it prior to my regular moisturizer. The great thing is that because it is so hydrating that I seem to use less of my regular moisturizer. The texture of this product is a clean feeling and lightweight gel. It goes on smoothly, absorbs quickly, and does not leave a greasy feel. The serum has no scent or artificial chemical fragrance which I prefer and a little of the product goes a long way. It takes two small squirts onto my finger to get a thin layer covering my face. Once it dries, it leaves my skin feeling absolutely refreshing. It is quite moisturizing as well, so it locks in all the water in my skin and gives it a supple feel all night long.

The serum takes a minute to dry and then I apply my makeup. My foundation goes on very smoothly over it and it seems like I have been applying much less makeup lately. It helps keep my makeup looking smooth and moist longer. I find it work better as a makeup prime than many premium brand makeup primers I have tried. My facial lines around my nose has even seemed less pronounced under my makeup. In just two weeks I have been using the serum, I have noticed that my skin tone has become more luminous and healthier looking. I have not seen any fading of sun spots that I have, but I am hopeful with long term use that they will eventually lighten up. Based on what my experience has been so far, I am confident that with consistency and patience, I will see more progress down the road. This is a wonderful wrinkle smoothing serum and I highly recommend it.

The colors in the palette are true to the images, and go on staying true to color as well. They stay in place well without using any type of eyelid/shadow primer, but I’m sure would do even better if you use one. The only complaint I have is that the glitter color tends to go on in fewer, larger pieces, rather than more, smaller pieces. The result is that it’s not extremely pigmented when applying the powder directly to your lid without a brush or any additional techniques or products. I’m sure there’s probably a hack to fix this if you watch a tutorial online or something like that, but I haven’t tried.

title: Something that finally works.
text:
I'm a 23 year old female that has battled acne for 10 years. It's not just mild acne- it's cystic, life-damaging, skin-destroying acne. I get it mostly on my outer cheeks and chin. I've tried exfoliants, cleansers, toners, masques. I've done home remedies. Egg whites, oatmeal and honey, hydrogen peroxide, oil cleansing. Things will start to work, or work for a small time, and then my face will be back to it's oily, cystic self.

Recently I've been using an Aveeno daily exfoliator with an Aveeno moisturizer. It wasn't really doing the trick. I thought, perhaps I need to use toner. Since Aveeno is all natural, I decided to stick with that theme.

I *LOVE* this product. I will take off my makeup at night, spritz my face with toner, then apply moisturizer. After the first day I noticed my skin was less greasy/oily. It just felt better. I started to get concerned when I began getting small white pimples appearing, but friends told me that was my face getting rid of the junk. I was just thankful they weren't huge cysts! A week later, my skin is almost completely clear. I only have one active pimple on my face that is in the process of healing. I hope that it stays this way!

Also I must say that the smell is divine! My boyfriend even likes it. I wish the bottle would never run out, but I know that when it does, I'm buying another.

text:
I'm very impressed wit this hair care kit. I've never done so many products in one go but it was worth it.

First I used #0 on my dry hair. My hair is a bit longer than shoulder length and I used the entire bottle of #0 but once I got the hang of putting this on my dry hair, I think I could have gotten 2 uses out of that bottle. After 10 minutes I added #3 and let it set for 10 minutes. I know I can get another use out of that bottle.

Then I hopped in the shower and rinsed my hair and it felt very smooth as I rinsed it. Then I shampooed with #4, rinsed and then conditioned with #5 (left on 3 minutes). Once I towel dried my hair and I applied the mask #8. After 10 minutes I rinsed the mask out of my hair.

I really didn't notice the scents of #0 and #3 but #4, #5, and #8 have nice, light scents. I can tell my hair is in better shape after these treatments. I can get two full uses out of the kit in the future with additional uses out of #4, #5, and #8.

On one hand, I was putting off going through all these steps but now I see that it's worth the time it takes.

title: Lovely Deck With One Gripe
text:
I pre-ordered this deck months ago and after much anticipation, it was very well worth the wait.

I'm slowly going through the deck card by card. The packaging is nice,easy to take out without destroying the box. It also comes with a Spread Sheet. Literally. *snerk* A sheet which illustrates different spreads on the front and back. Very handy for beginners. The deck is roughly 2"x 4" and included are two extra quick reference cards -- one for the majors, the other for the minors. Nice touch. I wish all decks provided this.

My only complaint so far is they provided a 70pg. LWB. Nothing more. No large reference book with extensive background on the cards symobolgy, like they've done in the past with the Celtic Dragon and ShapeShifter decks. Kinda disappointed (hence the 4/5 stars). But if I wish to carry this deck around, a big book would be cumbersome I suppose.

HOWEVER, what is nice about the LWB is they provide a mythical background on the creature, a divinatory meaning, AND magickal use of the card. Nifty! Never have I seen the Magickal Usage option before in a tarot deck.

So, card by card, I'm taking in what I think the symbology means then reading the LWB and finding I'm fairly accurate. Either I'm getting
better at Tarot or the deck really syncs with me like the Celtic Dragon and Fey decks do (ShapeShifter is a more difficult one for me to grasp now, but I have faith in the future it will become quite the tool for me when I'm ready).

Lastly, and one of the reason why I love Lisa Hunt's decks, is the Wands/Air - Swords/Fire connection. Few decks represent that and I've always been more intuitively drawn to that way of thinking, even before my Tradition's teachings reflected the same.

If you are a fan of Lisa Hunt -- get this deck.
If you are a fan of mythology -- get this deck.
If you are a witch or tarot reader who is more connected to the Wands/Air, Swords/Fire -- get this deck.
If you are like me and need a reference card now and again (lol) -- get this deck.

So often in the past, sellers would advertise cosmetology mannequins as having afro hair, then you washed it and the coil pattern was completely gone. The money I lost trying to find a real African textured cosmetology mannequin back in the day, was unbelievable!

A few things to note.....While washing her hair there was tons of shedding. I've come to realize this is quite normal. However, after the washing is said and done, the shedding is minimal. Thank goodness because there are cosmetology mannequins where the shedding continues in massive balls even after washing.

The ends are thin and stringy and that's where I'll take a one star deduction. She'll be gettin a good trim here soon, but I definitely recommend her. I'd say her hair is in the 3b/3c range? I could be off about that because I'm still a bit shaky on the hair typing system. Either way, you'll definitely be satisfied with your purchase.

I've attached pictures of before washing her hair, after washing her hair and what her hair looks like after I dried it and dry combed it. Lovely soft hair. I almost didn't wanna ruin the rod set because it was so cute but I always wash the hair of any cosmetology mannequin I buy, right outta the box.

title: This flat iron is MAGIC!!
text:
As you can see, my “before” hair is very badly damaged: drugstore dye every 3 weeks, regular exposure to the AZ sun/heat & pool chlorine, plus I haven’t gotten a haircut in nearly 2 years so my split ends have split ends. Yet this little flat iron somehow makes my abused, frizzed-out hair look smooth, shiny, and healthy! It also feels very soft, with nice movement & body. The photos have not been edited aside from brightening up my bad bathroom lighting, and I did not use any oils, sprays, or other product in my hair after the usual shampoo & conditioner. It took me approximately 6 minutes to style, not including time for the iron to heat up (it’s pretty fast, I just didn’t time it).

I dare say it might even work better than the $129 “professional” flat iron I got at a beauty supply store, though my old iron has been with me for 12 years so it definitely has some wear & tear. Still, it’s pretty impressive considering the very reasonable price for this one! The only minor drawback is the awkward control buttons, which are inside the handle & close to the hot plates, though I have not burned myself using them (yet). They’re also a little confusing and I have no idea what the strip of “infrared” lighting inside one plate is supposed to accomplish. So, I sought out the enclosed instructions and found this paragraph (verbatim):

“Amino-bond is produced with the photosynthesis of ambipolar light of 68000Hz(wave length 680nm) and the elemental amino acid made up of the horny layer of hair so that the hair fiber and its elasticity will be restored, the hair squama gap will be densified again and the cellularity and squama gap will be restored.”

Sooo...yeah. No idea what any of that means! But I really can’t argue with results. You definitely will not find a better flat iron at this price point. I’d give it 10 stars if I could!

text: I've been very happy with this brush.  My hair has always been thin, but since it has started getting more gray, it has become more dry & coarse. I discovered I could use a dry wash cloth or heat resistant glove to assist in keeping  my hair against the warming surface.  As I place the brush under my hair & brush downward, I place my other hand (protected by cloth or glove) over the nubs, thereby holding the hair tight against the surface.  The smoothing effect is great without any burning of the hair like with a straight iron.  We also used it on my mixed race granddaughter whose hair is much thicker and kinkier. title: Surprisingly good
text:
I heard this was similar to one of favorites, Bvlgari Man in Black. It’s not, and that’s not a bad thing. There is a passing similarity during the first seconds of the opening and then they quickly diverge. Frankly, I think it’s awesome.

To me this has some nice freshness in the opening. I was expecting spiciness so I was initially disappointed but I’ve grown to really like it.
It has some wine-like sweetness, similar to its name sake although their aren’t any wine accords listed in the notes. (I am familiar w/the unique alcohol used but I really don’t know how much that effects the profile)

As it dries down it interacts with my skin really well, it develops this really nice slightly resinous tone.

Personally I use this during the day. It can be used at night, although I have so many evening fragrances this isn’t my first choice but it could easily fill that role. It reminds me of sharing a bottle of great wine with friends.

In the end, I took a chance on a brand that isn’t too popular outside of Brazil and I believe it paid off. And to top it off the presentation is quality. The flacon has a nice soft-touch finish and the sprayer is decent.

This won’t appeal to everyone. It’s not particularly similar to today’s designer frags. But if you want something unique to add to your collection I highly recommend giving it shot. An affordable, unique fragrance with above average performance.

title: Buy this toothbrush
text:
My dentist recommended that I buy an electric toothbrush. After doing some searching and reading the other Oral B reviews, I bought this toothbrush. I've been using it for about one month now, and I can feel and see a noticeable difference. My teeth, and mouth feel cleaner, my tongue less furry (for lack of a better scientific term - more technically, if using a "tongue scraper," there is less to scrape), my gums look better, and my teeth do appear whiter. I've used the "dual action" head, and the polisher in conjunction with Arm & Hammer Advance White Brilliant Sparkle Baking Soda toothpaste. Like some of the other reviewers provide, all the attachments probably aren't necessary and may not be used. Charging the toothbrush has not been too much of an issue.

Overall, I have been very happy with the results in the short time period that I have used the toothbrush, and hope to have better results next time I'm at the dentist (a less painful cleaning, and hopefully no cavities). I would strongly recommend buying this item to anyone who is in the market for an electric toothbrush - I didn't know it could make such a difference, and wish I had purchased it sooner.

title: This vs. Clarisonic Uplift?
text:
I haven't been using this item long enough to report on any discernible difference in my face but I can speak to a couple of other interesting tidbits.

I know that these have been in use for generations and they must work because people swear by them. If that weren't proof enough, I use my Clarisonic Uplift daily, and it comes with an attachment that does the exact same thing that this roller does, only with using technology. The instructions on this roller is to use it for 5-10 minutes a day, 2-3 times a day. That's a lot and I don't know of many people who care to carve out time to do this, but if you're sitting quietly watching TV or even reading, you can do it absentmindedly. With the Clarisonic, you're supposed to use it with a moisturizer or a serum but with this, you use it on a dry face. With or without a lotion, the massaging affect is exactly the same.

The jade roller feels cool across the skin (even if mine does squeak a little) and it feels wonderful. I'm not sure it does anything if you're rolling it on your chest, but it feels amazing if done with a bit of pressure. It comes in a nice little Asian-inspired embroidered bag, so it doesn't look bad if you want to leave it on your bedside for easy access. I'm going to continue to use the Uplift each night but this item doesn't require a battery and I can whip it out anytime.

I can't rave enough about this product. I've had it for a couple months now, and I've used it with mostly eyeshadow, but all sorts of colors. It's removed them all pretty much instantly! I will say that the only problem with this is that it will probably make people forget that even though it's taking off the pigment, it's not removing bacteria and such, so you should probably still wash your brushes once or twice a month.

And yes. I know that it's just a stippling brush in a little can. So if you want to DIY it, I'm sure you could. I find this a lot more convenient than trying to spend an afternoon coming up with a copy of this. Part of its use is the can: the stippling part doesn't move around (well, it rotates a little) because it's contained in the can. So I just have it sitting in a corner of my makeup box, and I can just brush my brushes towards the inside corner, and it doesn't move. Alternatively, you could put some hot glue or silicone on the top face of the lid, so when you put the lid on the bottom (like the picture) and had it on your countertop, it wouldn't slide, either.

Anyways, love this product! Also works with bigger brushes. I'm wishing I'd bought the duo, though, because it's supposed to work with creme make up.

I had a Norelco years ago, then I went through three Brauns (the micro-foil ones that a straight instead of having three circular blades like this one). All my razors were expensive, they were all the best in the bunch. This is the best by far.

title: A fairly aggressive razor
text:
Coming from my mild Rimei and Baili razors, I'd say this razor is pretty aggressive. Significantly higher blade exposure than what I'm used to. I have very coarse, tough facial hairs, but pretty sensitive skin on my throat and upper lip, so as you can imagine, shaving can be a nightmare for me if the razor and blade combo is wrong.

I like this razor, but it will take some getting used to. I would recommend using a less sharp, smoother blade at first, such as a Derby or a Big Ben, unless you already know you can handle the combination of an aggressive razor with a very sharp blade.

I first ordered the Rapira Swedish Supersteel razor, but it came with a bent guard (looked damaged in shipping), so I sent it back. Aside from that, that razor has a metal handle (zinc?) and the weight was more balanced towards the handle. This razor is overall lighter and the weight is more balanced towards the head, which I prefer. The head on both razors is the same Tech-type design.

The handle is good, probably not as tough as a metal handle though. I'd prefer a better grip on it, similar to a rougher checkered surface like on a plastic rifle stock or something, but it does the job.

title: Great razor,great company!
text:
I am a woman with facial hair. I have used mostly electric razors of many kinds to avoid the nicks I sometimes got with non-electric shavers. I bought the Arcitec about 2 years ago,and it DID give me the closest shave I ever got from an electric,with less irritation.SOOOO smooth and comfortable. I just cleaned my face with a cotton ball or two and witch hazel,and that was enough to prepare my skin for shaving. The shape made it very comfortable to hold,and gave excellent control. It was very well made,and looked it. I traveled on airlines with it twice,using the included hard travel case/recharger,and it came through it perfectly. I only shave 3 times a week,so the blades lasted over a year.And since it was the most expensive razor I ever bought,I read and followed the owner's manual very closely and took very good care of it.
Suddenly,though,the battery wouldn't stay charged. I had to fully charge it to use it,and if I left the Arcitec off the charger,the battery drained itself dead. I had lost the receipt. I went on the company website and did the online chat with a service representative. The representative was very polite and helpful,and I explained the problem,and admitted to having lost the receipt,and he STILL said that they're replace it right away,if I would agree to send the broken one to them promptly,postage prepaid by THEM. The new razor arrived in a sealed new package,like they have at the store,and they also sent a postage paid label,and instructions to send the old razor and all accessories and a copy of the invoice in the box the new one came in,and I could then just put it in any UPS drop box to mail it.
I would buy Norelco again,ANYTIME!

title: Pretty natural looking
text:
Finally, after over a year of having these, I actually tried them out! I’ve never worn false lashes before and was hesitant to use them (obviously since I’ve had them a year without using them - lol!). I’ve seen so many false eyelashes that are so crazy over-the-top obviously fake looking. These are not that way at all. You get a generous supply of them (see photos) and they are reusable too. With the rate I’m going, mine should last forever!
I don’t have get up close vision so it was a little bit harder for me to apply them than it would be for someone who can see better. I used a magnifying makeup mirror though and did fine. The photos of the eyelash after it was applied was my first attempt ever to do this so it’s definitely not perfect but it was much easier to apply than I expected it to be. I am sure my results will improve with practice. These are secured in place with magnetic eyeliner (I guess I am pretty ignorant about these things but I had never heard of that!). The eyeliner goes on smoothly; actually better than some liquid eyeliner that I’ve used in the past. It’s a little tricky to get them in the best spot. Like I said previously though, I think this will get much easier the more times I try them. It comes with tweezers to use but it was almost easier for me to apply them without using them. Once in place, I was amazed at how well they stayed in place!
They were easy to remove and the eyeliner did require makeup remover to get it off, but it also came off without a problem.
I didn’t wear them long. I will have to get used to how they feel; it wasn’t uncomfortable, just different for me. I have very thin, light-colored eyelashes so I think I’m really going to enjoy these!

title: Deceptive, and cheap.
text:
I am so very disappointed with this product line by Amorepacific. I love their other brands, IOPE and sulwhasoo. But I was in the search for a more affordable toner/emulsion/serum and was excited when they introduced this line and gave a discount. They really sold this beta-hyaluronic whatever that works 1.5x better and I thought it was a new patented technology. But no. Contrary to their marketing claim, there is no such thing as beta hyaluronic acid. Yes I looked up patent registry and trademark registry and Amorepacific didn’t register anything new in the past few years related to hyaluronic acid. They just put a new spin on beta glucan, which according to some studies works 20% better, not 150% like they claim. Also beta glucan is toward the end of the ingredient list, meaning we have no idea how much of it is even in there. It’s so disappointing that Amorepacific decides to just flat out lie to customers about it. Makes me go wonder what else they are lying about.

Now I would not have done all the research if the serum worked well in the first place. But it came with no safety seal which made me go um. The packaging felt cheap. The liquid felt cheap and diluted. My skin smelled like plastic. My skin didn’t stay hydrated like other serums and that’s when I knew something was up. I bought toner, emulsion and serum. The emulsion was sealed but the toner and serum was not. I didn’t even bother trying the emulsion. I’ll be returning these all. I will also be seeking new skincare products that are not made by Amorepacific. Goodbye.

text:
Ok fellow Amazonians, I have been on a search for over 2 years for the perfect shampoo and conditioner. I used to use Pureology, but then, a few years back, they started messing with their formulaes. I was definitely not happy as the new stuff left my hair lifeless or at worst created a snarled mess. My search brought me through over a dozen misc brands as well as the more well known such as Chi and Phyto, but nothing provided any stellar results. My hair would also somehow get used to a new shampoo and stop looking decent. No idea why, maybe it got bored.
Anyway, I am 50 years old, colored my hair forever, and have fine, thinnish hair. I found this brand on a random search and decided to give it a try.
I started off with their Lemon Scented set and OMG give that a try too. I had such incredible results, as in like nothing I have EVER tried. Within a few weeks of use I noticed new hair growth at my temples! That and my hair had a new body like it has NEVER had. A few weeks more and I noticed I now had to really work the shampoo down to my scalp BECAUSE there was so much new hair growth at the crown of my head. I gave a set to my daughter who has always had these very thin areas at her temples and she too has new hair growth that is VERY apparent. She would not wear her hair up because of those patches, but now, you can easily see all the new hair. This stuff is amazing.

Now, you get a jar that is gritty with the salt and very thick. This seems to confuse some people, but PLEASE, just dip a finger in, swirl it a bit, and scoop out what you need (You will figure out the right amount for you quickly enough)
You put the gritty(salt) stuff onto your scalp and start working it in and VERY quickly you will have a thick and luxurious lather as the salt and minerals dissolve. The scent is over the moon, enveloping you in a fresh zingy peppermint haze and the Peppermint creates the most incredible tingly sensation.
Trust me, you are going to want to try these products. The Lavender, while I love the scent, for me, it seems better suited to oily hair, but the Lemon set and Peppermint Rosemary are my favorites.
Earth Chemistry will be the ONLY products touching my hair from now on.

However, this brand has fewer ingredients,  no penetrants to inflame my eczema, and comes well-reviewed. It was also not terribly expensive. By the end of seven days, my pores appeared smaller, even on my nose, and the overactive sebum glands in my T-Zone were shrinking. White heads were either coming to the surface and easily extracted after a shower, or shrinking below the skin. I started using this on my neck and noted increasing firmness (which I badly need). I am not much concerned with wrinkles, as I had oily skin until menopause, and have not yet noticed any difference. Because this gel is thick, I first spray with a non-alcohol toner, and then put one or two drops on my fingers and spray three times with the toner before applying. This amount covers my whole face, neck and eye area. I then apply a lightweight moisturizer  after the B-3gel has sunk in. At first, I only did this one time a day There is a very tiny bit of flaking from this gel--it is drying a little. That, I think, is why the acne scars improve. I plan to keep using this product and have ordered oral B3 vitamins, also, but have not yet begun taking them. I feel I must be deficient in this vitamin to have such a positive response topically. title: Interesting idea ... smells great. Cheap packaging.
text:
At first, I was a bit skeptical about baby cologne. The act of spraying down your smelly little bundle of joy with cologne seems a bit weird. Are babies supposed to smell like anything but babies? So, we actually bought this spray for us, figuring the ingredients would be healthier if it was meant for youngsters. This does smell pretty darn good!

When the bottle arrived, it came capless in an envelope. The bottle feels like very lightweight plastic and cheap. Not sure why they did not go with a thicker plastic or even glass given the price point of this being not exactly on the cheap side. The packaging does not match the price or quality.

I wanted the white blossom/citrus version, which was unavailable and worried lavender would be cloyingly sweet and feminine. A few squirts from the bottle and my fears were gone ... this leans more towards feminine but could be worn by a man as well. The note I smell most is orange blossom followed by a faint lavender. It is fresh and captivating and I do get the mediterranean influence ... it smells like Spring on the Amalfi Coast. It's classy and well balanced ... I am a huge fan of colognes/perfumes and have lots of the high end Creed, Aqua di Parma, etc. and while you'll never mistake this for a luxury scent, it's better than a lot of the cheaper colognes and perfumes.

I wish I could tell you how babies like it, but mostly my 40 year old girlfriend wears this. It's a splash she puts on after the shower or before heading out when she wants something not as strong or distinctive as perfume. This doesn't last a long time ... maybe an hour or two. Nor does it project incredibly well ... it sits close to the skin. But for the price and how refined it is, it's worth keeping in your overnight bag or gym locker.

The ingredients seem to be similar to a normal eau de cologne. I am not sure I'd spritz down an infant with this too often ... but it seems to be a slightly scaled down version of bottled perfume. It still contains alcohol as the first ingredient but feels lighter on the skin.

Overall, despite the cheap packaging, this is a nice light scent that is good for adults and probably kids. Orange blossom is one of my favorite smells and it's high on the list of basenotes here. I'd recommend keeping a bottle of this on hand for a quick refreshing spritzdown. It smells nice and seems high quality.

title: Twice As Much of A Waste As One Bottle!
text:
The current version of Tsar is a pitiful, inert, dullard of a fragrance that smells markedly like Old Spice. No need for anyone save masochists to stockpile!

Per other reviewers considering vintage bottles, this fragrance used to be an interesting powerhouse. Unfortunately, as IFRA (regulatory agency) restrictions on perfume content and overall manufacturing costs have increased, many manufacturers have simply stopped trying to inventively reformulate older fragrances, so what the buyer ends up with is the modern version of Tsar: a weak not especially complex or interesting scent with minimal projection and average longevity. When applied, I get a burst of alcohol and green, and then in about 10 minutes, some hint of pine, amber, and florals (carnation, geranium, lily of the valley maybe?). I smell no leather, no oak moss, no vetiver, no tonka beans, and only the slightest hint of patchouli. This becomes a skin scent really quickly, i.e. no projection, but it does last for about 6-8 hrs as a skin scent. This long duration is really the only major advantage Tsar has over Old Spice, which sells for half the price and smells oddly similar!

On Fragrantica.com, there are like 27 different scent ingredients listed for Tsar (or at least claimed for Tsar by its manufacturer), which is simply absurd. VC&A are either having some fun with us, citing historical formulas that are 10 years put of date, or have succeeded in generating the blandest possible result from the most ornately Byzantine of recipes. In comparison, Terre D'Hermes, with a mere 8 ingredients cited on the same site, smells like it is several magnitudes of complexity higher, a symphony compared to Tsar's hummed nursery rhyme.

Frankly, I think most buyers should spend their dollars elsewhere. Many of the old vintage powerhouses have not been reformulated into the same decreptitude that Tsar has; Azzarro Pour Homme, Lapidus, Aramis, Havana, Tuscany, Yatagan: all still around, all smell great, though maybe not quite as good as they used to. Even Grey Flannel, which is currently much cheaper than Tsar, smells much better and still has some of its cojones attached. So if you want to see what the 80s (or earlier!) smelled like, you have a lot of options. Tsar certainly won't appeal to most young modern male fragrance buyers who love calone, seaweed, and apple. And if your tastes are for more refined "older" stuff, the dull ghostwater found in bottles of Tsar holds little appeal at the current price point. Get Azzarro PH or Lapidus for less money and have more fun!

On the plus side, Tsar is certainly workplace friendly, as no one will smell it on you unless you are giving them a piggyback ride or are lying on top of them, both of which circumstances are uncommon enough in the workplace so as to preclude their likelihood of occurrence.

Other exhibits in the realm of the Former Powerhouse Roll of Dishonor are worse than Tsar: the current Halston Z14, Ungaro III, and Paco Rabanne all have been even more neglected / manhandled into smelling weak / unpleasant/ or both. And even weak Tsar smells better than many modern fragrances, alas, but that's beyond the point. Bottom line: unless this falls in price to the level of Nausea Voyage, there are many better options for less money.

They do give good "color" information, but I found a lot of it to be repetative, which makes me think I just need to hit the auto changing light!

No specific instructions on how long to use a given light, or its intensity. The device control is auto set at 30 minutes, upon plug in, but the ad (which I just looked at again) mentions 10 to 20 minutes a couple/few times per week. And, the control device does not have an on/off button, as far as I can see... you either have to slowly cycle down the minutes button, or, reach for the plug and pull it out of the socket while the mask is on. The other thing is that the control box itself is labeled "Facial Whitening Instrument." What's that all about? I am already too white looking! It is not mentioned in the ad or on the box.

I know that red light therapy is now touted as a good thing, but I am afraid that if the instructions are not good and thorough then it could also pose some dangers. I will look elsewhere to find information about how to use this device. I am sure it is actually a fairly worthy instrument, but the communication needs to be better!

title: Major price hike, small quantity.
text:
The listing is for 3 sheets of 18 graduated sizes of stickers attached to a central strip, so 6 stickers of any given size. The "54 strips" refers to the quantity of individual stickers, not the quantity of sheets. At $13 USD, that's $4.33 per sheet and $0.24 per sticker. Since most people don't have 9 different sizes of nail beds on every finger, you'll go thru the ones that fit pretty quickly and have to either trim down or throw out the ones that don't fit.

In Sep 2018 I ordered a pack of 40 sheets (720 stickers) from Dashing Diva for $25. That breaks down to roughly $0.62 per strip of 18 and $0.03 per individual sticker. They worked well and I felt happy with the results. Although they've tweaked the product in the last couple years and the stickers are now a thicker material, and 2021 is a different world in terms of supply chain costs, I'm not convinced a ~587% price increase in less than 3 years is justified by slightly thicker material.

Although these strips are effective at protecting your natural nail and easy to use, the value for money is not great in my opinion. Unless the price comes back down I can't see myself ordering these again, and will have to find more cost effective ways to keep my nails healthy.

The decoration itself is just amazing sparkle, with three small crystals used to make each leaf, larger crystals for drops, and small flower designs made up of crystals. title: Over [price] for a toothbrush?? It's worth every penny!!!!
text:
First of all, I am not a dental professional...
I didn't think much about it when my wife told me that she wanted a new toothbrush for Christmas...but I took notice when I found out how much the one was that she wanted. Around [price] for a toothbrush seemed a bit excessive to me at first! But we went ahead and got one anyway. My wife is a dental hygienist, and the dentist she works for highly recommends this product (and he rarely if ever recommends dental products!). As it turned out, we received a second toothbrush from my folks at Christmas, so we are the proud owners of two Sonicare toothbrushes.
I've been reserving judgement on this product until I've had a good chance to see how I like it. After a month of regular use I've got to say that it's GREAT! The internal timer is a good idea. It helps you to pace your tooth brushing, making sure that you spend enough time to insure adequate cleaning. Though one 2-minute cycle is long enough for a good brushing, I often brush for two of those cycles. I sometimes use the brush without toothpaste and sit and read while I brush for two or three cycles. The sonic cleaning really does a great job! When I'm done my teeth feel clean and smooth, as good or better than after I get done with a professional cleaning.
I can honestly say that my gums feel like they are in better shape than they used to be, and my teeth are cleaner on a regular basis.
After a full month of using a Sonicare brush I give it two thumbs up. Our children (ages 6, 8, 10) use it as well, and they enjoy it too.
The brush handle contains a rechargable battery, and the brushes are available in different sizes. I like the compact head better than the larger head. The handle takes a little getting used to, since it is much larger than a standard toothbrush's handle. It also takes a few brushings to get used to the rapid vibrations in your mouth -- it can really tickle -- and I imagine that if you have sensitive gums that it could cause some mild painat first, but will certainly firm up the gums and help their condition improve in good order. It really made my saliva run the first few times I used it, but that's not a problem now. Another thing that takes a little getting used to is the fact that you don't have to supply the muscle power to do the brushing. All you have to do is to hold the brush head gently against the teeth and the handle does the rest.
All in all, I'd say that Sonicare's brush is the best oral hygeine product I've ever used. Definitely in the 5-star category!
Brush on!

title: Comparison vs. SKII Facial Treatment Essence

The AMAZING thing about this 'miracle water'? it actually doesn't bead up like water on your skin, but SINKS in and ABSORBS into your pores, what we in the beauty industry call "high skin affinity". Your skin just DRINKS it up. You use it as the first step after cleansing and toning -- this mineral rich, fermented water will act as your "reservoir" BEFORE you pile on the serums and creams, locking in all the hydration so that the essence stays in your skin and doesn't escape.

I have gone thru 5 full-size bottles of SKII over the years and every time i use it, my skin feels rougher and rougher and the hydration level doesn't seem to go up. This doesn't happen with Cremorlab. Moreover, Cremorlab's essence absorbs better than SKII. (SKII can bead up slightly, so you have to work harder at pressing it into your skin). Both SKII and Cremorlab have fermented extracts and good-for-you water-based ingredients; however SKII costs $100 and Cremorlab only is $40 -- and i like Cremorlab's performance more.

I'd say 2 or, at most, 3 times a week would be fine for all skin types. I did end up making a few red marks after I got used to it and got a little cocky (lol) but that was absolutely my own fault as the instructions also warn of this and how to prevent it. The discoloration (again, self-caused) went down with some icing and was completely gone by the next day with no issues since. I am AMAZED by the amount of GUNK pulled out of my "clean" skin every use, especially in my T-zone. I usually use this and follow with a deep-clean mask for my especially stubborn blackheads and I have to say the combination is without parallel. I've never seen such dramatic results with one single product and this device boosts the effectiveness of the products I already Iove by clearing the way for the next product to penetrate appropriately. I am so, so pleased and amazed with the results of this device, the gentleness (when used appropriately), and the ease of use/cleaning after use. The only question I might have is how to clean the little catch-all pad inside (a great design note as this prevents the "gunk" from clogging the vacuum itself), but that is likely easily remedied and I'm sure I will find a natural cleaning solution to keep my device and all its parts clean and functional for a long time. (Another side-question could be "what type of damage is the suction doing to the elasticity of my face?", though I've looked into it enough to learn this is viewed to be less damaging than some other pore excavation methods I've used.) Overall: I love this product and will keep it as part of my routine until the next beauty wonder is revealed!

title: Makes an awesome occasional pre-shampoo scalp scrub!
text:
As a facial scrub, I'd rate this better than average, and designed for oily (not dry or normal) skin, but where this really stands out from other products is as a scalp scrub, not to use every time you shampoo, but more like once every couple of weeks as a pre-wash scalp deep-cleaning. I have dryish hair, but my scalp tends to be oily. I have tried many scalp scrubs over the years, but they all left residue and/or just didn't seem to do much of anything.
The way I use this product is to wet my hair and scalp thoroughly, apply a small amount to my scalp, massage in (with fingertips or a scalp brush) for a few minutes, and leave it sitting on my scalp for a couple more minutes (not more than 3 or 4), then rinse, then shampoo and condition as usual.
What I notice right away is that my regular shampoo feels like it is actually cleaning my scalp instead of just sitting on top of it, and even many days later my scalp just feels healthy and clean. I've been using this scrub this way for over a year now, and it continues to work well for me. It's more effective and much less expensive than any "scalp scrub", and the small (1.7 ounce) plastic container, means it's very portable for travel.
One caution though - I don't color my hair (I've earned my gray hairs!), so I can't comment on whether this scrub would mess with the color of dyed hair. I can say it has no effect on the color of my own brown hair with an increasing number of white-gray strands, it just seems to help my hair grow out thicker and healthier with long term use.

title: If you used to Oral-B Glide floss, you would not like this!
text:
Product reviews on Amazon are something I always rely upon to make my purchase decision. Before buying this brand of floss, which was first time for my family (We usually buy Oral-B Glide floss at Costco), the straight 5-star reviews caught my attention so I thought this must be really good stuff. But as it turned out, this is nothing near the dental floss we expected - the line is too thin to hold on to; there is no waxing so moving in and out of the teeth gap is frustrating, not to mention the effectiveness of cleaning stuff in there. After a few attempts, we gave up using it and now there are 99% of unused packets. If anyone has really used this brand of floss and likes it, please let me know, so I can send them to you with no charge (but please send a prepaid return envelope). Hate to see the "5-star" stuff got wasted like this!

After all, even though the Glide floss quality has somehow gone down in recent years (the line become easier to break, which wasn't the case a few years back), it is still 10 times better. So I guess we have to stick with Oral-B Glide floss and pray they will improve their outsourcing process and bring the Glide quality back to where it was before outsourcing production to some foreign place where they don't give a damn to Americans' teeth.

Sorry, Flosscard maker and vendor, I have to do this to somewhat bring the review ranking to reality so none will be misguided again and make the same mistake we did. I know there are many Glide floss users out there who become unsatisfied with the worsening of Glide floss quality in recent years, especially with the tendency to break prematurely, and want to try something else. I was one of those and now I am here to tell you, my adventure has failed.

Nice Case. And YES - IT HOLDS THE REMMINGTON BEARD BOSS: Trimmer, plastic height adjusting heads, Charger, Beard Trimming Scissors, Manual and even the Beard Brush that comes with the Beard Boss set. And there is a little room left (mostly in the pouch in the case's inside cover) to fit some other small or thin items. I would describe the Case itself as being semi-rigid - there's a very tiny bit of flex at the center of the bottom and top - but it's more than rigid enough to protect the trimmer inside a suitcase. Very much like those hard camera cases which it resembles but I don't want to imply here with that comparison that you can also adjust the partitions, you can't, they're fixed. The area for the trimmer itself is a little narrower at one end, giving it a more "custom" fit, but which also means that the trimmer only fits one way.

Single zipper pull unlike the double zipper you frequently find in other types of cases now, but that is a minor characteristic that really doesn't affect its functionality.

There's also a very small metal ring (about an inch or so) at the end of the zipper run and I'm really not sure what the purpose of that is except to maybe to attach a tag of some sort.

Overall, a nice functional case.

title: You get what you pay for
text:
These plates are just cheaper (price-wise and quality) versions of Konad plates. You get 21 plates for about $18, and shipping is free, so that's quite an irresistible deal, but I have to say, these plates CANNOT compare to the Konad plates.
First of all, there is no safety backing on the plates, as many people have written already; the plates are very thin, and can be very sharp. I resorted to pasting the plates to index cards so it's less likely to slice into my fingers, and to prevent the plates from scratching each other.
Secondly, the designs of the plates are not as intricate and well done as the Konad plates. I have a bunch of Konad plates, and the BM designs definitely don't come close. The BM designs are not as detailed, and just are not as "pretty" as the Konad designs (but of course, you get what you pay for). Also, some of the plates I got, seems like there were manufacturing flaws. The designs on the plates appear smeared, or smudged, and when I tried to stamp them, the images do not transfer properly, if at all.
Thridly, the full nail designs don't actually fit on your whole nail (unless you have really small hands, or are a child). I learned that if I'm very precise on how I stamp, I can get away with stamping the "full nail" designs from my index to my pinky. Thumb is definitely out of the question, lest you end up with a half stamped thumb, or you're good enough to stamp in two halves (you have to really match up the designs). I've never had this problem with Konad designs.
Fourthly, some of my plates arrived with water and rust stains. I don't understand how this happens, since there is a thin Saran type film ontop the plates when you first get them. This must mean that the plates have somehow gotten wet during manufacturing process, but before the packaging process. This doens't interfere with the stamping process, but I just find it annoying to have rust and water marks on my plates.
Overall, these plates are dirt cheap (under a dollar for each plate), compared to Konad which are between $4-7 per plate, but you get what you pay for, and Bundle Monster plates definitely do NOT compare to the quality of Konad's.

title: Polished, Sleek, Modern!
text:
We have been remodeling our bathroom since we moved in last April, a few of the last touch up items we needed were towel racks and hand towel holders. The post is a nice length and appropriate design for hand towels, which are normally hung close to the sink for hand drying. The post has an upper piece to keep the towel in place and refrain from it falling after each use. Installation was a breeze, simply peel the sticker backing off of the 3M foam tape, wash the surface off where the adhesive will be applied and allow it to dry completely, when this is finished firmly press with two fingers on either edge the hook against the wall and hold for at least 30 seconds to allow full pressure and contact. This hook is perfect for a smaller towel or even a larger body towel, I like that I'm able to dry my towels off and continue using them until they are ready to be washed. The hook looks great in my bathroom and matches my already placed decor, the stainless steel is polished and sleek giving my bathroom modern accents. I am very pleased with the design and quality of the Lingstar hook.

title: A wonderful garden that you can plant in your nail art!
text:
I ordered these plates because I love stamping nails. I use the stamps for stamping my nails and also for testing out ideas for new nail art designs.

So finding a set of 5 plates that were well priced like this was amazing. I was thrilled to snap them up. The package was shipped extremely promptly and arrived very quickly after ordering. Everything was well packaged and safe. When I opened it up, everything was separated into their own little zip top bags. Each stamper and scraper were in their own bags and the plates were separated from them by another bag. I really appreciate this because the scrapers have metal blades and I always fret a bit that the plates will be scratched in transit.

First thing I noticed was the metal scrapers, and that was almost enough to drop the star rating. I despise metal scrapers. I have had them scratch up my plates before, so I won't use them. I used an old Starbucks card for scraping instead for this review.

The plates are all a little thin, but they don't bend all over the place, they don't warp or get misshapen through general handling. They do not have the backing of plastic coated cardstock like some plates do, so I absolutely recommend getting a plate storage device of some kind. I have a little binder style one and these plates fit easily into the sleeves.

I did test out all three stamping heads on the stampers that came with the plates. The stamping heads are very firm. VERY firm. They are not my favorite, however, they picked up well and transferred the images pretty easily most of the time. There is a learning curve with stamping and sometimes an image just doesn't pick up. I did experience that a few times, but I experience that with most plates at least once or twice. All of the images that I tried picked up very well with the stampers that came with the plates. I tried both unprimed and primed. I would recommend testing first and see how they pick up for you. I think mine would have been just fine with a quick wash in warm soapy water and not much else in the way of priming.

All the images that I tested out worked very well. I really love the goldfish and the frog images. There is a huge selection of plants and flowers, and it's not a preponderance of roses like with so many plates. I really love the ivy and there's an image of strawberry plants (no berries, just the leaves and a flower, I think.) There are quite a few butterflies, but not just one style. There are several styles of butterflies. So I really enjoyed the plates, they will definitely be regulars in my nail art.

The stampers won't be tossed, but they won't be my go to stampers. I like slightly softer stampers, and I admit a definite bias towards my clear jelly stamper. :)

Is this a good buy? Yes. The plates are beautifully engraved, and make for a lovely set either for a beginner or someone just looking to expand their collection of plates. There are a lot of images to choose from, and while the images are not full nail for someone with really long nails, they are full nail images for a more average length and a moderate length nail. Most images are about an inch tall, and I had no trouble filling a swatch nail with the frog image. If I have friends who are looking to start a stamping plate collection, they will be pointed here for sure because I really do like the plates and the images and the quality.

And THAT is why metal scrapers couldn't take away a star from the 5 star rating. Because I have a large collection of stamping plates and these are a fantastic addition. I can get rid of the metal scrapers and use my regular scrapers and no harm done.

I did receive these plates at a discount for consideration and review. However, this does not impact or affect my review in any way. This is my honest opinion on this item.

text:
Arrived ahead of time which was super cool! I was incredibly excited to try this product out after seeing the buzzfeed video with them using it.
When I first opened the package, I was a bit shocked at how big of a bottle it was but how it seemed like barely half was full. When attempting to squeeze is out it was very much like trying to get the last of a product out of a container just as you're about to run out of it. All air, very little inside.
I did a small test area just to see if there was any kind of crazy reaction and I didn't have any issues. Goes on, peels off, wash away any little flakes that don't peel with it. However, when I went back to do a full mask I noticed that even though I had totally sealed it up tight, within about 20 minutes a massive amount of the product had leaked into the lid. I cleaned it up so it didn't solidify and placed the bottle upside down, so the lid was facing up instead.
The full mask itself went on nice and easy, just like the test. When I peeled it off, I did notice my skin felt fresher but it didn't really pull anything out. I checked the peeled off mask itself and while it had plenty of little itty bitty hairs from my face, nothing really noticeable. I checked out problem areas in the mirror and they looked basically the same, maybe with some blackheads and things closer to the surface and drawn up so they could be removed. The effect was minimal though and pretty disappointing.
I'll finish it off since there isn't much left and there is no point in not using it, but I won't be buying any more after this.

text: I used to do a lot of nail stamping back in the day and cannot find my older plates for the life of me! I ordered this set because I loved the holiday designs and remembered how much fun these were. I like that this came with a clear silicon stamper. It is so much easier to see that you've picked up the design and where you are trying to place it. This also came with a thick sturdy scraper, about the size of a debit card. It actually scrapes quite nicely and doesn't scratch up the plate like other scrapers I have used in the past. With regular polish, this works very well but you have to work quick. With gel polish, you have to let the polish set into the design for about 20 seconds, scrap, let set another 20 seconds, then pick up the design. You also have to really know exactly where you want to place your design and instead of rocking back and forth, you firmly place down the stamp for the best, most crisp stamp. If not, with gel, it tends to be less crisp or smear. It's definitely a learning curve if you are working with gel. Still, this set works really well and I can do more designs rather than trying to hand paint details on. Love this nail stamping set!

The instructions state that to properly clean after brushing, you need to remove the brushead and rinse under running water.

PROS:
This model has a rubberized grip, 2 minute timer (I didn't brush long enough before), rechargeable, never experienced overheating, since using these brushes my dentist says my gums look great, small enough to get precision cleaning

CONS:
Will most likely need to replace unit every 2 years or so, expensive brusheads (keep an eye on Amazon sales) - I might put too much pressure on my brush but I have to replace a brushead every 2 months although the savings in dental bills make up for that!

title: Treat your face (or legs) to a classy shave
text: For quite a while i have wanted to experience an open comb razor, particularly since I have understood that they are more effective against multi-day growth. Sometimes i go four or five days, if not more, between shaves and, in general I prefer to use my butterfly razors because i can open, remove the blade, and clean them quicker than standard two and three piece DB razors. Also I have learned the hard way that one should not rush when unscrewing and reattaching the head pieces to the handle to avoid stripping the threads. So i approached my initial experience with the Shash open comb with more a little curiosity and anticipation. Well, i was not disappointed. It moves through the stubble with ease and a quick rinse in water removes the residue. I was pleasantly surprised with the ease and facility with which the razor travelled over my face. I must admit that I was very cautious the first time and even took precautions that I normally forego with other razors. I didnt spend much time on my chin and nose area which are my most problematic regions. For those I prefer to use smaller handled razors where I can have better control and access. But on those fairways which are a straight shoot downward to my chin bones, I was mowing the hair down like an Eastern European peasant harvesting grain. The razor also worked well on the straighaways from chin down to the neck.  It should be admitted that I have yet to put the razor to the ultimate test of a week-long beard growth, but i do not anticipate any increased difficulties with the later. The open comb facilitates easy cleaning whether rinsing in a bowl or under the faucet. As for the razor itself, it appears to be well constructed. I would guess it is a product of Germany which augurs well for precision instruments. It is probably the longest handled razor i own yet it functions well. It is reputed to be made of brass and chrome which should guarantee long life. The handle is striated enough to preclude slippage even when wet.  As a bonus it comes with three boxes of Astra blades (about 15 I believe) plus an alum stick and pre-shave oil. I can't vouch for the oil since I don't normally use it bit I can't see how it would hurt. And the entire ensemble is tidely packaged in a neat and attractive box. Certainly a fine addition to one's own toiletries collection and definitely something to consider for the upcomung gift season. Recommended.

title: It will leave your skin feeling soft and hydrated... down fall is how long they instruct you to leave on skin before rinsing.
text:
I have sensitive skin. I also have these small bumps where my body hair is coming through my skin's surface. The bumps are only bothersome because of appearance. I have a hard time using exfoliators because they end up irritating my skin. I love the properties that Coconuts possess and that is why I decided I would give Baebody's scrub a try.

This scrub has a very pleasant smell of coconut and almond. It has a similar texture to sugar, although the scrub has a wet feel to it because of the oils that are in it. The directions say to apply to clean damp skin. So obviously you would want to do this in the shower for a whole body scrub. The downside, and the reason for giving a 4 star and not 5 is that once you have massaged the scrub onto your skin you are then instructed to let the scrub sit until it dries (5-10 minutes). This is a time frame that really can not be utilized to shave your legs, or be done while conditioning your hair, you get to just stand there being cold. Also, I am a mother of a 2 year old boy... I am lucky to get 5-10 minutes to shower! It is difficult for me to use this product as directed in order to get the maximum benefits; however, there have been a couple occasions that I have been able to take my time in the shower and wait the 5-10 minutes. The way your skin feels on the surface isn't changed much by waiting out the time, If you use the scrub your skin is left feeling soft and hydrated. If you are able to wait the directed amount of time it will be worth it. Not only will your skin feel soft and hydrated, but if you let your skin really absorb the oils in the scrub then your skin is going to feel amazing for 4 or 5 days. If I am going to be applying the scrub I don't bother using my body wash. Instead I just use some shampoo to get my body clean because your going to be exfoliating anyways and the scrub has all the moisturizing power you need.

I use this scrub about once every 10 days or whenever my skin is really starting to feel "thirsty." I paid $1.95 to purchase this Baebody body scrub due to a discount that I received so that I could use it as I would normally in my everyday life and develop an honest opinion about it. I then take the time to leave a review detailing that opinion on Amazon in order to help shoppers know more about the product. I feel that it is very important to be honest and unbiased when leaving a review because it can have an impact on the decisions people make. I too rely on reviews that other post on Amazon when I am looking into products that I am considering purchasing even if I don't intend on buying the product on Amazon. There is no better feedback than that from actual customers and that is why I participate in reviewing products. The Baebody scrub will leave your skin feeling amazing, for how long depends on how long you are willing to let it dry before washing it off.

title: Shaves as good as a blade - if you use it right
text:
This is the second 7775X I have owned. The first lasted two years, but this after extensive travel all over the world. It does shave as well as a blade (I use one of those too now and then) if you use it right (see below)

Positives

1) Quick charging - less than an hour to charge.
2) Long lasting - I have used it 10 days without recharging - great if you travel.
3) Seems to prevent ingrown hairs - which is something I run into when I use a blade consistently. My face definitely breaks out much less when I use this razor versus a blade (and I own some expensive blade razors as backup!).
4) So long as you follow instructions (don't press down hard, but when you need to go over an area again, do it firmly) you won't get nicked. Nice when you are in a strange hotel in a strange time zone and waking up jet lagged but needing to look presentable for a meeting.

Negatives

1) A little expensive
2) The shaving lotion cartridges are also expensive - I would just buy a can of regular shaving Gel (eg Edge).
3) Constantly pressing the dispenser for more gel can be a pain in the neck, and you go through those cartridges quickly (one every 10 days at most). If I wanted to redesign this shaver, I would junk the shaving dispensor entirely - I now find it just another moving part with the hinged lid.
4) I wish Norelco had come up with a way for this razor to use a standard charger jack of some kind, as having another electrical cord when I travel (especially one that does not work with multiple corded adaptors such as I-go) means I don't take the cord unless I am gone more than 8-10 days.

To use this right, just buy regular shaving gel, put it on your face, wait 30 seconds for the gel to soften your beard, and go for it. This is the best way I have found to get a clean, smooth shave. Gel in a can also has the advantage of going on thickly (versus the Coolskin dispensor) and not drying up quickly. Also, having a can of the shaving gel when you travel (checked baggage of course) can also come in handy if your Norelco runs out of charge, and you need to switch to that backup Gillette you should have in your shaving kit (I travel with enough cords as it is).

title: An excellent soap, and much less tempermental than I thought it would be
text:
I've been trying out new shaving soaps, and this was the latest one after trying Tabac (really loved that one too). From all of the reviews I've seen here I thought it would be tempermental to work with, but it wasn't that bad at all. In fact, if you can get a good lather out of Williams shaving soap (and yes, it can be done), then lathering with Mitchell's Wool Fat is a snap by comparison.

The big thing to remember is that just like Williams and Tabac, this is a hard-milled, tallow-based soap, and unlike the glycerin-based soaps of Van Der Hagen or Colonel Conk, a tallow soap needs to be used with lots of water, and the hotter you can get that water, the better the lather and cushion will be.
The big secret to getting great lather when I use this soap-or any other tallow soap-is to fill the bowl it's in with boiling hot water until it's about 1/2inch over the soap and let it soak for at least 5 minutes before lathering. After that the soap is properly hydrated and will work very well with whatever brush you use in your daily routine, just be sure to dump out the water before you lather up.

Some people have compared the scent to Williams, and it definitely has a "clean" scent, but it's not nearly as "cleaning product-y" to my nose. My wife REALLY likes the scent a lot, too, so it's a winner in my book. Will definitely buy again.

It went on smoothly and after rubbing gently in circles around my eyes, it was absorbed into my skin and left a nice matte finish.  I have been using it twice a day as recommended, after I take my make up off at night and in the morning before getting ready for the day.  After just a few weeks, my wrinkles seem to have become finer and the dark circles have become noticeably lighter.  The serum feels cool upon application, and I feel that has really helped with the puffiness.  I look forward to the results in the months to come.  I'm going to keep on smiling and would recommend this product.

We've got a bit of experience in this house with magnetic eyeliner and lashes. We've tried super expensive ($75/pair), super cheap (Wish is NOT the place to go for lashes) and everything in between. My daughter has TTM and has no natural eyelashes, so magnetics are the ONLY type of lashes that work for here.

She liked the look of the lashes in this set. They weren't all over-the-top, super glam. There were quite a few pairs that she thought she could use for daily wear and even liked the look of "glam" pairs that were included for when she really wants to go all out. So it was HUGELY disappointing that there were NO MAGNETS on ANY of the pairs of lashes. She did try the eyeliner with lashes she already had, but wasn't very impressed with it either. It didn't seem to completely dry down and had a slightly tacky feel even after waiting about 10 minutes. I thought maybe they had mixed up the order and sent her regular lashes & lash glue, but it wasn't tacky ENOUGH to hold a lash in place. Overall, it was a fail for her. Which is disappointing because she quite liked the style of the lashes offered in this set.

title: OMG! I'm in LOVE!!!
text:
Ok...I'm going to try to not write a novel here, but I am sooo in love with these polishes!!! I read a ton on reviews on these peel off polishes and finally chose these not expecting a whole lot. I have 100% no complaints!!! But I will say that I guess it all depends on what you are wanting out of your nail polish. If you are wanting it to last like it lasts on artificial nails... this is not for you. If you are wanting options and to not have to deal with nail polish remover...THIS IS FOR YOU!!!

I have loved painting my nails and having polished nails since a kid. I've always hated nail polish remover. I have thin nails and can't change my polish often because nail polish remover dries my nails out and makes them even weaker and it stinks...even nail polish stinks for that matter.
To make the polish last I've always added a top coat about every day or two and I've learned how to do touch ups that hardly show when the polish on tip of the nail (natural nails) chipped or wore away, so that I didn't have to use acetone any more often than necessary. But it was really self defeating because the more polish I had on, the more acetone I had to use to remove it.
So anyway...I got these little gems in...they are small....but then again, when you compare the price to buying regular polish ( I buy OPI normally ) and the fact that you are getting several colors of these for the price you'd pay for 1 or 2 bottles of decent regular polish, it's not a bad deal at all.
I tried them right away and
#1...they are hardly smell at all! I don't smell them unless I actually hold my nails or the bottle to my nose to smell them.
#2...the polish went on fine. It's a little thick, but it settles down smooth as it dries.
#3 I love some of the colors and some will be just for having fun, but they are fun t play with. 5 colors are opaque and 4 are transparent, so they are fun mixing and matching. I like using the transparent ones as top coats on the opaque ones.
#4 They lasted about 3 days with no chips and very very little edge wear (with the daily addition of a top coat for shine) until I couldn't stand it any longer and had to try to peel them off. Some of the reviews said they were hard to peel off, but I had no problem at all. And all but one came off in one full piece! Amazing!!! So easy and NO ACETONE!!! And the other thing I like is that with regular polish, I would sometimes try and peel of as much as I could before using the acetone and some would come off but my nail always seemed super dry under the polish even when it was peeled off. That is not the case with these at all. My nails were not dry at all. They were still healthy and not dry at all!!!
Oh and the BONUS ....since they peel off, any polish that gets on to your skin peels off easy too after it dries. :)

title: I'm happy with this toothbrush...
text:
I wanted to shop around for an electric toothbrush because, despite my best efforts to brush at least twice a day and floss, I still felt like my teeth weren't getting clean enough. My battle involves bleeding gums, which requires that much more cleaning power in between your teeth in order to get rid of the bacteria that's keeping them inflammed. The Vitality brush does a pretty decent job of reaching deep into the surfaces and the spaces of your teeth to get them clean. Licking my teeth, they feel pretty smooth, too.

The toothbrush is recharged with an adapter unit. Remove it from the base, put on your toothpaste, and turn the unit on. The agitation has a little bit of splashback to it, so minimize it by brushing the back of your teeth first and then moving to the front; then the outside surfaces, then the inside. Also, the brush head is fairly small compared to standard brushes. I thought it was a little distracting at first until I started brushing to pay more attention to individual teeth rather than sweeping broadly across them. Finally, I thought the timer was a digital read-out; your brush will vibrate a couple of short pulses to let you know that two minutes is up. It was disorienting at first. I thought the brush was out of power, but I figured it out.

It's a solid investment, and the good thing is that it's relatively affordable and still an effective device compared to more expensive powerbrushes on the market.

text:
I have so been wanting to get one of these stainless steel makeup palettes and this one by MOKALE is just perfect for my needs! I really didn't need it for the purpose of a "palette" used for mixing makeup colors, I wanted it for 1) a place to squeeze out makeup products that come in tubes, 2) a place to portion out eye liner / eyebrow products that come in jars that dry out ever so quickly because you leave them open too long while you are applying the product and 3) to have an easy to maintain and carry with me portable surface that I can keep sanitary to use my makeup as described in 1 and 2, but also to lay the ends of my brushes / applicators as I'm using them. The spatula type tool makes it easy to get products out of the little jars I use. I use this at home and when I travel, and I just clean it with a microfiber cloth and also with an alcohol free hand sanitizer product everyone other day. And it isn't so big that it takes up a lot of the limited space on my bathroom vanity. This was a very good choice to add to my makeup bag. I very highly recommend the MOKALE Stainless Steel Cosmetic Palette.

I appreciate the opportunity to purchase the MOKALE Stainless Steel Cosmetic Palette at a discount and provide an unbiased review of my experience using it.

The diffuser and the remote work well and it has a very cute look with a wood grain base. The colors are very bright and pretty when lit.
Thank you Depree for working with me and I am enjoying my new free 400ml diffuser just as much!

title: For the price and overall result - you can't beat it!
text: I will give this keratin treatment five stars.  It arrived very promptly and no issues with bottle leakage.  I started by washing my hair with Dawn dish detergent (as noted by another seller who provided feedback), did NOT condition and blew it completely dry.  I then separated my hair into four sections and added the solution to each section separately while combing through with a fine tooth comb.  I did my best to get as close to the roots as possible and saturate all strands without 'over saturating'.  I chose to leave the solution in my hair and dry it immediately following the application.  I dried it straight on the highest heat setting.  Once this step was completed I flat ironed while going over sections 3-4 times.  I did this step on a Wednesday evening and washed it out the following Saturday.  It did feel a bit heavy, needed hot iron touch up each day and smelled a bit like pickles.  But I found the cons totally worth it once I washed and styled my hair on Saturday.  It looks and feels healthy, is FAR less susceptible to frizz and is holding up quite nicely.  This is huge given that I have curly - frizzy hair AND happen to live in humid Florida.  For the price and overall result - you can't beat it!

I love trying different lotions, particularly those that have nice fragrance, but when I received this set, I almost threw it away! I the bottle, the smell of the lotion is horrible - I found it to have a strong, artificial scent similar to alcoholic spirits. I decided to give it a try so that I could write an accurate review. The "lotion" is quite thin, much more watery than any other moisturizer I have used. Just to spread on my elbows requires at least 10 pumps from the tiny bottle. The good news is that once on the skin, the distasteful fragrance does not last; I didn't really detect much scent at all after that, but there may have been a faint hint of rose in the dry-down. The moisturization was adequate, nothing more.

I do like the Nail & Cuticle Oil, which comes in a little roller bottle and actually DOES have a rose scent. But this set is absolutely NOT worth the cost, especially given that the lotion is likely to be completely gone after just a few weeks of daily use. Not recommended.

NOTE: At least one other reviewer ("Jam Blaster") mentioned the same issue with the lotion smelling bad and gave this product just 1-star as a result.

UPDATE, 2/1/21:
Since I don't like the scent of this product, I decided to try it on my feet. Despite the lotion being very thin, I actually found it to work quite well on my feet! I put it on in the a.m., then put on socks; by the end of the day, my feet definitely felt soften and smoother. I think the product is too expensive to purchase for this reason alone, but it does work, and so I increased my rating to 3-star.
