title: It may be good for peole with thin to somewhat thick hair
text:
I have thick, coarse..wavy hair. I have REALLY thick coarse...wavy hair. My hair is not that long, but since I have so much of it...when it starts to grow past a certain length..it can longer pomp up and slick straight the way i would want it to. I have tried Layrite (strongest hold), Imperial (strongest hold), American crew (strongest hold), Suavecito (regular & firme/strong hold)...I've also used some Murray's but that s*** just brought the waves out even more.

JS sloan has a very strong smell that I am not fond of...this product is definitely not worth me buying again. It may be good for peole with thin to somewhat thick hair...if you have really thick hair & coarse wavy hair then i'm sure you must use an extra amount of pomade to try and give the look you would want...but this product has an overpowering smell...i feel like my coworkers can smell it when I'm talking to them.

I've wanted to try other pomades, but when I hear that people with thick coarse wavy hair has had better experiences with the pomades that I tried and did not like..i'd figure there was no use in wasting my money.

I always keep on going back to Suavecito firme/strong hold.

It's the only thing that works best for my hair and gives the look (The closest as possible) that I would want to achieve.

for people with such hair, you must come to the realization that as your hair gets longer, it may become more difficult to achieve a hair style that's more suitable for people with straight hair (thin or thick).

Even so, I'd recommend Suavecito firme/strong hold...it's a very good price for a good product.

Also--I noticed that some people reviewed it by saying they had thick hair with great experiences...be advised that that not everyone has the same level of hair thickness as yours...to them it might be thick...but to you it might not..

I feel that I may have a thicker set of coarse/wavy hair...I'm going back to Suvaceto.

title: The facial cleanser is great! Body wash was meh...
text:
When I bought this product, I received both the cell stimulating body wash and the facial cleansing creme and I feel differently about each product so I will write my review accordingly.

Body Wash (2/5 Stars):

I actually bought this because I needed a new body wash. I was hoping that the mint and argan oil would make my skin feel refreshed and very clean, but it really didn't. The body wash leaves a filmy sensation after I use it, and the mint scent/sensation does not pack the amount of power I was hoping for when I initially bought this item. I used the body wash for exactly one week before I put it in my cabinet to gather dust, as my back-up "I forgot to buy extra body wash" bottle. I really didn't like it much.

Facial Cleanse (4/5 Stars)

The facial cleanse was just the freebie that came with the body wash I wanted, so I wasn't really expecting to replace my usual face soap. I was so disappointed with the body wash, I almost didn't try it at all but I am glad I did. The facial cleanser delivered the minty sensation that I wish the body wash had. It was reinvigorating and made my skin feel both clean and fresh, without leaving any residue. I definitely have kept this product in my shower and would definitely consider buying it on its own because I enjoy how gently it cleans and how well it removes my make-up at the end of the day.

Overall, I rated it 3/5 Stars because of the average review of both products, but I will never buy the body wash again; the facial cleanser definitely made up for the purchase for me.

text: Of all the wigs I have, this one is the softest. (I don't have any real human hair wigs) It is luxury and soft like mink. It is actually the color of a mink, too. Dark brown with a hint of red. The wave and bounce is nice. Thick, realistically long, and a full head of generous hair.  The fit is good with adjustable straps on the inside. The thing is tho...the thickness just looks a little fake at the top with a center part and no bangs or shorter pieces in the front. Yes, I believe I could trim it or pluck it or something but I am inexperienced at that and I never have done that to my wigs. I have washed them and gently brushed them and trimmed one piece out of the eye area, but this one would need more work than I know how to do in the front and center to make it look natural. It is a single uniform colour, which makes it look a little fake to me. I think this one looks great from the back and side and on the bed just lying there next to my other wigs, as I was trying my collection on today to compare. This one stood out as silky and luxury and rich and deep in colour because I mostly go blonde. But it just doesn't look real when on (me? Maybe it's just me?). I'm sorry. But I still like it. The length is fun and it feels so good and soft around my shoulders. It might be an "around the house fun wig" just for myself to feel happy to bake a pie or something, but I doubt I'd go to the store shopping with it.

title: A convert!
text:
I had a Norelco 6800 series shaver before this one, and it did great for me. However, my wife wanted to use it ... and I made her promise to let me buy a new "good shaver" if she took my 'old reliable'.

So I bought this shaver. I have always been intrigued by the idea of a wet shave, since shaving 'wet' always shaves better.

This shaver delivers on the promise and it does it extremely well. I use it with shave gel, and it gets closer and cleaner than any foil shaver or any other electric I have EVER used. That's saying a lot, since I've tried almost every kind out there that there is to try, starting WAY back when Norelco only made the two-head shaver.

A big Plus to this shaver is that you can rinse it out right away and hang it up with the little strap provided. It hangs head down, and it dries out just fine between shaves for me. The stand they provide with it doesn't make you fiddle about with the strap to disconnect it; rather it just drops into the charging stand to recharge.

To say I'm happy with this shaver is to understate it. I have MUCH less of a 5 o'clock shadow, and I am very happy with the way I look when I leave for work. To me, clean and neat is professional, and this shaver enhances the look.

title: Best bang for your buck
text:
I have used just about every type of hair extensions out there & tape ins are my favorite! I always purchased my hair from the salon so I knew the quality was up to par...but it's EXPENSIVE...I mean $600-$700 expensive. I kept those for a year each time because of the price. I finally broke down & gave these a try & I was pleasantly surprised. The quality is good...not great, but good. They are so affordable that I can get a new set every other time which is also a plus! $120(for 2 packs) is way easier to budget than $600!

Some pointers:
-wash with purifying shampoo. I know that's a no no for extensions but trust me, I've bought several sets & this is the best way to get off that thick coating they put on them to make them extra shiny... it makes them not look as natural.
-After shampooing, use a deep conditioner & let them set for at least 20mins.
-Remove the tape that comes on them & retape. Ok, TBH, I haven't used the tape that comes on them but the reviews I read scared me & I didn't want to chance them falling out or harming my hair. Sally's brand is ok to use & won't come out until you're ready.

Hope this helps.

title: Great for under the eyes
text:
I bought this powder specifically to use under my eyes. What makes it different from most loose powders is that it contains cornstarch, giving it a smooth finish without being too drying. The only other loose powders I've been able to find that contain cornstarch are the Ben Nye Luxury Powders, and the Col-Lab Set the Stage loose powder from Sally's, which is sold on their website only. I've tried samples of the Ben Nye Luxury Powders in a few colors and liked them, but decided to try something different, and a little cheaper.

I apply this powder in one of two different ways. If I want a minimal makeup look, I'll use my ELF blush brush to pat the powder under my eyes, tapping off any excess from the brush before application. If I want my undereyes to look especially smooth, and my deep tear troughs less noticeable, I use a dry foam wedge sponge to pick up the powder, then stamp it under my eyes, and gently brush off the excess after a minute or two. It does not make my undereye area look or feel dry. Sometimes I use it all over my face, if I'd rather not use my usual matte pressed powder. I have fair skin, so the white color appears translucent on my skin, but I'm not sure how someone with deeper skin would fare.

Because I use this powder sparingly, this jar should last me a long time!

title: Absolutely the best curl activator on the market
text:
I've been using this for well over a decade, as my go to curl activator. I agree that it blows everything else out of the water. The secret is to dip a fingertip in, and just get a dab, a small dab. Wipe it on the palm of the other hand, then rub your hands together until it has foamed a little, which you'll know by its turning white. Then smooth it over your hair. Rub your hands together again, to move what's left to your fingers, then run them through a little. Apply Curl Keeper (Original) or a gel lightly. Then scrunch. Correct your part, if necessary. Let you hair dry fully before you touch it again.

Unlike the curl activators with epsom salts in them, the Boots Curl Crème will refresh your curl when misted (with plain water).

Thank you for reading my review. I hope you found it helpful.

title: "Sea" Mist is a Misnomer
text:
*Sigh*
This product received rave reviews, so I was very excited to purchase and test it out.
My hair is naturally very wavy. If the wave doesn't have product, it isn't tame. So, most mornings I dry/straighten it to avoid looking like a wild banshee at work.
However, I recently moved to Florida and because of the humidity, my waves are being a bit more cooperative. That being said, a product like this that would help hold the wave throughout the day and tame the "wildness" is desirable. Unfortunately, this has not worked for me as it is advertised.
There isn't enough salt to hold the hair in place. Instead of a subtle stiffness to hold the 'beach wave', my hair appeared a droopy, greasy mess that looks like I'd slept in a frying pan (with leftover bacon grease) rather than the just-off-the-surf look that I was anticipating.
Everyone's hair is different, so perhaps this product works better for others. My hair is long and thick. I would think that this may work better for people with shorter hair where gravity isn't fighting with the product all day.
Okay, so why did I give this more than one star? IT SMELLS AMAZING! If anything, I'll be using this as a perfume rather than a hair product. Seriously, I can't get enough of the coconutty wonderfulness in the bottle.

text:
Having used the disposable razors now for 25 plus years i decided to try an electric razor again, given the fact your considered a terrorist if you have shaving cream cans in your luggage while traveling, the electric razor seemed like a viable solution. After much reviewing i decided to go with the 9160xl at christmas, it was almost march before i recharged it, and after a few days of use, i was used to how it works, its much faster to complete a shave, trim my mustache and gote, and off i go with no worries of water on my shirt, or shaving cream to wipe off. You can also shave while walking around as your not tied to the sink and running water to clear off the razor. The key to any battery operated device is to properly charge it when you first place it on the bathroom sink. And do not return it to the charger until the shaver shows low battery, that way you keep the battery life good. And yes its quiet. Does not sound like a small airplane nor does it make a high pitched whinning noise. Comments about not having power or cutting of skin are ridiculous, i have never had a problem, all i do is clean it out each use, and rinse the head out when the razor indicates it wants a water cleaning. Simple as that, follow the instructions, and youll be fine. Remember the key to the battery as that is the life of the razor, same rules apply to your cell phone.
Good luck.

First I would like to say that this is the best Norelco I've used, and I have been using many of them over the last 30 years. However, the cleaning device is poorly conceived and cheaply executed. The biggest weakness is that it is not a "smart" charger, and does not stop charging when full. This shaver is actually a lithium battery, which means run it all the way down after it's first full charge, then keep it topped off, like a laptop. The cleaner liquid itself is super. I tried different soapy water and alcohol solutions and all of them resulted in worse shaves.
My protocol is to rinse the shaver under water right after shaving, to get rid of most of the hairs. Then I dip it briefly into a small container with the cleaning solution, then rinse it again. Works like a charm, and the cleaner device went to the trash. BTW, this is now a clearance item, so shop around.

You simply take a wooden cutical pusher and gently slip it under the gel nail and slowly push the glue- which feels like a glue dot- upwards to wards the tip of nail. Do not pull it off. Because when I did it created scales on my nails like it was stressed or might break. Be patient it really only takes 5 minutes total. The Nails underneath should be undamaged. I now can grow my nails much longer because anything that my nails knock into are first protected by the gel. I do my normal house work. Although I almost always use gloves before washing dishes. I get so many compliments! All of a sudden I have stunning French manicures all the time. It looks high maintenance but the best beauty secrets are simple!

title: Contains “Preservative” that Irritates Sensitive Skin—Burns Eye Area
text:
This face wash by Whitney Jean is a clear gel with no smell so I had high hopes for it being safe for sensitive skin/areas. Unfortunately when washing near my eyes as it’s advertised as “makeup remover” it irritates my eyes a bunch so much to where it burned. It took over half an hour for the stinging/burning sensation to completely go away.

title: Favorite Palette Ever!!
text:
I purchased this product in a store, but I am such a fan I had to write a review. Ever since I purchased this palette, it has been my go-to for everyday makeup. I am fair-skinned with dark hair and hazel eyes, and the colors are perfect. I don't always use every color in a palette and I don't always place the colors as directed, but in this case, Stila knows what they are talking about!

The large color on the left is your all-over base, and I apply that first. Next, I go to the top right corner and apply this grayish color from crease to browbone. Third, I take the darkest color and place it quite heavily (but narrowly) in the crease and a little in the corner and lash line. Next, I put the highlight (lightest) color just under the brow and also outside the inner corner of the eye. Finally, I put the shimmery gold-like color in the middle across the lid and blend all the colors with a blending brush. I use the darker blush normally, but use the light one as a highlight if I want the added effect. I love that when I am doing my makeup on the run, I only have to grab this one container and my makeup brushes (I have the EcoTools Eye Enhancing Duo Brush set with four tips on two brushes, so even there you don't have to take as much with you).

The quality of the product is excellent and it blends well. Other than the darkest brown, the eyeshadow pigments are not super intense, so you can go light or apply more for a deeper intensity.

text:
I've used a few SFX colors and have never been disappointed!

• Cupcake Pink: love this color so much, but definitely needs a very pale base (closest to white blonde, and porous, as possible) or it'll turn a salmon/peach color.
• Atomic Pink: the absolute best hot pink! Deep, electric, and long lasting.
• Sonic Green: more blue-based than I originally realized, I loved the green-teal color. Perfect mix of green with a bit of blue and fades almost minty. It covered over orange bleached hair well.
• Blue Velvet: a gorgeous deep denim blue that starts out deceptively dark and begins to lighten after a few washes. Easily applied over orangey bleached hair.

These are direct, veggie-based dyes, so it does NO harm to leave in your hair long. The longer you leave it in, the more difficult it may be to remove later when you want to change colors, but it'll also ensure you don't need to touch it up for awhile. I easily went over a month on the above colors without needing to refresh.

My hair was damaged at a hair show a few months ago while I was a hair model for Trillion Tones. After they fried it, I decided to keep heat off my hair as much as possible. I've used them twice and each time my hair held the curl well for 3+ days since I slept with a silk scarf on at night. I highly recommend these if you like tight curls and want to keep heat off your hair. I start the curl closer to the scalp then wrap the ends around more like you would use a curl wand instead of wrapping from the bottom. I'm sure starting at the bottom works as well, but I wanted to be clear how I got these types of curls in the photos.
The first photo with the star earrings is day one of curls. The piggy buns are day two, and the brushed out curls are day three.

text: I use this for easy clean up when painting my nails and doing nail art by just brushing some around the cuticles letting it dry down, then painting my nails and  peeling off after. I actually decided to take this product and transfer it to an empty nail polish bottle to make application easier as the container is some what large for what I need to use this for and can get messy easily or spill.  If you are going to transfer this product the best way I recommend to do it is thru an oral syringe  (the kind used to give infants medicine), usually you can find one for cheap at your local pharmacy. Transferring this product was also very easily and practically mess free and clean up was a breeze since all you have to do is just wait for it to dry and then peel it off! I would definitely recommend this product to anyone looking for easy clean up for nail art but doesn't want to pay the crazy prices these polish makers/companies want for one tiny bottle. I think the fact that I didn't wash my face meant that my skin had a small layer of oil on it for protection against staining and irritation. A little oil also will not hinder the hair coloring process.

I used the included application brush, putting very small amounts of the dye on the brush and applying it in light, careful strokes. The movement is like sketching in a sketchbook instead of drawing solid lines all at once, and I did not have a pile of dye on my brows at the end.

I know that with my hair, I need to leave dye on it for a long time, so I left this on for 10 minutes. I rinsed the dye off with cool water to avoid opening up my pores. I checked my brows and thought they could be a little darker, so I re-applied and left on for another 5-10 mins. Total of 15-20 mins.

Finally, I washed it off for good with a gentle unscented soap, using my fingernails to help get all the dye off and exfoliate the skin underneath and around my brows, so I was left with no stains.

And that was that. I have eyebrows now! I can even TOUCH them! I can't believe I never tried this before, this will be a staple in my life now.

text:
I am really impressed by this guide to Yokosuka, which written by a Navy spouse who was recently stationed in Yokosuka, Japan with her husband and kids. The guide is packed full of really useful information (IN ENGLISH!!!) about local restaurants, shopping, entertainment, beauty/health, schools, and practical tips about living in and around Yokosuka. I haven't seen this much English information about Yokosuka in one place...not even on web blogs or review sites. I have lived in Yokosuka for nearly three years, and there is a lot in this guide that I previously wasn't aware of because of the cultural nuances and language barriers that challenge us "gaijin".

A lot of my friends in Yokosuka have this book, and their relatively new copies are dog-eared because they are really USING the guide to explore the areas in and around Yokosuka. This book is very family-oriented, since there is a lot of focus on restaurants and fun stuff that doesn't include the local bar scene...which is a nuance rather hard to find online. However if you're new to town and looking for a watering hole, there are tons of restaurants, izakayas, and karaoke places listed in this guide which have a much better drink selection and atmosphere than most bars in the Honch.

I hope that future editions of this book will include photos, but I'm incredibly pleased with this guide, and only wish that I had more time here to explore it ALL!!

I have a big fluffy beard. Unfortunately in the winter, it more resembles a brillo pad in texture and I sometimes look like a homeless person.

This oil works well to condition and treat your beard, and the skin underneath. I apply it right out of the shower after towel drying my beard while it is still damp. I use three squirts of oil, placed in my palm, run my hands together and massage into my beard. It keeps my beard soft and supple all day, and treats the skin underneath to stop dryness and itching.

I almost thought of trimming my magnificent beard down because it was so rough, and it was itchy, this is allowing me to continue to grow it.

My beard hair is soft, manageable, and free of knots.

The glass bottle is heavy duty, so you can take it when you travel.

My ONLY complaint is the cost. It's pretty expensive, but I think a bottle would last you 2 months or so, but it's still a pretty hefty price to pay for a soft and manageable beard, free of itchiness.

text:
So you may be interested in this product to be hairless below the belt. Fortunately the product actually works.
The creators actually put alot of thought into this.

The wooden sticks are used to spread the cream on the hairy area. I found it easier to use latex gloves, but you do not want to rub the cream in your skin. You want to coat the hair at the root. Never use your bare hands, it will smell like the products for hours.

Depending on where you put the cream and your sensitivity will determine on the time the cream stays on. Groin is mostly 8-10 minutes I would say. Any other less sensitive areas would be 4-5 minutes.

When the time is up you will use your glove to remove the hair. I think this is the most genius part of the system. The hand glove is the most versatile tool for hard to reach areas. It is always easiest to perform the task in the shower. When you are done, just rinse and wash with soap.

Overall:
Nair for men has the same results. However, Nair for men smells very foul. This product does have a lighter odor to it.I would recommend cleaning the glove with detergent after each use. Surprising hair does not cling on as baldly has I expected on the glove so washing should not be an issue. I think this is a must buy. If you are on a budget, then nair is the way to go.

title: 3.5 stars
text:
Philips Norelco Arcitec 1090 is my first electric shaver ever and I've been using it for 7 months now. I had been pondering on whether to take Brown Pulsonic or Philips Norelco for quite a while, when ultimately it was probably the looks of the latter that prevailed so I ended up with it.

All in all it is a pretty good shaver, but not great. Perhaps I should start off with mentioning that I am NOT one of those with a thick and bushy beard, so I usually shave every other day. Normally I spend about 5 mins on shaving. At times my skin gets slightly irritated, which might result in light-red patches under my chin. Most of the time it's fine though, and I can get a decent shave. However, not always is the shave that clean. Sometimes certain hairs (esp. on the side - around my jaw and around my whiskers, or under my chin) will be left out, so I'd have to trim them separately with the trimmer.

Oh yes, the infamous trimmer. It really is more of an aesthetic feature on the shaver than a tool serving its real purpose. It's just too small and inconvenient. At times I'm having difficulties accessing parts of my face with it, unless I took off the shaving heads.

The shaver also comes with a neat LED display that shows how many minutes of shaving time there is remaining. Great. This was one of the features that won me over about this shaver. But what I resent is that it's inaccurate. Well it does accurately show how many minutes you have shaved, but when it comes down to 0 mins, one would expect the battery is about to die, yet usually I can still squeeze several shaves out of it (which means additional 10-15 mins). In the instructions manual it says that after 3 charges it should display the remaining shaving time accurately, but I've already charged it at least 5 times now, and no difference. The highest shaving time is supposedly 65 mins. What is rather curious about all this is that on each charge I've actually been gaining additional minutes to the proposed 65 mins, so the numbers have gotten up to 81 mins on my most recent charge. I would be perfectly happy with getting those additional minutes if that means that the shaver will eventually display the time properly so that if 0 mins is remaining, then 0 it really is. (Perhaps once I've have charged it 10 or more times the display will finally get normal, as suggested in the manual? If it does, I might as well mention it here.)

Anyway, speaking of the battery, this is one of the features I am really content with. I can get numerous shaves out of one charge; therefore, there's nothing but praise on this part.

I also like the fact that the shaver is easy to wash. You simply open the shaving heads and rinse it.

One thing that I as well dislike though, is the On/Off button's silver paint peeling off already after only a couple of weeks' use. But alright, that's already going into details now.

Pros:
- attractive looks
- long battery life
- light and not too loud
- easy to wash

Cons:
- trimmer
- doesn't always shave ALL the hairs clean
- sort of inaccurate LED display
- paint peeling off of the On/Off button

If I could, I would give this shaver 3.5 stars. However, for a 4, I guess it will still at least have to get the LED display straight. So if after 10 or so charges it does, then I am giving it a 4. We shall see.

title: Fine for Home Use; Not Professional
text:
I wanted a Nail Display Stand for the same reason others do; to hold full cover false nails in place while they're being polished and decorated with various nail art elements.

Nail stands are small by necessity; they have to be small enough so when a nail is affixed to one, it can be slid into a UV/LED nail lamp to cure gel polish and any UV/LED activated glue used to attach embellishments to the nails without scraping the ceiling of the lamp.

These Nail Display Stands (both the acrylic bar and crystal) work perfectly well for that purpose.

Nail display stands are also used by some professional nail techs/artists to display samples of their work at their place of business.

Clients prefer to select a design for their nails from displays of finished nails showcasing the designs offered by a nail tech/artist instead of a portfolio of still photos. Photos may not reproduce colors accurately, and can be edited to eliminate evidence of sloppy workmanship.

These Nail Display Stands should not be purchased for that purpose. The metal dots on the acrylic strip to which the five magnetized stands attach weren't glued on straight, so the stands won't form a straight line and won't be equidistant from each other.

The metal dot atop the crystal was also glued off-center.

So, while these Nail Display Stands are perfectly serviceable for home use, they simply aren't good enough if you're a professional nail tech/artist wanting to showcase your best work to clients.

The description for this product states that it is non-toxic. According to the back of this box it is VERY toxic! Keep it out of reach of children and pets and lock it up when not in use! text: I bought these at the recommendation of a friend and I LOVE THEM! For background, I am very low maintenance makeup-wise and have pretty minimal knowledge. I didn't have anything going on so I left them on all day just to test them out and see how durable they are. I took a nap in these. I wore them for 10+ hours before they started to detach a bit on the inside corners. I'm so impressed they lasted this well with no prep at all. To increase wear I recommend adding a primer first before putting on the eyeliner. Also the included instructions say to attach the lashes while the eyeliner is still wet but I think it works better if you let it dry first. I love how easy these are to use and I think the different sizes are great for different occasions. (The ones pictured were mid-size, there were longer and shorter ones in the pack).

title: great shaver, cleaning system superfluous
text:
This is my 4th Norelco, going back quite a few years. My last one was not very good, although the first two were great. The 8160 shaves very close and can handle a two day growth. How long an electric razor stays sharp is very related to how clean it is kept, as hair in the heads will dull the blades faster. To that end, Norelco ships this razor with a motorized stand to clean the razor heads. Basically what it does is submerge the razor in the cleaning fluid and turn it on and off occasionally. So you need not buy the XLCC, just buy the 8160 XL. You can submerge the razor in fluid yourself and turn it on and off a few times to do the same thing, and not have to worry about having space to store the stand. I'm experimenting with making my own cleaning fluid, which as far as I can tell is distilled water with a small amount of glycerine and a bit of an additive such as photo-flo which breaks the surface tension of the water so it will drain right off.

One huge improvement over my prior Norelcos is the ability to rinse the razor throroughly with hot water. It does an excellent job of cleaning the razor, and then the fluid bath is only really needed to condition the heads. You can also buy a silcone spray which lubricates the heads to have them wear better. So save some money but make sure the razor you buy is washable and water tight. I highly recommend the razor itself.

title: My Favorite!
text:
Near the beginning of the pandemic I saw these bottles next to the checkout lane at Walgreens and bought one. It quickly became my new favorite hand cleaner!

First use was odd, it took around forty seconds for the soap to dry, feeling sticky like honey until it dried. I have no running water so I have been relying on hand sanitizer for several years. While this would likely work better, without the after effect when using water, I am happy with it even without water.

This soap has a very pleasant, natural smell. It is viscous in a good way that feels like it is grabbing debris from my hands while cleansing. It does not have the stinging sensation nor the odor of most hand sanitizers.

This opportunity to purchase bundles of this product at a reasonable price was much appreciated. title: Love these!!
text: I really liked how these locs looked, when I finished.  They were flexible and super-light-weight, so they weren't too heavy on my head, once they were all installed.  They have a few golden strands that didn't look tacky, and really made them pop.  It took me about 10.5hrs to do them, because I did them myself, and it was my first time doing them.  I was able to wear them for about 6wks, before they had to come out (this is through no fault of the product-- people are generally supposed to go 6-8wks with them, and my hair is pretty silky, so it doesn't hold braids well... after the 5th week, they started slipping down, and I had to randomly do touch-ups to keep them looking nice).  The only criticism I have for this product, is that it would be nice If they came with a crochet hook, instead of random false lashes.  I haven't used the false lashes, but I really needed that crochet hook.  They aren't expensive (about $1.97, I think)- and your local beauty supply store should have them-- but it was an inconvenience to have to go out and get one. Also, the locs are really small and thin, so  you have to braid your hair really small to pull the hair through the middle with the hook (which is the best method for these locs).  You can also unwrap them a little and then re-wrap them  around the braids, but they aren't as neat that way and also get fuzzier when you do that. Overall, I got tons of compliments on this style and I really loved how they looked on me.  I only need 2 packs to do my whole head, and I have plenty left over! So, for the price, the quality, and the results, this product is definitely worth it!

title: Very good with limitations
text:
I've owned this toothbrush for nearly a year now and have no problems. I do, however, recognize the limitations of the design. If you expect to be able to rinse off the handle or submerge this toothbrush, you will be one of the many disappointed reviewers. Now, I owned two previous sonicare toothbrushes and I was never really happy with the life of the internal batteries. This is the reason I decided to go with this unit and I have not regretted my decision. My 12 year old daughter has also had this toothbrush for almost a year now and NO problems. While I do believe there could be inconsistencies in quality control, I think one can work around these shortfalls.

Here's how I believe I've managed to keep my sonicare running.
1. I don't put the handle under water, only the part that goes in my mouth
2. I ALWAYS make sure to place a little vasoline on the O-Ring when I replace the batteries
3. I fling the water off the brush after I rinse the end off.
4. I don't leave the brush standing up. This prevents any residual water from running down the handle. I always leave the brush laying out flat/horizontal.

Now, I realize one shouldn't have to do all this stuff to keep the brush working properly but, for me, it's a small inconvenience considering I have the ability to change the batteries.

Bottom line. I really like my toothbrush but the design is not bullet proof.

title: Ridiculously overpriced, but the performance is decent.
text:
I am conflicted about this product, same as I am with the sister shampoo. I think it's a great product in terms of quality and performance; I really like that it's sulfate free and not filled with a bunch of additives. I have noticed that my hair is very soft as a result of using this mask, so I will give credit where credit is due in that regard. It smells good, and it hydrates well, which is what it promises to do. I have no qualms with the performance, packaging, concept, or marketing of the product.

I am docking two stars, however, for the price point. I am all for luxury products and I am happy to drop money on products that work. However I think that the price is grossly inflated for the performance of the product. While it's a nice product, it's nowhere NEAR to being a $32 hair mask. With prices like that you're definitely in the middle of high end, luxury pricing for haircare products. To give you a few examples you could be purchasing Bumble & Bumble, Oribe, R+Co, and Kerastase for a similar price. I think for a mask that is going to be used regularly you need to offer a reasonable price for the product, especially given the fact that there are stronger, higher performing luxury products on the market. I also think that the packaging and the container is a bit cheap looking, considering this is a $32 product. If I'm buying something so expensive I expect it to have some really nice packaging. I understand that they are meant to look like yogurt containers, however I think that it's a bit silly to have a nice cardboard packaging on the outside yet leave the container for the product itself looking so bare and unappealing.

While this is a good mask and I think it performs well, I don't see myself repurchasing this at the price it's currently listed at. I think that for the amount of product you receive (a small amount, especially for the price) a more reasonable cost would be $20.

Disclaimer: I purchased this item at a discount in exchange for my honest review.

title: coming from someone whose had pro 28 full body laser removal treatments and 50 hrs of electrolysis
text:
Needless to say i have xp with hair removal. I was never really a super hairy but loved the feeling of being totally hairless from head to toe.

With all the sessions and hrs i barley have any hair but do have some spots on thighs, arms and other spots, that are fairly light even with all the professional laser treatments and electrolysis. IPL aka this device is NOT the go-to treatment for hair reduction but it does work.

Firstly, you need to use an electric razor or standard razor on the areas your zapping. Freshly showered, no oils or lotions on skin. If you dont feel heat your not killing hair follicles. The laser targets the pigment in the hair and absorbs the heat, so as they stated vampire skin, dark hair gets the best results.

If you have never gotten any sort of pro hair removal your hair is going to be fuller and courser. Like the subject heading states, ive had 28 full body laser hair removal treatments aka real hair removal that leaves you with red bumps, plus hrs of electrolysis and I still have hair grow back.

People it takes a long time to remove hair! This is not designed to be a one zap and the hair is gone. It will grow back finer and weaker, until it eventually is killed off. It literally takes years.

I zap each spot 5 times on the highest setting. The heat will build on each subsequent zap, meaning im actually hitting follicles. I would not recommend this if you have course hair or never had pro hair removal - build up to that, but this device is a nice supplement to the pro hair removal. It will never replace it and will take longer. For me its perfect and thats why i gave it 5 stars.

Once you zap the hair you should see a reaction, raised bumps, some redness, along the bikini line for example its very noticeable since the hair is courser - that means its working. It takes about 10 -14 days for the zapped hair to push its way out. Its not instant, the hair still remains in the follicle. You can expedite this by lightly exfoliating in the bath or shower. You may see little black spots in the follicle where the hair has been zapped and effectively targeted.

Hair grows in cycles, doing this every week is pointless, if the hair is not in the growth phase you cant kill it. Every 4 weeks, multiple zaps per spot and the hair WILL fall out and come back weaker. Different areas have different growth cycles but 4 weeks is a good middle ground.

This is used for hair reduction. If you want permanent (still takes multiple treatments( you need electrolysis.

If you want faster hair reduction result you need to use laser only found at the dermatologist or reputable laser spa. IPL is not laser treatment. This is not going to ever replace that. A combination of all three over 3 or 4 years will leave you hairless, so keep your expectations realistic.

title: 2 of 3 have micro glitter (mica). Sticky but not too bad. Moisturizing
text:
These come in a nice little box. They are vegan and cruelty free. They are made in the USA. I included the ingredients at the end of my review.

You get 3 glosses - a peachy pink toned one that has a strawberry scent/flavor, a more reddish toned one that has a grape scent/flavor, and a clear one that has a bubble gum scent/flavor. As for the scents, I can notice them when applying, not so much after the fact. I don’t really notice a taste really with any of them, but the ingredients do list “flavor” not fragrance/parfum, so it made me think they’d have more taste to them. Not a big deal to me though.

While 2 of them are tinted in color, the color doesn’t really translate onto the lips. They just look clear on the lips. They don’t change any color of lip liner, lipstick, matte lip, etc. that I put them over top of. So, I liked that.

The formula is nice. It feels nice and moisturizing on the lips, which I expected given they have nice moisturizing ingredients like Shea butter, coconut oil, and squalane. They do feel SLIGHTLY sticky on the lips. I hate sticky glosses, but these aren’t overly sticky. They don’t feel thick or heavy on the lips. They feel nice and thin. They are glosses so they do need re-applied often throughout the day. But, I’m used to that with glosses so it’s not a big deal to me.

The strawberry and grape both have micro glitter in them (mica). I didn’t know that when I got these. None of the product photos showed they had glitter and the description didn’t say it either. I’m not a fan of micro glitter in my lip glosses. I feel once the gloss wears off, it usually leaves behind glitter particles on my lips. Also, they can sometimes feel gritty. So, I was surprised when I saw 2 of the 3 had glitter. Luckily, these didn’t feel gritty. I do notice that there are some glitter particles on my lips after they wear off, but it’s not too bad. The glitter particles are really small, so it’s not really noticeable. So, I don’t mind that.

Overall, these are nice glosses with a nice formula. They might seem pricey when seeing the $30 price tag, but you’re getting 3 tubes of glosses, so that’s only $10 a piece, which isn’t bad. Of course, it isn’t great. You can get a tube of gloss that looks great and works just as well from the drugstore for slightly less. But, the ingredients might make it worth it to spend the little more. I give them 4 stars.

text: Okay, so I bought the Luscious Raspberries, totally excited to get the deep red shown on the box. Well, I can honestly say it turned a bright fuchsia/pink color instead. I have long hair, and required two boxes. This stuff is extremely hard to work with and it took at least 2 hours of dying before I was finished (this didn't include the hour of dying my hair blonde the night before). I chose to not use the bleach included to keep my hair from being fried, but I fear it may have turned out worse and my hair would've been way past fixing. The consistency of the die is not even close to a regular hair dye kit, it is like jelly and you are not able to squirt a bunch on and just rub it in. My boyfriend had to keep squirting a glob into his hand and smudging it into my hair that way. Then once the color is on, it will not spread. It coats the outside hairs and leaves ones on the inside uncolored, therefore it is extremely hard because you have to touch every single hair with the color individually or you will have blotches and dark spots. Also, I would recommend not getting into the shower to rinse because it stains the entire tub - walls, shower curtain, EVERYTHING. Looks like mass murder in the shower. It also stains anything that it touches. I am okay with how my hair turned out, only because I can rock the pink. If you are going to be pissed that your hair doesn't match the box, especially after all the hassle and money, DO NOT PURCHASE THIS PRODUCT.

title: Works Good For Minor Stretch Marks

Because I am a plus size woman, naturally I have stretch marks on various areas of my body. I have been using this Stretch Mark Cream by Luxy Beauty Care for a couple of weeks now, and I have had some pretty decent results so far using this.

I have stretch marks on my stomach, upper arms and around my bust. The stretch marks on my arms and bust are fairly small in size and more minor than the ones on my stomach. I have found that this cream is working well for my arms and bust, I am seeing progress in their visibility. On my stomach, the ones that I call my tiger stripes, they are a bit more stubborn. I think that if I use this cream for a while, and keep up my routine, results will come. I do recommend for those stubborn stretch marks to exfoliate the area a few times a week. This method in combination with this stretch mark cream has been my best friend!

I give this 4 stars, it is a great product, and one that I definitely recommend giving a shot if you want to treat your stretch marks. However if you have the stubborn ones, this will work, but it goes a bit more on the slower side.

Please note that I was sent this product complimentary to try out in my home in order to share my honest experience, thoughts and review.

title: Warped from Containing Polish Remover
text: After containing Mineral Fusion nail polish remover (one of the most popular, most effective removers on the market), this bottle stopped dispensing as well as it had. Upon inspection, we realized the acetone had started warping the all the parts so that the lid wouldn't totally close anymore, too much acetone started coming out per pump, and, most dangerously of all, the bottle itself had begun warping and starring. What's happening is it is liquifying the plastic and causing it to become molten, but on a very slow level, with the plastic molecules moving because of the organic chemistry of the acetone interacting with this particular type of plastic. It was only a matter of time before it bottomed out in my bathroom cabinet all over everything. Basically, this should be made of the same type of plastic as bottles that hold acetone and for long periods of time, at that. Furthermore, the straw should be of a sturdier material.

There is a small section in the very front of the closure that is lace and it has baby hair attached, but I believe you can cut that part off. I chose to keep it on with the baby hair in place. The lace and the baby hair is not very noticeable, which I like. I might choose to cut it off next time because I don’t think the lace or the baby hair is necessary. I’m expecting to get a lot of use out of this closure. I plucked some hair from the part and I like the way it turned out.
***Edited 10/24
After wearing the silk closure for a couple of weeks, I’ve decided that silk closures are probably not for me. It doesn’t sit as flat on the head as lace closures and that bugs me. Lace is much more pliable. The silk closure is surprisingly stiff and doesn’t mold to the shape of my head. I’ll be going back to using lace from now on.

The information on the pamphlet that came with the eye drops was interesting; it stated one ingredient keeps the eye moist, it is naturally found in the eye, body. Another ingredient is a vitamin that doctors use to help the cornea... heal.
So I figured these might be good for pollen, mold exposure allergy increased by airplane fumes (low flying jets that go to the airport over my apartment.) and 2 other chemicals in our air; neighbors e-cigarette and drug pipe vaping fumes and laundry mat constant white cloud blowing out into the air, into our apartments; bleach, chemical soaps...

Many of my neighbors have the same uncomfortable feeling. Increased in spring, late fall by certain pollens. We live next to a marsh.

I been taught by natural eye doctors to avoid eye drops. But; for the first time in my life I thought I might try these until my eyes, nose get used to the air here (if that is possible), or I am able to move.

The drops felt nice the first night; but next day I had extreme dry eyes, dizzyish, crawly kind of feeling in head, sinus. Then much itching! I was walking to the store and on the way sniffled. I think the eye drops caused the pollen, mold, chemicals to flow through from the eye-tear drainage tube into the nose, then up the sinus when I was sniffling in the rain yesterday. Today pain still bad but itching less. Following day two; no drops for 3rd day; pain, itching less. Pain gone after days no eye drops. Went back to using humidifier.

Maybe the drops are good for other conditions a doctor might apply for. I do not know. I definitely have decided to go back to my usual use of a steam humidifier, natural food, natural methods, natural medical and eye, nutrition doctors advice. And to keep looking a for a better place to live. After 2 moves in last 3 years; I think this time I know how to avoid a bad real estate deal.

Eye doctor, driving test recently says eyes, eyesight is very good. But got allergy to whatever is in the air. And the air’s chemicals can cause dry eyes.

title: Just Buy It!!! Worth Every Penny.
text:
This wig is absolutely beautiful! I will be buying this one again and again. This was my first time buying hair from Amazon. I'd put off trying Amazon wigs for years. But wow! Huge mistake. I didn’t have to cut layers into it or really do anything other than set it. The hair quality was outstanding. The unit was soft and silky, hardly any shedding, no tangling so far, and it’s next to impossible to tell it is synthetic. My head measures 22.5 inches around, so the cap size was a perfect fit for me. I am SO IN LOVE!!! For the record, the wig did NOT look like this straight out of the package but don’t be disappointed. It’s not a “shake and go” wig. You will have to customize it a little, but it isn't hard. It's pre-plucked but you may want to thin the hairline out a little more if you want to pull the hair off your face. But a beginner could easily customize this with minimal effort.

What I Did To Mine:

The curl pattern is loose. But be advised, if you brush this unit out, it will explode. You really have to condition it first and train it. I washed and conditioned mine with Silicon Mix and Silicon Mix Conditioner to wash out some of the dye and get it ready for training. I wouldn’t advise washing synthetic hair with any other product. Silicon Mix makes it silky so it feels and behaves like real hair. This hair does NOT respond well to curling irons. At all. The curls droop quickly, even if you wet roll it and put it under the dryer. This wig requires wet heat for lasting curls. So I rolled it up with FlexiRods, boiled a kettle of water and poured boiling water on each FlexiRod. The bigger the rod, the bigger the curl. I DID NOT soak the wig in boiling water. I just wanted enough heat to seal in a loose curl. If it boils too long, the curls get too tight and they frizz.

I let it air dry overnight. As I took out each rod, I moussed each curl with Cream of Nature Style and Shine Foaming Mousse to avoid frizz. For hold and definition, I used Cream of Nature Moisture & Shine Curl activator lotion to seal in the curl pattern made by the rods. I finger combed out the curls, brushed them out and then rolled them around my fingers with my Denman Brush for definition and to shape the curl pattern. This was the result. If the curls loosen, just spray some water on them and brush them back into shape. The curls are permanent until you wet heat the hair again for a different style. The first three pix are dry curls, but the rest are wet-look curls.

I thank you, Thank You, THANK YOU, Andria for an extremely satisfying first experience with your products. I will definitely be buying more!

title: Pleasant Enough, Not Much Scent, Need a Lot of Product To Shower
text:
Like all too many organic soaps, this example ends up being a bit too subtle and bland in scent and power to justify its price point. I love vetiver but even with a generous dollop on the loofah, I get only the faintest scent of that fragrance here. The hemp / vetiver combo smells pleasant in a mild sort of way, but this is not what I expected at the price point and given the product name. If I wanted "fragrance free", I'd buy it!

Besides the really mild non-especially vetiverish scent, NH IH&V body wash also needs a lot of soap to generate any lather, and even needs a lot just to get through a whole body wash. Lather may or may not be to your liking, but having to reload the loofah halfway through your shower is no one's idea of fun. At the rate of product usage, I would be amazed if this 13 oz bottle lasts me for more than 2-3 weeks.

Ultimately, even if you want to stay organic, there are better choices with more prominent scents and better product consumption rates. EOs Cedar & Mint for Men works well enough and can even be used as a shampoo and shave cream for the undemanding. My personal favorite semi-organic products are from Every Man Jack. Their cedar and sandalwood (two separate types there) body wash have great smells and give adequate lather and cleaning duration with roughly half the product needed to get similar effects from NH IH&V wash. (I call Every Man Jack semi-organic as I haven't bothered to assess all the ingredients on their label, but they have no parabens or SLS derivatives, so they pass my personal screening standard.) Both of these product lines are much cheaper than Nubian Heritage.

For vetiver lovers who want that scent in their bath ritual, Provence Sante makes a good vetiver beauty bar soap, and also a rather expensive vetiver body wash. which I have not tried due to its high cost. I have tried the beauty bar, and though not cheap, it does indeed give the user a noticeable vetiver smell when applied, which is always a good thing when buying a vetiver named product!

title: Great for mixing oil blends for rollerballs
text:
I use fractioned oils to make rollerballs for my oil blends and for a carrier for various topical uses.
I have been wanting to recreate a muscle cramp relief oil from a major essential oil club and lucked up with a copycat recipe. These oils are over $30 for 5ml and, while it works great and smells amazing, I just couldn’t bring myself to spend that knowing that I have a box full of single oils.
When I saw this bottle with the pump, I knew it was time to try my hand and mixing this recipe. I had a few other rollerballs that I wanted to make (some decongestant and immune boosters since it’s getting to that time of year) so I inserted the pump and got to work. The oils mixed VERY well and the pump on the bottle made it very easy to dispense just enough into the small rollerball opening. That is SUCH a nice feature – manufacturer, please don’t remove that from the item. I can’t tell you how many times I’ve spilled my fractioned oil everywhere because it was difficult to contain since it’s thin.
Once I had worked through the 5 rollerballs for my family needs, I had enough room in the bottle to make a BIG batch of the massage oil with the rest of the fractioned oil. IT WORKED!!! I’m soooooo happy with this bottle of fractioned oil. I can easily pump out what I need to work out my sore muscles and apply to hubby’s back (he has scholosis and other degenerative issues). I would highly recommend for anyone wanting to use fractioned oil for their essential oil uses.

I have never used a felt tip brow pen before. For being a 1st time user, I have to say this took me longer to do than a brow pencil & powder. (Approx. 20 mins)

Because I have barely any brows and draw them pretty thick, the areas w/ just pen flicks, turned shiny after a while. I have combo skin, so I always fear my brows will look oily or somehow fade away during the day. But I did appreciated the long wear of this product.

Since I didnt know how to use this pen well, during application, it seemed like it was "drying out". DONT CAP & SHAKE! It made a mess into the cap and all over the tip.

All you need to do is hold the pen at a vertical angle while flicking and gravity will do the rest. I also suggest standing it cap side down in your pencil cup, so it will always be moist.

Im sure with more practice, it will be easier & faster to use. The end result does give a more natural look resembling hair strokes and I was satisfied w/ the color.

title: Why do I like this thing?
text:
I have used this for about a month and here is my take on it.

Cons:

1. I get a better shave with an old Sensor II Gillette razor.

2. I agree with another reviewer who complained about the recharger. It is flimsy and I am never certain the razor will stay in the holder. It looks and feels and works cheap.

3. I have a handlebar moustache and sideburns. Shaving near either doesn't work. Nor does the trimmer attachment work for me. I end up cleaning up with my trusty blade.

4. The gel packs work, but also seem cheap. I mostly end up using my normal shaving gel (Edge).

Pros:

1. I like the fact that I can use it wet.

2. The charge lasts a very long time, and the recharge is very quick.

3. It is very convenient to use. I find myself shaving more often than I did with a blade just because it is easy to use. For example I find myself shaving quickly before my wife comes home. Never did that before. :-)

4. The ergonomics are good. Good fit in my hand. Good balance. Easy glide over face, neck, chin.

5. I hav oily skin and find I get a better shave before washing my face rather than afterwards.

Conclusion: I like the thing and decided to keep it, but I will be darned if I know why. Oh, and I just truned 67 and haven't had an electric razor since the 60's.

title: Comparable to the basic Waterpik portable with a few improvements and extras
text:
This unit is comparable to my very basic travel Waterpik flosser. In fact it has several features that the basic model lacks for around the same price. This unit has three speeds, whereas the entry level Waterpik only has one. The fastest speed is comparable with the one speed on my Waterpik, and it’s the only speed I need. This unit has a charge light (blinks until charged) while there is no such light on the comparably priced Waterpik. This device has about the same sized reservoir as the Waterpik, but because of the design, it’s on the bottom as opposed to along the sides of the unit, the result being that it makes it a lot bulkier, which is unfortunate in a travel water flosser. Unfortunately, there is no advantage to this design as like the Waterpik, it begins to stop pumping water as the tank gets lower, forcing the user to keep the unit vertical in order to get to the water at the very bottom of the reservoir, which can become quite awkward while trying to get around the teeth and gums. I’ve owned several of these, and to be fair, they all suffer from this same problem.

One more thing: this unit comes with a nice case and a stash of attachments (which are usually found in home units and don’t generally come with portable units ,) none of which I have much use for, but I guess it’s good to know they’re there. It does include two of the standard water flosser adaptors, so two people can use it.

The only thing that remains to be seen is how long this puppy will last. This is my 3rd travel water flosser. I’ll report back should something ontoward occur, or if it continues to work well.

title: Innovative twist on your typical hair tie.

Being a mother of three girls and now four granddaughters I have used a lot of hair ties in my lifetime. text:
As it turns out I live only 20 miles from West Coast Shaving. I called them and said I would drop in. While I was there I picked up a bunch of different blades, a new boar brush and Mitchells wool fat shaving soap. I've been wanting to try this stuff for a long time because of the reviews. Because everyone is different and must find the best combination of razor, brush, soap and blades I will not say that this is great and that over there is terrible. But I will make an observation. A new boar brush must be broken in which takes a couple of weeks because the tips of the bristles seem too firm and rather sharp when it's first used. My observation is that not only does the lanolin soften up your skin nicely but it has helped brake in the boar bruch very quickly. The lanolin seems to soften up the brush just like it softens up your beard. This only took about three shaves and my boar brush is perfect.

I read all the reviews and saw the videos on this soap. I didn't find any problems with the soap as far a lathering. I soaked it in WARM water and took my boar brush to start to lather it up. No problem. I didn't find all the problems that other people talk about. This might be the results of the water hardness rather than the soap itself.

title: My new favorite product!
text:
Update - May 19 2015:
Well here we are, one month later, and I just finished my first tube. I have been rotating between three flavors, mint, cherry, and vanilla, but I always carry one with me. These things last! They are much better than any generic I have tried, and my lips aren't a chapped, uncomfortable mess. I am very happy I tried these and recommend them highly. A quick word on the flavors I have tried. I like the mint when I am on the go. It has a light, natural flavor that is strong enough to notice, but not so strong that it is overwhelming. The balm is uncolored, so there is no concern about it looking like lip gloss or lipstick. I like the cherry as a change of pace, but it is tinted a light shade of pink, and while I don't notice the color on my own lips (I have a medium skin tone), I would test it before wearing it in public if color is a concern. The vanilla, well... different people have different tastes. I won't say it is bad, but I like the other two flavors much more. My issue with the vanilla is that the cocoa butter in the balm is very noticeable in scent and flavor, and when I apply it, my mind is immediately taken to thinking "sun block, or sunscreen." The fragrance and flavor remind me more of a skin lotion than something I would reach for to put on my lips. Some people may like that, but I prefer something else. That, however, is the only negative I found. The product itself is outstanding, it does exactly what one wants it to do, and saves the user money as compared to using other similar products. If you are debating on this one, try it. I don't think you will be disappointed.

title: The silver bullet for small breed teeth problems.
text:
We have a lot of dogs and they’re chihuahuas. They are known for having notoriously bad teeth as a breed even when you do everything right. Our littlest has been losing teeth left and right and is at the age where cleanings are too scary with her size. She would realistically need a cleaning much more often than yearly because the plaque builds up so fast.

I bought this as a shot in the dark, as we have burned hundreds on every product known to man. I mixed the product parts together in the large bottle and sprayed 4 of our dogs’ teeth as instructed. After a SINGLE application, our girl with the bad teeth had a 25% reduction in plaque. Our other three had a reduction of 40%, 60%, and 90%. I am not joking - this stuff has carbolic acid in it and it WORKS. The two components mixed causes some type of fizzy reaction and really works between the plaque and teeth/gums and between teeth. I tasted it first myself to be sure it wouldn’t be traumatizing to our pups and it tastes like flavorless alcohol free mouthwash.

Since, I continue to spray once or twice a day as I remember to and the plaque keeps disappearing. I did check with my dental tools to be sure it wasn’t just bleaching the plaque and it is not- it’s physically breaking off their teeth. I don’t know how we will get larger bottles of the stuff with the number of dogs we have but it’s true, it works. I paid my actual money and used it on my real dogs. This is not a paid or discounted review. Please give this a shot on your Littles!

I purchased my starter kit directly from Revel, plus an extra color. Since I rely on reviews from Amazon, I'm including mine to help others.

My first attempt was with Shady and I did a great job on my left hand, but didn't smooth out the right enough. It held up well, but I only got a week out of it because I couldn't deal with the bad job I'd done on my right hand.
The second photo is the second time I did my nails and first time I used Starburst. Glitter is more forgiving. I realized that with two coats of the color, you could still see the white of my nail through it. The second time I used this color, I used a white base (Fresh Cotton from Sally's). This second time is the grid photo with the purple/silver.

From start to finish (with bare nails) this takes about 45 minutes.

Advice:
1-Watch YouTube tutorials. All systems have different instructions, so they might not all apply to your kit. Keep that in mind as you watch them.
2-Let the dip dry before you brush off the excess. I didn't do that before, but employed that advice my third time (purple/silver photo) and it was a better experience.
3-Don't do this without a good buffer. A plain old nail file ain't gonna cut it!
4-I bought nail clips to hold the acetone-soaked cotton on my nails and it works way better than foil. I can do all my nails at once.
5-Before stating dip polish, after washing hands, wipe nails with alcohol pad. It gets all the oils off your nails. This is good advice for regular polish, too.

title: Decent, but disappointed
text:
I have ordered these several times now, and they do work out okay. You need to make sure to have everything correctly sized/at the right resolution and set to A4 paper size before printing so that the images turn out well. You also need to apply the adhesive sheets with a lot of care and patience to ensure there are no bubbles or wrinkles.

When applied, the tattoos are shiny, as most temporary tattoos are. This can be fixed with a dusting of baby powder or matte makeup powder. The only issue I've had is that the edges tend to peel quite a bit if you place the tattoo near a joint/bending part, like your elbow/inner elbow, knee, etc. Any place that moves a lot. But as long as you put them somewhere that doesn't move so much, they last several days as long as you don't pick at them or fiddle with them.

My biggest complaint is that the last time I ordered these, I went ahead and printed my images, and then as soon as I went to apply the adhesive sheets (which is quite a process and definitely made easier with two people and a good amount of patience, if you don't want any bubbles), I found that every single one of my adhesive sheets were defective. I've attached photos so you can see what I'm talking about.

In between the adhesive layer and the yellow backing paper (which you peel apart to apply to the printed designs), there were tons of little black specks/dirt. They were stuck in the adhesive, which obviously rendered them useless, seeing as I don't want black flecks all over my printed tattoo designs. I am super disappointed in this considering how expensive this paper is, but I don't think I can get a return since I already printed on the sheets. I just can't believe that something of this price would have such a flaw in the quality, and despite having success with these previously, now I'm hesitant to buy again.

We have used it for insect bites (specifically spiders and mosquitos), mild sunburn, burns from chemicals and of course as a daily moisturizer. The smell is a little stinky, so what we do when we use it as a daily moisturizer is soften it and mix it in with our store bought cocoa butter and shea butter lotion. The store bought lotion really does smell like cocoa so mixing it with the raw shea butter eliminates the shea odor. It actually allows the cocoa butter smell to overpower it. I feel and smell like a nice, soft milk chocolate bar after showering. A friend of mine had to crawl under a house full of mold, mildew, spiders, etc. Although he was fully covered in protective clothing and a gas mask, his arms were swollen, stinging and very painful when he came out. I gave him a chunk of the shea butter to rub all over this arms and hands and he felt instant relief from the stinging and pain. There are many uses for this shea butter and I'm sure most people will discover a use no one else had even thought of yet. Don't be afraid to put it on any part of your skin that needs some relief from pain, no matter what the sourse was. It truly is like real butter, so use it plentifully and use a clean towel to remove any excess after most of it has absorbed into your skin. This is a big chunk of shea butter, but I think it will come in so handy it won't be long before I need to order more. The price, shipping, packaging, etc can't be beat either. title: Much better than a regular toothbrush
text:
I finally broke down and decided it was time to get a power toothbrush. I decided to go with the Oral-B over the Sonicare per dentist recommendation. I am very happy with the decision.

It does take a little time getting used to brushing with a power toothbrush over a regular one. You have to get used to letting the toothbrush do the work. You also have to get used to the pulsating action, it can feel a little weird the first couple of brushes.

I have been working on brushing for the full 2 mins, I don't find it that hard to do. It goes by pretty fast for me. I use the toothbrush's built-in timer.

I also don't have a problem with the toothbrush heads. I find I can reach the back teeth easier with this than a manual toothbrush. It is really not that uncomfortable for me either.

One thing I found that is an added bonus with this toothbrush are the "Made in" stampings on both the toothbrush and the charging base. I prefer to purchase as many things as I can that are made in America or Germany. It turns out both this toothbrush and charging base are made in Germany and not China.

I am also not certain about the reviews of this product stating that they meant to order the 7550 and got this toothbrush. I just ordered mine last week and I got what I ordered, the 7400.

I would recommend this toothbrush.

title: Grainy but perfectly fine to use
text:
This shea butter is a good quality shea butter. It is ivory and reasonably priced. As a person whose been using shea butter for well over 10 years for ecezma treatment I can say that this shea butter is a quality product. Although it is a quality shea butter, the way it has been processed left the butter very grainy and not as creamy as I was expecting. It is a thick, heavy butter that is solid at room temperature and has a lot of use for hair and body purposes. It is sourced from an area in Africa that doesn't produce a real rancid smelling butter. It smells distinctly like shea but not like the shea sourced from more eastern countries. The butter when applied to the skin feels thick and heavey but that isn't a problem for me. I would need to indirectly melt and re-solidify this butter in order to smooth it out and kill the grainy texture it comes with. I'd also whip this butter to make it creamy.

Price: Reasonable
Texture: Grainy but not too smooth, sort of like peanut butter but thicker
Color: Ivory, more of an off white, cream like tone
Scent: Hard to describe but it's distinctly Shea which never smells pleasing

Overall, this company's shea butter is a good quality butter, high quality for some but for me good/decent due to the fact it's grainy and doesn't have the smooth texture I'm used too. The color is normal and the butter feels thick, heavy and heavenly on thick dry skin like eczema. I'd recommend this company's shea butter and possibly repurchase in the future.

•This quality shea butter was purchased for a promotional price in exchange for my unbiased and honest review.

title: Fades, but very vibrant color
text:
This color is pretty good for the price. There are a few pros and cons to it that I will explain below, but overall I don't think I will buy it again.

Pro:
Comes with 2 containers which is enough color for any length hair
The ability to adjust the shade you want by adding conditioner to the color
A little bit goes a VERY long way
Price is very reasonable
When it fades, it fades all the way out so it doesn't look like some weird shade of orange when it starts to wash out
You don't need any heat to get the color to stick
It doesn't smell like anything

Cons:
Fades INCREDIBLY fast - I had it in for maybe a week or two before it washed all the way out
You have to use a ton of conditioner to create a light soft pink color - the size of a dime with about 2 cups of conditioner do the trick
It will dye everything it comes in contact with - use thick gloves
If you are diluting the color with conditioner, it will take some time to sit on your hair
If you are diluting the color, you'll never need both bottles - it would take 5 years to use all of it

I think overtone color conditioner is an easier system to use and the color stays longer.

title: No Fragrance, Moisturizing, Not The Greatest Value-Improvements Could Be Made
text:
These Doctor Babor Hyaluronic Acid Serum Power Serum Ampoules seem pretty good. I definitely like this better than their collagen concentrate ampoules, but there are things that could have been changed to make me like this product a lot more.

-Received 7 glass ampoules with 2ml of product inside each one
-Well presented in a nice looking silver display box
-You have to snap the glass ampoules open. They do provide a plastic cylindrical piece to aid in doing so. I’m a nurse, so I’m used to breaking open these kinds of ampoules without any issue. I can imagine that some people would not like this though
-Watery serum that glides across skin easily
-Honestly, a little seems to cover a large area of skin. 2ml may not seem like a lot, but a single ampoule seems like way more than would be needed for one application. I have split one into 3-4 uses to be honest
-I’m assuming the company intends for one whole ampoule to be used as one application because each one is labeled as day 1-7, and they provide no way to seal an ampoule back after using which I found to be rather frustrating
-Absorbs rapidly and doesn’t feel sticky or tacky after drying like the collagen concentrate did
-Their collagen concentrate ampoules also had a heavy fragrance, so I was SO relieved to find that there is no added fragrance with these
-Made in Germany

So does it really help with plumping, smoothing, and reducing wrinkles? I don’t know. I definitely like the way my skin looks and feels right after application, but I haven’t noticed anything drastic.
As I previously stated, the 2ml of serum feels like A LOT to me if you try to put it all on your face at once. Unfortunately, this company also does not provide a way to seal an individual ampoule back for future use since they apparently intend for one ampoule to be an entire application. I remember I tried a set by the ISDIN brand with glass ampoules just like these. In the kit, the company included a top to slide over the opened glass ampoule with a cap to seal for future use. This was awesome and so convenient. I was disappointed to find out that this company did not include anything like that (I took a picture of that top and cap on one of these ampoules so you can see).

Anyway, it is possible that this product may provide good results when used long term, but I just don’t really like this being intended for use over 7 days only. If they included a top with cap to seal each individual ampoule so that the product could be used over a longer period of time, I would like it much more. I would definitely prefer a serum in a larger bottle with dropper lid.

Anyway, I hope my review was helpful in some way, and if so, I would love to know – thanks! I’ll be sure to update if I have any other comments to add.

title: Great product, better value
text:
TL;DR - It's cheap and it works.

Actual review:

I have been using Beardsmen Beard Oil for about 4 or 5 months now. There were 3 key factors and things I wanted to achieve in a beard oil (I had never used it previously):

1. I wanted it to stop the itching.
2. I wanted it to soften the hair for less of a "coarse" feeling.
3. I didn't want to spend $15 for 1 ounce of oil.

This bear oil hits all 3 points. Anyone who's shopped beard oils at all already knows it's probably the best value by far, you get 4x as much as what most other companies give you for the same price.

As for the itching, it definitely helps with that. You do have to make sure to rub the oil deep into the beard so it gets to your skin (Beardsmen gives you a link to a very detailed PDF guide on beard care and product use). If you just put the oil on the hair, it's not going to help your itchy skin (this is true for any oil).

Finally, beard softness. One quick anecdote will answer this: About a month ago I got lazy with my morning routine and stopped using beard oil (along with other things like face wash and cologne). About a week into this, I had some contact with my ex-wife (don't ask) and she specifically asked if I was still using the oil, as my beard was not as soft as it had been. When the ladies notice that you stopped using it, you know it works.

Long story short, I would easily consider this the "best buy" in beard oil.

title: Follow the instructions. Mostly...

I broke the rules in one respect- when I took off the booties, I left them sitting in the shower. Seeing them the next day, I put them on AGAIN for an hour. BUT after all was done, my feet were a bit red, and more dry than I expected. I'm sure it was a result of this double application. But I'm a man, who wears boots- my feet needed this. I wasn't afraid of redness and such. I wanted a good peel. On day seven I scrubbed my feet extra good with a pumice stone, and 90% of the skin sloughed off. The rest over the next day or two. But as I said, especially after the pumice stone, my feet were red. It wasn't so bad, but unpleasant. Now after some lotion, two days later my feet look great.
