title: Now I'm too sexy
text:
Now that I bought and used the T980, my cool slacker goatee is attracting too many women. I'm not getting any rest.

Naturally, a product that causes grief should be down-rated, but I won't here because this shaver is just doing its job.

And, we all like things with "turbo" in the description, however loosely that term is applied. It makes it go faster with a cool noise, so even in a shaver that is attractive to many.

Electric shavers for beards sure beat the heck out of scissors! The Norelco has a wide range of cutting depths and my beard comes out a uniform length. I did not feel any pulling or other discomfort. The charge seems to last for days and the charger itself, like the shaver, is a decent and modern design.

The little detail cutter is easy to attach and does a great job of defining the beard area and also clipping any stray hairs under the nose where the big cutter head cannot reach.

Some people think the closest cutting position is still not close enough for that short-stubble look and that does seem to be the case. I don't want mine that close, but I understand those who do and I take off a star for brotherly solidarity. Actually, I'm sure that if it was to cut more closely, that would take it into the realm of regular shavers, an expensive world of high-tech blades and lubricants. Actually, if you press down a little, you can get closer.

The turbo thing works well. It vacuums almost every hair into the storage chamber. I didn't expect the vacuum action to work so well. I think the turbo button should be the only button, but there it is. The non-turbo setting is less noisy...

The parts detach easily and the little supplied brush works well to clean it out. The little travel pouch is nice.

The T980 works just as it should, for me, and the price is reasonable. I think it will last a long time and I am glad I bought it.

As for the women, I did exaggerate. One did make a favorable comment which is one more than before. That is an improvement, eh?

title: Excellent Hair Care
text:
Disclosure: I was contacted by Luseta and offered this product. I accepted, promising a fair and honest review in return.

This is a clone of the review I wrote for the Luseta Argan oil shampoo/conditioner set. I have nothing else to add about this product; all things I said in that review apply here.

I love this product, and will look to buy it again, even online. I think it smells great, and it has done a fantastic job of cleaning and conditioning my hair.

I like the packaging, a simple deep crimson/violet color, classy and not overstated. No screaming text, just a simple logo and simple listings of what you get inside.

The color is a simple white cream. No outrageous greens or pinks or blues; colored shampoo only seems to make sense if you've got colored hair. The scent is fantastic, understated and clean-smelling, not overly flowery or soapy or thick with artificial perfumes.

The shampoo pumps out of the bottle easily and under control, just the right consistency to pump well but not to shoot all over the place. Same with the conditioner. Both go on easily, mix easily, and rinse just as easily and completely.

The two bottles are not gigantic, but I am only now running out of this product after approximately eight weeks of daily use. A set will easily suit two people for a month or more. That makes it most definitely cost-effective for the current sale price of approximately $26.

Bottom line: this is an excellent product that I will purchase again.

title: After 1 year of using the product, great traveling shaver
text:
First of all here are some points to put into consideration before buying. This shaver is for...
1. Someone who is looking for a TRAVEL shaver that is small and convenient to carry. It comes with a neat carrying case, and only requires two AA batteries that can be found anywhere. One set of batteries can approx. last up to 20 days/shaves-ish. It will still go on, but I can feel the motor running at lower speed.
2. Someone who prefers WET shaving experience whenever possible. (Wet shaving with this product is great. Dry, not so much.)
3. Someone who needs to shave everyday or simply want that clean shaven look everyday. ( It's still a foil electric shaver, it's fast, efficient, everyday.)
4. Someone who needs his travel shaver to have a trimmer. (Frequent long trip? just like me.)
5. Someone who doesn't want to spend 15 minutes cleaning the shaver. Who wants hassle-free and easy cleaning shaver.

This shaver however isn't for someone who is looking for a blade replacement shaver. I say, wake up, electric shaver will never give you that baby "skin" shave like you get from a proper blade shaving method. However, for $15 this shaver can deliver a very decent shave, very close, but definitely not alike. It also isn't quite for someone who plan to use it 7/365 days. You will probably be better off buying other wet/dry panasonic shaver that is rechargable, and have more than one moving blade, linear-super fast motor and on.

It's been a year and I still use it on every one of my trip. no problem. Impeccable reliability there, and well made.

--------------------

If you decide to buy it, here are my tips and tricks for you. It's based on my experience with it so perhaps it will help you get a better shave with this shaver.
1. YES, it will take up to 2-3 weeks if you are coming from blade for your skin to adjust. This is normal and all you need is patience to get through it.
2. It's miles apart better wet shaver than dry. DO NOT shave dry unless absolute necessary.
3. With that said, all the techniques in wet shaving apply. You should shave in the shower, or right after you come out of it. Your skin should be clean prior to shaving. One trick is that this shaver works better if your shaving gel/foam/cream is "light" or "not dense". Lather up too much or a very dense cream can make the foil/blade hot during operation. (Thick cream will cause more friction and blade moves pretty fast.) Last, don't forget a splash of cold water to seal in and a good aftershave.
4.DO NOT press the shaver, or foil against your skin. You will only get irritation out of it. The trick is to shave everyday, go against the grain, let it GLIDE SLOWLY on your skin, rinse it whenever you feel there is too much foam in the shaver, use trimmer to take out long stubborn hair like those on the neck, and under the chin. DONE.

Thank you for reading my review. I know it's long but this shaver, for $15, deserves a decent review from me imo.

This Cleancult liquid hand soap comes in a high quality, glass container that’s thick and strong with a plastic pump that works well. I’ve been using this coconut based hand soap daily and find it pleasant. It glides and lathers well when I rub my hands together and stays on my hands long enough to be thorough washing. This soap isn’t overly drying, though I almost always need lotion after hand washing. The lavender scent from essential oils is light, which is a plus as I’m not a fan of heavy scent. The container holds 12 oz. and the company sells 16 oz. refills (currently $6.95) in a paper based container styled like a milk carton to reduce plastic waste.

The glass container has a modern design that looks nice countertop. It has a beige or taupe color silicone (or similar) material on the bottom and lower sides that prevents slipping and adds breakage protection. The plastic pump is also beige and good quality but may not last as long as the glass container. Beige isn’t my favorite color but it’s neutral and the company offers a blue shade that looks pretty in the photo. This soap has coconut oil, olive oil, potassium soap, aloe juice, vitamin E, citrus acid, sodium chloride and a natural essential oil blend (not in that order). I assume “potassium soap” is potassium hydroxide (caustic lye), but believe it’s found in all liquid soap under various names. Overall, I like the hand soap and container. 4 stars.

title: GLITTERING burnt orange
text:
This review is for the Emilie Heathe - Lip Atelier Lip Color in the "Shimmering Burnt Orange" shade, which I believe is the only "shimmery" color offered at the time of this writing. It comes in a super-chic understated black box, and the tube itself is also black and square with a magnetic lid.

Calling the shade "Shimmering" is an understatement - this shade is GLITTERING. The pigment itself is a really pretty Sienna / rust color that's very flattering on my pale, warm-undertoned skin, and it has a LOT of coppery-gold sparkle. It glides on my lips smoothly and puts down a good amount of pigment (and glitter) in a single swipe. It does feel a little bit gritty from the glitter, but doesn't leave my lips feeling dry at all. It does have a little bit of a scent that smells floral to me.

My problem with this particular shade is that the pigment fades (as all lip colors do) throughout the day, but the glitter does NOT. The glitter just migrates outside of your lips and you end up with it all around your mouth. So I personally wouldn't order this shade again. However I like the formula overall, and the fact that it's made in the USA from clean ingredients, so I'm sure the other (non-glittery) colors are amazing and would be right up my alley!

The smell is not as strong as other cleaning solutions I have used, but there is a light chemical smell. It comes with a pair of disposable gloves but I did not use them. Since it is a gel it is fairly easy to handle without making a mess. After one hour I wiped it clean with a damp cloth. On the tile it works about the same as soap and water. It still required some scrubbing in certain areas. On the door seal it performed much better. The areas where the gel was applied cleared up not only the mold, but also the soap scum which would not wipe away with just the wet cloth alone. text:

This is a combination of several good bath elements in one product!

1. The "poof" part on one side for exfoliating - Just enough of the "poof" material to exfoliate without being too thick!

4. Its WASHABLE! Can't do that with a loofa or a regular, round "poof" (they fall apart)
5. Because of the material, you will use less body wash-it makes a little go a long ways

Looking closely at the construction of this, you can tell its well made with good, solid stitching
I think what sold me was that you can put this in the washer. The other bath helpers I've used have ended up being disposable when they get yucky :(
You get TWO of these, which is great! The only thing that would be better is if it came in camo fabric for the burly guys! :O
I bought this as part of a promotion to test and review, otherwise I might not have even found this!
Without a doubt I can highly recommend this bath cloth and am getting a set for both my older mom and my in laws for Christmas! Great helper for seniors who have a hard time reaching to wash their backs :)

This is a nice acrylic brush. It has a pretty pattern on the handle and the bristles are nice and straight. Though this #8 brush is smaller than all of my other #8 brushes, it works very well when applying acrylics. Whenever I get a new brush, I always do a burn test on a few of the bristle strands. The bristles in this brush are some kind of natural fiber or fur, but I can't say that it's a Kolinsky Sable, as true Kolinsky Sable is usually much more expensive. The bristles are rather short, leaving me to wonder how well the brush will hold up in the long run, but it should last a while..
Overall this is a nice acrylic nail brush, that has a very pretty pattern on its handle. It works well when applying acrylics, and I've had no problems with bristle loss. I would recommend this brush to those who are just starting out or those looking for a good budget brush.

title: Won't Compete with Norelco Triple it's Styled Like
text:
UPDATE: This does get a little better with use, or I got a little more used to using it, or a little of both. My Norelco is a little old and needs a new switch. I use the Rozia most of the time now when I shave. I dump the whiskers out every time I shave. The assembly that mounts the shaving heads will come loose from the driving assembly that is the lower half of the shaving head replacement part. It then has to be reconnected to the little metal hinge and latched. That's slightly difficult to get right.

It's competent but misses many improvements incorporated into more expensive razors twenty years ago. The Norelco that this one looks like has a suspension system with integrally spring damped "driveshafts" connecting each head to the motor(s). That keeps the heads in contact with your face more effectively, making shaving quicker. This one lacks that important advance and seems a little inept in comparison. My Norelco has a broader range of head flexion. At rest the Norelco's three heads form a more convex shape together. When pressed inward against a face there is also more deeper (concave) movement allowed.

The heads on the shaver being reviewed seem to pull on my whiskers when shaving around mouth and chin. I suspect the slots aren't as rounded at the ends, rather coming to a point where a whisker catches. There is no sensitivity setting as well. But it works. I will use it occasionally and keep it as a backup. If I didn't know that better equipment exists I might be more satisfied with it's shortcomings. Of course the better equipment does cost four times or more the price of this one.

title: Not that great...
text:
I am always walking around barefoot. Not a big fan of socks, except in closed toe shoes, hence the dry heels. I used this religiously every night for about 1.5 weeks. I put it on, then put on socks at night (this is torture for me, by the way). While it is working and my heels are nicer, this has not "healed" the cracks (which were and are not that great or noticeable). It's definitely made my heels look better but no "healing" there.
I have also been having trouble with an awful looking elbow for years (cracked, bleeding skin and nothing's been able to heal it). I put this on and it's helped tremendously. It healed in within a few days. The only trouble is that I have to keep on using it, otherwise the dry skin comes back.
I guess the skin on the heels is so much thicker that it may take longer to heal than the elbows. I don't know. I have used other products for my feet and they work just as well as this.
In the end, paying $9.95 for this little thing just to use on my elbows - I don't know that it's worth it. As for the feet, you can get a $2 tube from Walgreens and you're better off.

U P D A T E: Three weeks of continuous use, every single day, sometimes three to four times a day, has not "improved" my cracked heel (I only have issue with one). It still works for my elbow, but if I miss a day, my dry elbow comes back with a vengeance. I will definitely not be purchasing this again.

2nd UPDATE: I've been using this for almost two months now, as directed. I am almost out of this product and nothing has really improved. The cracks are still there (just softer looking). In fact, another issue has propped up; tiny bits of skin on the bottom of both my feet are "peeling off" so badly that it bleeds under them. I have stopped using this product and I am going to see a podiatrist. I don't know if it's a direct result of using this, but I haven't used anything else on my feet other than the heel repair.

title: Milk Perfume
text:
Just received Milk perfume by K.Hall Designs and I love it! I ordered the candle from this line earlier so that I could have an idea what the perfume smells like and I have to say that the two is very close in scent, except in the perfume I can detect a hint of coconut that I wasn't able to in the candle (even though it's suppose to be there, but maybe that's just me). Milk is not overly sweet at all, it is a perfect balance between creaminess and sweetness, a mellow concoction that is very comforting, a darling little scent that delivers creaminess with a hint of vanilla and coconut. Because it is not a serious scent, it might appeal to a younger audience or to those that normally don't wear perfume. I think it is excellent in the winter time when one uses moisturizers such as almond, honey, vanilla, cocoa etc. as it does combine really well with these scents. In fact, I bought Milk to go with L'Occitane's Almond line and I must say it layers very nicely with it. Like I said, this is such a simple scent, but by no means it is cheap, gaudy or car-freshener like, it reminds me a little of those baby-colognes that you can buy..but a little more grown up.

Update 1/30/2012:
..so, I've been using this perfume for a few weeks now and I noticed that it turns a little too coconutty. When I compare the scent of the candle and the perfume, I can definitively detect more coconut in the perfume, like I said before, and it just has a toasted coconut with a hint of vanilla scent. I much prefer the milky-vanilla scent of the candle, without the overload of the coconut. I think a more appropriate name for this perfume would be "Coconut".
As far as lasting power goes..it's not bad for a perfume.

I've always been wary of electric razors, but I have to say this one works pretty well for me. I would recommend this product to anyone looking to make the switch.

title: Very impressive for wavy/curly hair
text:
My hair is naturally wavy/curly and tends to be dry and on the frizzy side. I don't use heat tools other than for special occasions. It's also on the fine thin side. I have the length I want, it goes to the middle of my back, but i'm looking for something to help with making it thicker. I don't know if this product will help with that but willing to give it a try. It does say that it will make it fuller so that gives me hope. I have tried probably every hair care product there is from cheap to expensive. I have found some that i'm more pleased with then others.
So now the selling points of this product are:
~This serum will stimulate hair growth at an impressive speed; just after 1-2 weeks of usage your hair will start getting longer and fuller!
~The enriched formula of this serum will nourish your roots and follicles deeply, helping your hair become denser, fuller and stronger.
~This serum will offer deep moisture to your hair, making it look healthy and glowing. Your hair will soon be silky soft and tempting to the touch! Forget dry, frizzy hair once and for all.
~ Just 5-6 drops of this amazing serum will rejuvenate your hair, making look it good when you don't have time to wash.
My honest and unbiased opinion for the discount price I paid for this serum:
The fragrance is a light soft scent which I like alot. The serum is light and easy to apply to the scalp. I pump 2 drops on my finger tips and massage in a section of my scalp. Repeating this till my entire scalp is massaged. I also use it on the length of my hair to tame the frizz. Just 4 or 5 drops in palms and smoothed down the length of hair is all is needed. I am very impressed with this serum. I have been using it for a week. No noticeable growth or fullness yet but the texture of my hair is so much smoother and noticeably less frizz. Some reviewers have stated it made their hair greasy feeling. Maybe they used to much or have straight hair. Curly wavy hair is drier due to the natural oils from the scalp can not travel down the hair shaft like straight hair. I am very pleased with this product!

text:
This is just something I wanted to try out for whiter teeth, since mine are too sensitive for the chemical whiteners on the market or even a good dental whitening. After the first couple days use my teeth were shinier & slightly not as stained. I'm not expecting dramatic results over night.

I wasn't expecting this product to clear out the rest of a gum infection, but it did.

Some of the others uses I have found for this are as a facial wash (quarter size amount of castor oil & a tsp of charcoal make a good facial), for insect stings (gets rid of the itching), cuts, the list goes on.

I thought the price was expensive at first, but compared to some of the other brands this one has less ingredients, also a better quality of them. I'm not disappointed.

To use this as a toothpaste is very messy & I still have not mastered how not to get it all over the sink or myself when brushing, but that's ok. It does clean up easy. There is no taste or smell, just a gritty feeling to the charcoal.

Don't expect miracles over night though, because as with all natural products they lack the chemicals that provide extreme results in a short amount of time. Natural products take time to work with repeated uses.

title: Works well IF...
text:
The first time I used this, I could barely get the polish to lift up. I used cuticle oil and a cuticle pusher and I wound up tearing up some of my natural nail. After doing some reading, I saw a suggestion to use a traditional basecoat under the gel peel off basecoat. I thought that it sounded silly, but I was willing to try it, as I wanted to have an easy way to take off my gel polish. I have been using Nailtiques Nail Protein Formula 2 as my basecoat because my nails are thin and then tend to peel. Then I put the gel peel off basecoat over the Nailtiques. After that I polish as usual with whatever color/brand of gel polish I have selected. I used an orange stick to assist with lifting and peeling off the polish when I want to remove it, Following this method has worked REALLY well for me and I have done it 4 or 5 times now. No natural nail lifting up! This also lasts a long longer than when I tried to use UNT. UNT lifted on my nails after one 1-2 days usually. This lasts *easily* 1 week+ for me. Capping the free edge properly is key. I rated it 4 stars because, IMO, I shouldn't have to use a traditional basecoat with the peel off basecoat.

UPDATE 12.6.16: I have found that using an orange stick to assist in lifting the gel polish is a KEY FACTOR in making sure that your natural nail does not lift. I figured this out last night. Additional tips for minimal damage: file down your nails prior to taking off the polish. Breaking the seal on the free edge and then washing your hands helps loosen things up, making it easier to lift. Happy peeling!

title: Great Horse Hair Brush
text:
This is my first horse hair shaving brush.. and a great one at that! Its said that horse hair brush is the medium between badger and boar. I tend to disagree more than agree. For me, it's a choice unto itself.

In any case, this is a great brush. The bristles are incredibly soft but nowhere near as thick as badger or boar. Which is to say that this bristles are more brittle in comparison. This is not meant to be a knock on the brush. Rather this means that you'll have to build your lather differently than those brushes (think painting rather than hard swirling).

The heft of this brush is noticeably lighter than other brushes I own. I believe this is due to both the light weight of both the acrylic handle and the bristles. While the weight may take some time getting used to, the brush itself has great balance and builds a formidable lather.

The smell was quite strong on first couple of shaves but will dissipate upon proper conditioning and continuing usage.

The one worry I do have is regarding the bristles. While this brush has been very good with hair loss, I do wonder about long term use since the hair is more brittle than badger or boar. So far however, it has not been an issue. In fact, its slowly becoming my go to brush.

At roughly 30 dollars, it's worth a shot.

With that being said, Korean skin care is always amazing. This lotion in particular smells like roses, but it's not overpowering. It's also light enough where it absorbed into my skin, which I am happy about, because I want to be able to put this on in the morning and put makeup over top of it.

title: A Giant Leap Forward in Dental Care.
text:
I bought a similar model of Sonicare toothbrush about four years ago and I still marvel at how well it works. Honestly, when the price comes down everyone will own one of these.
I never used to enjoy brushing and I never used to brush my teeth as much as they needed it. I was just too lazy. My teeth were a little discolored and my gums were consistently a little puffy around the tooth. Then I bought a Sonicare toothbrush with the interval timer and now I'll never switch back to a manual toothbrush.
After the first few brushings my teeth were noticably whiter and after a few months I noticed the puffiness in my gums was gone.
At 30,000 strokes per minute it's like brushing hundreds of times with a manual brush. But all you have to do is "aim the brush" while it glides back and forth across your teeth. It feels like a vibrator in your hand. The timer pulses every thirty seconds to prompt you to switch from front to back of teeth and from top to bottom. After two minutes it shuts itself off after what is supposedly the ideal length of brushing time.
You can also take this brush with you when traveling as it works for more than a week without recharging.
Could it have any downsides?
Although I consider it easily worth every penny, the upfront cost is staggering compared to a manual toothbrush. It also requires a replacement brush head approximately every six months at about $15 each. But this is a sophisticated unit and is more like a medical device than a disposable supply item. The only thing these two have in common is the brushes on the end and I'm sure the Sonicare's brushes are higher quality.
It is important to note that the brush head will slowly wear out without any visible sign of wear. The performance gradually degrades until the unit seems nonfunctional. I know because I tried to save money by not replacing the brush heads according to schedule. I thought the battery had gone bad and I called customer service for advice. It turns out that the brush head was way overdue for replacement. Fortunately all the moving and wearable parts (including brush, magnets and metal connecting parts) are in the brush head and when they are replaced performance is restored to like-new again.
The first time you use this product it may make your teeth sensitive for a few days (because of the vibration) and while its permanent and rechargeable battery will last through most trips it is physically larger and takes slightly more space to pack than a manual brush.
Now I have never had to share the brush with anyone so I never had to switch brush heads on a daily basis. This seems to me like it would be an enormous hassle as you have to unthread and detach the head each time. While this is possible, I would probably buy two units instead if the finances allowed.
This is one of the best purchases I've ever made.
In summary, if you think you might like it and you can afford it, then go ahead and get one. They last a long time...

title: Works well overall - but "bristles" vary in length year to year, become brittle and break off too easily.
text:
It is difficult to find a large barreled curling iron/brush. HELEN OF TROY offers a broad range of assorted sizes, and they work well. This is my third or fourth purchase of this same model in about 10 years. Even though I purchase the same model, I find that the hard plastic "bristles" vary in height from year to year. The short "bristles" sometimes place the hot barrel too close to my skin, especially when the "bristles" break off (which is fairly easy and common, possibly due to overexposure to heat). The models that arrived with longer "bristles" are more suited for longer hair, however they sometimes "tangle" in the hair -- and THEY, too break off all too easily. (I have recommended to the manufacturer that they add something slightly more flexible to the "bristles" to keep them from getting brittle and breaking, or perhaps design the barrels so that new sets of bristles can be installed, however -- why would they take my suggestion when consumers can simply replace the entire unit with a new one?) The heating elements in these units have never failed; only the "bristles" are problematic.

Overall, I like this model, but I find that I need to replace it after about 12-18 months of use due to loss of "bristles".

title: This is a great product line.
text:
This product is exactly as advertised and shown in the images. This mini system does not come with color, so be prepared. The packaging is attractive, and the products came very well packaged and arrived safely in perfect condition. This gel nail polish kit has a little different texture than some of the kits available these days. This system has a complete nail prep and foundation product line-up much like the really great gel nails from 20 years ago. I'm hoping the long term quality of the nail growth and health with this product line, is as good as the old products as well. As well all know, products can help your nails or destroy them, and this product line, the formulas remind me of the better products that were once available and were very expensive to buy.

The thing people may not be used to is the last step of using the finishing wipe to remove the sticky layer once the manicure is complete. Some top coats are completely set and free of any tackiness right after the curing process. These products cure quickly with some heat, and 60 seconds seemed to be plenty of time. After the top coat and final removal of the tackiness, the nails are perfect. This kit doesn't come with color, so I experimented with a milky white and some blue ink, using the wood tools included in the kit to move and swirl the pigment around. It's a fun, creative way to change up polish. I think stencils could be fun, and I do have mica powders, some bling pieces, to play with as well. I like these products, and the box came with a nice catalogue of other products available.

This product is easy to use, I've experienced no irritation of my cuticles or nail bed, no itching or discomfort at all. The light is really cute, tiny and it works. Just one easy button and it turns off automatically in a minute. I pressed twice to get 2 minutes but found that 1 minute was enough, which is great. The result of this product is thin, but strong, offering flexibility of the nail as well, and no cracking. I'll update with wear and removal. Very reasonable and competitive value. 5 stars.

title: Worst Adidas Shower Gel I've Ever Tried
text:
Let me start this review by saying that I normally really like Adidas' shower gels. I've tried almost every variety in their men's line and none of them have come close to offending me like Water Sport has. Right out of the bottle, this shower gel stinks. It has a very strong, bitter chemical aroma, and it makes me think of both bathroom cleaning solutions and a hair salon. I have no idea what's in this that combats the effects of chlorine, but I imagine this ingredient is to blame for the foul smell.

Using the product, it feels thicker than it looks and goes a long way, like other shower gels from Adidas. As soon as I started to wash my body with it, the fragrance quickly turned into a very heavy single note of burnt hair. It smelled so bad that I was immediately checking myself out to make sure it wasn't chemically singeing my body hair off. Fortunately that wasn't the case, but it really did smell that horrible. Out of the shower, the fragrance left on my skin is slightly sweet and bitterly floral; I'm not an expert, but it smells like iris to me.

I'm not a swimmer, so I have no idea whether or not this shower gel is beneficial regarding marine salts or chlorine. Its only saving grace for me is that the gel is mentholated and gave me a nice cooling feeling. I hate to waste products but I'm very tempted to just throw this bottle away after one wash.

title: good size. keeps my hair dry.
text:
My friend loaned me a reusable shower cap one time and I loved it so much I decided I needed my own. I wanted to find something in a solid color because so many of them are patterned and very loud and that just isn't really for me. I mainly wanted the silver and gold ones, so I gave the pink and purple to the friend I borrowed the cap from so she has spares. I've used them a couple times and they seem to work well. They're big enough to fit all of my hair and my ears in them and they do a reasonable job of keeping the water out. The elastic band lets in a little bit of water around the edges, but that's to be expected. It's not enough to be a problem. The main part of the cap keeps the water out nicely, and the satin layer helps reduce that very loud noise that is caused by water hitting plastic.

As others have complained about, the band is a little bit prickly on the head. I don't have overly sensitive skin, so I don't notice it very much, but if that is something that would bother you, these may not be the right choice. I think a little head prickling is worth it to have the color and style I want, so it really isn't a big deal.

While the size is great for me (I have about chin length, very thick hair) I'm not sure if it would work if your hair was much longer (unless it was very fine). I use up just about all the space in the cap fitting my hair in it, but I also think I have a slightly larger than usual head.

Overall, it works for me and I'm happy with it.

title: Very rich and moisturizing - thick cream
text:
This is an interesting face mask. You get 5 masks for $20 so an ok price, maybe slightly more expensive than usual. You apply this mask to a clean face like you always do. When you open the package you find 2 masks in it, they split the mask up into 2, the top and bottom.

This mask is the first cream mask I have ever used. You will first notice the pleasant scent, the reason I ordered this in the first place. I have a serum by Abib that I love and has an incredible fragrance so I figured this one has to be a great product. This mask feels kind of weird on your face because of the cream. It reminds me a bit of nivea cream to be honest, fragrance wise and thickness / consistency wise. So after the 20 minutes are up you take it off and realize there is still a lot of cream on your face. So you gently massage it into your skin. My face felt a bit sticky from all that extra cream to be honest. After about 20 minutes or so that feeling did start to fade, that is just how long it took for all of it to absorb. This is one rich cream I tell you. My face was nicely moisturized though and it definitely had a bit of a glow from all that cream to it to be honest.

All in all this is a nice mask, but maybe a bit too rich for me. I think this would do wonders when your skin is super dry, like on a horrible winter day when you have been outside in the wind all day and your skin is almost peeling off from the cold dry wind. This would restore it back to health. Right now my skin is just a bit too healthy I would say and this one would just be so much better when my skin is in dire need.

title: Splat vs. MP
text:
Ok. So let me start by saying that until last month I had virgin hair. I went to a professional stylist to get my tips dyed rainbow colors. He used 3 different brands. One had stayed in nicely, the other two washed out in one wash with color safe shampoo and I was left with bleached tips and some random blue strands. So I decided to do it myself. I read all the reviews for both splat and Manic Panic and the tips from people who had used them before purchasing 4 colors of Splat and 2 colors of Manic Panic. I used splat beach however because there were several tips that my stylist had left untouched. I have black hair and the bleach lightened it to a medium blonde in about an hour (I wrapped the tips in tin foil to keep it off my skin) plus it didn't fry my hair! I then colored chunks of hair in random order using all 6 dyes. I wrapped the tips in tin foil again, put a plastic bag over my head and waited 3 hours. After removing the tin foil and washing my hair in cold water (which ran clear after 5 minutes at the most) I towel dryed my hair (the towel wasn't stained) and lo and behold. All the splat colors were vibrant and beautiful and one of the MP colors didn't even turn out. Those chunks are still bleach blonde. I love this stuff.
Now then. A few things to note. Even with 6 color packets on my counter I didn't make a mess. Nothing got stained. Nothing dripped. I just used latex gloves and a whole lotta patience. The stuff is pretty thick so if you're careful you can do this without staining your forehead :)

title: Don't buy it for the vacuum
text:
This popped up in my gold box, and I decided to give it a whirl since the idea of trimming my beard with no mess had a lot of appeal. The vacuum does half work. Unfortunately, catching half the mess won't change the need for clean-up--there's less to clean, but you'll still need to do it. So my main recommendation is that you shouldn't let the vacuum "feature" be your reason for buying this. If anything, it's a slight negative, because the opening for the vacuum gets in the way when you are doing edge trimming without the attachment.
The next down-side is the "memory" rechargeable batteries. Basically, unless you let the batteries completely discharge before recharging, they will hold less and less charge each time. This is mentioned in the folded up piece of paper that passes for a manual--you will want to read through that. Which leads me to my final gripe: That piece of paper is extremely poorly done--diagrams with no explaination, unclear instructions, etc. So you do have to read it, but you're going to spend some time trying to puzzle it out before you actually figure it out.
For all my complaining, the trimmer isn't completely without merit. It does do a decent job of trimming my beard, which is of course the main point of the thing. I also didn't have any real noise complaints, which seems to be an issue for other reviewers.
On balance though, my main recommendation would be don't pay for the vacuum, because you won't be getting what you paid for.

title: Lovely oil with so many uses
text:
I love apricot kernel oil. It definitely one of my favorite carrier oils because it has so many uses. It's nice to have a 16 ounce bottle of cold pressed oil to work with. Here are just a few of the uses for this wonderful oil:

1) Apricot kernel oil for Skin
Apricot kernel oil is good for people with sensitive skin. It is non-irritant and soothing for the skin. It is light and quickly makes the skin soft and smooth. Apricot oil penetrates deep into the skin. It is easy to apply on the skin as it quickly spreads on the skin. It soothes irritated skin. A massage with apricot kernel oil is good for dry, parched skin. It can be used post shower to lock the moisture into the skin. Since it is light, it wont leave a greasy residue. Once absorbed into skin, it provides moisturization for hours. Apricot kernel oil is one of the best carrier oils for massage as it penetrates nicely into the skin and also improves the delivery of essential oils and other herbal agents. This oil is also good for infusing with herbs and absorbing their essence. It can be utilized for various kinds of massage that require an oil.
2. Apricot kernel oil for Hair
Apricot oil is loved by many people around the world for their hair care. When applied to the hair shafts,it helps to detangle hair. These are the health benefits that organic apricot oil provides to hair. It promotes hair growth because of the nutrients in it, especially Vitamin E. It reduces dry scalp problems and helps to achieve gorgeous shiny hair without any greasiness. When used as a hot oil treatment, it conditions the hair and provides them nutrition. It softens the hair, so that they are more manageable and easily combed.
3. As an Under Eye Cream
Apricot oil can be applied just like almond oil for healing under eye skin. It aids in reducing dark circles, puffiness and helps to strengthen the skin around this region. With regular application of apricot kernel oil, one can reduce the appearance of fine lines and wrinkles around the eyes.
4. Face Oil
Apricot kernel oil is a nice face oil, especially when compared to other heavier oils. It helps to improve skin tone, nourish the skin and lower the appearance of aging signs, like wrinkles, lines and blemishes. However, this oil should be avoided by people who are suffering from acne or are prone to acne. That is because it has a comedogenicity of 2. This means that the oil is mildly comedogenic and it can clog skin pores. This may result in acne breakouts and blackheads.
5. Heart Health
Consumption of apricot kernel oil can be a healthy choice for the heart and the cardiovascular system. This oil has demonstrated the ability to lower the risk of heart attack in rats and can possibly perform the same function in humans. You can use apricot oil as a salad dressing and by using it for cooking certain recipes that go well with the flavor of this oil.

I tried this recently on my dry knees and on my wife's dry itchy back. I used a bit on my knees, and it felt cool and moisturizing. I used quite a lot on my wife's entire back, and I could really smell the Tea Tree oil in this, that is without question. The product is a white lotion of normal consistency. I would not say it stands out in my mind as "breath taking" or anything like that. But, it is a well blended lotion with Tea Tree oil, as advertised. I have several bottles of Tea tree oil, and have used it for years, so I'm quite familiar with the scent and it's positive effects. This lotion is not runny, and holds together well as a large dollop on the back of my hand. It's texture is silky smooth during application, and it absorbs quickly, leaving a non-greasy feeling, with a moderate Tea Tree scent that lingers. When dried (less than 5 minutes), the skin is softer, and more hydrated feeling. This, like many "general blend" lotions containing a specific essential oil, gives you the short to medium term benefit of hydration and softness, with the nice smell and implied benefits of the oil it is blended with. This is not a high end night cream or eye cream, but a good quality hand, body, and face lotion in my opinion. Just as advertised. It's a good product.

title: A Must Have, REALLY!  Buy It!!!
text:
Just so you know, I have seen the original version of this glove for awhile & have been extremely skeptical about how useful it could be. It looked silly to me even with one thumb, LOL! However, I am coming off of two arm and hand surgeries back to back (right & left ) & all my brushes were extremely dirty and I was dreading washing them like the plague. (I'm still recovering so my hands & arms are only at 80% strength) I ran across this new version & watched the video on Sigma's site and thought I would try it out because I really needed something to make this easier right now.

I have many brushes including a bunch of big dense ones like the SigMax brushes. I loath the chore of washing my brushes. I do it less often than I should. My hands become prunes, I wreck my nails and it takes for-like-ever! Plus, I can never seem to get the big dense ones clean enough deep in the center no matter how long I stand there and try to wash them.

Today I used this brush cleaning glove and HOLY FRIGGIN' MOLY!!! It's next level stuff!

It was so EASY to DEEPLY clean all my brushes in a FRACTION of my normal time. My dense brushes have never been this clean. It was an actual pleasure to wash them! Never thought I would ever say that.

Do not get an imitation. I saw those & thought about saving some money but in the end bought this glove. They really designed this to actually do all the work for you AND save your hands & nails. It is well thought out.

All the different areas have a very useful purpose that do all the work. You need all the different areas. The area where you shape your brush at the end actually also squeezes out all the excess water from even those dense SigMax brushes. They felt 50% dry right after washing! I'm sure they will dry faster than ever. The terry inner glove made the whole silicone glove experience really nice and cozy. Your hand is comfortable all during the washing & after. None of that sweaty, sticky feeling you can get with rubber gloves. My hand was completely dry even after about 30 brushes!

I like this new design, with the 2 thumbs, because you can always use your dominant hand to hold the brush. With one thumb you would have to switch hands to use the other side of the glove. One side is for face/larger brushes & the other is for eye/smaller brushes.

I use Dr. Bronner's Castile Liquid Soap in the Baby Mild formula. Get yourself a pump dispenser & mix half soap and half water in the dispenser. Having the pump helps speed along the washing process as you just pump the soap onto the center cleaning area of the glove. You never have to put down the brush you are cleaning. This also helps keep the brush aimed down helping you not get water running up into the ferrule by accident as you work.

This glove also makes it easy to know, just by sight, when your brush is completely clean, soap foam is white, and completely rinsed, no foam comes out of your brush when swirled after rinsing.

My brushes are thoroughly deep cleaned for the first time in ages. They look brand new!

If you have a bunch of brushes or even if you don't have that many but have some of the big dense ones, think of this glove as an investment. It will help you preserve the life of your brushes and keep bacteria off your face, yuck.

It is really well made and should last a really long time. They only thing I could see happening is replacing the inner glove as it is terry cloth.

I LOVE this and will happily be washing my brushes all the time now. My face, hands & nails are all going to benefit.

title: Over all really good, once you get the hang of it.
text:
The scraper is plastic so you don't have to worry about it scraping up your plates. I've seen people using just old credit cards to do scraping but because it's free why not use it, plus it fits in your hand easily so it's easier to grip, which is great if you have small hands like me.

The stamper itself, is made up of two parts. The squishy thing to actually transfer the stamp to your nail, and the tube thing that holds it. They do come apart so it's easier to clean (or whatever).

And now for some things I wish I knew sooner:
1. You do not have to press as hard as possible when scraping the plate. Just as long as you move the excess polish out of the way you're good.
2. Newer polishes work best. I know there are specifically polishes for stamping but I don't have those. I have tried to stamp with several different polishes and I've found that newer polishes are easier to pick up with the stamper because they are more liquid like.
3. Move quickly-ish, no you don't have to race to get the polish on your nail but remember that it's a very small, thin amount of polish that dries very quickly, so don't wait a millennium.
4. Roll the stamper over the plate. Start with one side and roll to the other, I've found that this works best as opposed to just straight down on the plate.
5. Remember to use the clearness of the thingy, it's easy to forget that it is clear so remember it is the diffrence between a straight design and crooked design.

title: The Sdara Hydrating Sheet Mask is definitely worth a try.  I will be buying it again.
text:
As of today, I have used these Sdara Hydrating Face Masks on two separate occasions. The first thing I noticed was that it stayed in place on my face better than the mask from a different brand I had used previously. The Sdara mask seems to be of a somewhat thinner material and it is well saturated with the hydrating ingredients. Due to both these factors, it molds to the surface of the face more completely, as well as probably staying in place more easily.

After sitting with the mask on for a while, I experienced a noticeable soothing sensation on my skin. I found this to be pleasant and relaxing.

The directions on the back of the packet containing the mask say to leave it on for 25-30 minutes. From my two times experience with this product, I have to agree with that. One time I left it on for more than 30 minutes and noticed a kind of astringent sensation on my skin. The mask is not meant to be on for longer than 30 minutes.

The directions written on the back of the packet are clear and easy to understand. I was also thrilled to see that the mask is 100 percent biodegradable and cruelty free (no harsh laboratory testing on animals).

Looking at the results afterward, my skin definitely looked less dry and felt softer. I do plan on ordering a supply of these sheet masks again. Thank you.

title: Solids don't cure.
text:
So, the glittery ones work just fine, they fully cure and are decently durable. They have a shiny clean finish and you can spread them out in patterns to give a cool effect. But the solid colors suck. They never fully cure, I've held them under the light up to 4 times the usual cure takes. And that's upside-down and right-side-up. No angle with the light on your finger will fully cure the layer of gel close to the nail. And your nails will pop off and leave you with sticky smears of uncured gel on your nails. The only thing that made this purchase not awful, was the glittery gels. The light penetrates easily and they are sturdy nails.

The best I can suggest for the solids, is using paper nail forms and curing thin layer by thin layer. And even then I don't have high hopes of it fully curing.

title: Great price, fantastic products
text:
I've been searching for the perfect liquid lip stain for years now, and all three products in this set (the ink velvet and the water tints) fit the bill. So many other products dry too quickly and have applicators that are either stick straight or a standard doefoot. Neither is great for poutier lips, and mine aren't even that pouty. Peripera managed to perfect the formula and applicator for me. The applicator is at a slight angle, which helps to follow the curves of your lips while still getting an even line along the edges. The formulas apply uniformly, and you get a bit of leeway before they set. They also don't enhance lip lines or dry out my lips (my biggest pet peeves with other liquid lip stains). I think the contour product is better as an overall bronzer than a contour because it's so sheer. The blush is a standard pink that should work for most skin tones.

My only complaint is that when you put in all the shelves, all five products will not fit in the fridge. I've tried various combos and can only get four of them in.

After all, mucous is supposed to protect delicate tissues. That's what it's for.

Well, now here comes this snail mucous skin cream and I was very interested to try it, and I haven't been disappointed. A few years ago my skin started to get dry and flair up in red after I shaved. I tried moisturizers on it with varying degrees of success. But this skin repair cream did just that in a couple days, it repaired my inflamed facial area.

This is the best cream I've tried so far. It's not greasy and soaks into my skin quickly so a few minutes after I put it on, nobody can see that I've used it. And, a little goes a long way if you just apply what you need.

title: 6 piercings, quick and painless!
text: 6 piercings for $9! Not bad at all. Easy to use, common sense really. Tip: be sure to remove white square and push the blue thumb tab in just a bit (until you hear a click) to make it easier for when you are ready to pierce the ear. Not necessary, but highly recommend. Also makes it easier to align the earring to your placement marking. I pierced my second lobe holes myself, easy and painless. Next day, my sister asked to me re-pierce her holes and add her second holes. She took all four like a champ, wasn’t too bad, just sore for a few days because the backs of the earrings are kind of uncomfortable (especially when trying to sleep on your side), but bearable. I’d be sure to have the backing of the earring at the farthest end to ensure space for your lobe to breathe and in case there is any swelling. Also be smart about the whole process, use common sense. Wash your hands with antibacterial soap, wear gloves, clean the lobe and surrounding skin with alcohol (it includes some alcohol pads by the way, so no excuse), mark your spot (triple-check if it is even!), and take the disposable out of its sterile packaging, consider my tip above, align with marking, and push blue tab quickly. Voila, your lobe is pierced. After care is just as important, so clean your earrings and freshly pierced lobes with a saline solution!!! I wouldn’t recommend alcohol or hydrogen peroxide as it can be drying and may irritate your pierced lobes and possibly become infected. So yeah, saline solution, or ear cleaning solution. You can buy a bottle at Claire’s or even here on Amazon. Twice a day, every day, for at least 6 weeks straight. Try to avoid makeup in your ear/neck area, but if anything, just remove your makeup at the end of the day and clean your piercing with saline solution. You can occasionally do salt soaks or saline solution soaks. Helps deep clean and heal faster I heard. Anyway, I’d recommend this product if you’re looking to pierce your lobes and don’t want to pay to have it professionally done at a more costly price. If you have the guts to pierce yourself with a hollow piercing needle, i’d do that instead, but because I couldn’t do it myself, I chose to get the disposable ear gun/staple.

text:
Pros
• Sturdy and durable – The tweezers themselves are aluminum, but surprisingly sturdy.
• Great carrying case – Tweezers fit inside tube, just like a lipstick!
• Convenient mirror – Located inside of plastic tube that stores the tweezers.
• Easy to understand – Push a button and use.
• Light – Bright blue, useful in a way.
• Packaging – The packaging is honestly one of the best I’ve received a beauty product in. The bag is sheer with a ribbon in place for the draw string. It’s already filled with my other beauty products. The carrying case is what makes it though! It looks like a tube of lipstick, and when you remove the tweezers there’s a little mirror inside.
• Bellabe-esque spring wand – It works! It hurts like anything but man, it gets the job done. Beware areas with high density hair, it will nearly bring tears. Also, I didn’t find it effective on the outer lying hairs of my eyebrow, I believe the skin is too loose.

Cons
• Light – The button is flimsy and seems like it may break eventually. Also, when I attempted to turn the light off the first time I accidentally held down the button which actually made the light strobe. Also, it may seem silly but I felt like the light was a little too bright and washed out the area of my skin I was attacking. Finally, the light takes 3 of those watch like batteries, and I’m sorry to say that the odds of me taking time out of my day to go get these things once it dies are very slim. It does come with them included though, so for now that’s not an issue.
• Mirror – The mirror is definitely a convenience and the placement is a great idea, however, I feel like it would be more useful if the mirror was a magnifying one so I didn’t need to hold it so close to my face.
• Tweezers – The ends are not as slanted as I would like, and while I may be just tweezer challenged, I found myself chasing the same strand of hair for minutes at a time. It would be great if you could switch the tweezers that the light attaches to, but that doesn’t seem possible.

Overall, while the packaging for this product is awesome, I don’t think it’s for me. But hey, I could just be less tweezer savvy than others.

title: Good, not perfect, but really nice
text:
This is now the second makeup removing towel of this kind and I will admit I was a skeptic about this magic towel concept, but I was offered the opportunity to review it at a reduced price and curious to compare it to the other brand I have tried. The towel itself came with instructions to wash before use, after washing I immediately noticed when I pulled it out of the washer the towel felt nearly dry already.Which is the same experience I had with the other towel. So instead of drying it with the rest of the load, I left it out to air dry to see how long it really takes to dry. One of the things I was really wondering about this towel is, if it works, could it be something to take on a long trip, where I will be packing up and moving locations every couple of days. I wouldn't want to through a moist towel into my bag and end up with a musty bag of cloths for the entire trip! This did take a while to dry, maybe a couple of hours, but that seems far less than a regular washcloth or towel.

The washcloth itself is super soft and plush, and when you get it wet is holds ALOT of water, which might be part of its magic. The directions say to get the towel wet and rub the towel with tcircular motions. Once done you can choose to flip the cloth to the to exfoliate. This towel feels really nice and gentle on my skin, and and it definitely took off the BB foundation and undereye concealer I was wearing. As for my eye shadow, eye liner and mascara, it did a decent job, but there was definitely residue left over that I felt I needed to to back over with a little soap and water. I actually went back over my face with a wet wipe to see if there was any other make up residue left behind and did find that a light amount of my face cream still wiped off, but it was a very small amount, it seemed that it was mostly my eye area that needed a little extra wash.

Overall I really like this washcloth. The idea of rarely having to use soap or chemicals to get a clean fact is really appealing. I am prone to stye’s so I will always be more vigilant about cleaning my mascara and eyeliner area more, but overall I am presently surprised by this product.

As stated earlier, I received this product at a reduced price for my honest and unbiased review.

title: The Root to my Happiness; Male, African with afro living in Minnesota Winter
text:
I have been using this product on and off for 2 years, it is very hard to find good products for black hair; especially in my case very frizzy nappy hair + Minnesota weather = bad hair days. I have tried a number of products claimed to be for my kind of hair but they fall short 90% of the time, either too thick to apply or too watery to even make sense of. I am surprised that each time I get disappointed, I run back to Garnier like an Ex.

I use it once or twice a day or pretty much as many times as I choose to shower, I also use it with Garnier AntiFrizz serum. Works wonders! A little squirt of both in my palm, rub together and massage into my hair, comb, style and ready for anything. My hair retains its moisture for about 70% of the day, when it feels dry, I can still feel the silk on the strands. My hair doesn't smell like carpet any more, the fruity smell is powerful enough to last days. Even better in the summer, no carpety smell!

Until another magic formula shows up, this is my best product yet.

text: This self tanning mitt is perfect for applying the self tanner. I also used the latex gloves that come with the actual sunless tanner lotion as well for extra protection but honestly, I don't think I even needed them. I have never used two tanning mitts to apply self tanner before, but the self tanner came with one and I purchased a second one so I could try using two at once and I'll never go back to using just one, it's so much easier and quicker to apply the sunless tanner with two mitts. And if you are looking for a great sunless tanner, check out the sun labs self tanners that go with this mitt. I've never tried a better self tanner in my life, and believe me, I've tried them all. title: Pretty decent product but do your research
text:
Overall, this product isn’t horrible compared to others on the market. It is paraben-free, sulfate-free, EU Allergen free and uses minimal ingredients however it also contains alcohol, silicone and is not safe for fungal acne. After running this product through a cosmetic ingredient safety checker, it scored an 88% one the EWG Health Rating. Most popular, name-brand face lotions are around 65%-80% on the EWG Health Rating. I use the EWG (Environment Working Group) as a reference when checking products and try to stay away from the alarmist side. Only 8% of this product is considered “moderate risk” mainly polyarylamide, Fragrance (unnecessary additive; possible allergy) , alcohol denat. (Bad for dry skin, bad for sensitive skin, potentially block pores) and BHT (also found in edibles, rubber products and is banned in UK and EU due to limited research showing BHT is linked to cancer). This product is good for brightening, anti-aging and promotes wound healing. It also contains steric acid which can potentially block pores.

Keep in mind, everyone’s skin is different and what effects one person may not effect another. Learn your skin and what products work best for you. Personally, I would stay away from this product if you have very dry skin and/or sensitive skin. I have “normal” skin (no sensitivities, not overly dry or oily, limited acne, no allergies) and didn’t have any issues with this product so far. It has a light scent that isn’t overpowering but completely unnecessary (I HATE fragrance in beauty products; stick with essential oils). It absorbed nicely and didn’t leave my face feeling oily. I am giving this product 4 stars as of February 21, 2021 due to the minimal ingredients and will update this review once a larger amount of time has passed to fully understand how to works with my skin.

title: Not as Strong As I Hoped
text:
I am relatively new to solid colognes. I own this sampler set, Oak City Beard's Sandalwood Bourbon, and a sample set from another company. The other company's set was my first venture into solid colognes. I liked the variety it offered, and their colognes usually lasted most of the day.

I expected the same from this set.

I will admit, I liked variety that this offered, which is why I ordered it. Now that I've had time to try out each one, here are my thoughts. (Please note, cologne can smell different on each person, so what didn't work for me, may work for you.)

Barista - I don't drink coffee, so the thought of smelling like coffee all day was not a selling point for me. I figured this would be my least favorite of the four. When I opened the tin, it smelled like a 30-year-old motel lobby. A powerful scent of cheap black coffee, with a hint of musty cigarettes and pleather couches. I was not impressed. Still, I put it on and the smell changed to more of a 1990s coffee shop. Fortunately, the cocoa smell came forward more once it was on me, and the coffee was not as strong. I don't hate it as much as I thought I would. In fact, I kind of like how it smells on me.

Woodland Ranger - My favorite out of the bunch. While you may think it would make you smell like a Christmas tree, it's more of a clean outdoors scent.

Snow Leopard - I love me some sandalwood, so this was the one I really bought the set for. It says there is peppermint in it, but I can't smell it. Also, I feel like the vanilla overpowers the sandalwood. Not as good as I had hoped. Not bad at all, just not what I expected. (This one also seems to dissipate quicker than the others.)

Uncle Jack - I smell the bourbon and a trace of tobacco, but once again, the vanilla is the stronger scent here. It's definitely not a bad smell, probably my second favorite of the pack.

As I mentioned in the headline, the colognes are just not as strong as I hoped for. I mean, I don't want to overpower everyone in my general vicinity, but I do like to smell the cologne throughout the day and none of these do that. Perhaps I'm not putting enough on. Like I said, I'm new to this whole solid cologne thing.

title: I wear them everyday
text:
10 months ago, I cut off ALL my hair, (49 3/4 inches, so A LOT) to give to a coworker whose teenage daughter had cancer and needed hair to have a wig made. I had enough hair where she wouldn't need to even ask anyone else, so yeah, I chopped it all off. That girl cares more about the way she looks, then I do, at my age. But I remember being 14...and I cared at that age what I looked like. I cared a whole bunch. But now, not so much, and since locks of love and other charities don't give wigs to cancer patients because "their hair should grow back" (nonsense), her parents were looking for something affordable and found a place that would make a real hair wig, for about $1000, if they supplied the hair.

For the first few months after I cut it off, all was fine. I have never had short hair before and honestly it was nice. But as it grew out, it started to become annoying. I have a very prominent widows peak, so never had bangs, and it was getting long enough to get in my face which was super aggravating. Plus, having it on my neck...can't even describe how that cut the nerves....

I have never really wore headbands, so didn't have any, so started searching online for something to help keep my growing hair off my face. I read the reviews on this headband set, and many others. Focusing only on the negative reviews, because...thats what matters right? Why don't people like these? Only thing I saw on this set though was that people thought they were to tight.

I have an average size head, definitely not small, but don't think it overly large either...and since they were cotton, I saw this set as a win, win. They were the width I wanted, the neutral colors I wanted, and if they were a bit small, would be more likely to hold up the hair behind my head better. If they were TO small, they were cotton, so I could stretch them out. Plus, the price was definitely good for the number you get, compared to others I looked at.

So, I ordered them in June and have pretty much had them on my head everyday since. I didn't find them to small at all. Only problem I'm having is, I keep misplacing them! So, actually came on to order more, as I can only find two at the moment...but decided I would go ahead and write a review while I was here. It's still going to be a while before my hair is long enough to pull up in a ponytail, so until then, I am 100% reliant on these to keep my sanity, as my hair grows back in.

text: I bought two different dry eye masks, the Dry Eye Mask by Heyedrate and the MediViz Blepharitis Eye Mask.  When I received them, I noticed that they were virtually identical: packaging identical, shape and size of the masks virtually identical. The only two differences I found are (1) that one came with a green pouch and the other came with a blue pouch; and (2) the MediViz may be just a slight bit smaller. I went ahead and tried the MediViz on the third day, mainly to compare the two.  In my opinion, they both felt the same on my face, both seemed to work well, and my experience with both was the same.  After microwaving them for 20 seconds, neither were too hot to the touch, so I could immediately apply them to my eyes.  And as several reviewers noted, both cooled off within 5 to 10 minutes. I did not feel this was a bad thing, since the instructions say to apply for up to 10 minutes. So the 5 - 7 minutes I used each of them seemed sufficient to alleviate my symptoms. title: Itchy scalp & covered in hives ... again :(
text:
I wanted to like this shampoo. With the reviews, how couldn't I? I came to Amazon several months ago looking for the right shampoo that was paraben & sulfate free. I am trying to be more conscientious about the chemicals and scents that I use on my body and this over-delivered. I purchased it in the vanilla scent and anxiously awaited for my hair transformation.

After two shampoos, my scalp started itching constantly. My scalp, back of my neck, and the top of my back (all areas where the shampoo had come into contact with my hair and skin) were covered in itchy, irritated bumps. I stopped using the shampoo immediately. It took me two weeks for my skin and the itch to clear up and go away. I passed the bottle on to a friend with the disclaimer "People love it, but it covered my skin in hives ..." I was later told it worked just fine for them. Go figure.

A few weeks ago it was time to hunt for a new shampoo. Again, I found Sweet Baby Shampoo. More stellar reviews, one of which specifically called out the hives. That reviewer stated that after switching to the unscented, the hives never re-appeared. Perfect! One-click purchase. I was down to give it another go. Again, stellar reviews.

Three shampoos and the scalp itching is back. The hives are smaller this time, but they're still there. I do not get it. What is in this stuff?! In a pinch, I have washed my hair with all sorts of crummy products. I spent a week in the desert with high alkaline dust matting down my hair and washed my hair with bar soap. No problem (other than dried out hair). I've used $1 drug store brands, the crap they stock in hotels, even the all purpose shampoo / conditioner / soap concoction they supply for free in the gym. Never had a single reaction to any of it. Think about it. Something isn't adding up. Sadly.

title: Good color match and full coverage without feeling too heavy
text:
I often struggle with finding foundations that are light enough and match my undertones. A lot of brands’ lightest shades are either too dark or too orange, and I jumped at the chance to try this after hearing good things about 000.

It arrived the next day with lightning fast shipping. I like the interesting design of the bottle, which has a pump that twists up and retracts. I would feel comfortable taking it on the go and hopefully not making a mess in my makeup bag.

While 000 is described by the manufacturer as a neutral shade, it did look very yellow when I first swatched it. But it looks more neutral blended out and appears to be a near-perfect match for me. It is very high coverage, almost more like a concealer than a foundation. I think a full pump is too much product for my entire face, so this will probably last for a long time as little as I need. While I’m not normally a fan of full coverage foundations due to not liking a matte look, this one has more of a satin finish that looks natural, and it really feels lightweight.

It does stick to very dry patches, so exfoliating and moisturizing prior to use is a must, and I wouldn’t recommend it if you have extremely dry or textured skin. On top of sunscreen and primer, it covered my pores and fine lines without making them more noticeable. I am a little concerned about some of the reviews that said the pump mechanism stopped working for them, but so far haven’t had any problems with it. I definitely recommend trying 000 if you are also pale and struggle to find the right shade match.

title: Yes the Hair Grip Works
text:
I first saw this concept, Grip wrap for Wigs on Youtube. I searching on Amazon, I found many different makers, sellers.
I chose this one by the embroidered Logo (on the side) hoping for quality. They all resemble each other, quality didn't appear to be
the same, as you can find many of these for sale, names vary.

My (Brown) Hair Grip arrived today. I have tried it with two different Wigs.
1. Outre Dominican Blow Out Color #2 Half Wig with back and front combs and adjustable strap
2. FreeTress Equal Evyln lace front in Taffy. 2 side temple combs, back comb and adjustable strap

1. Outre: I did not need to use the front comb at all. I did apply the back comb, it's not necessary though.
I did it out of habit. The Half Wig is in it's natural place, snug, it's moveable yes, it's not going anywhere,
The Grip actually makes the wig look more natural upon my head, it pulls it inward as natural hair looks.

The Hair Grip wrap works as intended, no combs required to keep the wig in place, snug.

2. FreeTress Evyln Color Taffy. I did not use either side temple combs.
The Hair Grip I chose is dark brown.

Taffy Evyln is a dark root, darkest brown, blonde ombre,
if you really stare hard you can slightly see the grip/wrap in the part.
You would have to know it's there to detect it. I do not believe anyone would see it outright.

Again same result, The Hair Grip works as intended. The wig fit is snug, no way is it coming off.
Whatever the magic is with this The Hair Grip, it does enhance the actual fit of your wig in the positive.

I am glad I chose the Dark Brown Hair Grip vs the Beige, the Black, my natural hair is Darkest Brunette.
The brown color for me will be the most versatile for longevity of use and wear.

The actual fabric is very light, it's nearly weightless, it is not a velvet material.
The Velcro is soft to touch. I do not foresee it damaging my wig interiors, nor the hair either.

The Hair Grip is Firm " in place" there is not a feeling that I am wearing a headband..
No ring around the head feel. It's adjustable too, you can lighten or pull tighter, the velcro is ample.
The attach part of Velcro is about 2 inches, the connect side of the Velcro is several inches, this
will fit all heads, I can't see how it wouldnt.

Remember if you are wearing " wide' part lace fronts,
Color will come into play, the Grip is going to be visible depending on Wig color nearest the part.

I hope my review helps out, as it's a bit confusing with so many nearly same, yet not alike.

I am satisfied with my purchase, it is a worthy investment.

title: Massages, Cleans, Exfoliates Lips
text:
I have a bunch of these little brushes. I love the feel of the silicone "bristles." So I have some for lip exfoliation, a few for facial massages, and even separate ones for facial cleansing. They're easy to clean and so soft.

What I haven't had is a single brush that does it all. And when you travel, it's just ridiculous to be carrying not only a toothbrush, a sponge blender, and two makeup brushes, but three additional silicon brushes. You end up with a makeup tote instead of a makeup case, and suddenly you're checking a bag just because of your annoyingly overstuffed makeup bag.

Not me, because now I have one, and a spare, silicon brush that does it all. One side for massage (which, by the way, if I am so lacking in good taste, I can do in the comfort of my seat on the plane), one side for cleaning, and one appropriately small-sized area for exfoliating lip and/or nose. And that lip exfoliation is one of my favorites - back in college, we used to grab a towel and do a quick scrub before putting on lipstick, but this is so much nicer to your lips.

And these two brushes are so much more efficient and space saving for me.

title: Nice Brush | Similar To We Love Doodles & Chris Christensen | Cats Love It | Easily Removes Hair
text:
If I didn't already own & love my "We Love Doodles" brand of big slicker brush, I would have rated this brush at a full 5 stars. Mostly what I don't care for this brush vs Doodles is the handle. It is a little more narrow so it's a teensy bit less comfortable to hold. I have carpel tunnel. I've been grooming cats furever & grooming English angora rabbits for well over a decade.

🐱For short & long haired cats, this brush works great. All of my cats love this brush & my Doodles brand. I can comb all of them except for my 14yo with a surprising amount of pressure & they roll around purring. Tons of hair gets picked up into the tines. Unlike some styles of brushes & combs, no hair is left behind around the tail area.

Removing the hair from the brush is very easy. Start at one side from the bottom to loosen & then move to the other side. Keep working your way around & it comes off in a nice clean loose mat. I actually prefer these types of slicker brushes over self cleaning brushes & also over brushes with the little plastic beads on the ends. If you groom your animal properly, you don't need little balls on the ends of the tines. Those balls also make it a little harder to get the brush fully clean of hair.

Cosmetically, I like the look of the brush much better than my Doodles brush. This is all black with a more classy branding in small white text on the head. We Love Doodles is blue & loudly brands itself on the head.

🐰I don't recommend this style of brush for English angora rabbits. I have found that my bunnies seem to be more comfortable with smaller slickers with shorter tines. You'd think with their dense long coats, you'd want something large with long tines, but it really doesn't work out like you'd expect. At least for me it doesn't.

🐰Recommended for English Angora Rabbits:

🐇Doggy Man sells a small soft slicker brush that my angora rabbits love. It's plastic with a little blue ring on the handle. I have purchased/replaced many of them over the years (the handles tend to break over time) because they work well.
🌐 https://smile.amazon.com/gp/product/B001NLVFH2
🐇I also recommend if money allows, a small slicker brush by Chris Christensen. I've never needed to replace it.
🌐 https://smile.amazon.com/gp/product/B00GU7NKWW

Personally, I'd shop between this brand (Rita's), We Love Doodles, & Chris Christensen. Chris Christensen is top of the line. They are worth it if you have the money. We Love Doodles has been the middle ground for me. They were originally priced at $50, but the price has been a lot lower for a while now. Rita's is currently the second most expensive & probably the lowest quality of the three brands. However, I've been using it for the least amount of time, so it's too early to know for sure. So far I like all three.

title: These are not USDA certified oils. 2 stars ✨
text:
First, I will say these oils seem fine. They work well together or apart, mixed into other skincare products or alone. I use these types of oils to make my own facial oil mix or to add to my moisturizer.
The thing I absolutely hate that companies do to try to sell their products is to say things that aren't true. The USDA does not certify oils - food, cosmetic, or otherwise. The fact that the bottle says this product is USDA certified on one side, and the other side says not intended for ingestion should speak volumes. The USDA certifies and regulates the welfare and production of food products; meaning products that you ingest. So, why on earth would they certify a product you cannot ingest? The bottle also makes outright claims of known cures from using these oils. There is no disclaimer on either bottle that states that these claims have not been approved or proven by the FDA, or whatever the disclaimer is that is mandatory. There are ingredients listed, one ingredient for each product, the oil, and that's it. Nothing tells how these oils were extracted. Therefore, we do not know if they are refined or unrefined. They probably don't know either. So you see, therein lies the lies and deception.
These oils would be much better if they weren't tied to lies. Because you know what they say about lies... if you tell one you have to tell more to keep up with the first one. Is what they say in the bottle really what's in the bottle? Are they pure oils or mixed with a lesser oil? Oils are greasy. If they are unrefined, why aren't they greasy? When you refine oils, you take away a lot of their natural properties and their nutritive value, is that why they aren't greasy? Because of the lies and lack of important information, I really don't know for sure what these oils are.
Because of the deceptive practices and claims made, I would not recommend these or any of their other oils.
