title: Dyed perfectly, so in love 💜
text:
Okay... I just got this hair and just dyed it and cannot tell you how it sheds (because it didn’t at all during the whole dyeing and styling process) how it tangles (also didn’t tangle at all that whole time) or how long it will last, but if you want to hear how silky soft and gorgeous and beautiful it looks when it’s dyed then keep reading 😋

I used just ONE box of Revlon Color silk #60 to dye a 10” frontal, 12” bundle and 14” bundle of this hair. It was my first time ever dyeing bundles, but I’m thrilled with how they turned out. Literally PERFECT. Everyone on youtube suggested this dye for 613 hair and you just can’t beat the price. I never really wash my bundles (gross I know, but I like only wear them once or twice) so I can’t say how long the dye lasts. What I did was cowash the hair with the conditioner in the box first and then first put the dye on the roots of the frontal. It stained the lace underneath in weird polka
for patterns, but you can see it so it doesn’t matter. Again, I did *not* know what I was doing lol. Then I put half the dye on the bundles while they were still wrapped and worked it through with my hands, without combing it through. Then I went back to the frontal and combed all the dye through evenly after giving the first round of dye to sit while I was working on the bundles. Once that was all even I went back to the bundles, unrolled them, put the remaining half of the bottle on them, worked it through with my hands on both and then combed it through each strand. I rinsed the frontal out first, in the sink with the highest water pressure and only rinsed for about three minutes. Then rinsed each bundle for three minutes and then went back and rinsed all the dye out of each one. By doing everything in batches and unevenly it left behind a bunch of different colors and made it look so natural. If you let it sit longer than 30 minutes it will start to turn a way different color than blonde haha so beware. You can see the roots on the frontal look much darker because they had dye on them for the longest period of time, but even though that was an accident I think it looks even better haha. And when you put the dye on be sure to use vertical stripes, not horizontal ones! I am in love with the color and this is probably the only dye I will ever use for 613 hair.

I let it air dry for about 30 minutes, which if I’m honest was not enough, but I’m so impatient lol. They were mostly dry except for at the very top. I did not blow dry them (so important). I just used a flat iron to curl small strands one by one (whole styling took one hour 🤦‍♀️). And even though they were a bit damp they still came out perfectly and they HOLD a curl like none other. Idk how it would be if you used a curling iron, but curling with a flat iron always gives the best results. They smell so good from the conditioner even though I just conditioned and then dyed and then didn’t put anything else on them. And they are so silky like Disney princess hair. I don’t plan on wearing these for a few months, but I love them so much.

PS I took those pictures outside in the sunlight so you can really see the true shade!

title: Works surprisingly well
text:
I've seen these steamer machines that are used to remove gel nail polish and while I've always wanted to try them, I was very skeptical and unwilling to spend the money on a gadget that may or may not work. But, removing the gel polish is the worst part or the thing I hate about gel polish: it's time consuming and so hard on the nail bed. I've seen mixed reviews online about gel polish steamers but I finally decided to try one.
This gel polish remover machine actually works. It was easy to put together and I was able to completely remove my gel polish in under 20 minutes. First and most important is to file the top layer of gel down first with a nail file before using this device. I was not able to get the gel polish offf without filing the surface first. I put about two capfuls of 100% acetone (you can use less) into the little tray and turned the machine on. Once it beeps, you can stick your fingers inside. It gets a little hot but it's not painful. After five minutes the machine will beep and I am able to scrape off most of the gel polish. I have to do a second round to get certain areas that just won't scrape off. And when I say scrape off, I mean easily scrape off not scraping and hurting the surface of the nail. I guess I should say push off the gel polish to remove it. I leave the remaining acetone in the tray and either reuse it or dump it. I would say this is easier than using aluminum foil or plastic nail caps because you do the whole hand at once. With foil or plastic caps, I never get my whole hand done at once. This was easier and I didn't use any cotton balls and I used less acetone.

The device is a little pricey. It's basically a warming plate fitted inside a contained area with holes to place your fingers. It's worth the money to me because I hate the process of gel removal. I like that the company provides four replacement plastic pieces for the nail holes. One of the attached photos shows a close-up of the spacer bar and the brush tines to illustrate the parts and the holes in select tines. Amazingly, it is a working setup.
The rubber bristles are excellent to run through the hair. It is slightly curved, with long bristles. They are firm, but not inflexible. My initial impression is very positive, it's an excellent brush.
Cleaning is simple, too. Just pull out any errant hair strands, and run it under hot water. Done.
Overall, the brushes match up to the descriptions and depictions in the product details. It fully met expectations, too. In fact, I think I like the feel of the brush more than I expected. title: Smooth Teeth Afterwards
text:
Your teeth feel very smooth after ever session with the Oral-B Professional Care products. The question is which one to get? If you have sensitive gums, then I recommend the more expensive versions (3000 or higher) since they have sensitivity settings. If you are sharing the device with others in your household who may not have the same gum sensitivity as yourself, again, I recommend version 3000 or higher since you may not fully understand others' sensitivity levels. Plus the 3000 model (or higher) comes with a covered container for holding multiple brushes which will prevent the family from misplacing or swapping the heads.

I own the Oral-B Professional Care 1000 Power Toothbrush and now the 4000. I was perfectly happy with the 1000, but I had the opportunity to acquire the 4000 so I thought why not? The 4000 though gives you different modes as well as a easily seen red light letting you know if you are pushing too hard. I didn't really need these bells and whistles, but they don't hurt. I've always thought that if this kind of tooth brush was painful then I either need to stop pushing so hard or buy softer heads. That's just me, but I know others prefer having the feedback.

It's hard for me to spend $100 plus on a toothbrush, so if money is a concern, I recommend the 1000 or the 3000. I don't really need those extra feedback lights, and often I have to change the 4000 to polish mode to get it to behave more like the 1000 (which is ideally what I want). Note for me that the grip of the 1000/3000 feels better in the hand as well due to its smaller size compared to the 4000.

I further recommend you order at least two different kinds of heads so you can figure out the style you like. The 4000 does come with one head, and this is the type that integrates some sort of rubber/plastic in addition to having bristles (e.g., FlossAction). I think I prefer the heads that are made up of only traditional bristles but heads with the added plastic do seem to polish more.

Whether you get Braun or Phillips, do your teeth a favor and get a power toothbrush. Once you use these power toothbrushes, you'll never want to go back to the manual way.

title: Pricey, But Worth It To Have a GOOD Charger
text:
I own a Galaxy S6 Edge Plus... AND an iPhone 6 (Work Phone), AND a Galaxy Tab4 10.1, AND a New Trent Battery 12,000 mAh Pack. With that said, each one of these devices is using it's own charger and because of that, I had to resort using a power strip by my bedside JUST to charge all my devices.

The current chargers I use are all stock (1 Apple Charger, 3 Samsung Chargers). One of the Samsung Chargers is directly from the S6 Edge Plus (supports Adaptive Fast Charging/Quick Charge 2.0), yet it fails to work 80% of the time on my S6 Edge Plus for whatever reason...

Another issue is when I go away for overnight trips somewhere. For a day, I could probably just get by with just the iPhone charger & Samsung charger, but when I have 3-4 night stays due to work, I have to pack all of them!!! It's just a big hassle. That's when I decided I'm just going to resort to buying a GOOD multi-port charger. I've used Ankur devices in the past and I've been very pleased with all of them. After reading various reviews, I decided the 3-port is perfect for my situation.

For $25, you get a 3-port charger: 2 PowerIQ ports and 1 Quick Charge 2.0 port (which the Edge+ takes advantage of).

I've used the Ankur PowerIQ tech before via an Ankur Car Charger and I can definitely say it's almost as good as the Quick Charge 2.0 technology. What I like about it is that it supposedly "detects" what kind of device is connected to it and charges accordingly. Whether this is true or snake oil, I can say that it charges my devices fast and never has any kind of power dip when you have multiple devices connected to it. I use these two ports for my iPhone, Galaxy Tab4 and New Trent Battery pack.

The single Quick Charge is dedicated to my Galaxy S6 phone and right out of the box (same cables and all), it would fast charge my phone 100% of the time. Unlike my old stock Quick Charge Charger, it never seemed to work. So when I'm charging my phone and seeing it will fully charge within an hour makes me happy!

The only initial turnoff is the $25 sticker price. Yes you get a multi-port charger, but I think maybe that sticker price will scare some people. But after experiencing and using this product, I think that $25 is DEFINITELY WORTH IT. Never have a poor quality/flaky charger again. I'm 100% pleased with this item!

title: My go-to stampers
text:
These are the stamping plates that I use all the time. I stamp over gel nail polish with konad stamping polish, Essie polish, or Sallie Hanson insta-dri polish. When you first pull off the blue protective film, clean the plates really well with acetone. Then, I usually paint, scrape, roll, and then clean everything off without actually rolling the first stamping on my nails. I find the first stamping doesn't go well on a fresh plate, so I just don't waste my time.
After doing that, they stamp fine all the time. I have found at least one image in every stamper bundle that has stamping issues. I just don't use that stamp. These plates have intricate designs that transfer well. If you find that not all of your design is trasferring, first clean the plate really well with acetone. All that built-up dried polish affects the stamp. There are lots of good videos on stamping troubleshooting, too, if you are having trouble.
I stamp with a konad stamper, and scrape with an old credit card or empty gift cards. Metal scrapers will damage the plates.

title: Nothing spectacular. I have received more... for this price.
text:
This Hair Removal Device by Ulike just as well as a couple of other IPL devices I have that cost much less. It comes packaged nicely, though I kept trying to open the flat two-sided green piece that covers the accessory side. It doesn't open.
The device does look quite fancy, and I was interested in skin rejuvenation, which is in one of the photos (that is mentioned in the other listing that shows this exact same device). The instruction booklet contains about as much as the empty listing page that I ordered it from. That page has no bullet points, only one photo.
They do have another listing for this same exact device, showing the accessories, extra photos with bits of information, and bullet points telling a little about it. I got my information from there.
The device does have the cooling feature, as many others do, which helps it not to zap too badly. It also comes with a razor and eye protection.
What it lacks, that many others include that are in or around this price range, is more attachments for the device. There needs to be at least one smaller light head for use around the lip area, as it's very hard to use the main one with the device being so large.
This IPL device works pretty much as well as any other, with none having the ability to make you completely hair-free at any point in the future. As far as the studies that I have seen, with diligent use, home IPL devices can only offer a little better than 50-60%-ish less hair.
My preferred device, which costs very little more than this one, has several attachments, including some specifically for skin rejuvenation. You do get a fancy box with this device, and it looks nice, but I don't think it provides any more or less than devices that cost much less.
I haven't found one yet that really only takes 10 minutes to do your legs, but if I ever do, that is the one that would probably take the cake! If you like fancy boxes and a sleek-looking device, I would recommend this one.

title: Lightweight, Easy to Use Facial Brush with 2 Speeds and Pulsing Action
text:
I have used a Clarisonic Mia brush for more than two years, and although I like it, I've read that the Clarisonic brush can be too harsh. So, I was interested to try the Philips PureRadiance brush. First, the differences:

1. The Philips PureRadiance brush has two speeds, one is gentle and the other is a more intense option. This is a good feature, as in the winter when my skin is dry, a gentler speed is better for my skin.
2. The Philips PureRadiance brush has rotating bristles plus an pulsing feeling. The brush head is smaller than Clarisonic, so it is easy to use in small areas such as between your nose and mouth.
3. Similar to the Philips toothbrush, the PureRadiance brush has three timed sessions of 20 seconds each for three zones of your face. This is beneficial if you have a tendency to over scrub or irritate your skin.
4. The PureRadiance brush is smaller and lighter than the Clarisonic.

The PureRadiance is a different experience from the Clarisonic. It's not bad, just different. If this is your first facial brush, I think you will like the PureRadiance quite a bit. If you currently use a different brush, you'll need to compare features. If a gentle, light, easy to use brush is what you want, the Philips PureRadiance is a nice choice.

title: Good but not perfect
text:
I bought this to replace a Norelco 5885 XL after the battery stopped taking a charge. I had the 5885 repaired at a Philips authorized place, but it still didn't take much of a charge, so I went back again and, in the end, still didn't have a razor that I could use for more than a few days. I finally decided to give up and get this. I paid about $40 for it (the price has since gone up) and the repair was $30, so I figured this was a faster way to get something that worked.

In general, this is a very nice shaver. It's super-quiet, noticeably quieter than the 5885. It shaves a tad closer and needs less pressure to do so, and it seems to take a few less passes over the same area to get a close shave. The trimmer is just okay -- exactly like the old one. It won't cut you, but it won't easily make a clean edge for your sideburns, either. It's nice to be able to rinse out the head under running water.

There are a couple of caveats, though. The design of the head is slightly different and it doesn't move as smoothly over my skin. For me, this is a noticeable and moderately significant disadvantage. The old one felt better. It took a bit more effort to get a close shave, but I enjoyed the process more.

There's no battery meter. The old one told me how much of a charge I had. It wasn't all that accurate, but it let you know if you needed to charge the thing before going on a trip. But the battery lasts a long time -- I've had it for three weeks and I'm still on the first charge (I don't necessarily shave every day, though).

I never cut myself with the 5885. With this one, I've had two nicks in the first three weeks. Using less pressure may help.

I bought this over the more expensive Norelcos because I didn't want to carry a charging base on trips -- I just wanted a cord. I would have paid more, but Phillips just doesn't make the shaver that I want, which would be similar to the old one -- no base, but with a charge meter. In general, Phillips makes way too many models and it's awfully confusing trying to sort out the differences.

Overall, I'm happy, but replacing my old one, for a dead battery, was way too much hassle and the result is a shaver that isn't quite as nice as the one it replaced.

A note for those of you who've never used one of these: you'll get a close shave, but a blade will always be closer.

title: It Curls But Material is slippery, too much movement
text:
This heatless curler is ok, it’s as described and curls hair without having to utilize a curling iron. I find that it works best when using a light mist of water from a spray bottle and a texturizing spray.

It’s somewhat easy to use, but because it’s made of a silky material, it tends to slide around on my head and not stay in place.
The outside silky liner loosens, twists and loses its original shape after using it. I have a soft cotton one by another brand that works better, so in comparison, this one isn’t as good. It also doesn’t come with a headband to help keep hair wrapped and secure. It’s a bulkier wrap and leaves the top strands of hair looser which can cause the curls to not be as defined as they could be.

I started by putting the wrap at the top of my head, claw clipped it in place and moved strands of hair from the back of my head, underneath to the front and combined it with strands from the front, then continued to wrap the strands of hair around the wrap. I repeated this on each side until I was done. I used the hair ties at the ends to secure my hair in place. Getting strands of hair from the back to the front in sections can be a little complicated. With practice, it gets easier.

I let it sit in my hair overnight, it worked as described but left wavy/ loose curls rather than tight curls. It’s a good alternative for heat free curls.

title: Thick hair, but U-tips are huge for fine hair. Removal breaks natural hair. Please see update!
text:
My once beautiful long hair is finally growing back in from chemotherapy for breast cancer. I had had it bonded by my hair salon about 6 months ago with Cinderella bonds that shed like a cat almost immediately and had hair that was split and damaged before I ever even washed it.

I took a chance on ordering 2-18 inch packs of #613 and 2-16 inch packs of #613 of Sunny hair. The hair looked beautiful and was a perfect match for my own color, but there is no way of telling until it's been washed, conditioned and blown out over a few weeks to really know how it will hold up.

My stylist, who specializes in hot fusion bonds, put in 1 pack of the 18 inch Sunny hair (50 U tips) and one pack of Cinderella hair (25 U tips) 5 days ago. I have very fine hair and a tiny head, so more would not have been possible (this amount also equals a full head of hair for me). We are experimenting to see which hair holds up better.

After one wash, conditioning and blow dry yesterday, the high priced Cinderella hair was tangling in the middle, while the Sunny hair stayed tangle-fee, but did shed quite a bit. The Sunny hair has more weight to it than the much more expensive hair though and combed out better.

One star off for how huge the actual keratin U-tip are and the shedding. My stylist tried to cut some of the tip off with great difficulty. This is an FYI for those with fine hair or those who want to be able to pull it back without the bond showing (the more expensive type has much smaller Keratin u-tips).

I will update this review after 4 weeks in, but for now, I'd like to thank other reviewers for their input as it helped me choose Sunny hair. You were all correct in saying the hair is thicker than most online hair, even though each strand is a bit different in strand width, health and quality. As the industry is unregulated, it's hard to know what you're getting and with blonde hair, just how much processing went into coloring the hair (causing damage).

If my Sunny hair holds up well, my stylist, who does at least 10 hot fusion bondings per month on clients, will be ordering directly from Sunny hair instead of the company that charges $125-$150 per pack. We are both hoping this is the case.

I hope others will try this brand and leave reviews on their experiences. Also, if this is your first time with bonds, please remember on length that it's not going from the top of your head. The lower layers will fall much longer - I'm 5'7 with a long neck and the 18 inch lower tiers fall just a few inches above my waist.

UPDATE: please don't buy this hair if you value your natural hair.
It's impossible to remove the bonds without breaking your own hair.
It breaks, frizzes, knots up like crazy if in a warm climate.
I loved those first packs until summertime. Absolutely awful in heat and humidity. I couldn't get a brush through the hair. It would just snap off. The knots were horrific. I had my hairdresser try to remove and this is more like crazy glue on the bond than keratin.

text:
As a Mother to 4 I absolutely love my bath time, it's one of the only times of day I get to myself; I'm sure there's many out there that can relate. I've always propped my head up against the wall as I soaked in the bath but that would only be comfortable for the first few minutes. title: Do not buy during the summer months!
text:
These Live Bearded scents always take some getting used to; the combination of aromas are not as simple and straightforward as they seem. They never seem to smell quite like I expect, but I do tend to get used to them.

My beard is crazy. It literally grows in ten different directions and refuses to lay straight without a lot of coaxing.

This butter does a really nice job of conditioning my beard and taming fly-aways. I also find that it imparts some sculptability so that I can give my beard a little shape. I have to follow a bit of a routine in order to get it to cooperate, however.

I start the week out with a clean, freshly shampooed beard. I then warm it up with a hair dryer, to the point that it is damp, but not wet. I take a liberal amount of butter and rub it on my hands, warming it up, then I work it into my beard evenly. I use the hair dryer again with the flat concentrator attachment and a round brush to coax it into place. I have to brush it straight up and out first, which I find helps to straighten out the wavy parts, and then brush it into the final shape that I want. I also use a boar's-hair brush on my cheeks to get the fly-aways to lie flat. Once it is laying how I like, I use the cold button on the hair dryer to set it. I then do not wash it again for several days, (depending on how much I sweat or spill food/beverages), and only apply about half the amount of butter in the morning, though the brushing and drying routine remains the same.

I have found that this butter really does help my beard to keep its shape. It has a little bit of holding power, like you might expect from a pommade, but it is extremely light and clean, unlike pommade which tends to be sticky.

This is a great product, and one of the main reasons that I have kept using it is how well it works for me and the value/quantity when compared to other brands.

I will keep trying the other scents till I find one that I like.

Just a word of caution, don't buy this in the heat of the summer. The product I received had clearly melted and the resolidified, making one big solid mass of butter. It is described as being gritty and malleable, which I have experienced with previous purchases of this product. It still seemed to work alright, but was more difficult to use.

title: Mowin' the five-o'clock shadow
text:
There was a time when I couldn't stand shaving my face. No matter what type of instrument I used-- single- and double-bladers, Norelcos, EpiLady-- after the act I usually found myself annoyed by skin irritation, razor burn, and nicks that took forever to stop bleeding. But when I tried the Mach 3, which changed the dreaded shaving ritual from a bothersome, dreadful task into... well, a less-bothersome, tolerable task. I got closer and cleaner shaves with fewer strokes than I did with previous depilatory implements, and my face didn't sting quite after the deed had been performed. I also experienced fewer nicks and cuts, helping to keep my styptic pencil bills down. Unfortunately, the max number of shaves I could ever get out of a single Mach 3 V 1.0 cartridge was six before the dullness set in (partially due to my coarse facial hair) and the lube strip began to poop out.
I was surprised by how well Gillette managed to improve on most of the Mach 3's designs with the release of the Mach 3 Turbo. Now it takes even fewer passes to get them cheeks & chin baby-bottom bare, and I've managed to make the average Turbo cartridge last through eight shaves. And thanks to the apparently-improved lube strip and that little face-stretcher thingy on the bottom part of the tri-blade, my face only feels a light sting in a stiff wind after a shave. Another great surprise: I didn't have to buy a new kit for the Turbo cartridges-- they snap right onto my original Mach 3 razor handle, no sweat!
Thanks to the Gillette® Mach 3 Turbo, that semi-weekly shaving ritual I once dreaded has gone from a less-bothersome, tolerable task to... an even-less-bothersome and even-more tolerable task! Boy, if Gillette keeps improving on this product, I might one day actually find myself enjoying the act of mowin' the five-o'clock shadow!

title: An Honest Review
text:
My friend introduced me to epilating about 5 years ago. She had a double headed one from Spain it was amazing you could barely feel a thing. I searched for one similar everywhere and did some research that said the 40 dollar epilators do just as good as the more expensive ones. So I settled and bought a 40 dollar one, it did the job yes and I got use to how it worked (I usually waxed though since the epilator never removed every thing) Well it died about 4 months ago after, I decided that I wanted an epilator that would last and actually get the job done.

I went back to researching, I read so many reviews and many of you probably have and will. It is from my experience it depends on the person and the day that makes the review (I am having normal day.)

I decided in the to buy the Braun 7281 and crossed my fingers. Since I had grown use to my last epilator I was extremely surprised that this one felt so much better and barely noticed any pain; as well as I don't have to wax anymore saving so much more money now by spending more on the better epilator. But I decided I would give myself about 6 weeks and see how it did pain wise. It didn't feel the worst but it did sting for a few minutes and then I got use to it again. I must say that it still didn't hurt as bad as the 40 dollar one did and it still did just as good as a wax would. (Any epilator is going to sting if you haven't waxed or epilated in a 6 weeks +, I recommend waxing if you have sensitive skin before you jump back into epilating.) In the end I would even say this one is equal if not better then one my friend had and would recommend it to anybody. Added bonus is that it comes with many different tops as well as an electric razor.

If you are still on the fence about buying this one verses the 40 dollar one you have also been looking at. Buy the 40 dollar one first and in a few months when it dies, come back and buy this one. But if you want to save yourself time and money then make the jump and buy the Braun 7281 you won't regret it.

Also if you aren't familiar with how to use and epilator read the instructions it doesn't work like a razor and if you use it like a razor it will hurt. I feel it is the only reason people would complain about this epilator.

The only drawback to goat milk soap is that it goes so fast. If you're not familiar with it, it "melts" away much faster than commercial soaps. However, I'm well aware of this, so it doesn't affect my rating.

title: Works great, but make sure you understand how to control the device before use
text:
Of you’re looking to get your feet in shape fast, this is the tool. I have always had dry feet and large caluses in my heals and under my big toes in the ball. This is the first time a sanding tool has actually made my feet look and feel like new.

I have read reviews that say this product is dangerous and can burn your feet. Well that is true if not used properly. Here are just s couple tips that I have learned from a weeks use:

1. Make sure the device is on the lowest setting before use.
2. Do not make contact for longer than 1.5 seconds, even on hard caluses.
3. Use light contact and pull the device against the rotation on each pass.
4. Let the pad do the work, you do not need to push it into the foot. This is most likely the reason for the negative reviews reporting pain and burning.
5. This device is powerful! If you’re not comfortable using it right out of the box, practice for a few minutes on an Apple or other soft surfaces until your get comfortable with the control.

Enjoy your new feet!

title: Get rid of tinea pedis in 1 week.

I went to doctor suffering with tinea pedis in my groin area. I had it for months and didn't know what it was (thinking it would just go away naturally). It finally got so bad that I had to see a doctor. He prescribed a topical treatment to use twice a day for 7 days. It didn't work. I went back and he prescribed a stronger topical treatment along with antibiotics to use for 5 days. It too didn't work. He was out of ideas and referred me to a dermatologist. While waiting to see the dermatologist, I decided to do some research on my own. I bought the following products and used them every day for 6 days straight so far. I am about 95% cured. I plan to use this for another week thinking I will be 100% after the second week.
This stuff works.
1. Product #1: Defense Soap Antifungal 4 Ounce Bar. [[ASIN:B01E0D6PIS DEFENSE Ringworm Treatment Kit - Bar Soap 4 Oz and Body Wipes 40 Count]]
Shower 3 times a day…once in the morning, once when you get home from work and once before bedtime. Use this bar soap 3 times a day for the infected area, once a day for your whole body including fingernails and feet.
2. Product #2. Wipes. (Link in above product description)
Use the wipes periodically throughout the day..every few hours and especially after getting sweaty.
3. Product #3: Antifungal Soap with Tea Tree Oil, Helps Treat & Wash Away Athletes Foot, Ringworm, Nail Fungus, Jock Itch, Body Odor & Acne. [[ASIN:B00HNWNXAW Antifungal Soap with Tea Tree Oil, Helps Treat & Wash Away Athletes Foot, Ringworm, Nail Fungus, Jock Itch, Body Odor & Acne. Antibacterial Defense Against Common Fungal and Bacteria Related Skin Irritations 9oz.]]
In addition to the bar soap, I used this product on the affected area once a day (at bedtime shower). When using this, lather well and let it sit on your skin for 3-4 minutes before rinsing off.
4. Product #4: Zeasorb Super Absorbent Antifungal Treatment Powder. [[ASIN:B005GM3LW6 Zeasorb Super Absorbent Antifungal Treatment Powder for Jock Itch 2.5 oz]]
After showering, completely dry off then use this powder on affected area.
5. Product #5: BUICED Liquid Multivitamin. [[ASIN:B00DSAA3L0 BUICED Liquid Multivitamin, 1-Pack]]
Internal treatment. Tinea Pedis condition can also be made worse by poor diet. I took a shot of this liquid vitamin once a day (when I got home from work each day).
6. Product #6: “Raw Organic Apple Cider Vinegar with the ‘Mother’”. [[ASIN:B00H4I4DRC Bragg Raw Organic Apple Cider Vinegar-16 fl. oz. Bottle]]
I don’t know how much this helped, but I read how beneficial apple cider vinegar is to your health so I gave it a try. I drank 2 tablespoons once a day (at night an hour before bedtime). I mixed it with orange juice and it wasn’t quite so bad.

I used these products for about 1 week and I am very pleased with the results.

title: Awesome!  Glad I spent the money...
text:
Okay. So this product was one I finally said, screw it I'm going to try it, because I have been looking for mirror like polish for almost two years. The mirror wffect is amazing! Especially if you do it right. I posted 4 photos, from start to finish. The real metallic mirror finish definitely looks better before you put on the top coat, but it will rub right off within a few minutes to hours if you don't seal it with a top coat. The first photo is with the bottom coat, second the mirror effect chrome, third the finished product.
Another thing you have to know is your surface needs to be smooth and clean before beginning, just like any work space. Second, once you paint on the chrome don't go over it again, it'll look terrible in the end. So once the chrome mirror polish dries, leave it alone! If it doesn't look the way you wanted, just grab a dry napkin and wipe it off and start again. Trust me it'll look better this way.
Now... For the product quality itself... I would say it is good but not great. I have a better quality gel top coat that I use and like better. I actually used it the second this doing this, and it worked better. But this top coat I used when doing other things to my nails. Not sure why it doesn't perform as it should, perfectly, like my other brand top coat, but it doesn't do ya... It's a good top coat still, so not a total loss there... And yes it does chip if you don't use at least 3 coats of top coat. 3! That's key to a good gel top coat... Layered for strength. I do my own acrylic nails and all my decorating, so I have a good quality gel setting lamp, with 6 bulbs inside, and I use good quality products... It's worth it to spend an extra $2-3.
But overall great product and I'm happy I spent the money! I love my chrome nails!

title: Where Has This Stuff Been All My Life???
text: Oh. My. Word. *Excuse me while I go throw away all my regular nail polish.* This is a Game. Changer. I'm a busy mom and honestly, I just hate going to the nail salon, and who has time to wait for 300 hours (Ok, maybe not quite 300) for your regular nail polish to dry, only to smudge it or have it chip within 2 hours? I had pretty much given up on nail polish and just been resigned to the fact that I would have boring nails forever. This stuff is seriously incredible. You just paint it on, cure it, wipe the top with the cleanser to remove the tacky finish, and VOILA! Perfect nails! I did mine last week with this set and they still look AH-MAZING. When this set arrived, I was a bit bummed to find that there's no color included, just base and top coat. I live an hour from the nearest mall and so I couldn't just pop into the store and get a color, and yet I wanted to try it out... Like, right now. I did some reading and found that you can actually use regular nail polish to make a "Gel-y" sandwich. Once you have the base coat on, cure it, then paint your regular color over the top and wait the "300 hours" it takes to dry. Then paint the top coat over the regular color, cure, wipe with cleanser and enjoy your stunning, long lasting nails! The only thing I would change about this set is the light. I wound up buying a larger light because the one that comes with this set is quite small and I wanted to be able to fit all my fingers or all my toes in at once. This light is great for storing and being portable, but I personally wanted something bigger. Overall a fantastic set. I'm never going back to regular polish ever again!

title: Colored natural, kinky hair
text:
I have bleached and colored natural, kinky hair. This is the first time I've ever colored my hair and I made sure to do my research on colored hair care, which includes protein treatments. Well, months had gone by and I still hadn't done a protein treatment. Madness, right? Eventually, the dyed parts (especially the ends) started to feel rough and dry.The ends were also knotting like crazy! I remembered a YouTube video I watched about hydrolyzed wheat protein. I ordered that and a pair of hair shears (prepared to do some clipping, which I had also been neglecting). I heard that you should expect to see results after the first use, but I was blown away! First, I cleansed my hair with shampoo. I didn't measure how much of the treatment I used but I mixed it in with my regular, wash out conditioner. After coating my hair in it, I covered my hair with a plastic cap then sat with my conditioning heat cap on my head for about 15 minutes.
My hair in general, not only the dyed area, feels softer and the colored ends feel smooth and manageable again. Also, waaaaay less knotting. After washing my hair, I put it in twists to dry. 2 days later I pulled out the twists to get a lovely, voluminous twist-out. Unfortunately, I didn't get the shears but Amazon promptly refunded me and I plan to reorder them shortly. I'm ashamed to say its been months since my ends have been clipped (which just compounded the problem) and I plan to use my protein treatment around once a month and trim when needed.

title: My favorite natural fragrance lotion: No Sensitivity problems for me!
text:
It does smell like an orange creamsicle in the best way (yummy!), but if I get a big direct sniff of my hand right after putting it on, it does have the smell reminiscent of eating a really good tangy, fresh apricot, too.

Even some lotions that advertise “natural fragrance,” I have sensitivity to, but this one is no problem! No sneezing, wheezing, or headaches from it. It’s a delicious smell, but not too strong or overpowering, and not fake smelling. The scent subsides quickly after a short bit of time passes, but is still there if you sniff the skin directly. I’ve tried their lavender & lemon coconut (both tend to be favorite scents/scent combos for me when done naturally), and those are nice, but this is my favorite one, unexpectedly.

I normally make my own really moisture intensive thick creams & lotion bars (with beeswax, cocoa butter, shea butter & olive oil.) These I usually apply to my hands every time I wash, because my skin dries out so easily. It keeps cracked hands at bay. This lotion is not a replacement for intensive creams like that.

But this lotion is lovely when I want something that *doesn’t leave my hands feeling greasy*, applies easily, soaks in nicely, & smells good. It’s kinda my “treat myself” lotion. I can also put it out for guests who are used to more traditional lotion consistency, and have them like it, while not being a problem for my breathing. It works great to include in a gift basket, too.

I can’t say this will work for every person with scent sensitivities (and don’t assume it’s okay if someone’s told you no scents...some people have dangerous health reactions to even natural fragrances, among other possible serious concerns that need to be respected), but it is definitely one worth looking into if you are the one with sensitivities, trying to find scents you are okay with. It is 1000 x better than most of the lotions with synthetic fragrances, and even some of the stronger ones that claim natural fragrance.

title: Perfect for a good warm lather and no clanking the brush on the rim!
text:
I've been using (or rather, trying to) Col Conk's shave soap pucks and their shaving soap mug. I was not getting the performance I'd heard of that makes shaving with a DE razor and warm shave soap so enjoyable. I decided to change both the mug and my soap. I've had this bowl for a few weeks now-it holds heat well and with my super badger brush and Proraso shaving cream (in a squeeze tube, not the pre-filled bowl of Proraso) I get a very fast, think 20 seconds or so, thick and warm lather built up. I've found I get best results when I add the hottest water I can get from the tap to the bowl add the brush to soak and then hop in the shower to let the brush and bowl warm up. I then dump the water out and refill it with hot water, let it sit for a minute or so then pour it out. (The initial fill of the hot water loses a bunch of heat just warming the porcelain, the second fill of hot water is the heat you'll use to make a nice warm lather. The bowl retains the heat while you apply the shave soap.). Don't forget to refill with hot tap water and let the heat build back up before you pour all but about a tablespoon of water out then add an almond sized dollop of the shave cream from the tube. The raised swirl on the bottom I'm of the bowl seems to work well and help build the lather.

One more thing-the bowl is wide enough that I no longer need to worry about clanking the brush against the rim and waking my wife up.mthat was a problem with my Col Conk mug-too narrow at the top. This bowl works very well for me, I'm quite pleased with the purchase!

The Choo Choo Stripes Adult Shortall is an amazing, cute, functional product from Baby Pants! I bought these as a birthday present to myself a year ago and they have held up very well through play and washings. That being said, I would consider choosing the larger size if you're on the fence about what size to order.

I agree with LollyLaLaz's comments in her review about the Baby Pants patch logo on the back and recently decided to remove it myself so that I would feel comfortable when discretely wearing these in public. This is a common feature in the few Baby Pants products that I've bought, but it is very easy to remove without damaging the fabric.

There are six snaps in the crotch and three on each side by the pockets, each labeled with the Baby Pants logo. These logos on the snaps are a nice touch and are not noticeable unless seen up close. Also, the five pockets are deep and functional as well.

Overall, I would definitely recommend these to anyone considering buying these super cute, childish, practical shortalls! Enjoy!!

title: Relatively strong water flosser but reservoir is attached which makes drying it nearly impossible
text:
I have used various countertop water flossers in the past such as the countertop WaterPik and the [[ASIN:B07HRNGS3Q Truwell Handheld Water Flosser]]. I love the idea of a hand held irrigator and this does work to remove most stuck debris from between the teeth. What is nice about this one over the other handheld I tried, is that there is very little splash back. However, I personally do not like that the reservoir is not removable for drying.

IN THE PACKAGE
- One reservoir attached to handheld flosser unit
- One USB cable (wall adapter NOT included)
- One instruction manual
- One standard jet nozzle
- One orthodontic nozzle (larger brush)
- One pocket nozzle (smaller brush)
- One tong scraping nozzle (what looks like a spoon)

I charged the unit fully before use. The white light on the side blinks when charging and remains steady when it is fully charged. Note the charging port is hidden behind a silicone nub below the grip dots on the top of the unit. Be careful to cover the charging port with this nub when the flosser is in use.

There is an on/off switch and a mode switch. The three water pressure modes are soft, standard, and massage can be cycled through using the mode switch prior to turning the unit on. The jet tip (or any of the other three tips) gets inserted into the top. Be careful to make sure it is seated with the notch in the groove as the first time I put it in the hole, I did not have it seated all the way. To eject, press the release button to the left side.

The reservoir IS NOT removable. Instead water enters through the small opening on bottom through which one has to fill the unit. I do not like that the reservoir is attached as I have to drain the remaining water out of that hole and leave the door open for drying. Also, the little button through which the water enters can easily break after lots of use. I personally would prefer not to have to use that hole.

I held my mouth almost totally closed during use and tried all three modes. I did not have splash back, which was very nice. Splash back is usually typical of almost any type of water flosser so to some extent I was surprised. This flosser does work to dislodge most debris between teeth but not everything because it is not super powerful but is powerful enough. I am also impressed that the manual is relatively well written; kudos to the manufacturer on this. Normally, I feel as if I am reading Pig Latin when I receive products from China or other countries.

In summary, my biggest disappointment with this unit is the attached reservoir that prevents me from drying this out easily.

title: A Thick and Rich Eye Cream.
text:
EDITED REVIEW as of 9/25/21.

I came back to edit this review and to lower my rating from 4 stars to 3 stars. Here's why:

After a few weeks of using this cream, I started to develop some sensitivity to it. When I say sensitivity, here's what I mean: 1) The scent bothered me more than it did when I first used the cream. In fact, I started to sneeze most evening after applying it. 2) I'd used the cream on other areas of my face, and noticed minor breakouts in those areas.

Basically, I think the cream was just too oily for my skin. Even around the eye area, which has virtually no oil glands, the non-absorbency of the cream left me feeling sticky and greasy even though I gave the cream plenty of time to absorb.

End of Edit.

***************************************************************************************************************************

Everything else I said in my original review still stands. But the above edit may help you decide if this is the right eye cream for you.

If you're looking for a natural, plant-based eye cream that is ultra-thick and rich, you'll find it in this 2 oz. jar.

The jar will last a VERY long time, because you only need a tiny amount of this cream to cover the undereye area and the corners where crows feet form.

I'd advise putting the cream on a couple of hours before bed, since it takes quite a while to absorb into the skin. (If you don't wait, you'll end up depositing most of the cream on your pillowcase.)

I've also used a small amount of this cream on other areas of my face (nose to mouth lines) and the results were the same as around my eye area.

So what were the results? The skin around my eye area looked smoother and brighter after one night of use.

I'm rating the cream 4 stars instead of 5, because of one major issue I have with it, which is: THE SCENT.
The cream has a rather strong minty (?), menthol (?) medicinal smell that takes some time to fade away.

text:
I used to use the J.Crew "FIBER" Styling cream. This is not quite as nice to use. It is more crumbly and brittle compared to the J.Crew product; however, the J.Crew product has a very strong cologne smell that I quite dislike. Pros:
Unscented
Works just as good as J.Crew product I used to use.

Cons:
A little more crumbly and not as nice to apply (very minor complaint)

The one review I saw that was negative said that the product was difficult to apply, but I think hair wax just can't be applied like hair gel. I thought I might share how I apply hair wax.

How to apply:
1. Wet your hair
2. Wet your hands
3. Take a small finger tip sized amount and rub it between the palms of your hands (like its a cold winter morning)
4. Keep rubbing until the wax turns into a cream which is covering palms and fingers in a thin coating.
5. Work it into your hair moving your hand back and forth through your hair vigorously.

This always gives me good application of the wax while still using a small amount of the product. I used to go through this stuff much faster when I tried to apply it dry and without "melting" it first.

I love this mask! For those who have not yet tried it... You need to first open your pores. I do this with a nice hot shower. Then after my shower, i pat dry my face and apply the mask. You need a good thick coating of mask otherwise it does not work as well and is hard to remove. I found that using a mask brush of some form works best, you can squirt a little right from the tube onto the brush and apply it. This way you can avoid getting it all over your hands and nails because it can be a little difficult to wash off. Make sure it is COMPLETELY dry then peel it off at a smooth steady rate of speed. title: Great in smoothies and cold-brewed coffee
text:
Great carob powder. Best I've tried yet.
Carob has calcium and Cacao has magnesium, which is necessary for the absorption of calcium. Use together for maximum effect.
I use this in a couple different recipes.

Chocolate Almond Smoothie
1-2 cups Raw Almonds (Soaked overnight)
1-2 tbsp carob powder
1-2 tbsp raw cacao powder (Pure Natural Miracles brand is my fav by far)
1 tbsp raw honey
bee pollen granules
maca powder, protein powder (Vega brand is my fav)
liquid stevia, cinnamon and vanilla to taste
Add ice and blend until smooth and creamy. (You'll need a big powerful blender)
Yummy!

Cold-Brewed Homemade Mocha Java
2-3 cups cold brewed Coffee (super easy to make yourself)
1 tbsp carob powder
1 tbsp raw cacao powder (Pure Natural Miracles brand is my fav by far)
1 tbsp raw honey
bee pollen granules
protein powder (Vega brand is my fav)
liquid stevia, cinnamon and vanilla to taste
Blend until smooth, then pour in glass and add boiling water. (I shake it up in a mason jar)
(Don't blend with boiling water, otherwise it will explode and burn you!!)
Homemade Mocha Java! Yummy!

title: One time use.  NOT reusable.
text:
Problem #1- I bought these because they are stated to be reusable. I assure you that they are NOT. The attached microbead is literally glued onto the extension, so you cant even use a new microbead. Whenever you install these (mine were installed by a professional), the attached beads crush, so they CANNOT be moved up (nor replaced with a new bead as the other is glued on).

Problem #2- Due to the way these are made (Your hair is pulled through a smooth tube and the microbead clamps over it), they slide right out of your hair with the slightest bit of pressure. On the first night I had 56 extensions loose and sliding out. I then had to go pay to have another box installed. FIFTY SIX.

Problem #3- the ends of the extension (closest to your scalp) are frayed edges. Instead of being keratin bonded and smooth, they are like little brooms of sharp hairs that constantly itch your scalp. I mean, insanely uncomfortable.

I attempted to contact the seller. She stated she would send me a new pack of beads to try. She never sent them. It wouldn't have mattered anyway because she has clearly never seen the product or she would realize that you can't use a new microbead with these as here is literally no way to get the old, broken bead off.

These were purchased for approximately $325. I spent another $300 to have them installed. $625 to have them in for less than a week. If you want to spend over $600 for a week of slipping extensions, then these are for you.

title: Leaves You Feeling Silky Smooth
text:
Like another reviewer, this was not an item I would have selected myself. I received it as a gift from a friend and was hesitant to use it out of fear that it would have an overpowering floral smell due to the lavender. However, the bar ended up being a pleasant surprise, and I will likely buy it again.

Since I don't like too many bubbles in my bath and, more importantly, like stretching my Lush products as much as possible due to the cost, I cut the bar into fourths. I found it to be a lot harder to cut than most Lush products, so if you're going to cut it, use a really strong knife and be ready for it to blow apart a bit as you slice through. (It's pretty crumbly.)

What I like about this bar is that, even though it's not very bubbly -- even as someone who cuts bars, I usually get more from others than this one -- it leaves a wonderful silky feeling on your body. I love that, even in the water, I can feel it on my legs, and not in an annoying greasy way at all. It's so relaxing! I usually put cocoa butter on my legs after shaving, and I don't need to do anything after using this bar. It has some sort of wonderful lotion quality about it that I adore. More than the scent or bubbles, that is the reason I will purchase it for myself in the future.

The only objection I have is that it seems to melt a bit more than other bubble bars. I've kept it in a sealed container in a cool area, but it just doesn't keep well. If you're going to cut it, be sure to use the other pieces within a couple weeks at the most. And, like all bubble bars, don't get it wet unless you're going to use it right away, because even the tiniest bit of moisture gets it going.

title: Unique product, tastes good, and it works!
text:
I know this candy is expensive, but it does what it says it will, which is a big deal for me. This candy is actually sort of a life-changing product for me, and I'm so excited it's available in the US now.

I sweat easily and profusely. It's an embarrassing problem, but this candy makes it much less so. I shower and use underarm deodorant, obviously, which helps the situation there, but the rest of me sweats too... just a general moistness of the skin all over, which often has a somewhat sour smell. Yuck. I'm always the first one in any group to start to sweat if it's warm or we're doing something vigorous. Usually this leaves me feeling really self-conscious and I will stand apart, etc. I've even avoided certain activities with friends during the summer because I knew this would happen. For this candy to help me, I just eat a few pieces an hour or two in advance! Then, when I start to get warm my skin will give off a subtle lovely smell instead of the usual sour smell. I can't tell you how excited I am about this! Also, a side bonus, it has a nice effect on the breath that lasts longer for me than any breath mint I've ever used.

Maybe it's just the way it reacts with my own body chemistry, but I don't think it smells particularly like roses, or even flowery... it's hard to explain, it's just a subtle clean & fresh smell that comes through my skin. You know how some people just smell good, not like product, but just like a nice skin smell? That's what this does for me. A friend of mine ate some and I thought she smelled more flowery, more reminiscent of roses, though not quite. I'd expect it's going to smell a little different on everyone.

Oh, and since it's a candy, I should probably mention: It's delicious! The very first taste when you pop it in your mouth is a little "rosey", meh, but that is almost immediately replaced by a very nice tangy tangerine flavor. I have to keep myself from eating them all up so I'll have them when I need them. :) I buy the regular sugar-sweetened kind, since I don't use artificial sweeteners, so I can't comment on the taste of the sugar-free ones.

title: but I always hated feeling like I NEEDED to do my eyebrows before ...
text:
Honestly and truly, this eyebrow tint changed my life. I have naturally blonde hair, eyebrows, and eyelashes. I dye my hair regularly to a dark reddish brown, and obviously need my eyebrows and eyelashes to match so as not to look weird. I wear mascara everyday no problem and have been anyways for years, but I always hated feeling like I NEEDED to do my eyebrows before I went into public. Plus I hate feeling like they look drawn on and too done up. Beyond that, if I spent the night at anyone's house I would have to wear at least brow mascara to bed and risked looking bad when I woke up with it smeared all over my face.
I read the reviews before I used this and everyone said to leave the dye on for around 5 minutes. However the box says 2 minutes. The first time I used the dye I was freaking out a little because I thought I was messing up by leaving it on so long. DON'T WORRY. After the first time, I leave it on for closer to 10 minutes now. The dye definitely makes your brows dark, but that's what I prefer.
The first time I used this, it was before I went over to my boyfriend's house for the night. I literally was just laying in his bed smiling at how happy I was that I wasn't wearing any makeup, I felt confident in my brows looking good, and that I wouldn't have to worry about how I looked in the morning. It was such a great feeling! My eyebrows are one of my biggest insecurities and this gave me such a confidence boost!
I actually ended up opening all the little capsules and emptying them into the little bag provided and I just scoop out a little at a time to use. I did this because when I emptied an entire capsule into the little mixing pot, it made SO MUCH DYE and I ended up throwing away 3/4 of what I made. They give you 16 capsules but this still felt like a huge waste. This way I make smaller batches and have less waste and can stretch the product longer.
I'd say the only two cons of this product are that it only lasts maybe 5 days before I have to reapply, and that it's hard to apply it without staining your skin. So don't dye your eyebrows right before you leave your house, I try to do it at night and by the morning my natural oils have made the dye lift a little. By day two you can't see the stains anymore.

title: Much better then the Sonic Spinbrush by Arm & Hammer
text:
Until a year ago, I never liked the idea of owning an electric toothbrush: I'd owned several cheap ones and never liked any of them. Then I figured that I'd try one again about a year ago and so I chose the Sonic Spinbrush by Arm & Hammer. I chose the Spinbrush because it had a large brush, which I thought meant less time/effort brushing my teeth.

The Spinbrush worked pretty well, but the large brush head gagged me horribly. Because of this, I decided to give the Oral-B Vitality a try and I like it much better. The first reason I prefer the Vitality is because it has a much smaller brush head (you don't need a large brush with an electric toothbrush, since the toothbrush is doing all the work.) The smaller brush head also allows me to reach places the larger Spinbrush cannot reach, because it's too big. The Vitality is easier to maneuver in your hand as well, thanks to the smaller handle base.

Another thing I didn't like about the Spinbrush is how it would click off automatically after 2 minutes (I don't think all models of the Spinbrush do this, though.) The Vitality purposely sputters after 2 minutes for it's timing function, but then continues it's normal operation after a second or two. I still find this annoying, but at least I don't have to remove it from my mouth, dripping with toothpaste, just to turn it back on. And if I finish early, the Spinbrush required me to punch the button twice to stop it (again, something not easy to do with a vibrating toothbrush in your mouth), whereas the Vitality only requires a single button push. These two things alone make the Vitality much more convenient.

I also think the Vitality is more powerful then the Spinbrush. The reason you had to push the button on the Spinbrush twice was so you could use it at a lower speed if necessary, but I never found that necessary at all. I prefer the more powerful Vitality, because it feels like it's cleaning better by not slowing down if I push too hard.

About the only thing I liked better about the Spinbrush was that it had an indicator light on the base to tell you it was receiving power (I think it gauged the charge, too, but that was never a problem for me.) I'm not sure if that's even important, but it is something I tend to prefer with rechargeable items. Other than that, I love the Vitality and I much prefer it over the Spinbrush. Now I can brush my teeth without gagging and I am thankful for that.

text:

Pros: arrives wrapped to prevent leaks when shipped, does an ok job with medium hold, not stiff or sticky

Cons: smell nothing special, did not control fizz

Initially, I really like that the product comes wrapped (please see the attached picture which shows the plastic wrapped bottle). I have used it for myself (I am a woman and have shoulder length curly hair), as well as for a family member who is a man with a short hair cut.

The smell is nothing special. I do really like that the ingredients used include both natural and organic ingredients (Green Tea Extract, Ginseng Root Extract, Vitamin B5 and Organic Chamomile). I would prefer those ingredients over a more preferable smell. While this gel is not super sticky/tacky, it did leave my hair a bit frizzy and a bit stiff. Now for short hair, this was not as noticeable and it worked much better. Based upon my experience, and to counter another review by a woman, it was just ok. I do believe that based upon my uncle's experience, and other reviews, that it would be something safe to recommend for those with shorter straight hair.

title: Pain Relief in a Roller!
text:
I got the hot pink Derma Roller yesterday and immediately put it in the freezer. This morning I got it out to give it a try, and I'm already addicted! I was actually a bit dubious about this product, truth be told, but it's fantastic!

It feels wonderful to roll it across my forehead, throat, and eyes. The first touch made me jump a little bit because it's REALLY cold, but after the initial contact, it feels good. I'm probably too old to anti-age, but I'm going to use it just because it makes me feel so good, and I plan to give one to each of my daughters.

I get migraines, as does my youngest daughter, so we spend a lot of time in the dark, with ice packs on our necks and foreheads. The next time I'm struck, I'm going to roll this magic device on the back of my neck, and I fully expect it to work better than just an ice pack or bag of frozen peas. Hopefully I won't have to test this anytime soon, but after I do, I'll update this post to let you know how/if it worked.

Last year I broke my wrist and even after weeks of physical therapy, I was still in a lot of pain and, again, spent a lot of time on ice and heat. I wish I had this then because as I roll it over my wrist right now, I can tell that it would have felt SO good when I was still recovering.

The bright colors are cheerful, and make me smile, and anything that makes me smile, is worth having.

I received this product at a reduced price in exchange for my honest and unbiased review, and that is exactly what I'm providing. I never give an item a better review than I think it deserves because as a customer on Amazon, I know how much I rely on consumer reviews.

title: More Than Another Steelbook
text:
Review For Mondo X Limited Edition Steelbook

El laberinto del fauno (Pan's Labyrinth) is a fantasy film from the director Guillermo del Toro (Hellboy,The Devil's Backbone,Hobbit). Everyone should know the film but for those who don't i will quote the plot from IMDB "In the falangist Spain of 1944, the bookish young stepdaughter of a sadistic army officer escapes into an eerie but captivating fantasy world."

The Main Draw for me was the Steelbook itself, iv seen the movie countless time's and wanted to have a collectable version of the movie that would showcase my love for the film and del toro. Upon receiving this steelbook the first thing i noticed was the protective sleeve underneath the plastic, most steelbooks don't have these and you would have to purchase them separate and that it was included shocked me, the protective sleeve also has images and the information about the release and special features and a great touch. There are images on the front,back and inside of the steelbook itself and looking at pictures online don't really show how gorgeous the product really is, once you hold it as a collector i'm almost positive you will be more then pleased. There are two disc (One DVD, One Blu-ray) inside on the right side of the case, my guess for putting both disc on the right is so you can view the artwork on the left but still if you want to see the full image u have to take all the disc out. The next surprise is on the disc themselves, there not just disc from another version but there labels match this exact release and that really just seals the complete packaging into perfection. This review was more so for the steelbook, but i just fell in love with and had to share

title: Realistic expectations
text:
After reading the mixed reviews of this razor, I decided to take a chance and purchase it. I don't regret the purchase one bit.

The positive things that have been written about this razor are true. So are most of the negatives. But I think the biggest problem most reviewers had are setting their expectations, so let me recap my experience.

I've shaved with blades, foil electrics, and rotaries all before. I have sensitive skin, so as much as I like the close shave a blade gives, even the best moisterizer leaves razor burn. Foils have never done anything for me. So I always find myself with a rotary razor. The last razor I *loved* was a Norelco, but after five years, the battery simply could not hold a charge. I tried a Remington last year and was disappointed. Better than a foil, but not my trusty Norelco. So I bought this.

First, there *is* an acclimation period to this razor. Even with my skin "experienced" to rotary razors, it took a month before I started getting *really* close shaves. So people that write and only gave it two weeks and were disappointed...take it with a grain of salt. The manual should say *at least* three weeks. To acclimate faster, you should shave daily. I know a lot of guys with thin or slow growing beards "cheat" and shave every other day, but it makes adjusting slower. Every day. For a month. You'll be happier.

Secondly, many reviewers comment about how this razor only works on stubble. This is true, and yes, my older Norelco (and so I assume the Speed XL's still) can tackle longer fur on your face. But a weed whacker is not a lawn-mower. The lawnmower you use on your yard is not the same quality as the lawnmower a golf course uses on its greens. It is about precision. This razor gives *the* closest shave I've gotten out of an electric. INCLUDING my old Norelco. This gets closer. It is designed for the discerning male who wants a device that grooms with precision and closeness. The trade-off is, to get that close, the lift-and-cut system simply can't handle longer hairs. If you shave daily (see above) then you'll never notice this drawback. But if you let your beard go a day or two at a time, you'll be disappointed. But this razor isn't for that man. If a man is okay with letting some fuzz go for a day, he usually isn't looking for that "perfect" shave, and won't notice the difference between the closeness of a less demanding razor and this one. So this is a device for the elite.

The small trimmer is another criticism. Again, the facts are true. It is small. It is not meant to chop down your entire face. Philips makes beard groomers for that. The trimmer, like every other feature of this device, is designed for the man who shaves daily. It's narrow blade makes grooming sideburns a breeze. Wider clippers make sideburn sculpting far more clumsy. You trim and sculpt, then take the razor to the skin and, since it doesn't do longer hair, you get a perfect sideburn. Again, a design for the man who demands the "perfect" look.

So why four stars if I love this razor so much? One word. Price. The numeric display is nice. The metal finish looks better than the finish on the 1050 as well. But neither of these justifies the $140 premium. I paid it because I think it looks nicer that the 1050, and if I had to, I'd pay it again. But it doesn't mean I actually think it is *worth* the price. I just spoil myself that much. Call me shallow. But the price, for the comparative lack of features does deserve a loss of a star.

--

In summary, if you want the closest shave from an electric ever then this is the razor for you. But it asks for some discipline in return. You have to put attention into yourself to get the most out of it. If you are fond of facial hair, like growing a goatee or chops, you'll want a groomer as well as this razor.

If you are less demanding about your shave then another Norelco device may be a better option. The Speed XL is essentially the newer revision of my old razor and I was perfectly satisfied with it for five years. It was plenty close (but not as close as this) and very comfortable, so really you just have to decide how close you want the shave to be. If you are a perfectionist, get this. If not, save your money and get a Speed XL.

title: Ingredients
text:
These have very little odor. They include a lot of currently popular natural ingredients along with a few ingredients not favored by those most into that kind of thing.

Barrier

It isn't quite like a protective glove. Probably does help with protection for a limited time, not a whole day of work with your hands, during which it gets absorbed, wiped away, worked out by other substances and so on. Takes a couple minutes to soak in, but it's not very greasy once it does.

Active ingredient: dimethicone.
Inactive ingredients: deionized water, stearic acid, propylene glycol, glyceryl stearate, isopropyl palmitate, Ricinus communis (castor) seed oil, cyclopentasiloxane, phenoxyethanol, ethylhexyglycerin, sodium hydroxide, mineral oil, Simmondsia chinensis (jojoba) seed oil, xanthan gum, disodium EDTA, acrylates copolymer, Aloe barbadensis leaf extract.

Hand cleaner

Looks like it has plenty of charcoal, it's so dark, but more of the grit--and it's very gritty--is from pumice than charcoal. Does't foam, cleans surprisingly well anyway, moisturizes a little.

Ingredients: aloe leaf juice, pumice, glycerin, sunflower seed oil, sorbitol, carbon [that's the charcoal], grape seed oil, lanolin oil, vitamin E acetate, xanthan gum, carbomer, 2-phenoxyethanol, ethylhexylglycerin, sodium hydroxide.

Hand cream

Not a heavy-duty cream but has some nice stuff in it that's thought to help with skin health, moisturizes for a while.

Ingredients: water, glycerin, stearic acid, dimethicone, sunflower seed oil, cetearyl alcohol, ceteareth-20, allantoin, petrolatum, hydroxyethylcellulose, aloe vera, Symphytum officinale (comfrey) rhizome/root extract, Calendula officinalis oil, tocopherol, diazolidinyl urea, iodopropynyl butylcarbamate, acrylates/C10-30 alkyl acrylate crosspolymer, sodium hydroxide.

text:
I'll start with the best things about this curling iron. The heating element is encased in plastic so its easy to use without burning yourself. I am not sure why most of the deep wavers these days got away from that and now its all this exposed hot mettle that one wrong move or a slip of the wrist and you are burning your neck or face or hand with it. But not with this one. Its nice that way. That's probably one of the biggest reasons I went with this one. Its very attractive and sleek looking with a nice swivel cord. It shuts itself off after an hour which is nice as I have left it on by mistake before. Gives you peace of mind if you can't remember if you left it on after you've left your house which is awesome.

Now it works alright and you can make nice waves with it if you are careful to align the waver properly because its like they went a little cheap on the waving plates. You really have to think about it and position it right each time because you have one and half wave on each plate as apposed to two full barrels on one side and one full barrel on the other that fits between the two on the one side, which makes it easier when trying to align as you work your way down your hair each time. But with this one if you don't do it right you end up sort of straitening an area that you were trying to produce a wave. And then its hard to fix it. I suppose you would get used to it over time and it might not be a big deal but I didn't like it. I kept trying to not let it bother me but it bothered me. Also I didn't think it went as deep as I might want sometimes. With the one I posted on here in the photo which is a Bedhead waver, you have that option to go deeper by leaving it on longer and also it has hotter settings that this one doesn't have. This Wessopan iron that I am reviewing only goes to 200 degrees. It takes longer to do my hair for sure. My new one which is a Bedhead goes from 250 up to 400 degrees. Much easier to use and faster. Its only half enclosed in plastic for some reason but it has a plastic nob on the end to hold if you need it also. Its pretty good, I only burned myself a little on the side of my face once. Ugh. How much extra can adding the other side of plastic casing really cost anyway? Seriously. But I digress.

title: It is actually stretchy
text:
I had ready this wax is a flexible wax. Yes, all similar waxes flex to a degree but this one is supposed to be a bit more elastic. That's to help it wrap around tricky areas (ankle bones, knees, etc.). It's also supposed to work well for large areas. I prefer to wax myself, and I don't have assistance. I also like to wax everywhere. I waxed my own back with this stuff and it actually worked. I did larger sections, and was reaching behind myself to both apply and remove the wax. It did indeed stretch and flex well so there wasn't any wax or hair breakage. The hair on my back is the typically fluffy vellus hair. It showed up after I had my second and I just don't like it even if it's not super obvious (or even visible 90% of the time). Admittedly that hair type did make it difficult to see, but again this wax wasn't too fussy. I'm 100% positive I applied it in the wrong direction at times and removed in the wrong direction too. Still, worked great.

I also tested it out on my legs. The hair there really varies from fine and barely visible blonde to thicker and quite dark (and rather stubborn to remove in places). It did a decent job on most of my legs. In the areas where the hair is a bit more stubborn I really had to work in smaller sections to get a good result. But in areas like my thighs I was able to do wide areas with ease and little left behind. On my thighs I have small areas that grow in different directions for no reason. I thought I'd have to do second passes, but I rarely did.

All that aside, I don't think this is the best wax for everyone. If you have a lot of very fine or fluffy vellus hair on large areas. Especially if it's on tricky areas like the stomach or behind your shoulders, and areas such as my upper arms where the hair literally grows both up and down in the exact same spot. This will get the job done. If the hair is even a little bit stubborn, you will probably run into some issues. For those places I'd say the pink version (their Best Loved wax) is a fantastic option.

title: Works, but you have to have realistic expectations
text:
I have abundant, thick, coarse, wavy hair. I have done it all to tame the volume and sponginess of it, but finally gave up as it was too time consuming. I have very little time to get ready in the morning before heading out to work, so I bought this brush to try it, since I am always looking for a solution. Now the verdict:

It works well as long as you are not looking for a fast miracle. It heats up quickly and and goes through your hair like a regular brush. It dies tame unruly hair and gave me a flatish look very quickly, I went through my entire hair in less than four minutes and my back of the head volume went down and the sponge "pyramid" went down. I ended my few minutes long styling with balm and there! I looked human again and it lasted all day. My hair feels silkier and definitely looks like I spent more time styling it, but not salon styled of course. It suits my needs so I am keeping it. I would say it gives 68 percent flat hair, which is a good result considering the time invested, If you want to look like Hollywood star or the girl in the advertisement of the product, this is not for you, and you will need to go to 30 minutes blow dry and 30'minutes flat ironing if you want flat straight perfect results.

Pros
-Attractive packaging
-It works if you have reasonable expectations
- Fast fair to good results

Cons
- Product looks cheap and chintzy
- The brush's bristles are made out of very hard plastic, ouch!
- No glove included, although the handle doesn't get hot

I am satisfied with the results. Now I can go to work without looking like a mop everyday. Whenever I want my tresses to look flat, I would use my flat iron, but for every day, go and run quick styling, this seem like a good compromise. Hope it lasts as it looks like a cheap price of Chinese rubbish.

text:
This is well worth the price. I was looking for a low end electric toothbrush to see if I like having an electric toothbrush. I have been sold on the electric part and I really see no reason why I would need to upgrade to a more expensive toothbrush. I have been a manual toothbrush person forever. I had one other electric one a long time ago but it was loud and didn't hold a charge well so I was always skeptical. But this Oral-B toothbrush is great. It isn't super loud and it is comfortable to hold. The charge lasts for several days before it begins to lose brushing power.

What I really like is the 2 minute timer. It has made me much better at brushing for a the correct period of time. Some of the more expensive brushes beep every 30 seconds so you know when to switch regions, but I have gotten so used to this that I usually finish brushing everything within 5 seconds of the 2 minutes. In addition to a more thorough cleaning, I can definitely say that the electric brush cleans much better than a manual brush. The brush heads last, the entire assembly is easy to clean, and replacements are not that expensive. If you are trying to decide whether or not to try an electric toothbrush, this is a great one to start with. It is inexpensive and works great. There is no need to spend upwards of $100 for something like this. If you already have an electric and are looking for a replacement, well my dentist likes the results of this brush so this is a keeper.
