title: Pretty Good
text:
I've only ever owned this epilator, but in the 4+ months I've had it, I've been pretty happy with it. The epilator itself is very well built, it's very sturdy, I've never had problems with the tweezing mechanisms, and it has a nice, solid feel. I chose this epilator because it was relatively well-reviewed, though I was worried by some of the negative reviews. I wanted to be able to epilate my legs and underarms, and this product performs pretty well. There are a few notes:
The light, this makes all the difference, and I never thought it would. I can see EVERY hair growing out of my legs, even if I'm in a dimly lit room.
The trimmer works fairly well, and it's nice to have a device that is so multifunctional (great for traveling).
Some have complained about the battery, but I've had no problems. Even when I was just starting and took forever trying to get every hair, it lasted till I was done.
The noise is fairly loud and menacing, but it's one of those things you get used to. Roommates may get annoyed though.
I don't have any trouble with ingrown hairs, but some people do, so be mindful of that.
I really wanted the wet/dry capability, but the wetness makes the tweezers slide off the hair, so the hair ends up getting pulled pretty hard but doesn't come out. This feature didn't help me in the least. Also, it's harder to get a good grip on the device when it's wet.

Yes, anything that takes your hair out by the root will hurt, I don't think the best epilator in the world could stop that, so don't ever expect it to feel like a massage. Everyone who is saying the first time is the worst is absolutely right - when I did my underarms the first time, I was seeing spots it hurt so bad. My legs were a little difficult but after awhile it was easy to keep going. I tried the bikini line, but couldn't get more than a few hairs out until it was unbearable. It is a good idea when you're starting to epilate to epilate every few days for a week so that all the 'cycles' of hair can be initially epilated. It got much less painful very quickly each time I'd epilate, though I still can't do the bikini (upsetting because I was planning on completely doing away with razors). Now, legs are no problem, though my underarms still hurt some. Tip: make sure you don't have any deoderant on your underarms when you epilate, it makes the hairs slick and the tweezers don't grip well.

I really love having underarms with no stubble shadow, and they feel much smoother. Even when the hairs grow back, they are tapered, so they are much softer than shaving stubble which would irritate my skin. Similarly with the legs, tapered hairs are much less visible than blunt ones, and I do think it is growing back slightly more sparsely (I've heard with routine use, you can stop a lot of growth permanently).

I also had the same issues with 1) never getting a just-shaven smoothness 2) the finer hairs do break - these are best to attack with the slower mode, which is easier on the hair 3) the hair grows back faster than I expected. I have a fair complexion with fine hair, and my hair doesn't grow particularly fast. I have to epilate my arms once a week, and my legs every other at best, so 4-6 weeks is a pretty blatant lie.

So, I'll give it four stars because it does as good a job as any epilator could, most my complaints have to do with epilating in general. One star penalty for misleading description and useless wet/dry feature.

title: You made it to this point - just get it
text:
You got here 1 of 2 ways - you are either into cyberpunk aesthetics, or you were searching for a specific scent. I was trying to track down vanillas and citrus scents, and came across Proto Alchemy, and they instantly got my attention. I am a dude. I am not a lumberjack, and I am not a suave, dapper, 3 piece suit wearing gentleman either. But every freaking beard oil hammers one of those two stereotypes home. It's really hard to tell if any of these companies are actually genuine, or just some faceless sub-brand marking up some garbage because having a nice beard is cool.

So I can tell you these guys (actually just this guy I think) are legit. Matte finish packaging, commissioned art from legit artists, and even a little bit of world building just for a beard oil. I am a designer - little details are important to me and can often speak to the quality of the actual product. And in this case it does, this is some damn good beard oil.

The oils work well, providing light shaping and conditioning. The bottles dispense nicely - I like being able to easily tap out a couple drops which is all i need for a 3-4 inch beard. I've had similar droplet dispensers (I don't know what those are called) that were slower or didn't work as well.

I first bought Anti-Hero. I don't drink whiskey and don't smoke, but this smell is really something else. Sweet, vanilla & musk with something else special to it. It reminded me of the hotel elevator in Athens during my honeymoon, that was overwhelmed with some foreign, exotic cologne. That will help none of you, but regardless, I believe it will still be a scent that reminds you of something or somewhere, but you can't quite place it. It drove me crazy for a week before I figured it out, and that scent is something I have been trying to figure out for a good 7 years. It's unique, I love it, and I still can't explain it. I was finding excuses to use it more than I needed to, and quickly ordered the other 2 scents.

Botanist is awesome. It is so far beyond what I can explain - I've read reviews on plenty of colognes and then gave up when I realized even if I knew what those words people used meant, I'd still have no idea how it could smell. I can definitely buy into the botany idea behind this scent, there is an earthiness to it but it also leans sweet. Another scent I really haven't come across before.

Islander I was really hopeful for, but it smelled a little too generic cologney. Maybe it's the rum? My previous favorite beard oil was citrus + vanilla, and I think the vanilla really sells the other two proto-alchemy scents. I don't hate it, it's still wearable unlike some others I have had to get rid of immediately, but I won't reorder it - unlike Botany and Anti-Hero, which I am planning on stocking up on, right now. I'd hate for them to disappear forever.

If I ran any sort of men's store, barber shop, or just a place that sold cool doo-dads, I would absolutely stock these and most likely sell a ton. They smell great, they look super cool and premium, and they are unique. Sadly, I don't. If you do, try that out for me. Best I can do is give them as gifts for now (or just hoard them for myself).

This is basically a rebadged pumice scrub that you can buy at the drugstore - check the ingredients, it's right there - pumice. There are no specific ingredients to help with KP, just some essential oils that you'd find in most scrubs.

Just like the cream, this product is for sale anywhere besides Amazon - you can see that because they've printed the Amazon barcode itself right on the label. There's no real UPC. This product can't even be sold in stores because of it's labeling. Just another marketing company relabeling a basic scrub for KP. Don't fall for the new products like this one that pop up periodically - go with something that's been around for a long time.

title: My Lips Look and Feel Great Thanks to Hudson and James Cloud Lip Balm!
text:
Usually, by this time of the year (late October), my lips are already chapped. Thanks to Hudson and James Cloud Lip Balm my lips are still looking, and feeling, great. I received the balm inside a short, round, 0.5-ounce glass jar. It came tightly sealed inside a form-fitting bubble-wrapped envelope. There was a tiny, round transparent protective seal on the jar and its large black lid. The seal is not very effective. I was able to easily open the cap without realizing the seal was there. The print on the jar is very tiny. After looking at the jar several times with a magnifying glass, I couldn't locate an expiration or a best by date. Many hygiene product don't have them but they should. These dates let me know if the ingredient are still fresh.

I use the Cloud Lip Balm twice a day, once in the morning and once in the evening. The balm feels nice on my lips. It is very easy to smooth all over my lips. It reminds me of some expensive high-end lip butter that I once owned. The jar is small enough to fit inside the pockets of my jeans. During the day, I use Carmex Classic Lip Balm when necessary. The Cloud Lip and the Carmex are working together well to protect my lips and to keep them appearing healthy and attractive. I've been faithfully using the Cloud Lip Balm for nearly three weeks and have not experienced any adverse side effects or allergic reactions. It doesn't have a noticeable scent. Also, I would like to note that the balm has a light-yellow waxy color whereas Amazon's website shows it to have a creamy white color.

The Hudson and James Cloud Lip Balm doesn't sting or burn my lips after applying it; I hardly notice that it is there. What I do notice is that my lips are feeling and looking great despite the change in seasons. I wish I knew the price of the lip balm. At the time of this review, it wasn't available for purchase. Overall, I like this hygiene product and would strongly recommend it to anyone who suffers from dry, chapped lips.

title: WOW. Great exfoliation!
text:
So I've never had a professional microdermabrasion session and can't compare to that, but this is definitely the most amazing exfoliation I've ever had! The written instructions with mismatched photos for setting up are pretty bad- probably should've checked-out the video, but I was too impatient! Not sure I got the little disk filter thing in right, but onward and upward!

I used the diamond tip- medium size- and suction level 2 (I have pretty thick skin). I did give myself a little hickey next to one eye before I realized I could change the suction level while it was already in use (since you set the timer and the suction and then start it, I thought it was locked-in). But even that already looks a lot better 24 hours later.

I started with just one side of my face (line right down the center) so I could see/feel a side-by-side and while, of course, it's not like all my fine lines or hyperpigmentation disappeared after one session, my skin on the side I did was BABY SMOOTH while the other side was my usual not so smooth (Though I exfoliate a LOT)! Just keep in mind that your skin may be a little tender in some spots and you DO NOT want to use any chemical exfoliants (like AHAs) for a bit! I'm not a professional, so I don't know the time to wait, but I'll try a bit of my usual AHA serum after 48 hours. For now, I'm just using my hyaluronic acid and peptide blend serum and DMAE moisturizer and my skin is super glowy and nice!

title: Mother knows best!!
text:
My mother told me never to use a brush on wet hair, because wet hair is weaker and more vulnerable to damage than dry hair, and needs the most gentle touch. Well, for years I was faithful to her advice. But then I strayed…

For the past few years, my newest hair stylist has used a brush to comb out my wet tangles. So when I left my trusty Fuller Brush wide tooth comb at a motel, I had only my brush. I figured “Well, my stylist uses a brush and she must know about these things, so I guess mom was just old fashioned.” But as my hair has grown (now at the middle of my back), I’ve been seeing tangles in the brush, even with the best detangling brush around. I was losing too much hair, but not from the roots (which is normal); it appeared to be breaking at some of the tangles, EVEN THOUGH I did not feel any particular “pull” with the brush.

I ordered this comb specifically because of its claims about detangling WET hair, but wasn't expecting much, except for a replacement of my lost comb. But after the first use on my clean damp hair, I saw only a few long and UNTANGLED hairs clinging to it, and they appeared to have come from my head, as in normal. I didn't see any hair that appeared broken or tangled. The combing was QUICK, easy, and completely without frustration. What more could anyone want? Those funny squiggly teeth DO SOMETHING, but how it works is a mystery to me.

I’d recommend this for any adult with medium to long hair, and particularly for CHILDREN who dread the after-shampoo combout.

SORRY, MOM, you were right all along!!

I'd be remiss no to mention the two products that have done the most for the appearance of my hair over the years. Both are available on Amazon, with terrific pricing on hard-to-find larger sizes of Bain de Terre.

* Bain de Terre Recovery Complex smoothes and conditions hair with only a few drops, adding a healthy look to my hair.

* The very good detangling brush (for DRY hair ONLY) is the Mason Pearson detangling brush.

title: Sonic Complete S-200
text:
I received this toothbrush for a Christmas present. I had thought about getting an electronic toothbrush, but I had not done any research. In any case, I was eager to try it. When I first used it, it took a few seconds to get used to it. I thought it tickled my gums, but very shortly I realize how much the "sonic" action of the toothbrush is working on cleaning your teeth and you just make small circles with the brush and let the sonic action do the rest. I have used it a couple of times and already my teeth feel cleaner. I also find that it is fun to use so I end up brushing my teeth a lot longer than with a regular brush.

I went to see how much refills were at Wal-Mart and they were $7.97. This is why I gave it 4 stars and not five. $8 every three months is a bit more espensive than a regular brush (that I usually get free from Target when they have the tooth paste / tooth brush packages).
